items.body:

Eric-authorized bounded Ledgerline B0 leaf13. Source issue https://github.com/rickylabs/ledgerline/issues/13; parent epic https://github.com/rickylabs/ledgerline/issues/2; accepted milestone https://github.com/rickylabs/ledgerline/milestone/2. The existing T3 primary remains sole coordinator. Do not start other agents or coordinators. Old Harness811 must stay idle and its inbox immutable. Preserve PR10 ownership and PR12.

Part of #2. Milestone: Swiss receivables.

Eric accepted the narrow offline B0–B3 / QR Q0–Q4 cut on 2026-11-06. This is the first bounded B0 implementation leaf. Approved source plan: https://github.com/rickylabs/ledgerline/blob/7fc737f889db38ffe792d96dbacf7f3cc4ea9de4/docs/preparation/2026-11-06/open-banking-plan.md and architecture findings A2/A5. Preserve #8/PR10 ownership.

Problem: banking ingestion currently receives an actor but cannot establish bank-account/tenant ownership; matching and replay/review scope must not cross tenant boundaries or follow mutable creditor identity.

Scope:
- Establish an immutable, explicit bank-account-to-tenant authority boundary at service admission.
- Scope candidate matching, persisted/replayed transaction reads and review reads to that authorized account and tenant.
- Ambiguous references must produce explicit review, never first-candidate settlement.
- Preserve exact money, existing changed-payload conflicts, partial-payment/adjustment policy and issued snapshots.
- Keep transport and workers behind existing contracts/ports; interfaces never become recovery backends.
- Preserve legacy financial facts and fail closed where ownership is unproven; no bulk reassignment or deletion.

Acceptance:
- Tenant A's authorized account reconciles only A invoices.
- A principal using B's account/reference is rejected before any unauthorized persistence, including unmatched rows.
- Same account/key replay returns the same result; changed payload and cross-tenant reuse conflict/refuse without a second effect.
- Two eligible candidates require review. Later creditor edits cannot redirect old issued-invoice matching.
- Meaningful positive, negative, concurrency and fresh/upgrade compatibility tests at the exact PR head, using only an explicitly owned Ledgerline isolated test context.
- Root quality verbs including deno task test run with honest limits. No inherited/default database or Garage/host/foreign Docker.
- Independent plan review before implementation, and independent cross-family implementation review before merge. Startup or author tests do not constitute approval.

items.title: EWP-2: ingestion-cache store Connection-scoped refactor (#482b-ingestion)
items.body:
# Migration 3 — ingestion-cache → EWP-1 envelope (Option A)

**Corrected (2026-11-01):** ingestion-cache is **Cassandra-backed** (`CqlSession`), not JDBC. There is no `DataSource`/`JdbcTemplate`, so the `JdbcEventOutbox` + 3-arg `OutboxEventPublisher` same-transaction-JDBC pattern does **not** apply, and no store needs Connection-scoping. (This supersedes the original "Connection-scoped refactor" title.)

The Cassandra outbox already has LWT atomicity (`insertSourceVersionAndOutboxIfAbsent`), dead-letter (5 attempts), retry classification, exponential backoff, and per-aggregate ordering (`orderingBlocked`). Migration 3 **adapts its event envelope to EWP-1**, keeping the Cassandra store + `KafkaProducer`.

## In scope

- **`EventEnvelopeBuilder` extraction** into `eventing-outbox`: shared wire-shape validation (tenant scope, registered type-version, replay-class match) with **no JDBC dependency** — used by `OutboxEventPublisher` and the Cassandra path. This is the shared contract; `EventOutbox`/`JdbcEventOutbox` remain the JDBC storage impl.
- **Cassandra schema additions**: `schema_version`, `correlation_id`, `causation_id`, `replay_class`, `security_metadata` columns in `source_versions`/`source_tombstones` (+ manifest outbox).
- **SecurityMetadata propagation**: classification/actor from the ingestion pipeline must reach each event.
- **Typed payloads + registry**: `SourcePublished`, `SourceTombstoned`, manifest-transition types; `SourcePublished` = `REPLAY_SAFE` (fact); `SourceTombstoned` inherits Hazard H-1 (pin in #394).
- **Config fail-startup gate**: fail if `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS` is blank and dispatcher mode is not explicitly demo (same discipline as topology).

## Out of scope (explicit)

`EventOutbox`, `JdbcEventOutbox`, `OutboxEventPublisher`, `KafkaOutboxDispatcher`, `OutboxReader`, and reimplementing the Cassandra dead-letter/retry/ordering (those stay as-is).

## Preserved unchanged

`insertSourceVersionAndOutboxIfAbsent` (LWT), retry classification, dead-letter, backoff, `listUnpublishedSourceOutbox` + `orderingBlocked`, `replaySourceOutbox`, `listTenantIds()` / `tenant_registry` enumeration.

## Dependency

Blocked on the "outbox production readiness" PR (dispatcher gating + `EventEnvelopeBuilder` extraction + fixes).

items.title: P0: Coordinate parallel multi-chat dataset ingestion (source owners, branches, QA and merge gates)
items.body:
## Purpose

Run **multiple independent source-ingestion ChatGPT conversations in parallel**, without conflicting edits, duplicate source work, or false Source Health claims. GitHub issues/branches/PRs are the *only shared coordination system*; separate chats do **not** automatically see or message one another. The user can start separate sessions and direct each to this issue.

**Product scope: all industries and all facility types**, not FDA/life-sciences-only. Source identities are not automatically verified physical facilities, and no absent observation means zero risk.

## Snapshot at setup (2026-10-23; verify against latest main before working)

- EPA FRS national source identity index: 5,354,716; durable private serving remains outstanding, [#39](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/39) and [#3](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/3).
- NOAA Storm Events: source ingestion implemented in recent merged work; verify live/deployed freshness and browser visibility before marking fully production ready.
- NOAA OR&R IncidentNews: work in progress; [PR #72](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/pull/72) open for browser regression/status; **do not independently reimplement** this lane.
- FDA device/drug, Canada NPRI, Ireland EPA: already represented as distinct source registries; confirm published counts/metadata; avoid reingestion without a scoped fix.
- Foundational [#4](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/4) covers verified all-industry hazard, incidents, insurance and interruption findings.

## Parallel lanes (one separate chat/branch/PR per lane)

| Lane | Source focus | Boundary / distinct deliverable | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A: Flood & wildfire** | FEMA NFHL and official US wildfire layers, plus source-vintage/geometry QA | Geospatial hazard importers, staged tiles/shapes/point-in-polygon **only at corroborated site coords**; do not edit NOAA IncidentNews or FRS registry ingestion | P0 |
| **B: Environmental compliance** | EPA ECHO plus facility-level TRI/RCRA/RMP where permitted | Live download/import + stable program IDs, normalized findings, distinct source identities; never equate a compliance record with a physical insured property | P0 |
| **C: Industrial events** | USCG NRC, CSB, PHMSA | Independent incident parsers, dates, location uncertainty, severity context, **unverified report** flags, matching candidates, outcome corroboration | P0 |
| **D: Reliability & BI** | Public utility/provider mapping, EIA-861 context, outage datasets where available, public financial event reports | Contextual reliability and independently grounded interruption evidence; EIA-861 is not a facility-specific outage/claims database | P1 |
| **E: Registry/operations & integration (coordinator)** | [#39](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/39), shared provenance/manifest, private serving, canonical review-only crosswalk, report wiring, QA and deployment | **Sole owner** of shared schemas/UI/shared Source Health files and final merges; do not reimplement source importers already owned by A–D | P0 |

Additional future lanes can include other countries/global all-industry registries, earthquakes/wind, supply-chain routes, and outcome/claims validation. Create one issue/branch per source before touching shared code.

## Cross-chat synchronization rule

1. Each chat reads **latest main**, this coordination issue, [#3](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/3), [#4](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/4), [#39](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/39), and open PRs **before implementing**.
2. Each lane claims its ownership in a comment on this issue (lane, sources, branch name, linked PR, status, blockers). Do not duplicate a lane already claimed by active work.
3. Use `ingest/<source-or-lane>-<distinct-suffix>` from fresh main; no direct pushes to main; no changes outside owned importer/tests/source metadata except via coordinator.
4. Provide an isolated importer module, reproducible run command, tested source licenses/API requirements, deterministic transforms, source-specific fixtures, schema/identifier/duplicate/null/coordinate tests, and provenance+freshness manifest.
5. Record actual **data counts and evidentiary state**, not just HTTP test: NOT_TESTED -> PROBED -> DOWNLOADED -> STAGED -> NORMALIZED -> INDEXED -> VERIFIED -> DEPLOYED. Record latest run, published vintage, accepted/rejected rows, source IDs, coverage, null coordinates, checksum, failure modes, and known geographic bounds. VERIFIED requires content-level checks; DEPLOYED requires live app/backend verification.
6. Preserve original source keys and raw records separately from review-only candidate facility linkage. Use actual source-reported geometry/addresses and confidence; **never infer one facility = one source record**. Never represent external risk observations as insured losses or policy coverage.
7. Open focused PR with test evidence and deployment impact. Coordinator rebases/merges PRs one at a time, reruns full suite and live browser checks, checks Source Health statuses, publishes count/freshness ledger. No PR should declare another lane's status.
8. Hosting constraint: GitHub Pages is static; multi-GB indexes, private APIs, ingestion schedules and auth require a durable backend. CI artifacts are staging, not persistent production. Do not claim source availability if only CI artifacts exist.

## Per-lane definition of done

- [ ] Official source access and data-use constraints verified
- [ ] Real download/ingestion run completed (not simulation-only)
- [ ] Raw rows and accepted/rejected rows reconciled with checksums
- [ ] Source-specific IDs and geospatial limitations documented
- [ ] Transform, QA, and failure-mode regression tests pass in CI
- [ ] No unreviewed canonical physical-site auto-merges
- [ ] Query/storage integration and source health manifest are verified
- [ ] Deployment runtime/app shows **accurate** state and count; unreleased work remains labeled staging

## Copy/paste for each worker chat

> Work on **Lane [A/B/C/D]** in `jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest`. First read the master parallel-ingestion coordination issue and current open PRs. Claim the lane there with your branch and source list. Ingest real public source data, implement a reproducible pipeline with source-identity preservation and QA, and open a focused PR. Do not touch other lanes or shared registry/UI except through the coordinator; do not merge your own PR. Report actual downloaded, normalized, indexed, and deployed counts separately. All industries and facility types are in scope. Continue implementation and verification until your lane meets the explicit gate or document any hard blocker.

`scripts/architecture/runtime-complexity.baseline.json` holds 47 tolerated violations: 25 method-lines, 19 file-lines and 3 constructor-dependencies. The worst files on master 74592cef:
- `social-inbox-ingestion.service.ts`: 1,457 lines
- `content-optimization.service.ts`: 1,254
- `ads-research.service.ts`: 1,174
- `author-reply-loop.service.ts`: 1,159
- `articles.service.ts`: 1,153
- `stripe.service.ts`: 1,117
- `brand-remix-run-execution.service.ts`: 1,101
- `social-inbox-action.service.ts`: 1,099

## Scope

Behavior-preserving splits, worst first, one service per PR. Extract collaborators (pure helpers, query builders, mappers) behind the same public methods; keep NestJS DI, exceptions and `ConfigService` patterns. `stripe.service.ts` is billing: split only with its existing specs unchanged and extra attention to webhook idempotency. Serializers stay in `packages/serializers`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each PR removes its entries from `runtime-complexity.baseline.json`; the baseline never grows. First wave target: the 8 files above.
- [ ] Public service API and DI tokens unchanged; callers untouched.
- [ ] All existing specs for the service pass unchanged; new specs for extracted helpers.
- [ ] Every tenant-scoped query keeps `{ organizationId, isDeleted: false }`; `check:tenant-scope` unchanged or better.
- [ ] API type-check and `bun run audit:runtime-complexity` results attached on the Studio.

## Dependencies

Skip any file with an open PR; `stripe.service.ts` waits until after the Oct 27 launch window and needs Vincent's sign-off from Claude before merge.

## Guardrails

Full list in #7896. In short: ready PR only, no auto-merge, no merge without Claude's `Green light: merge`; no release, deploy, tag or publish; tests on the Mac Studio only; baselines only go down; at most 3 open PRs; do not start until `Queue open` is posted on #7896.

items.body:
<!-- planning-id: M06-06 -->

**Milestone:** M06 — Seller Onboarding & Moderation  
**Planning ID:** `M06-06`  
**Size:** L (planning estimate)  
**Requirements/traceability:** ADR 0008, ADR 0011

## Summary
All Stripe-originated state must enter through one verified, idempotent inbox.

## Dependencies
Blocked by:
- #12 — Gateway CORS allow-list, security headers and raw webhook pass-through
- #39 — Transactional outbox writer and relay (Postgres)
- #41 — Consumer inbox wrapper (idempotent processing)
- #16 — Apply the service bootstrap standard to the remaining seven services
- #17 — Neon development project, per-developer branches and bootstrap script

Do not start until the issues above are merged. If a dependency is missing, comment and stop.

## Current state
`apps/payment-service/src/payments/webhook.controller.ts` (`POST /payments/webhook`) verifies one signature via `PaymentsService.verifyWebhookSignature`, handles only `payment_intent.succeeded|payment_failed`, has no event storage or dedupe; `main.ts` sets `rawBody: true`; configuration is read inline without validation.

## Expected behavior
Routes `POST /payments/webhook/account` and `/payments/webhook/connect` (raw body, separate secrets from validated config; the service refuses to start without them or with a `sk_live_` key while `PAYMENTS_LIVE_MODE_ENABLED=false`); table `stripe_events(event_id PK, scope, type, received_at, processed_at, status, payload jsonb)`; handler: verify → `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (duplicate ⇒ 200) → dispatch to registered processors (none for payment events yet; `account.updated` in M06-07) → mark processed; unknown event types stored and acknowledged; failed processing keeps status `failed` for a retry sweeper; old `/payments/webhook` removed; database `bb_payment` migrations (`stripe_events`, `outbox`, `processed_events` only); payload retention job (90 days).

## Technical approach and files
Edit `webhook.controller.ts`, `payments.service.ts` (extract a `StripeProvider`), `payments.module.ts`; schema + migrations under `apps/payment-service/drizzle/` *(new)*; `src/config.ts`.

## Implementation steps
1. Config + Stripe provider guards.
2. Schema + migration.
3. Two controllers + shared handler.
4. Processor registry.
5. Failure sweeper.
6. Tests with signed fixtures.

## API / data / event / UI changes
New webhook paths; new tables.

## Security, authorization and tenant isolation
Constant-time verification via the Stripe SDK; no secrets logged; invalid signature → 400; the route must not pass through any body parser.

## Error handling, edge cases and recovery
Duplicate delivery; out-of-order events; DB outage → 500 so Stripe retries; oversized payloads.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the same signed event twice, then one `stripe_events` row and both responses are 200
- [ ] Given a bad signature, then 400 and no row
- [ ] Given a missing webhook secret, then the service does not start
- [ ] Given a live key and the flag false, then the service does not start.

## Testing requirements
Unit + integration with signed fixtures from the Stripe library; boot-failure tests.

## Documentation updates
Payment README; `.env.*.example`.

_Update in-repository files listed here. Maintainer-held design documents live outside this repository; if you cannot see them, list the required changes in the pull request description._

## Definition of done
Standard DoD. (see "Reference: dod-standard" below for the standard checklist).

## Out of scope
Payment-intent processing (M10-05), `account.updated` (M06-07).

## Embedded references
Essential constraints are inlined below so this issue is self-contained.

<details>
<summary>Reference: repo-context</summary>

**Repository:** pnpm 10 + Turborepo monorepo, Node 22, TypeScript. Apps (`apps/`): NestJS services `gateway` (4000), `auth-service` (4001), `product-service` (4002), `seller-service` (4003), `order-service` (4004), `payment-service` (4005), `notification-service` (4006), `media-service` (4007), `analytics-service` (4008); Next.js 15 apps `web` (3000), `seller-portal` (3001), `admin-portal` (3002). Shared packages (`packages/`): `contracts` (Zod schemas for DTOs/events), `auth-shared` (JWT/JWKS verification, guards), `kafka-client`, `logger` (Pino), `utils`, `ui`, `config` (eslint/tsconfig). Postgres (Drizzle) for auth/seller/order/payment; MongoDB (Mongoose) for product; Redis for rate limits/cache; Kafka-compatible broker for events. All datastores are managed cloud services — **no local Docker is required or may be introduced as a dependency**. Commands: `pnpm install`, `pnpm turbo run lint type-check test build --filter=<pkg>...`, `pnpm --filter <app> <script>`. Each service validates DTOs with Zod from `@betterbasket/contracts` (not class-validator) and exposes `GET /health`. Services compile to CommonJS.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: stripe-webhooks</summary>

Two Stripe endpoints/secrets: **account** scope (payment_intent.*, charge.*, refund.*, dispute events, transfer.*) and **connect** scope (`account.updated`, `payout.failed`). Handler order: verify signature on the raw body → `INSERT stripe_events(event_id PK) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (duplicate ⇒ return 200) → process in one DB transaction together with outbox inserts → mark processed → respond 2xx quickly. Stripe retries for up to 3 days and may duplicate or reorder events: handlers must be idempotent and use transition guards (`payments.status` moves `requires_payment → processing → succeeded|failed`; `failed → succeeded` allowed; `succeeded` is never downgraded). Unknown event types are stored and acknowledged. Missing secrets prevent startup. Stripe idempotency keys on API calls: `pi:<orderId>`, `tr:<subOrderId>`, `rv:<refundId>:<transferId>`, `rf:<refundId>`, `acct:<sellerId>`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: webhook-passthrough</summary>

The gateway must stream Stripe webhook bodies **byte-for-byte** to payment-service: create the Nest app with `bodyParser: false`, no body re-serialization (`fixRequestBody` forbidden), forward `Stripe-Signature` and `Content-Type` untouched, cap bodies at 1 MB (413), allow only the two webhook paths and POST. The gateway never holds webhook secrets and adds no trust; payment-service verifies the signature itself against `req.rawBody` (`rawBody: true`). A regression test compares the SHA-256 of the body sent with the body received by a stub upstream (ASCII, Unicode, odd whitespace).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: payments-model</summary>

**Test mode only** until the live-payments gate is explicitly opened by the maintainer. Model: one PaymentIntent per order on the **platform** Stripe account (`transfer_group = order_<orderId>`, card payments only); after success and when the release policy allows, one Transfer per seller sub-order using `source_transaction = <charge id>`. The platform bears Stripe fees, refunds and chargebacks (provisional policy). Refunding a charge does **not** reverse transfers — reversals are explicit. `reverse_transfer`/`refund_application_fee` are destination-charge features and are **not** used. Failed transfers are not retried by Stripe — the platform retries. Amount, currency and destination are always derived server-side from the persisted order; clients send only an order id. Config gates: `PAYMENTS_LIVE_MODE_ENABLED` (default false; live keys `sk_live_`/`pk_live_` refused at boot unless true), `PAYMENTS_ENABLED` kill switch, `TRANSFERS_PAUSED`, `SUPPORTED_SELLER_COUNTRIES` (empty = test mode only). Country, legal and finance policy are **undecided**; every country-dependent behavior must stay configurable and provisional.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: test-mode-gate</summary>

This issue is `gate:test-mode-only`: use Stripe **test** keys and test-mode objects only; the service must refuse to start with a live key unless `PAYMENTS_LIVE_MODE_ENABLED=true` (never set outside production after the maintainer opens the live-payments gate). No real card or customer data in fixtures, logs or tests. Provisional commission, payout, jurisdiction and legal assumptions must stay configurable and must not be presented as final.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: events-outbox-inbox</summary>

Delivery is at-least-once; consumers are idempotent. **Outbox:** events are inserted into an `outbox` table (Mongo: collection) in the **same transaction** as the state change (`outbox(id, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, type, version, payload, headers, created_at, published_at, attempts)`); a relay polls (500 ms, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, batch 50, per-aggregate order), publishes with `acks=all` + idempotent producer, marks `published_at` only after broker ack, backs off on failure, purges published rows after 7 days, quarantines rows that exceed an attempts cap. Alert when the oldest unpublished row is >60 s old. **Inbox:** `processed_events(consumer, event_id, processed_at, PK(consumer,event_id))`; handler effects and the inbox insert share one transaction; duplicate ⇒ ack and skip; retention 14 days. **Consumer behavior:** 3 in-process retries with jittered backoff for transient errors; non-retryable errors go straight to `<topic>.dlq` with `{errorClass, message, attempts, group, topic, partition, offset}`; a poison message never blocks a partition; a failing DLQ publish pauses consumption (never drops); the consumer loop is awaited/supervised (no fire-and-forget), disconnects cleanly on shutdown, and fails readiness on fatal errors. Handlers tolerate out-of-order events by comparing state/`aggregateVersion`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: dod-standard</summary>

Implementation matches *Expected behavior*; every acceptance criterion passes with automated evidence; required tests added and green in CI (no skipped tests without a linked issue); lint, type-check, build, contract and migration checks pass; docs updated; security requirements satisfied including negative/authorization tests; no secrets, credentials or real customer/payment data in code, fixtures, logs or PR text; PR description complete; deployment verification performed when the issue affects a deployed environment.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: agent-workflow</summary>

1. Read this whole issue; inspect the files named under *Technical approach*; confirm every item under *Current state* is still true (the codebase may have moved). 2. items.title: GET /v1/jobs — tenant-scoped ingestion job list (JobStore tenant_id migration)
items.body:
Follow-up to **#85** (split out during design review as a materially higher-risk change). Part of the dashboard/explorer epic **#82**.

`GET /v1/jobs` — list ingestion jobs owned by the caller's tenant. Deferred from the #85 read-endpoints PR (#98) because, unlike the other three read endpoints, it requires a **JobStore schema change + back-compat migration**, not just read-only count methods.

## Why it's separate
`#85` shipped `/v1/stats/stores`, `/v1/graph/stats`, `/v1/health/deep` — all read-only over existing state. `/v1/jobs` needs new persisted state (a tenant stamp on job rows) and a migration path for existing rows, which is a different risk surface and deserves its own review.

## Scope
- **Model**: add `tenant_id: str = DEFAULT_TENANT` to `IngestJob` (`jobstore.py`). Keep `source` as-is but **assert non-absolute / redact to basename** before returning (`IngestRequest.source` is unvalidated body input).
- **Schema + migration**: add `tenant_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default'` to `_JOBS_DDL`; add an **idempotent** `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` in both the sqlite and postgres init paths (postgres: `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`; sqlite: guarded catch of the duplicate-column `OperationalError`). Legacy rows backfill to `'default'`.
- **Store API**: `JobStore.create(..., tenant_id=DEFAULT_TENANT)` writes it; add `list_jobs(tenant_id, status=None, limit=50)` to all three stores, filtering `WHERE tenant_id = ?` (+ optional status), bounded by `limit`.
- **Caller**: `documents.py` ingest() must **pass tenant into create()** (today it drops it) so job rows match the chunks.
- **Scope**: **own tenant ONLY** (not `readable_tenants` — operational records are not the shared `public` corpus).
- **Contract**: promote `IngestItemCounts` to a component schema first (`contracts/schemas/ingest_item_counts.json`, `additionalProperties:false`) — `JobSummary.items` `$ref`s it and it's currently only a router-local Pydantic model. Add `JobListResponse` + `JobSummary`. Add the `/v1/jobs` path (query params `status`, `limit`).

## Tests
- `list_jobs` filters by tenant (cross-tenant no-leak: tenant B never sees A's `job_id`); status filter narrows; limit caps.
- Migration path: open a sqlite DB pre-created **without** `tenant_id`, ensure the ALTER adds it and old rows read as `'default'`.
- Conformance: schema-validate; cross-tenant no-leak with two mapped keys; `impl`-gated python-only (Go scaffold has no route).
- Consider adding a `created_at` column in the same migration for a stable `ORDER BY` under `limit` (list_jobs currently has only insert order).

## Risks (from review)
- Absolute-path / `../` leak via `source` — normalize/redact.
- Migration idempotency + back-compat backfill to `'default'`.
- `null`-vs-`0` Go parity for count fields when Go implements it (use `*int`).

items.body:
<!-- orchestration-gap-20261020:scoped-scheduler-attach -->
## Problem

A task server can remain reachable without an orchestrator. Starting broad recovery against its existing store can revisit historical failures and follow-up work that were not the intended new dispatch. The existing run task filter selects backlog/GitHub ingestion; it is not a frozen set of existing task IDs and versions applied to claim, retry and recovery paths.

Source checked against `main` at `eeb6f3bf90958e590ff213cc78b62b313b017bac` and compared with v3.22.0. The observations below distinguish executable fixtures from source inspection; no production credentials or private deployment data are required.

## Where to start

- [`src/bernstein/cli/run_bootstrap.py`](https://github.com/sipyourdrink-ltd/bernstein/blob/eeb6f3bf90958e590ff213cc78b62b313b017bac/src/bernstein/cli/run_bootstrap.py)
- [`src/bernstein/core/orchestration/bootstrap.py`](https://github.com/sipyourdrink-ltd/bernstein/blob/eeb6f3bf90958e590ff213cc78b62b313b017bac/src/bernstein/core/orchestration/bootstrap.py)
- [`src/bernstein/core/orchestration/orchestrator.py`](https://github.com/sipyourdrink-ltd/bernstein/blob/eeb6f3bf90958e590ff213cc78b62b313b017bac/src/bernstein/core/orchestration/orchestrator.py)
- [`src/bernstein/core/tasks/task_lifecycle.py`](https://github.com/sipyourdrink-ltd/bernstein/blob/eeb6f3bf90958e590ff213cc78b62b313b017bac/src/bernstein/core/tasks/task_lifecycle.py)

## Reproduction / evidence

Source inspection finds BERNSTEIN_TASK_FILTER at backlog and GitHub ingestion boundaries, not the ready-claim/retry sweeps. Build an existing-store fixture with one newly admitted task, unrelated failed historical tasks and an unrelated active claim. There must be an explicit supported operation that attaches one scheduler to only the newly admitted task set without re-planning or changing the other records. This is a requested capability; no claim is made that a destructive production restart was attempted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Accept an explicit admission manifest of task IDs/versions plus intended run/store identity; validate before side effects.
- [ ] Acquire and continuously enforce a single scheduler ownership lease for the selected scope; reject overlap/conflicting owner.
- [ ] Apply scope to claim, retry, recovery, decomposition, follow-ups and cancellation; derived work requires explicit bounded policy.
- [ ] Support finite accepted-claim, concurrency, elapsed-time and resource limits with a dry-run of the exact selected set.
- [ ] Unrelated task statuses, claims, versions and histories remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [ ] Restart/resume reconciles in-flight admitted attempts before retry and records unknown outcomes without duplicate dispatch.
- [ ] Expose scoped scheduler identity and heartbeat through execution-readiness telemetry.

## Tests and scope

Add real-store, two-scheduler concurrency tests: overlap refusal, disjoint scope, stale versions, bounded retry, crash/restart and historical-failure noninterference. Include a read-only preview and one real mock-adapter subprocess lifecycle.

Use synthetic local data and the existing task store, receipt and policy implementations. Preserve authentication, tenant boundaries, approval gates, model pins and cancellation semantics. Do not solve the issue by disabling verification or treating unavailable evidence as success. Update the relevant operator/API documentation in the same PR.

Keep existing backlog task filtering backwards-compatible. This is not a request to unpause every queue or automatically retry historical failures.

<details>
<summary>Brief for a coding agent</summary>

Repository: `sipyourdrink-ltd/bernstein`. Work on this issue in a dedicated branch/worktree.

Goal: orchestration: add bounded attachment to selected tasks in an existing server store

Start with the files linked above. Read the current issue comments and any linked PR before changing code; avoid duplicating an active implementation.

Change: make every acceptance criterion observable at the public boundary. First write a failing regression for the behavior above, then make it pass. Keep this slice focused; changes to shared task schemas must be serialized with other schema work.

Verify: `uv sync`; run the targeted test files with `uv run pytest <targeted-files> -q`, then `uv run python scripts/run_tests.py --affected`, scoped Ruff checks, and required repository API/type/doc checks. Record actual commands and results; do not pre-claim success.

Non-goals: redesigning the scheduler, changing provider/model selection, adding a second policy engine, or bypassing existing review/merge gates. Open a focused PR; attach a before/after reproduction and residual limitations.

One implementation decision is yours: Choose a native attach subcommand or a bounded resume mode, and explain how its ownership lease composes with the existing run lock.

items.title: Connect users and tenants to data access, then align ADR-0004 to ADR-0009
items.body:
### What needs to be documented or fixed?

ADR-0006 was revised in #64. A tenant gets one catalog by default, and a project can get its own catalog.
ADR-0004, ADR-0005 and ADR-0007 still assume one catalog per project but the discussion on this issue showed a larger gap.
The ADRs describe access for each project or schema, but nothing links a user or tenant to data access yet.

Today every app reads with its own credentials, and every user gets the same access.
Zitadel only decides who can reach a service.
Nothing creates project roles in Zitadel, so every user who can log in reaches every service.

The ADRs also contradict each other on this point.

- ADR-0006 says a shared tenant catalog separates projects "application-enforced", but names no application. A direct read (Tier A) passes no enforcement point.
- ADR-0008 and ADR-0009 (option 1) assume a Postgres reader role for each project. That does not fit a shared tenant catalog.
- ADR-0009 says materialization never crosses projects. That is only true if a user gets a shared catalog when all its projects are granted.
- ADR-0007 says the enforcement point sets the memory limit of a Tier A read. The client sets that limit in its own process, the flaw that ADR-0008 names for `READ_ONLY`.

### Page or section

- `docs/adr/0004-data-organization-and-ingestion.md` (`catalog = project`, `schema = layer`)
- `docs/adr/0005-authorization-and-data-access.md` (access by attaching catalogs per project)
- `docs/adr/0006-deployment-and-project-isolation-model.md` ("application-enforced")
- `docs/adr/0007-compute-and-scaling.md` (catalogs per project, the Tier A memory limit)
- `docs/adr/0008-identity-propagation-and-data-contracts.md` (reader role per project)
- `docs/adr/0009-data-plane-credential-materialization.md` (option 1, "never crosses projects")

### Suggested improvement

#171 gives the first version of access, which is per service. This spike is the next step, from service to data.

A spike by the core maintainers, in this order.

1. Connect identity to data access. Decide how a Zitadel user and its tenant link to the data, and which claims carry them.
2. Define a simple access tree on top of that. A user or role gets read, write or both on a project, or on specific tables in it.

   ```text
   tenant
   └── project            read | write
       └── table          read | write
   ```

3. Evaluate the access path that enforces the tree.
   - The API checks every read and write.
   - Postgres roles limit access to the DuckLake catalog. One Postgres instance also holds Zitadel, Dagster and Marquez, so a direct connection exposes more than the catalog.
   - A Quack server (ADR-0009, option 2) holds the connection, so no app or user connects to Postgres directly.
   - A combination is possible, such as the API for writes and Quack for reads.
   - Decide whether SRDP builds the access decision itself or uses an existing authorization tool.
4. Decide how a project declares this tree, through `srdp-project.toml` and `srdp-setup` or through the API.
5. Decide what the operator manages and what SRDP manages.
6. Update ADR-0004 to ADR-0009 to this model. Mark what is built and what is target design, as page 11 does.
7. Open issues for the follow-up work.

Compute access is out of scope and comes later.

#132 stays separate. It gives each platform service its own Postgres role, which every model needs.

items.title: File & Document Security: authenticated attachment ingress + tenant auto-activation end-to-end
items.body:
## Objective (Greg-approved)
Integrate real, server-received file attachments into **existing** authenticated tenant checks, not a parallel scanner/dashboard. No attachment ⇒ file rules not applicable; matching real attachment ⇒ enable applicable implemented file rules by default unless tenant explicitly set Off. Preserve tenant stage/rule action authority, all findings and fail-closed responses. Production approval gate was removed on Nov 5, but security, cost and CI controls remain.

## Existing implementation and gap
- `guardoath/attachment_probe.py` does bounded byte-only classification for CSV and explicit unsupported formats; `guardoath/csv_formula.py` detects risky CSV spreadsheet formulas in CSV text.
- `guardoath/tenant_record.py`, `guardoath/models.py`, `guardoath/app.py`, `guardoath/engine.py`, `guardoath/static/*` are **Director/shared reserved**; the probe is not connected to an authenticated binary ingestion API, record `auto` behavior, or the dashboard. **No PDF/DOCX/XLSX inspection is currently supported.**
- Reference: `docs/file-document-security-architecture.md` and `docs/director-agent-coordination.md`.

## Ownership and sequenced deliverables
1. **Director/shared-file owner: acknowledge paths and ownership in coordination file** before editing reserved API/tenant/dashboard files. Design bounded authenticated attachment representation, strict received-bytes vs claimed MIME/extension provenance, budget, format detection, per-tenant metering, existing input/output flow and safe AI gating.
2. Add backward-compatible explicit tenant `auto` vs `off` semantics, preserving stored explicit-Off tenant records and independent input/output actions; allow rule-level exceptions without silently mutating a tenant during requests.
3. Wire detected CSV attachment bytes through existing `csv_formula` and per-stage tenant action evaluation, return all findings and strongest applicable action. Unsupported/malformed/over-budget files must be reported `incomplete`/`unsupported` and never pass as scanned or get forwarded unchecked to the AI when required inspection fails.
4. Director: use existing dashboard controls/Example Picker for actual synthetic attached bytes and distinguish saved action, effective action and `not applicable — no attachment`; no second UI.
5. Atlas can add **non-overlapping** scanner/fixture acceptance tests and documentation, but must not edit reserved paths without acknowledgement.

## Required acceptance matrix
- Zero attachments, one recognized CSV with dangerous and benign cells, quoted mention of a file without bytes, renamed extension/MIME, multiple CSV, CSV + unsupported PDF/DOCX, malformed/encrypted/oversized/ambiguous bytes, CSV BOM and escaped formulas.
- Explicit tenant Off, new-tenant Auto, persisted legacy Off, per-rule Off, per-stage Block/Flag/Allow, two simultaneous findings and strongest action, tenants A/B isolated and authenticated; no unauthenticated upload; metering limits and no raw-content echo.
- Fail-closed on required unchecked attachment and no unsafe AI call; inspect request/output stages independently.
- Focused pytest/browser + **13/13 Tests and 3/3 CodeQL** at implementation SHA; report actual deployed SHA and 15 live verification outcomes after controlled deployment. Never claim unsupported parsers implemented.

**Restrictions:** No new AWS resources, paid services, CI bypass, weakened tests or unilateral changes to Director-reserved paths. Release approval gate removal does not eliminate these safeguards.

items.title: P1: Build trusted device enrollment, key revocation and authenticated lease control plane
items.body:
## Objective
Turn the policy and durable reservation foundations into a real trust boundary. The current policy crate validates signed approvals but does not itself enroll devices, own a trusted registry, expose authenticated endpoints or execute workloads.

## Required work
- Implement an authoritative device enrollment registry with lifecycle states, tenant binding and auditable ownership.
- Store trusted device/admin public keys in a protected registry; implement rotation and revocation with monotonic versions.
- Authenticate every lease acquire/renew/release request and bind it to device, workload, manifest digest, tenant and expiry.
- Add replay protection and clock-skew policy at the authenticated service boundary.
- Protect durable ledger integrity with a keyed MAC or signature whose key is outside the writable ledger directory; design recovery/rotation.
- Add restart, tampering, stale key, revoked device, replay, clock-skew, cross-tenant and concurrent reservation tests.
- Keep execution dispatch and sandboxing out of scope until control-plane authorization is independently verified.

## Acceptance criteria
- Caller-supplied keys cannot establish trust.
- A writer who can modify ledger files cannot recompute valid integrity without the protected key.
- Revoked/un-enrolled devices cannot acquire or renew leases.
- All authorization failures are fail-closed and auditable.
- Threat model and API contract reviewed before any remote execution integration.

items.title: Tenant health monitoring

milestone.title: Later
milestone.description: Unscheduled. Pulled into an R milestone when a customer or a regulation needs it. Holds the open remainder of M0-M2, M6-M9 and MVP 1 (MVP 1 items keep the release:MVP 1 label).

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

Platform observability, as currently planned, is aggregate: OpenTelemetry gives us request rates, error rates and latency percentiles for the whole deployment. That tells us the platform is up. It does not tell us that a 400-bed hospital in Pune has had a broken analyser feed into LabConnect since Tuesday, that another tenant's ABDM consent callbacks have been failing for six hours, or that a third has stopped using the discharge module entirely because a workflow confused their ward clerks.

With a shared-schema multi-tenant deployment, a single tenant can be entirely broken while every platform-wide dashboard stays green — the affected tenant is a small fraction of overall traffic. The failure surfaces as a support ticket, or as a renewal that does not happen. Both are late.

Who is affected: the hospital admin who discovers at month-end that half their OPD encounters never produced an invoice; the pathologist whose critical-result alerts silently stopped delivering because the tenant's WhatsApp Business API template was rejected; the biomedical technician whose FacilityConnect preventive-maintenance schedule stopped generating work orders; the ambulance crew on EmergencyConnect, where degradation is life-critical and a tenant-scoped outage is unacceptable at any duration. Commercially, Customer Success has no leading indicator of churn and no basis for a quarterly service review. Operationally, NABH accreditation expects a hospital to be able to evidence that its clinical information system is functioning and monitored.

Nothing of this exists today. Health is currently "no one has complained yet".

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** platform operations engineer and Customer Success owner
**I want** a per-tenant health model that scores availability, integration health, clinical-workflow completion, data quality and engagement, with tenant-scoped alerting and a health view in AdminConnect
**So that** a degradation confined to one hospital is detected and escalated within minutes rather than discovered by a support ticket or a non-renewal.

### Scope

**In scope**

* Tenant-dimension cardinality on the core OpenTelemetry metrics: request rate, error rate, latency percentiles, database time and queue depth, all labelled by `tenant_id` and product.
* Integration health probes per tenant per integration: ABDM consent callbacks, HPR/HFR lookups, LabConnect analyser feeds, Razorpay/PayU payment callbacks, WhatsApp Business API template delivery, e-invoice submission — each with a last-success timestamp and a configurable staleness threshold.
* Workflow-completion signals derived from domain events: encounters opened versus closed, prescriptions issued versus dispensed, lab orders placed versus reported, work orders raised versus closed, ambulance dispatches versus handovers completed.
* Data-quality signals: patient records without an ABHA link, duplicate-candidate patient pairs awaiting resolution, unpriced billable items, drug entries without a schedule classification.
* A composite tenant health score with named, weighted components and an explicit rule set (not an opaque number) — each component contributing a status of `healthy`, `degraded` or `failing` with the underlying evidence.
* Tenant-scoped alerting with per-tenant thresholds and routing, and a distinct, tighter alerting profile for EmergencyConnect.
* An AdminConnect tenant health view: score, component breakdown, trend, open incidents and the last isolation-verification and backup-verification results.
* A daily `TenantHealthEvaluated` event so Customer Success tooling and the compliance dashboard consume health rather than re-deriving it.

**Out of scope**

* NPS, satisfaction surveys and qualitative feedback capture — a Customer Success story in the AdminConnect epic; this issue provides the telemetry half of tenant health, not the sentiment half.
* Per-tenant rate limiting and quota enforcement — issue #447 (this issue exposes the signals #447 acts on, but does not throttle anything).
* Billing and usage metering for subscription charging — the Subscriptions epic; usage counters are related but have different accuracy and retention requirements.
* Automated remediation — health detects and alerts; it does not restart, scale or roll back.
* Clinical quality indicators such as readmission or infection rates — these belong to the analytics/OLAP product and must be computed on de-identified data, not on the live clinical database.

---

## Recommended Solution

Health is computed by a dedicated `tenanthealth` module in the Go monolith, fed by three sources and evaluated on a schedule.

**Signal ingestion.** (1) OpenTelemetry metrics are already emitted with a `tenant_id` attribute by the tenant-scoped middleware; the module queries the metrics backend for per-tenant rate/error/latency over rolling windows. (2) Domain events on NATS JetStream are consumed by a durable consumer `tenanthealth-signals` subscribed to `hms.*.*.>`, which increments counters in Redis for workflow-pair signals (`EncounterOpened`/`EncounterClosed`, `PrescriptionIssued`/`MedicineDispensed`, `LabOrderPlaced`/`LabResultReady`, `WorkOrderRaised`/`WorkOrderClosed`, `AmbulanceDispatched`/`HandoverCompleted`). (3) Integration probes write a heartbeat row on every successful outbound call.

**Evaluation.** A Temporal schedule runs `EvaluateTenantHealthWorkflow` every 5 minutes per active tenant (fan-out with a per-tenant workflow ID so evaluations cannot overlap). Each component is evaluated by a declarative rule loaded from configuration, so thresholds vary by tenant tier, country profile and facility type rather than being compiled in:

```yaml
- component: lab_result_turnaround
  product: labconnect
  signal: pair_lag_p95(LabOrderPlaced, LabResultReady)
  degraded_when: "> 4h"
  failing_when: "> 12h"
  applies_to: { facility_type: [hospital, standalone_lab] }
```

Data model:

```sql
CREATE TABLE tenant_health_component (
  tenant_id     UUID NOT NULL,
  component     TEXT NOT NULL,
  status        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('healthy','degraded','failing','unknown')),
  value         NUMERIC,
  threshold     NUMERIC,
  evidence      JSONB NOT NULL,     -- counts and window, never PHI
  evaluated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, component)
);

CREATE TABLE tenant_health_score (
  tenant_id     UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  score         NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL CHECK (score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  status        TEXT NOT NULL,
  evaluated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  previous_score NUMERIC(5,2)
);

CREATE TABLE tenant_integration_heartbeat (
  tenant_id     UUID NOT NULL,
  integration   TEXT NOT NULL,      -- abdm_consent | hpr | analyser | razorpay | whatsapp | einvoice
  last_success  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  last_failure  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  failure_streak INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, integration)
);
```

`tenant_health_component` deliberately stores counts and statuses only — the evidence column must never carry patient identifiers, because this table is read by platform operators who have no care relationship. That constraint is asserted by a test in the isolation suite (#32).

API surface (AdminConnect):

* `GET /api/v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/health` — score, components, trend.
* `GET /api/v1/admin/health/tenants?status=failing` — cross-tenant operator view.
* `GET /api/v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/health/integrations`
* `PUT /api/v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/health/thresholds` — per-tenant overrides.
* `GET /api/v1/tenant/health` — the tenant's own view of their health, scoped by RLS, so a hospital admin sees their hospital and nobody else's.

Events: publishes `TenantHealthEvaluated` (every evaluation where status changed) and `TenantHealthDegraded` / `TenantHealthRecovered`, consumed by the alerting router and by Customer Success tooling. Consumes `TenantBackupFailed` (#31) and `IsolationSuiteCompleted` (#32) as components, so the health view is the single place an operator looks.

OpenFGA:

```
type tenant_health
  relations
    define tenant: [tenant]
    define self_viewer: admin from tenant          # hospital admin sees own health only
    define operator_viewer: sre from platform or csm from platform
    define threshold_editor: sre from platform
```

Alert routing distinguishes severity by product: any EmergencyConnect component entering `failing` pages the on-call immediately regardless of tenant tier, because dispatch degradation is life-critical; other products follow the tenant's contracted support tier.

Sequencing: depends on the tenant-scoped middleware emitting `tenant_id` on traces and metrics, on the domain-event catalogue being stable enough that workflow pairs are meaningful, and on AdminConnect's shell for the console view. Should land after the first two or three domain modules publish events, otherwise most components evaluate to `unknown`. Issue #447 consumes these signals.

Risks. (1) *Metric cardinality explosion* — `tenant_id` on every metric multiplies series by tenant count; mitigated by restricting the tenant label to a curated set of ~15 health-relevant metrics rather than all instrumentation, and by aggregating at the collector. (2) *Alert fatigue from a noisy score* — mitigated by requiring two consecutive evaluations in the same non-healthy state before an alert fires, and by hysteresis on recovery. (3) *A new tenant with no traffic looks failing* — mitigated by an explicit `unknown` status and a grace period keyed to the tenant's go-live date, so onboarding does not page anyone. (4) *Health data leaking PHI to operators* — mitigated by the evidence-column constraint above and an isolation-suite assertion.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** an active tenant whose LabConnect analyser feed has published no `LabResultReady` event for 90 minutes against 40 open `LabOrderPlaced` orders, and whose staleness threshold for that integration is 30 minutes
**When** `EvaluateTenantHealthWorkflow` runs
**Then** the `analyser_feed` component is recorded as `failing` with evidence `{open_orders: 40, last_success_minutes: 90}` containing no patient identifiers, the composite score drops, `TenantHealthDegraded` is published, and an alert is routed to that tenant's contracted support channel within 5 minutes of the second consecutive failing evaluation.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** the metrics backend is unreachable and the Redis signal store is intact
**When** the evaluation workflow runs
**Then** the components sourced from metrics are recorded as `unknown` rather than `healthy`, event-derived and heartbeat-derived components are still evaluated, the composite score is suppressed rather than computed from partial data, a `health_evaluation_degraded` alert fires to the platform on-call, and no tenant is falsely reported as healthy or falsely reported as failing.

### Edge Cases

* A tenant is newly provisioned and has not gone live — all components report `unknown` under a go-live grace period; no alerts are raised and the console shows "awaiting first activity" rather than a red score.
* A hospital's genuine overnight quiet period produces zero encounters — the workflow-pair rules use rate-of-change against that tenant's own baseline by hour-of-day, not an absolute floor, so a quiet ICU-only night ward is not flagged.
* A tenant deliberately does not license PharmaConnect — components for unlicensed products are excluded from the score entirely rather than scored as failing.
* Two evaluations for the same tenant are triggered concurrently by a schedule retry — the Temporal workflow ID `health-{tenant_id}` deduplicates and the later run is dropped.
* An integration recovers between evaluations — recovery requires two consecutive healthy evaluations before `TenantHealthRecovered` is published, preventing alert flapping on an intermittent analyser.
* A hospital admin calls `GET /api/v1/tenant/health` — they receive only their own tenant's health; attempting to pass another tenant's id returns `404` and is recorded by the isolation suite as a covered case.

---

## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team's agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team's agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** a degradation affecting a single tenant is detected, scored and alerted without depending on that tenant raising a ticket; the hospital admin can see their own health view, and platform operators can rank all tenants by health.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** support becomes proactive, quarterly service reviews are evidence-based, and Customer Success gains a leading churn indicator.
* **Success metric or validation method:** at least 90% of tenant-scoped incidents in the first quarter are detected by tenant health before a support ticket is raised, measured by comparing alert timestamps against ticket creation; median time from onset to alert under 10 minutes; false-positive alert rate below 5% of alerts raised; zero PHI fields present in `tenant_health_component.evidence`, asserted continuously by the isolation suite.
* **Monitoring period:** 90 days, tracking detection-before-ticket rate, alert precision, evaluation workflow success rate and metrics-series cardinality growth.

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

None — all guardrails apply. This story includes an AdminConnect console view and a tenant-facing health page, so the accessibility and user-journey guardrails are in scope in full, including the loading, empty (`unknown` / pre-go-live) and error states called out in the edge cases.

items.title: content(tutorial): RAG foundations — Part 5/5 — Production RAG
items.body:
## Reader problem and outcome

Turn the series’ teaching application into a concrete production-readiness design covering permissions, document lifecycle, untrusted content, observability, recovery and performance/cost budgets.

**Parent roadmap:** #266  
**Series:** RAG engineering, from first principles to production — Part 5 of 5  
**Format:** tutorial · **Difficulty:** advanced  
**Starting point:** Parts 1–4 of `rag-foundations`; continue the same TypeScript example and source metadata contract

## Scope

- [ ] Build on Parts 2–4 and declare the example deployment assumptions, trust boundaries and threat model. Explain which controls are demonstrated, researched or still required before deployment.
- [ ] Derive tenant/user eligibility from a trusted authenticated principal; enforce it during retrieval and recheck authoritative source permissions before supplying text to the model. Fail closed when authorization state is unavailable or stale.
- [ ] Carry authorization through citations, source endpoints, caches and logs. Include negative cases for cross-tenant access, forged tenant parameters and revoked documents; avoid treating a prompt or caller-supplied filter as access control.
- [ ] Design stable document IDs, versions, idempotent ingestion, deletion/revocation propagation, freshness checks, reconciliation and reindexing. Explain embedding-model migrations and rollback without mixing incompatible vectors.
- [ ] Treat retrieved documents as untrusted data. Demonstrate prompt-injection and poisoned-source scenarios, isolate privileged tools/secrets, and explain the limits of prompt-based mitigations.
- [ ] Define useful telemetry for ingestion, retrieval and generation: source/version IDs, stage timing, failures, quality signals and resource/token use. Redact sensitive data and specify retention; avoid indiscriminate document/prompt logging.
- [ ] Walk through model timeout, empty retrieval, permission outage, stale index, partial update and restore/rebuild scenarios. Specify bounded retries, graceful degradation, backpressure and an operator recovery/rollback checklist.
- [ ] Set workload-specific latency, context and cost budgets. Explain caching with tenant/permission/version-aware keys and invalidation. Report hardware, versions, load and measured results only when actually exercised.

## Duplication boundary

Link to `small-rag-pgvector-qdrant-decision` for database selection and detailed storage trade-offs, and to Part 4 for quality evaluation. This installment owns application-wide trust and lifecycle responsibilities. It is not a vendor leaderboard, a claim of audited security or a request to deploy a backend for Daily AI Pulse.

Before drafting, inventory current main, open content PRs and editorial ledgers. Confirm the distinct reader outcome against the four existing guides named in #266.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An architecture/trust-boundary diagram and concise runbook show where authorization, freshness, failure handling and recovery are enforced.
- [ ] Reproducible negative scenarios cover forbidden/revoked sources, untrusted document instructions and dependency outages; mock checks are explicitly separated from real integration/load/recovery tests.
- [ ] Performance/cost claims match disclosed measurements or remain clearly labeled planning estimates. Remaining deployment prerequisites and limitations are concrete.

## Editorial and delivery requirements

- [ ] Read current repository instructions, Tools & Guides contracts, shared editorial voice v2, content/schema and applicable translation/publication rules before authoring.
- [ ] Use beginner-friendly explanations and the publication’s independent, factual, no-nonsense voice; explain concepts before code and keep examples coherent across the series.
- [ ] Set the existing series metadata exactly:

```yaml
series:
  id: rag-foundations
  title: RAG engineering, from first principles to production
  part: 5
```

- [ ] Cite current primary documentation; record source date/version, evidence type and limitations in the guide’s ledger. Distinguish documentation research, mock checks, illustrative output and actually executed tests; never invent results or verification.
- [ ] Prepare an original WebP editorial cover under current visual/illustration contracts, separate from precise instructional diagrams. Inspect the final artwork and verify binary-safe commit/read-back with evidence in its ledger; include accessible descriptions.
- [ ] Add relevant links to published earlier parts and existing guides using current related-reading/series conventions. Do not surface unpublished destinations.
- [ ] Keep copyable examples in the tutorial and changes proportionate to the publication; no new category, sample-app framework, permanent per-article CI suite or hosted backend is requested.
- [ ] Open one focused content PR; run current required source, content, asset and build validation at its final head and report actual execution limits.
- [ ] Follow current English/French review requirements. Human editorial review and merge approval remain the publication boundary.

**Planning issue:** creation of this issue does not authorize automatic publication or deployment.

items.title: [Feature]: APY-03 — Add secure real-time Apple Pay Shortcut ingestion
items.body:
### Problem / proposed capability

Add a secure API ingestion path suitable for an iOS Shortcuts Wallet transaction automation. Apple Pay -> Wallet automation -> iOS Shortcut -> shared Finance Tracker ingestion -> **canonical transaction created immediately**. A 19:40 payment must appear at ingestion and immediately affect expenses/income, Budget and reporting; do not wait for CAL. No native iOS app is required.

### Requirements

- Reuse the APY service and reviewed APY-01 contract; do not create independent duplicate logic or misuse a candidate signature as event identity.
- Use a dedicated narrowly scoped Shortcut authentication mechanism; do not give the iPhone broader service credentials or reuse privileged database/service secrets. Define safe issuance/storage/rotation/revocation and missing/invalid credential behavior. Never log tokens, headers or secrets.
- Strictly validate and bound fields, apply an appropriate rate limit and retry contract, and safely resolve payment source. Ambiguous/missing card identity must not silently select sources[0].
- Capture merchant, exact amount/currency and safe stable source identity where actually available. If the device has no stable event ID, implement the reviewed replay-key contract without collapsing two genuine same-value purchases.
- Accept/preserve optional occurred_at with timezone semantics; set observed_at server-side. No fabricated purchase time from receipt time; support date-only input. Preserve transaction_date and charge_date independence.
- Create a live canonical transaction immediately or reconcile a confidently existing purchase under the shared contract. awaiting_confirmation is metadata and must never suppress normal financial totals. Follow the explicit ambiguous-review contract, not approval for every ordinary transaction.
- Return useful idempotent results to Shortcuts for create/replay/reconcile/review/conflict/error, with stable safe identifiers and no leaked secrets.
- Produce owner-facing iOS Shortcut setup instructions, allowed payload examples, local/test validation, duplicate retry handling and safe troubleshooting. Do not alter production credentials/configuration during implementation without separate authorization.

### Actual device capability validation

Do **not** assume Wallet automation exposes every desired property (stable event ID, precise time, currency, merchant or physical-card identifier). During implementation verify the owner's actual iPhone/iOS/card automation inputs and limitations. Separately record (1) documented Apple behavior and sources, (2) server fixture assumptions, and (3) actual owner iPhone observations. If required data cannot be obtained safely, record the exact supported subset/blocker rather than fabricate it or claim device verification.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Secure narrowly scoped, validated and rate-limited ingestion uses the shared service.
- [x] Supported real-time input creates a visible and financially active canonical row immediately, without CAL or routine user approval.
- [x] Exact same observation replay is idempotent; separate equal-value purchases remain possible.
- [ ] Payment source, merchant, money/currency and identity follow the contract and actual supported device data.
- [x] Optional occurred_at is retained, observed_at is server-set and date-only input remains supported.
- [x] Awaiting-confirmation metadata does not change Budget/report eligibility.
- [x] Invalid credentials/input, unsafe card mapping and retries fail safely without secret logging or partial money effects.
- [x] Setup instructions and useful Shortcut responses are documented.
- [x] Server tests, documented Apple capability and actual owner iPhone acceptance are explicitly distinguished; no unperformed device check is claimed.

Server acceptance boxes above refer to automated HTTP/disposable-database evidence, not a verified Wallet capture. Owner runtime evidence: **iPhone 17 Pro Max / iOS 27.0 / English Shortcuts**, specific-card Apps > Wallet trigger, Transaction Magic Variable with exactly Card or Pass, Merchant, Amount, Name. One real contactless automation executed. Merchant and Name each appended to Notes as inline `Israel Post` for this purchase only. Amount serialized in Notes as `Attachment.txt`, whose content was `₪4.00`; Card or Pass also serialized as `Attachment.txt`, whose content was the selected Wallet display label (not retained here). **Neither attachment serialization establishes the original native type or proves raw-string output.** Native Amount/Card or Pass types and final explicit text conversion remain Pending. No separate date/time/offset/currency/event-ID/provider field was exposed. No HTTP POST/E2E or owner acceptance is claimed.

Preferred final mapping is one credential/source bound server-side to one payment source; normal requests omit Card or Pass/payment_method. Strict text normalization recognizes the verified ILS representation without FX or floating-point identity, and Merchant wins over Name with fallback only when empty/unavailable. The local capture-date fallback, null occurred_at/provider_reference and invocation UUID replay contract are preserved. Actual on-device plain JSON and HTTP/E2E acceptance remain Pending.

### Repository context / relationships

Parent: [APY parent #78](https://github.com/OzAvrahami/finance-tracker/issues/78). Follow its verified repository inventory, non-unique candidate/identity rules, immediate-accounting requirement and scope boundaries. Re-inspect current implementations before executing this child. Notifications #52 and Multi-user #63 are contextual only, not blockers; preserve their issues and relationships. Bank-balance #45 and tenant-ingestion #69 retain their separate ownership.

Blocked by: [APY-02 (#80)](https://github.com/OzAvrahami/finance-tracker/issues/80). These must be native GitHub dependencies as well as readable references.

### Project / triage

Finance Tracker Project: **Verify / P1 — High** after implementation/local verification. Labels: `feature`, `backend`, `testing`; no milestone or assignee. Owner acceptance remains Pending.

### Release / Version gate - APY-03 implementation

- Release impact: **Yes** - opt-in secure Apple source adapter.
- SemVer impact: **Minor** - backward-compatible capability within APY.
- Candidate release: **proposed v1.4.0**, subject to APY-06 revalidation.
- Grouping / included release candidate: **parent #78 / #79-84 (APY-01-06)**.
- CHANGELOG status: **Updated under Unreleased**, #81/APY-03 entry; no 1.4.0 section.
- Version-bump status: **Deferred to APY-06** coordinated preparation; all seven fields remain **1.3.1**.
- Publication status: **Out of scope**.
- Owner verification / acceptance status: **Pending**. Real contactless probe is recorded; native typed-value coercion, Shortcut HTTP capture and Finance Tracker E2E remain pending.
- Production migration/deployment/configuration: **Not performed; separately authorized**. Migration 036 in Git is not evidence of production application.

### Implementation authorization / boundaries

The owner authorized APY-03 server implementation and disposable local verification, superseding the original issue-creation-only restriction. No production migration/deployment/configuration/credential/source registration, commit, push, version bump, tagging or publication occurred. APY-04/#82 and APY-05 are not started. Owner picker and real contactless Notes evidence are recorded; final text coercion, HTTP/E2E capture and owner acceptance remain Pending. See the implementation/evidence handoff below and local `docs/APY_03_APPLE_PAY_SHORTCUT.md` for the capability probe and intended protocol.

Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OzAvrahami/finance-tracker/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and the [canonical development standard](https://github.com/OzAvrahami/finance-tracker/blob/main/docs/github-development-standard.md). Keep implementation, automated verification, owner acceptance, coordinated preparation, owner commit/push, deployment, annotated tag and GitHub Release publication distinct. A tag alone is not a published release.

items.title: [Agent 1/8] Platform Foundation, AWS EC2 Deployment, Authentication & Shared Contracts
items.body:
## Mission
Build the secure, deployable foundation for the **complete SomaLoom educational content platform**. All other agents depend on your initial repository structure and interface conventions. Deployment target: **AWS EC2 + Docker Compose**, with Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL/pgvector, Redis, HTTPS and durable storage.

## Ownership / boundaries
- **Own:** repository bootstrap and root config; `infra/**`, `docker/**`, `contracts/**`, `apps/api/app/core/**`, `apps/api/app/auth/**`, `db/migrations/**`, deployment workflows and project documentation.
- Create the minimal `apps/web`, `apps/api`, `services` workspace structure without implementing other agents' features.
- **Do not** write the other agents' ingestion, parsing, retrieval, authoring, assessment, or web UI implementations.

## Implementation guide
1. **Bootstrap first**: initialize `main` with a coherent monorepo, README, .gitignore, env examples, formatting/linting/tests, Docker Compose, shared type/schema conventions. Commit this early so seven feature branches can start.
2. Establish **versioned contracts** (OpenAPI + JSON Schema/Pydantic): `Resource`, `ResourceVersion`, `Extraction`, `ContentBlock`, `VisualAsset`, `Equation`, `CurriculumOutcome`, `EvidenceLink`, `GenerationJob`, `GeneratedDocument`, `Export`. Identifiers: UUIDs; UTC timestamps; tenant/school ID; source/license/provenance fields. Publish placeholder endpoints and working mock fixtures.
3. FastAPI `/api/v1` app: standardized responses/errors, typed validation, `/health`, `/ready`, OpenAPI, request IDs, pagination, job-status convention; auth with secure password hashing and roles `platform_admin`, `school_admin`, `teacher`, `reviewer`. All school-owned records must enforce tenant isolation server-side.
4. PostgreSQL + `pgvector`, Redis queue, transactional migrations, audit events, object/file abstraction backed by encrypted EBS for MVP; introduce S3-compatible storage interface for migration/backup. Never keep documents only in ephemeral containers.
5. Configure EC2 deployment: Docker Compose services for nginx/TLS, web, API, worker, Postgres, Redis; restrictive security groups (public 80/443 only; SSH restricted or Session Manager), non-root containers, secrets outside Git, IAM least privilege, HTTPS, secure headers, health/restart policy.
6. CI: test/lint/build on PR; staging deploy, backup/restore scripts, safe migrations, rollback instructions, logs/metrics, disk/capacity alerts, rate limits. Capture AWS and domain prerequisites in README; never commit keys.

## Shared API/data contract for all agents
- REST prefix `/api/v1`; authenticated operations; stable pagination `{items, page, page_size, total}`; async jobs `{id,status,progress,error,created_at,finished_at}`.
- Central schema reference in `contracts/`; feature agents own implementations in their own directories, **not** the contract source. Contract changes need a PR or documented agreement.
- DB migration ownership stays here: feature agents submit additive migration specs in `db/proposals/agent-N-*.sql` or ORM model proposals, which you integrate; no competing edits to migration head.
- Document pipeline: `Resource -> Extraction -> Indexed Evidence -> Generation -> Review -> Export`. Every object must retain tenant and provenance information.
- Branch convention: `agent/01-platform` etc; one PR per workstream to `main`; never force push another agent's branch. Do not publish production credentials or enable shell-access endpoints.

## Definition of done — final product
- [ ] One-command reproducible local setup; working authenticated web/API integration.
- [ ] EC2 HTTPS deployment, correct service lifecycle, database migrations and environment documentation.
- [ ] Tenant/role authorization tested including denial of cross-school access.
- [ ] Upload and generation job status can be tracked through common contracts.
- [ ] Working encrypted durable data storage and verified off-instance backup **and restore**.
- [ ] CI passes tests, secrets checks and deployment health tests; clear observability, recovery and rollback runbook.
- [ ] No open critical/high security issues at public launch.

## 48-hour checkpoint (26–28 October 2026)
**First 2 hours:** bootstrap commit + contracts + env examples; unblock agents. **By beta:** EC2 reachable behind HTTPS, basic authentication, Postgres/Redis, worker and app health checks. Hardening/scale work remains tracked here until final acceptance.

## Coordination
Act as the integration owner. Review contract-changing PRs quickly; publish stable mock payloads. Agent 8 owns the user-facing UI and end-to-end acceptance; you own reliable deployment and security. Related: agents 2–8.

Deliver MOTERVA Mission Treasury by the organizer's participant-Slack deadline **2026-11-15 11:59 PM PST**. Real Airwallex *sandbox*, Metal *testnet*, operational simulations clearly labeled; product finance-first, not merely cinematic 3D.

## Prize-led outcomes
- $30k Founder: real target buyer, clear economics, coherent reusable product, excellent UX.
- $20k Judges: depth of banking decisions, controls, independent financial provider evidence and measured reliability.
- $15k Metal: mandate-controlled agentic testnet payment genuinely influences financial plan plus Airwallex sandbox.
- $15k Visa: only if legitimate sponsor tooling and eligibility confirmed; no speculative qualification.

## Release gates
1. Actual sandbox/testnet transaction identifiers and independent status checks; never confuse SUBMITTED and SETTLED.
2. Deterministic authorization, concurrent commitment safety, revision-bound approvals, restart replay, no blind retry.
3. Agent re-plans when material financial context changes; a refusal/no-purchase scenario works.
4. Approved design references, licensed 3D assets, meaningful 3D-state synchronization and complete mobile/keyboard/2D support.
5. Reproducible fault-injection suite, benchmark, buyer positioning, honest simulated-versus-real evidence, working app and video under five minutes.

## Engineering contract
Read draft PR #1 (`docs/`, `AGENTS.md`, PR template), complete one issue per scoped PR, record SHA/test outputs/screenshots and review before merge. **Public repository:** no credentials, signing keys, sensitive accounts or private documents.

## Timing
Finish core provider work first, freeze risky features on Nov 13, reserve Nov 14–15 for verified replay/video/submission. Slack organizer confirmation supersedes older dates on the public landing page; recheck dashboard before final submission.

This epic is *planning*, not evidence of implementation. No code, real provider transactions, visual approvals, or tests verified merely because these issues exist.

- WIP limit: two implementation PRs at most when files overlap; one owner of shared money/approval schema. Freeze new work if the golden flow breaks.
