items.body:
**Stable key:** SC-06A
**Owner role:** Agent and research (shared-contracts maintainer); affected producer and consumer domain owners review. Named assignee/reviewer must be recorded at kickoff.
**Priority:** P0 — Blocks interoperable v1 contracts and consumer integration.
**Required for v1:** Yes. **Implementation state:** Planned.

## Current evidence
Live inspection 2026-10-10: main is c4caaccc2ea63b273eeac17ed89af8ac64f6bbde. [README](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/blob/c4caaccc2ea63b273eeac17ed89af8ac64f6bbde/README.md), [ownership](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/blob/c4caaccc2ea63b273eeac17ed89af8ac64f6bbde/docs/architecture/OWNERSHIP.md), [acceptance view](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/blob/c4caaccc2ea63b273eeac17ed89af8ac64f6bbde/docs/architecture/ACCEPTANCE.md), and [catalog](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/blob/c4caaccc2ea63b273eeac17ed89af8ac64f6bbde/docs/contract-catalog.md) are the entire tracked baseline. No AGENTS.md, executable schemas, package manifest, generated types, fixtures or CI exist. #1 is the original WP01 work package; merged documentation PR #2 establishes no implementation evidence.

Catalog defines UsageEvent prose and financial lifecycle distinctions. Current creative metering and harness durable observations exist locally, while EI calls its metering prompts unaccepted; finance owner agreement remains necessary.

## Scope / non-goals
For each named contract, deliver a versioned canonical JSON Schema, generated ESM-compatible TypeScript declaration, runtime validation helper with typed errors, positive and negative fixtures, and explicit required/optional/null/unknown/enum semantics. Keep structural validation separate from context checks supplied by authenticated domain owners. No validator creates authority or performs provider I/O. All billable modules emit UsageEvent observations; cost-intelligence owns ingestion/reconciliation, and harness owns transport traces. Define logical_operation_id, provider_attempt_id, transport_attempt_id, billable_attempt_id, usage_event_id and source observation identity with explicit mapping and no universal retry equivalence.

This repository owns interfaces, compatibility, generated types and validation only. Application behavior, authentication/approval authority, print composition, ledger/budget execution, provider adapters and UX remain downstream. This issue authorizes no provider charges.

## Acceptance IDs and expected outcome
Local requirement namespace: **SC-06.USAGE**; preserve existing global **CON-01, CON-02, CON-03** where applicable, without renumbering or treating structural validation as end-to-end verification. [Master definitions and evidence](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/integration-evals/blob/main/planning/acceptance-checklist.md) remain authoritative.
- [ ] SC-06.USAGE.1: Distinguish one logical operation, each provider execution, transport retry, separately billed attempt and duplicate observation. Provider adapters declare whether a retry reuses provider/idempotency identity or starts a new potentially billable attempt.
- [ ] SC-06.USAGE.2: Represent usage completeness and valuation separately: unknown/incomplete/complete observations; unknown/estimated/provider-confirmed valuation; never encode unknown as zero. Include units, model/provider, currency/precision, rate-card and policy versions, environment/billing mode, outcome and provider ID when available.
- [ ] SC-06.USAGE.3: Define duplicate/redelivery/correction identity, linked superseding observations and reconciliation references without implementing deduplication or posting. Estimated and confirmed observations must be joinable without another charge.
- [ ] SC-06.USAGE.4: Fixtures: two billed attempts under one logical operation remain distinct; duplicate observation is the same observation; transport retry may retain execution identity; timeout with unknown usage is retained; observed zero is explicitly measured; live/sandbox/simulated do not collapse. Preserve FIN-01/02/03/04/05/07 and BUD-03.

## Approach and migration implications
Use SC-02 canonical JSON Schema and generated ESM/TypeScript bindings with pure validators. Inspect existing downstream local shapes and fixtures at immutable revisions, record differences, and agree adapters with one producer and one consumer before removing any local type. Never silently rename semantics or claim a local prototype is canonical. Pin schema version, shared-contracts source SHA/package version and consumer revisions together; preserve old-version tests per SC-03.

## Relationships
**Parent:** #1 (WP01 / SC-EPIC).
**Blocked by:** #7 (SC-04), #8 (SC-11), #9 (SC-08A)
**Blocks:** #3 (SC-12 release gate) and completion of #1; downstream handoffs below depend on accepted contracts, not on closure of this tracking epic.
**Related:** [cost-intelligence #1](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/cost-intelligence/issues/1); [agent-harness #14](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/issues/14); [creative-engine #5](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/creative-engine/issues/5); [event-intelligence #4](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/4)

## Executable validation
These are required implementation commands established in SC-02/SC-09; they are not present or claimed run today. Run offline from a clean checkout, with no provider credentials.

```sh
npm ci
npm run contracts:check -- --contract UsageEvent
npm run contracts:fixtures -- --contract UsageEvent
npm run contracts:compat
```

Record exact commands, Node/package versions, exit codes and tested schema/consumer SHAs. Invalid fixtures must fail with the asserted typed code/path; positive and supported-old-version fixtures must pass.

## Required evidence for closure
Link merged implementation revision, catalog entry, canonical schema/types/helper (or policy/tooling artifacts for a foundation issue), fixture manifest with expected results, sanitized CI logs, generation-drift result and affected producer/consumer review. Include the migration/pin record and unresolved limitations. No unchecked acceptance item, unreviewed owner decision or missing dependency evidence may be treated as complete.

items.title: Tracking: high-throughput Rust ingestion with a three-replica WAL
items.body:
## Problem

Object-store WAL writes can put remote request latency and small-object overhead on the ingestion ACK path. A memory-only WAL removes that cost but cannot preserve acknowledged writes across process or node loss. We want an optional, high-throughput durable ingestion path implemented in Rust within lance-context, with minimal changes to Lance OSS.

This issue tracks incremental implementation and validation. Explicit Rust service paths now exist for durable append and mutable turn ingestion. They remain opt-in; workload-specific production readiness and large-scale qualification are still required.

## Architecture and current visibility contract

The mutable-turn service path now separates immutable bodies from current narrow
annotations. The diagram shows that path for one shard; the lower-level immutable
append API has a different ACK/visibility contract, described below.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    I["Ingress router: forward Arrow bytes"] --> O["Shard owner: ordered apply and point reads"]
    O -->|"Submit original request identity and payload"| L
    subgraph G["One Raft group: three durable replicas"]
        L["Leader + persistent WAL"] --> F1["Follower + persistent WAL"]
        L --> F2["Follower + persistent WAL"]
    end
    L -->|"Quorum-committed records"| O
    O --> S["Bounded active / frozen staging"]
    S -->|"Frozen batch"| P["Fenced Lance publisher"]
    P --> B["Blob: body and narrow-annotation snapshots"]
    B -->|"Compatible selected base"| O
    O -->|"Success after durable quorum and applied visibility"| I
```

1. **Explicit shard placement.** The current mutable-turn path hashes the turn ID
   within its tenant/table scope to a configured bucket and owner. Forwarding
   ingresses share the validated route map and do not keep independent staging
   views. Each physical annotation shard has its own body/narrow table pair and
   publication/recovery progress. The immutable append contract retains its
   session-key placement. Automatic session placement, shard migration and
   rebalancing are not supplied by these explicit shard APIs.
2. **Durable and visible mutation ACKs.** Three replicas persist the log on
   independent durable storage. A successful turn mutation requires majority
   persistence and ordered application to the owner's queryable state. A raw WAL
   append receipt alone is not that success. Raft supplies election, ordering and
   committed-prefix safety; it does not publish Lance manifests. The storage
   fault model tolerates one replica's loss, not loss of a durable quorum.
3. **Field updates and immediate point reads.** Patches preserve unspecified
   fields; status/score have explicit keep/set/clear operations, and labels have
   set addition/removal. Applications merge against the ordered current value.
   Point reads resolve active, frozen, then the compatible Lance base, projecting
   narrow columns only and never scanning the WAL suffix. Owner fencing and
   recovery barriers protect cross-ingress reads. Materialized status filters
   currently have a different freshness contract: they do not include active or
   frozen updates. CAS and cross-shard transactions are not implemented here.
4. **Batch publication without losing later updates.** Freeze one bounded
   generation at a source cut while later updates enter a new active generation.
   Existing annotation rows use native narrow-column rewrites; newly ingested
   bodies are appended separately and bound to the selected annotation snapshot.
   Confirm the exact fenced publication before installing its base and retiring
   only its frozen generation. Never delete active records by turn ID when an
   older batch finishes. Compaction is separate bounded maintenance, not a
   per-update rewrite of the immutable body.
5. **Recovery, exact retry and reclamation.** Recovery uses the selected Lance
   state, persisted request outcomes and the required WAL suffix. Retained exact
   producer/sequence retries return their original result; an unknown outcome
   requires the same identity and bytes, not a newly identified mutation. A
   producer has at most one unresolved request, and the bounded latest-result
   contract does not retain arbitrary historical retries. Unknown publication
   results are reconciled against the original publication. Source GC also
   respects readers, recovery and replica/snapshot dependencies; a materialized
   cut alone does not permit deleting every preceding log record.
6. **Bounded resources and measured copying.** Staging, caches, payloads, native
   workspaces, disk admission and replication queues have explicit budgets;
   pressure must leave publication and reclamation able to make progress.
   Replicas keep Arrow payloads opaque and ingress forwarding shares byte
   buffers. The current owner still validates by decoding on preparation and
   decodes again during ordered apply; this is not end-to-end zero-copy.
   Framing, integrity checks, native storage and kernel I/O also need measurement.

The existing immutable append API remains separate: its durable WAL ACK can
precede Lance visibility. Its readers and publication checkpoints follow that
binding's contract. Neither this issue nor an annotation-owner configuration
silently changes an existing immutable binding's semantics.

The implementation uses Rust raft-rs and raft-engine with Lance's existing
publication APIs. Useful references remain Flink's checkpoint/replay and bounded
flow control, and Apache Fluss's bucket ownership, batched replication and
asynchronous lake publication. Fluss uses leader/follower replication with ISR;
this design does not imply that Fluss uses Raft. Independent shard publication
does not create a global WAL position or a cross-shard atomic snapshot.


## Incremental delivery

Use small PRs with `Refs #378` in their descriptions. Keep this tracking issue open across individual implementation PRs; merge each only after its checks pass.

- [x] Lance 13 dependency/API upgrade: #374.
- [x] Rust Arrow IPC allocation/buffer-sharing and durable disk experiment tools: #375.
- [x] Stable session placement and scoped receipts: #376.
- [x] Shared node-wide proposal admission: #377.
- [x] Configurable maintenance headroom and pressure regressions: #379.
- [x] Validated Arrow IPC decoding with shared payload ownership: #380.
- [x] Shared opaque record envelopes and bounded payload validation: #381.
- [x] Move owned HTTP rollout payloads into core records without a conversion copy: #382.
- [x] Honor registered rollout dataset locations on cold open, metadata and deletion: #383.
- [x] Immutable ingestion contracts shared by ingress and materializers: #384.
- [x] Prevent concurrent dataset creation from overwriting committed data: #385.
- [x] Shared Arrow schema fingerprints for ingress and materializers: #386.
- [x] Guarded Rust experiment process runner and optional-feature CI: #388.
- [x] Read-only Rust process and cgroup resource observation: #389.
- [x] Optional process-owned TCP socket observation, with descriptor ownership, namespace and connection-state tests: #438.
- [x] Bounded vectored frame writes over shared payloads: #393.
- [x] Measure WAL component disk footprint from actual files: #397.
- [x] Isolate physical log read caches by engine lifetime, including rewrite reads: #398.
- [x] Shared durable Raft log storage, sync failure fencing and recovery contracts: #399.
- [x] Replicated append, durable quorum ACK, retry deduplication and leader failover: #400.
- [x] Local durable client journal, shared group commit and recovery tests: #401.
- [x] Reclaim obsolete client journal rewrite bytes before physical admission fences, with synchronized replacement, failure fencing and SIGKILL recovery: #430.
- [x] Durable local Raft checkpoint storage boundary: #402 (application snapshots and remote transfer remain separate work).
- [x] Atomic received Raft snapshot storage: #403.
- [x] Application checkpoint files, bounded transfer and retained-replica recovery: #404 (including interrupted transfer and full process restart tests).
- [x] Durable canonical table bindings and publisher ownership epochs: #405 (external Lance commit fencing remains separate work).
- [x] Bounded quorum queries for publisher bindings, accepted pages and producer tails: #406.
- [x] Immutable publication plans, fixed transaction targets and independent source-group selections retained across takeover and snapshots: #407 (source pins and external commits remain separate work).
- [x] Catalog quorum attestations and durable source-quorum pins across takeover, snapshot transfer and full process restart: #409 (source release and external publication remain separate work).
- [x] Immutable prepared Lance fragment descriptors, exact retries and real-file recovery across publisher takeover and full process restart: #410 (manifest authority and source retirement remain separate work).
- [x] Select immutable staged Lance manifests through the catalog quorum, with exact head reservations and recovery after lost replies, owner takeover and full process restart: #412 (outcome advancement and source retirement remain separate work).
- [x] Persist durable publication outcomes from the exact catalog-selected manifest, recovering identical confirmations across takeover and full process restart: #414 (source closure and retirement remain separate work).
- [x] Close source pins with durable publication fences, reject delayed repins and preserve exact closure retries across snapshots and restart: #415 (payload retirement and physical reclamation remain separate work).
- [x] Retire closed source payloads from new checkpoints while retaining original retry receipts and retirement boundaries across restart: #416 (physical reclamation and catalog advancement remain separate work).
- [x] Use optimized SHA-256 for opaque WAL payload validation while preserving persisted digests and record compatibility: #417.
- [x] Opt-in Lance object-store I/O metrics through the existing recorder, with core builds supported when metrics are disabled: #421.
- [x] Source-group closure attestations after a quorum read, with separate signing keys and checkpoint/restart recovery: #423 (catalog advancement and physical reclamation remain separate work).
- [x] Advance catalog source cursors only after every selected source attests durable closure, preserving exact retries and managed Lance recovery: #424 (physical reclamation remains separate work).
- [x] Bounded collection of obsolete application snapshot files, preserving installed recovery images and captured readers across shared groups: #426 (native log reclamation and maintenance scheduling remain separate work).
- [x] Explicit physical log segment reclamation with node-wide sync barriers and failure fencing: #427 (maintenance scheduling and replica replacement remain separate work).
- [x] Bounded managed-manifest history retirement with protected publication dependencies and explicit retired-retry boundaries: #428 (metadata only; object deletion and production reader integration remain separate work).
- [ ] Online replica replacement, durable-volume-loss recovery and operational recovery integration.
- [x] Lance materialization, fenced publication and durable source checkpoints: #450, building on the catalog/source protocols above. Sustained capacity remains under qualification.
- [x] Real Lance transaction-proof cleanup, protected version floors and delayed fixed-target commit regressions: #408 (coordinated GC remains separate work).
- [ ] Safe logical retirement and physical reclamation under concurrent activity.
- [x] Bounded durable replica workers with shared node credits, cancellation ownership, responsive cached status and joined shutdown: #441 (network transport, snapshot transfer and maintenance integration remain separate work).
- [ ] Producer batch sizing and end-to-end throughput/latency qualification with unchanged correctness gates.
- [x] Bounded reusable producer slots with durable generation fencing, exact-tail close, and reuse only after signed source retirement: #434 (optional for fresh groups; administrative authorization, SDK integration and sustained churn qualification remain separate work).
- [ ] Replica-pressure coordination, producer-state lifecycle and bounded steady-state operation.
- [x] Reusable Lance manifest reader/writer adapter over catalog quorum reads and fixed-target durable reservations: #439 (production transport and writer migration remain separate work).
- [x] Independent managed Lance readers with scoped catalog resolution and rejected write attempts: #440
- [ ] Production integration: visibility API, ownership/catalog integration, authentication and migration/rollback documentation.

- [x] Release engine directory locks explicitly at final owner shutdown, with duplicated-descriptor and pre-exec inheritance regressions: #465.
- [x] Distribute one pinned table publication across bounded authenticated Rust preparer services, keeping complete aggregation and manifest authority with one fenced publisher: #466. Independent process recovery has passed; Kubernetes scaling and sustained throughput remain under qualification.

## Validation before enabling the path

- Verify acknowledged records after leader crashes, follower lag, snapshot transfer interruption and full process restarts using real Rust processes and durable storage.
- Exercise ambiguous replies, stale publishers, concurrent manifest commits and retries; verify complete Lance payloads and source positions after recovery.
- Run sustained ingestion through publication and repeated reclamation, including controlled publication pauses. Report ACK latency, published throughput, backlog, RSS, allocated disk space and physical write amplification separately.
- Compare batching, serialization/deserialization, shared-buffer ownership, bounded parallel reads and replication-group placement using reproducible workloads. Short component benchmarks are not evidence of sustained end-to-end throughput.
- Publish only synthetic, portable workloads and sanitized results. Do not include private deployment identifiers, storage locations, identity configuration, business workloads or raw operational artifacts.

Related: #333 tracks maintenance scheduling in the existing system; this issue focuses on the optional durable ingestion path and its correctness/performance contract.



## References

- [Flink state backends and incremental checkpoints](https://nightlies.apache.org/flink/flink-docs-release-2.3/docs/ops/state/state_backends/).
- [Flink network stack and credit-based flow control](https://flink.apache.org/2019/06/05/a-deep-dive-into-flinks-network-stack/) (historical design explanation).
- [Fluss LogTablet replication and log lifecycle](https://github.com/apache/fluss/blob/0529ab053a92d7ac2a3c6fa611e6369f50eee57b/fluss-server/src/main/java/org/apache/fluss/server/log/LogTablet.java) and [Lance lake connector documentation](https://github.com/apache/fluss/blob/0529ab053a92d7ac2a3c6fa611e6369f50eee57b/website/docs/streaming-lakehouse/datalake-formats/lance.md), pinned to the researched revision.
- [x] Authenticated bounded TLS peer transport shared across Raft groups, with stalled-follower isolation and real three-process crash/recovery qualification: #442 (snapshot transfer, disk admission and service integration remain follow-up work).
- [x] Durable runtime checkpoint/snapshot installation and physical-maintenance transitions, with captured image ownership and durable completion tests: #443 (network image transfer and node-wide disk admission remain follow-up work).
- [x] Reserved snapshot completion lane with cancellation and saturated-control regression coverage: #444.
- [x] Bounded authenticated TLS snapshot transfer with interrupted-receive and full-restart process coverage: #446.
- [x] Shared node disk admission for logs, producer state, snapshots and reclamation, with restart coverage: #447.
- [x] Bounded TLS client RPCs with shared physical connection pools and real-process recovery: #448.
- [x] Rollout ingestion with shared memory admission, session buckets and durable receipts: #449.
- [x] Recoverable Lance file preparation, fixed-version publication and source retirement: #450.
- [x] Independent WAL node service, automatic maintenance and six-process restart qualification: #451.
- [x] Bounded HTTP gateway and journaled Rust producers with exact-retry and Lance recovery qualification: #453.
- [x] Add bounded materializer workers and independent managed readers (#455).

- [x] #457 — Idempotent managed rollout bootstrap with persisted genesis identity and crash recovery.

- [x] Reconnect read-only RPCs after a reused pooled TLS stream disconnects, preserving the original deadline and admission credits: #459. Mutating requests still require explicit original-identity reconciliation.
- [x] Local runtime admission observations with separate request/byte rejection counters and real-quorum pressure regressions: #460.

- [x] Expose local runtime request/byte admission observations through node diagnostics without changing readiness: #461.

- [ ] Qualify a single managed table with multiple independent session producers, including full per-producer payload scans and an aggregate table row-count check.
- [x] Parallel file preparation across workers for one table, with one fenced publisher aggregating a complete bounded set of fragment descriptors: #466. Scaling and sustained capacity remain under qualification.

- [ ] Handle and qualify larger inline payloads, including the 40/120 MiB cases in #222. The current replicated-record limit is 8 MiB; raising a workload size alone does not cover peer framing, bounded memory, journal/snapshot recovery, or materialization.

- [x] Compose bootstrap, authenticated ingress, materializer worker and managed-reader roles into a Rust application with executable recovery coverage: #462. Dynamic registry discovery and sustained scaling remain separate work.

- [x] Expose bounded cumulative materializer phase timing and outcome counters, with documented overlapping-duration semantics: #463. Instrumentation only; no throughput improvement claimed.

- [x] Add opt-in bounded streaming file preparation within one worker, preserving complete descriptor aggregation and cancellation ownership: #464. Default off; distributed same-table preparation and performance qualification remain separate work.

- [x] Add opt-in replica spreading for pinned WAL source reads, preserving exact source validation and all-voter fallback: #468. Recovery and single-reachable-replica tests pass; controlled throughput comparison is pending, default remains first voter.
- [x] Overlap bounded replication with leader persistence (default off; no throughput claim): #469

- [x] Reuse verified uncompressed engine read blocks to remove one allocation and copy on cache misses: #470. Local durability and recovery checks pass; end-to-end performance qualification remains separate.

- [x] Return already committed WAL fetches before unrelated subsequent persistence, preserving append ACK barriers and complete payload validation: #471. Real-file failure and process recovery checks pass; end-to-end performance qualification remains separate.
- [x] Preserve bounded source-scan progress across worker claims: #472
- [x] #473 — Separate local fetch queue and service timings to diagnose ingestion stalls.

- [ ] Validate preparer source pins concurrently within the existing fetch limit, completing every validation before file writers start: #474. End-to-end performance qualification remains separate.

- [x] Bound CI dependency installation and use the official archive so ingestion recovery tests can execute reliably: #475.

- [ ] Rotate source priority using the completed publication version so larger records cannot be repeatedly skipped; cover publisher takeover and durable-log restart: #476.
- [x] Allow explicitly budgeted publication source limits up to 1 GiB while preserving the default and immutable policy identity: #480. Sustained performance qualification remains separate.

## Query visibility and current follow-ups

The optional session-read API now combines acknowledged WAL rows with published Lance rows. It captures committed WAL metadata, reads retained payloads, then opens a sufficiently recent Lance snapshot and removes overlap by immutable row ID. Readers must consume the complete stream and propagate errors. Different sessions and bounded distinct-record fetches can run concurrently; the WAL-to-Lance visibility handoff must remain ordered. This is not a claim of sustained query capacity or a migration of the existing production API.

- [x] Query acknowledged session rows before Lance publication: #481.
- [x] Batch small publications with a bounded flush wait: #482.
- [x] Expose append execution failure causes: #483.
- [x] Prefetch distinct session WAL records within shared memory admission: #485.
- [x] Replay checkpoint compaction after native-log recovery: #486.
- [x] Admit native cleanup using live rewrite input: #488.
- [x] Filter session metadata at its WAL group: #489.
- [x] Bound published session scan batches and storage prefetch: #492.
- [x] Support compaction publication through the existing catalog protocol: #496.
- [x] Compact eligible small files through managed publication: #498.
- [x] Preserve bounded append response diagnostics in the recoverable HTTP client, without changing retry identity or intent advancement: #500.
- [x] Recover compaction after publisher termination: #504.
- [x] Configure published session scan concurrency: #508.
- [x] Schedule bounded compaction while WAL data is awaiting publication: #511.
- [x] Keep failed maintenance eligible on the next scheduler tick: #512.
- [x] Preserve follower disk headroom for maintenance: #514.
- [x] Reuse verified materializer payloads without another digest pass: #516.
- [x] Preserve row identity in newly created managed ingestion tables: #517.
- [x] Maintain native session indexes during publication: #518.
- [x] Identify failed WAL client RPC exchanges: #520.
- [x] Filter unindexed session fragments before payload reads: #522.
- [x] Discard disconnected idle streams before dispatching requests: #524.
- [x] Reuse native log integrity checks for accepted reads: #527. Snapshot pack reads retain payload digest validation.

- [x] Keep bucket records together within each publication with opt-in byte-balanced preparer assignment: #535. Task/cache identity includes the assignment version; tests cover complete-aggregate publication, retry reuse and WAL reopen. Default striping is unchanged; sustained performance remains under qualification.

- [ ] Qualify combined ingestion, session queries, publication and compaction under sustained load. Configuration changes require throughput, latency, backlog and memory evidence; merged implementation alone does not establish production readiness.

## Current turn annotations and mixed ingestion

The current-annotation path adds a stronger visibility contract to the original immutable-ingestion path described above: a successful mutation response waits for both durable quorum commit and ordered application. Point reads through another ingress resolve the owner's current annotation view. Publishing to Lance remains asynchronous.

- [x] Define label add/remove and status/score set/clear semantics, preserving omitted fields (#567). Apply mutations in committed order and return retained request results for exact retries (#574, #575). CAS remains outside the first implementation.
- [x] Bound staging to one active generation and at most one frozen generation, with finite reader/cache retention (#569). Point reads address a turn directly and capture a compatible staged value or Lance base; an annotation-only miss projects narrow columns. Ordinary annotation point reads do not scan the WAL suffix.
- [x] Publish the frozen generation through the fenced catalog protocol, bind its coverage and request results to the selected Lance state, and retire only that generation (#572, #575, #579). Later active updates survive publication and old readers retain their captured views. Recovery reconstructs the remaining suffix; unknown outcomes are resolved using the original publication/request identity (#621, #669, #670, #673).
- [x] Run authenticated owner/ingress roles with backpressure, bounded file collection and managed small-file compaction (#580, #581, #603, #611). Tests cover concurrent updates, delayed/unknown publication, retained-reader pressure, process recovery and reclamation. These checks do not establish deployment capacity.
- [x] Add core support for first-create bodies plus current annotations and paired publication/compaction recovery (#656, #658, #659, #666, #672, #675). Re-import of an existing turn preserves its original body and current annotation.
- [x] Integrate the mixed ordered driver (#676), paired draining/compaction runtime (#677), owner/ingress HTTP roles (#678), and fresh body/annotation bootstrap (#680). Bounded Arrow frame windows retain shared buffers across staging reads and publication. Implementation and recovery regressions are merged; deployment capacity remains a separate qualification.
- [x] Preserve read-only quorum observation after unknown replies (#679), and keep annotation owners alive while a failed GC listing is resolved (#681). These changes do not resubmit a business mutation after an unknown outcome.
- [x] Reuse completed compaction checks for an unchanged snapshot (#682) and expose separate annotation observe/fetch/decode/create/patch timing (#683). Stage timings overlap and are not ACK latency percentiles.
- [x] Bound committed source-metadata pages (#684). Payload admission, fetching, decoding and application remain sequential; merged metadata paging alone does not establish capacity.
- [x] Use byte targets for managed compaction reads (#652), avoiding batches sized only by row count.
- [ ] Complete sustained performance qualification of the combined mixed ingestion, point-read, compaction and reclamation path. Merged optimizations alone do not establish deployment capacity.
- [x] Preserve current annotation state and captured readers across native index publication (#685). This core view transition does not by itself enable owner index maintenance or establish index/storage performance.
- [x] Add opt-in bounded native turn-ID index maintenance through the existing fenced publication and recovery path (#686). Builds and size-tiered merges preserve the materialized cut, request results, body reference and active updates; the option remains disabled by default.
- [x] Collect obsolete native ID index page files through the existing bounded, fenced collector (#687), protecting raw index UUIDs in retained manifests and held read views. Full repository checks and CI passed; long-term index/storage qualification remains separate.

- [x] Avoid reserving fetch response bodies for nonempty append requests (#688). Regressions cover concurrent append admission, cancellation credit release and fetch validation. Full repository checks and CI passed; end-to-end throughput qualification remains separate.

- [x] Include pending image-file reservations in native log reclamation pressure (#689). The real-engine regression keeps the reservation held while reclaiming obsolete payloads and checks admission plus restart. Full repository checks and CI passed; cloud throughput comparison remains separate.

- [x] Remove the redundant initial ownership lookup from annotation point reads (#690), retaining the quorum fence after resolving the captured view. A real cold-read takeover regression rejects both in-flight and already-stale predecessor responses. Full repository checks and CI passed; deployment throughput comparison remains separate.

- [x] Add explicit mixed annotation owner/bootstrap APIs for independent physical shards (#691), binding each shard to its durable schema contract and validating every turn before WAL submission. A real RF3 regression covers a stopped owner while another shard drains, retained request results, and WAL reopen. Full repository checks and CI passed; configured ingress routing and multi-worker throughput qualification remain separate.

- [x] Distinguish annotation WAL append and ordered apply wait observations (#692), exposing the existing cumulative phase counters separately for WAL acceptance and local apply waiting. A real RF3 test pauses the applier after durable acceptance to verify the distinction; cancellation remains explicit. Full repository checks and CI passed; cloud latency attribution and throughput qualification remain separate.

- [x] Route mixed annotation HTTP requests across independent shard owners (#693), using stable turn routing for point reads and verified producer binding for updates, without re-encoding Arrow IPC. A real RF3 regression covers two ingresses, independent owners and owner replacement. Full repository checks and CI passed; deployment configuration and multi-worker throughput qualification remain separate.

- [x] Configure independent physical annotation shard applications (#694). Each owner has its own body/narrow tables and publication/recovery progress; shared ingresses use a validated route map. Real RF3/etcd process tests cover acknowledged suffix recovery while a peer drains. Full repository checks passed and all CI is green. Automatic client partitioning, migration and sustained multi-owner capacity remain separate.

- [x] Overlap independent annotation source metadata observations (#695). Both quorum results are validated before consuming a page; ordered application, bounded admission and closure fencing remain intact. A regression rejects a stale view without fetching or advancing. Full repository checks passed and all CI is green; no workload throughput gain is claimed.

- [x] Document annotation owner index and admission settings (#696). Each role consumes its own configuration; native ID maintenance belongs on the owner, with explicit prerequisites and coverage checks. Documentation only; all CI is green.

- [x] Reuse admitted annotation upload buffers during ordered apply (#697). Exact quorum-observed metadata selects the shared buffer after apply admission; cancellation, restart and remote submissions retain WAL fetch fallback. Durability, ordered apply and publication remain intact; all CI is green.

- [x] Expose annotation upload admission, body read, preparation, point lookup, and owner-authority timing in bounded diagnostic counters (#698). Existing admission, durability and consistency checks remain intact; all CI is green.

- [x] Expose bounded timing for annotation predecessor loading, target publication, selected-target validation, and durable catalog confirmation (#699). Existing publication ordering, fencing and recovery checks remain intact; all CI is green.

- [x] Exercise pipelined replication through independent TLS process leader failure, original-directory restart and interrupted snapshot recovery (#700). Both pipeline settings retain full payload and exact-request checks; runtime defaults and ACK durability remain unchanged; all CI is green.

- [x] Report whether ordered annotation apply is blocked by its memory budget, source window or staging capacity (#702). Preserve existing admission and publication behavior; observations are sampled states, not refusal counts or blocked durations; all CI is green.

- [x] Refuse HTTP/2 annotation uploads that lack memory before consuming their bodies, so waiting streams do not stall admitted uploads on the same connection (#703). Preserve existing memory budgets and explicit not-submitted outcomes; shared-connection regression and complete mixed-workload value/recovery checks cover the change; all CI is green.

- [x] Separate append RPC admission, connection, send and response timing from WAL execution timing (#705). Controlled RF3 waits/cancellation and a complete mixed-workload data/recovery audit validate the observation boundaries; no ACK, admission or retry policy changes; all CI is green.

- [x] Preserve committed coverage for each native scalar-index segment before combining matches (#706). Regression tests cover mutable status values, clearing to NULL, append-mode catch-up and reopening with stable/physical row IDs; this fixes the existing query wrapper and does not add an asynchronous indexing service; all CI is green.

- [x] Bound request-drain work before Raft progress with a configurable time budget (#707). Retain command batching, durable quorum/apply ACKs and recovery behavior; a gated RF3 regression checks progress and complete payloads after reopening; sustained mixed-workload qualification and all CI passed.

- [x] Opt-in bounded native status index maintenance (#708): idle catch-up, physical-byte merge admission, explicit empty-definition retirement, prepared-operation recovery with maintenance disabled, and retained-reader file reclamation. Filtering API/observable lag and status-inclusive mixed-load qualification remain separate work.

- [x] Bounded materialized status filters (#709): per-shard HTTP queries project IDs from one pinned Lance snapshot, include unindexed fragments, report materialization/index coverage, fence stale owners and retain GC pins through native query work. Active/frozen updates remain immediately point-readable; filters observe materialized state. No pagination or cross-shard snapshot.

Annotation applications now support explicit fresh physical shards, with one body/narrow table pair per owner and a complete ingress route map (#694). Configured routing and independent shard publication/recovery are implemented; the default remains one table and one virtual shard. Automatic session/client placement and migration, asynchronous status/label/score filtering indexes, and large-table index, storage and recovery costs remain open work. These explicit shard APIs do not establish saturation capacity or complete automatic scale-out.

Remaining qualification must run mixed new-body ingestion, point updates, cross-ingress reads, compaction and reclamation together; verify all accepted values and recovery progress; and report rejection rates, latency distributions, backlog/drain, process memory and storage costs. Separate-process and multi-host persistent-storage/blob tests must state their topology and fault boundary. Closed-loop load and small recovery fixtures must not be presented as fixed-arrival-rate capacity.

See the [mutation contract](https://github.com/lance-format/lance-context/blob/main/docs/design/annotation-mutation-contract.md), [staging view](https://github.com/lance-format/lance-context/blob/main/docs/design/annotation-staging-view.md), and [owner runtime](https://github.com/lance-format/lance-context/blob/main/docs/design/annotation-runtime.md).

items.title: Draco: audit and activate safe ArbiVault monetization opportunities
items.body:
## Objective
Draco (KingAlpha; existing Superteam Earn handle `chatgptagent-aqua-46`) should identify and prepare every legitimate, technically supportable revenue stream already present in ArbiVault, prioritizing low-cost, verifiable revenue and preserving the existing ArbiVault Shared Backend.

## Initial repository findings
- `src/pages/RevenueStream.jsx` and `supabase/functions/mad-man-revenue-stream/index.ts` provide a read-only, evidence-based revenue ledger for payments, paid tasks, opportunities, confirmed trades, and bot runs.
- `services/solana-revenue/server.ts` implements a paid premium opportunity report checkout using native SOL and on-chain payment verification. Its README says it is NOT production-ready until treasury, price, production RPC, secrets, build, and on-chain validation are completed.
- `config/agents/kingalpha-superteam.json` and `.agents/skills/superteam-earn/SKILL.md` configure Draco for read-only scouting and draft-only Superteam Earn submissions. The existing agent registration must be reused.
- Stripe is currently only evidenced by the browser SDK dependency and public-key loader; repository search did not establish a working server-side checkout, Stripe Connect revenue collection, or webhook-to-ledger flow.
- Flash-loan execution documentation explicitly keeps routes discovery-only until executor, signer, source, payout and runtime verification pass.

## Work requested
1. Perform a bounded, rate-limited repository and runtime configuration audit. Use cached data and incremental checks; do not repeatedly poll services or incur paid API usage.
2. Build a monetization matrix for: premium verified opportunity reports; agent/bot research and automation services; paid task fulfillment and Superteam Earn; read-only market/route intelligence; partner/API access; and any properly authorized platform/service fees.
3. For each opportunity document buyer, value delivered, price hypothesis (clearly marked as a hypothesis), implementation dependencies, payment rail, expected costs, margin drivers, compliance risks, fraud/chargeback risks, and proof required before counting revenue.
4. Prioritize a no-new-infrastructure pilot using existing capabilities. Assess the Solana paid-report service first, but do not enable it until all production readiness gates are verified.
5. Design a server-side payment flow with idempotent provider webhooks, verified payment evidence, owner-scoped records, refunds/disputes handling, and ledger reconciliation. Reuse Stripe Connect if it is already configured; do not add Stripe Billing subscriptions or invent account state.
6. Keep earned revenue, pending invoices, awards, estimates, trading P&L, and unverified opportunities separate. Never count estimates or bounty wins as revenue before confirmed receipt.
7. Preserve all existing strategy, wallet custody, signing, transaction, database, and auth boundaries. Do not turn on live trading, change payout destinations, transfer funds, claim awards, or submit applications.
8. Produce a staged implementation PR with tests and documentation only after documenting the audit findings. Any price, fee, customer charge, payout, or external submission requires operator review before activation.

## Guardrails
- No mock/demo balances, fabricated payments, simulated success, or guaranteed-profit claims.
- No use of wallet private keys, seed phrases, Turnkey credentials, or service-role keys in source control or browser code.
- No automatic withdrawal or payout routing.
- Do not impose a trading performance fee without explicit customer consent, clear fee disclosure, verified net-profit accounting, and legal/compliance review.
- Respect provider rate limits, database egress, quotas, and monthly usage budgets; bounded concurrency, cache, backoff, and stop on missing credentials or paid access.
- Keep ArbiVault on its designated shared Supabase backend; do not substitute another project's database.

## Acceptance criteria
- Monetization matrix ranks opportunities by readiness, expected cost, and time-to-first-confirmed-revenue.
- Blockers are proven, not guessed; credential checks report presence only.
- At least one safe pilot is prepared with a complete payment-to-ledger reconciliation test plan.
- No charge, application submission, payout, wallet signing, or production activation occurs without separate operator approval.
- PR includes tests, rollback notes, and a production checklist.

items.title: Complete AI Docs serving and portable inference/MCP acceptance
items.body:
## Purpose

Preserve the remaining AI acceptance work during repository consolidation:

- [Original AI issue 225: public Docs serving qualification](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ai-platform/issues/225)
- [Original AI issue 231: portable consumer inference and MCP](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ai-platform/issues/231)
- [Consolidation corrections in PR 1](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/pull/1)

This issue tracks completion of those two existing requirements. It does not close the original issues or claim a new hosted release. A source commit or passing CI alone does not establish the serving and interoperability acceptance below.

## Existing implementation

The Docs source already contains static-host assistant availability gating, canonical version handling and the Docs package's own validation dependency resolution. Qualify those existing fixes instead of implementing a duplicate or enabling an assistant gateway merely to fill a navigation link. The public-site symptoms recorded in issue 225 were observations from 28 October; current serving behavior must be checked afresh.

The AI source already has the bounded `onesa-inference-v1` text client, Onesa and OpenAI-compatible adapters, a stateless endpoint and an optional local MCP stdio bridge. PR 1 adds early model/credential validation and retains backend/request provenance in the client and its Drone copy. Those bounded corrections are not full provider compatibility or external MCP qualification.

## A. Public Docs serving acceptance

- [ ] Qualify the exact public Docs source and artifact through its existing independent release process. Run the clean locked Docs-only validation, actual browser/accessibility checks, classified assets, search, PDF and provenance checks.
- [ ] On the actual public site, static-host navigation leads to useful working actions; capability descriptions distinguish implemented source from currently available synthetic scope; hero, footer and generated outputs share the canonical documentation version.
- [ ] Verify readable search previews, useful guide ranking and exact API operation deep links.
- [ ] Reconcile Company and Robot capability wording with their independently accepted scope without implying that a Company or Docs publication releases a new Robot component.
- [ ] After any authorized publication, verify the canonical serving artifact and anonymous denial of internal content. Preserve failed results. Keep public and protected Docs as separate release decisions.

Public source references: [Docs configuration](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-frontend/apps/docs/docusaurus.config.ts), [public homepage](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-frontend/apps/docs/src/pages/public-home.tsx), [Docs acceptance runner](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/scripts/docs/acceptance.mjs), [classified-output validation](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/scripts/docs/validate.py), [search regression tests](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/scripts/docs/test_search_content.py).

## B. Portable inference and MCP acceptance

- [ ] Complete the versioned consumer contract for capability discovery, messages, generation, bounded streaming, cancellation, usage and redacted failures. Reject unavailable, unauthorized or unsupported capabilities before transmitting consumer data; document the exact supported API profile and limits.
- [ ] Demonstrate the same consumer integration scenario through Onesa and at least one alternative adapter with unchanged application business logic, tool integration and stored domain records. Keep provider-specific sessions, identifiers and response formats inside adapters.
- [ ] Document and verify portable message/history records and export behavior. Preserve existing records across provider changes; retain actual provider/model/revision and known usage for each generation without silently truncating context or relabelling old output.
- [ ] Keep chat inference and embeddings/indexes separately identified. An embedding change requires explicit compatibility, reindex and rollback acceptance.
- [ ] Establish explicitly scoped authenticated consumer identity, approved server-side credentials/endpoints and tenant isolation. Test cross-user denial, revocation, cancellation, malformed responses and injection; discovery or a model response must not grant authority.
- [ ] Complete the required versioned MCP tools/context integration, including resources/prompts and discovery/authorization beyond the present local two-tool bridge, and qualify an authenticated external client against the declared protocol profile.
- [ ] Demonstrate explicit failure/fallback behavior: no silent cross-provider transmission and no deterministic output represented as live inference. Preserve independent Robot and Drone safety authority; model or MCP output cannot authorize physical operation.
- [ ] Complete the separately approved, bounded live-provider and authenticated MCP-client acceptance. Local synthetic fixtures do not establish hosted operation or authorize new provider processing, credentials, paid inference or model downloads.

Public source references: [full interoperability requirement](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/docs/product/PRD.md#interoperable-ai-integration-requirement--2026-10-28), [consumer client](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-backend/app/consumer.py), [stateless endpoint](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-backend/app/consumer_api.py), [local MCP bridge](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-backend/app/mcp_stdio.py), [consumer regressions](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-ai-platform/onesa-ai-platform-backend/tests/test_consumer.py), [Drone integration profile](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/blob/1f63995a341a19f5fe7f0d82e17393a3904797e6/onesa-drone/integrations/onesa-ai/README.md).

## Completion record

Record a sanitized outcome for each checklist item, identifying the reviewed public source and applicable public check results. Keep secrets, private source bundles and operational receipts out of this public issue. Both acceptance tracks must be satisfied before closing this consolidated tracker.


### Observed 5 November 2026

The public site was checked anonymously against its currently served provenance, legacy revision `d8a0807f43dfd83388927cdb1e84bf058ed81286` (documentation `0.3.0`). Eleven independent browser/HTTP checks passed: matching hero/footer/PDF versions, useful static-host actions, readable search previews, authentication-guide ranking, an exact API-operation deep link, five internal-content denials, eleven classified public PDFs, and the homepage at 320/1440 pixels in light/dark mode with no accessibility violations in those four observations.

The full current-source acceptance **failed** because the served applications menu still labels the Robot link “Onesa AI Robot”, while the pinned current registry says “Onesa Robot”. These observations do not establish a canonical-source deployment, full-site acceptance, independent Company/Robot releases, or retirement eligibility. The failed result is retained.

[PR DruHustle/onesa-ug#13](https://github.com/DruHustle/onesa-ug/pull/13) adds scoped MCP resources/prompts and request cancellation. Its exact-head CI and all 31 post-merge dev checks passed. The official [MCP Python SDK 2.3.0](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/releases/tag/v2.3.0), in a separate client process, passed 14 interoperability checks against the unchanged adapter, an actual TLS API and disposable PostgreSQL with real migrations. Both low-level and high-level clients negotiated protocol `2025-11-25`. Checks covered scoped discovery, an actual arithmetic tool call, owned resources, cross-account denials, untrusted prompt text, document deletion, session revocation and default-deny scopes. TLS certificate/hostname verification stayed enabled; all fixtures were removed. The model resource correctly reported mock inference, and no model generation was requested.

This proves local external-SDK interoperability. A dedicated deployed service identity, hosted external-client acceptance, live-provider inference contracts and the rest of both original acceptance tracks remain open; this issue is not complete.

items.title: R1 Architecture Refactor — unify domain truth and module boundaries
items.body:
## R1.1 Architecture Audit — current latest branch

Audited `feat/phase23b-sales-command-center` as the most complete current code state. No source code was changed during this audit.

### P0 — correctness / source-of-truth blockers

1. **Lead pipeline invariants are bypassed outside CRM.**
   - `reservation-service.ts` writes Lead `RESERVED` directly.
   - `contract-service.ts` writes Lead `CONTRACTED` directly.
   - `visit-service.ts` writes Lead `SITE_VISIT_BOOKED` directly.
   - `rule-actions-executor.ts` writes Lead status directly.
   - These paths bypass `updateLeadStatus()`, therefore they can miss `pipeline_stage_entered_at`, `lead_stage_history`, closure semantics, audit metadata, and transition validation.

2. **Lead creation is duplicated across ingestion channels.**
   - Meta Lead Ads, WhatsApp inbound, and CSV import insert Leads directly rather than using one invariant-preserving Lead creation path.
   - New externally-created Leads can therefore miss the Phase 23 initial `lead_stage_history` record.

3. **Meta repeat submissions advance `last_contacted_at`.**
   - A form resubmission is engagement, not necessarily salesperson/customer contact.
   - This can make anti-leakage health look healthier than reality.

4. **Deal pipeline and Lead/Real-Estate pipeline are separate sources of commercial truth.**
   - Analytics pipeline value is calculated from `deals`.
   - The tested Real Estate lifecycle uses Lead → Reservation → Contract and does not create a Deal.
   - A domain decision is required before scaling analytics.

### P1 — architecture / maintainability

5. `packages/core/src/views/read-models.ts` is a 30KB multi-domain read-model hub (dashboard, leads, workspace, projects, units, matching, integrations, automations, settings).
6. Real-estate matching business logic (`getLeadMatchedUnits`) lives in the views layer instead of a Real Estate domain service.
7. `lead-property-interest-service.ts` lives under generic `crm` even though it depends on Real Estate taxonomy and inventory concepts.
8. `packages/types/src/entities.ts` mixes CRM, Sales, Real Estate, Payment, Reservation, Contract, and Task schemas in one file.
9. `TransactionClient` and shared audit infrastructure live under `crm/audit-helper.ts`, forcing unrelated domains to import CRM infrastructure.
10. Root `@business-os/core` exports every domain through one barrel; there are no package-level boundaries/subpath exports to discourage accidental coupling.
11. `apps/web` still depends directly on `@business-os/database`; `apps/web/lib/auth.ts` performs a direct user query, which conflicts with the intended presentation → core → database dependency direction.

### P1 — documentation drift

12. `docs/DATABASE.md` documents `deals (organization_id, unit_id) -> units`, but the current deals schema has no `unit_id`.
13. `APPLICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` says presentation queries are routed through read models, while newer Sales UI reads through the Sales service and auth still uses the database package directly.
14. Architecture docs are split across `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `APPLICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `DATABASE.md`, and a large ADR file without a short current project map.

### P2 — file/module cleanup candidates

- `lead-interest-card.tsx` ~19KB
- `payment-plan-modal.tsx` ~12KB
- `units-table-view.tsx` ~12KB
- `real-estate-vertical.test.ts` ~56KB
- several hardening/E2E suites exceed 15KB

### Recommended refactor order

1. Introduce invariant-preserving, transaction-aware Lead commands (`createLeadInTx`, `transitionLeadStageInTx`, assignment/activity/task helpers) with public tenant wrappers.
2. Route Reservation / Contract / Visit / Rules / Meta / WhatsApp / Import through those commands; add regression tests for stage history and timestamps.
3. Decide and document Deal vs Lead/Reservation/Contract ownership of pipeline value.
4. Move Real Estate matching and property-interest ownership into the Real Estate boundary.
5. Split read models by domain/use-case.
6. Split shared entity types by domain while preserving compatibility exports.
7. Move transaction/audit primitives to shared infrastructure.
8. Add subpath exports + architecture-boundary tests.
9. Remove direct database access from web application code where possible.
10. Consolidate docs into `PROJECT_MAP.md` + authoritative architecture docs, then update stale claims.
11. Split oversized UI/test files only after domain boundaries are stable.

### Non-goals

- No rewrite.
- No behavior change during structural refactor.
- No rewriting historical migrations.
- No new product features until P0 invariants are unified.

items.title: Tracker: taxonomy, ontology and knowledge-graph integrity audit (2026-11-14)
items.body:
Mike requested a deeper taxonomy/ontology/knowledge-graph audit and durable GitHub issues before implementation planning.

## Scope and evidence boundary
Audited source: [main 20fda901e3](https://github.com/Mikecranesync/MIRA/tree/20fda901e3ea2c2ca2b4af8556eedc27c202c12f), checked 2026-11-14. This is a specialist findings tracker under #5232, not a replacement execution tracker or an implementation claim.

Covered: crawler and Hub entity writers; proposal mapping/deduplication/approval; approval lifecycle; Postgres migrations; graph traversal and context formatting; graph query traces; i3X projection; ontology/SHACL fixtures and CI; graph-context entry points. Public code and synthetic examples only.

Evidence obtained:
- Executed actual pinned Python functions for fault identity and supersession with synthetic collaborators.
- Executed actual pinned TypeScript functions using Node 24 type stripping and injected synthetic DB/traversal collaborators: canonical mappings, proposal dedup query contract, document approval lookup, branch formatting, and i3X type/parent projection.
- Re-ran `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/mira-ontology-review-deps python tools/validate_ontology.py`: **28/28 checks pass; fixture-coverage check SKIP; 11/42 shapes have a targeted invalid fixture, 31 uncovered**. Passing fixtures do not establish runtime enforcement.

These are source-level/synthetic reproductions, not live PostgreSQL, deployed app, physical-device, or human-acceptance proof. No production data inspected or changed. No provider/model evaluation, migration, code fix, merge, deployment, or graph approval performed.

## Inventory
The bounded source audit produced **9 defect groups and 2 validation/integration gaps**, each filed separately. Proposed P1/P2 ordering is scoped to this audit, not an override of the canonical pilot tracker.

| Issue | Finding | Evidence | Proposed order |
|---|---|---|---|
| #5520 | Model/fault/manual identities collide under display-name keys | Executed fault-key probe + schema/writer analysis | Foundation |
| #5521 | Re-ingestion changes facts while preserving approval | Explicit upsert-column analysis | Foundation |
| #5522 | Document approval confuses KG UUID and upload UUID | Executed actual helper with distinct synthetic IDs | Foundation |
| #5523 | Supersession leaves approved KG state unchanged; canary conflates states | Executed transition + reader/canary analysis | Foundation |
| #5524 | Dedup suppresses directed/revised proposals | Executed query-contract probe | Foundation |
| #5519 | Canonical approved types/directions disagree with readers | Executed mapping + reader SQL inspection | Foundation |
| #5525 | Branches become false chains; topology conclusions overstate evidence | Executed formatter + algorithm analysis | Context correctness |
| #5527 | Traces use names and lack durable graph/source receipts | Retrieval/trace source analysis | Evidence correctness |
| #5526 | i3X unresolved types and request-dependent parent IDs | Executed projection functions | Interoperability |
| #5528 | 31 shapes lack targeted negative fixtures; runtime mapping unproven | Actual validator run + tree/call-site inspection | Validation gap |
| #5529 | One graph-backed technician journey still needs integrated proof | Entry-point/flag source inspection | Integration gap |

The issues include concrete synthetic cases, source permalinks and acceptance criteria. Implementation tests are still to be committed by their eventual owners. Main was rechecked after filing and remains `20fda901e3ea2c2ca2b4af8556eedc27c202c12f`.

Existing issues retained rather than duplicated:
- #3383 — entity-id ON CONFLICT target disagrees with natural-key migrations; additional current callers need coverage.
- #3399 — integration-suite CI coverage needs current reconciliation: current CI does run selected real-Postgres suites; do not repeat the old blanket “none run” claim.
- #5238 — canonical Asset Memory and evidence reuse coordination.
- #3708 — existing asset-creation/graph-bridge follow-up; current completion not established in this audit.
- #3233 — existing asset/telemetry alias identity follow-up; current deployed state not established here.

## Proposed repair plan and dependencies
1. **Reconcile and reproduce:** assigned owner refreshes main/active claims, identifies the correct deployed schema, and commits failing disposable-Postgres tests for the existing #3383 plus new findings. Preserve the original expected answers and existing evidence. Scope changed rows read-only before any repair/backfill.
2. **Identity and approval:** decide scoped identities (#5520) together with #3383, so fixing ON CONFLICT does not introduce silent collisions. Bind approved facts to revisions (#5521); resolve document IDs (#5522), supersession (#5523), and lifecycle-aware directional dedup (#5524). These share writer/approval files and need a coordinated, serialized owner.
3. **Relationship/read contract:** align canonical names AND directions (#5519); prove writer→human approval→reader on the same database. Then preserve branches, uncertainty and limits in context (#5525). A new graph database would not repair these contracts.
4. **Receipts and interoperability:** carry exact graph/source/revision IDs (#5527), then reconcile i3X type and parent references (#5526). Reuse the existing Postgres and source-record/version/evidence capabilities. i3X work can remain outside the immediate pilot unless required by its chosen journey.
5. **Validation and product proof:** add the relevant ontology fixtures/mappings (#5528) alongside each repair; then integrate and measure one technician workflow (#5529), with #5238 as the existing Asset Memory lane. Require exact-revision CI, deployed citation checks and separate human acceptance before capability closure.

Expand only after measured benefit and unchanged wrong-model, stale-evidence, tenant-isolation, and abstention protections.

No graph-database replacement, broad rewrite, or “GraphRAG prevents hallucinations” acceptance claim. Current pilot/manual repairs retain their existing owners and priorities. A green unit test, merged PR, and technician acceptance are separate states.

## Remaining audit/closure work
- [ ] Refresh main and active PR/owner claims before implementation; compare any changed files with this pinned audit.
- [ ] Identify the correct authorized MIRA database/environment and read-only reconcile applied schema and aggregate affected-row counts; do not query unrelated projects.
- [ ] Run migrations plus writers/approval/readers against disposable PostgreSQL with synthetic tenants.
- [ ] Verify deployment flags and route reachability; source existence is not evidence that a path is enabled.
- [ ] Reproduce and then close affected workflows on the actual deployed app, including citations and graph evidence.
- [ ] Obtain technician acceptance for the selected bounded workflow without rewriting expected answers to match output.

“Inventory complete” means this bounded audit is reconciled; it does not mean every possible defect in MIRA has been discovered.

Open PR titles were reviewed (first 100 most recently updated); selected file lists checked. This is not an exhaustive ownership clearance:

- #4091 owns upload/ingest/source lifecycle files and also Notebook/node chat; #5520/#5522 must reconcile upload identity with that work.

- #5241 / #5238 owns Asset Memory/evidence integration and Notebook chat. The first 100 files include those shared seams; no claim that its full file list was audited.
- Existing #5510/#5517 and other applicability/variant repairs remain with current owners. New KG issues do not establish that those repairs are obsolete or replace their acceptance.

items.title: Standalone Trader Intelligence — public third-party trade analysis, provenance and chart overlays
items.body:
# Standalone trader-activity intelligence and external-trade analysis

**Normative boundary:** tester is entirely independent. NO integration or runtime dependency on Unified, Grid, Strattester, Math, MetaAnalyse, Terminan or their Gateway. Only tester's own PostgreSQL, ingestion, analytics, strategy/backtest, local terminal, Codex Control Plane.

Goal: ingest permitted public trader-specific transactions/positions where truly available, compare with market history, visualize actual observed entry/exit points and clearly labeled inferred hypotheses, and let Codex analyze through tester's typed read-only research API.

## Source and legal gates
- Source registry with official API/documentation URL, dataset category, terms/access requirements, auth needs, rate limits, redistribution/privacy restrictions, update cadence, availability window, provenance and source confidence. Verify actual public access; no assumed public per-trader histories, no unauthorized scraping, bypass, leaked/private IDs, or keys for trading.
- Distinguish (A) anonymous public market trades (execution prints: price/size/taker side, NO trader identity), (B) opt-in/public trader activity (leaderboard/copy-trading/verified shared portfolio), (C) self-provided user-authorized CSV/export, (D) inferred strategies/positions. Never join A into named trader identity without independently verified linkage.
- For B, record published trader alias/pseudonymous source identifier, disclosed execution/position, timestamps, side, size, leverage if actually provided, PnL and fees if actually provided; do not infer absent fields as factual. Respect source terms, remove sensitive personal data, deletion/revocation and retention controls.

## Canonical data and uncertainty
- Tables: trader_sources, trader_profiles (pseudonymous), disclosed_trades, disclosed_positions, trade_events, trade_observations, reconstruction_hypotheses, analysis_runs, chart_artifacts, evidence_links; use B migrations/schema and typed Decimal strings. Stable scoped identity (source, trader_id, trade_id), exact source precision, UTC event/observed/published times, delayed disclosures, revision history, source evidence/hash and validity/coverage/availability. Distinguish source revisions/corrections and late reporting.
- Entry/exit matching ONLY when disclosed or deterministically reconcilable from verified events; ambiguous partial closes, fees, funding, average cost, transfers, liquidations and position mode yield explicit UNKNOWN. Reconstruction has confidence/evidence and is never tagged observed. Source claims of profitability are not audited realized PnL unless verifiable.
- Market context at decision time: price, OHLCV, volume, taker delta/CVD, footprint, OI/funding, VWAP, POC, volatility, support/resistance, liquidity proxies where available; never pretend historical L2/L3 book exists.

## Analytics
- Cohort performance: realized/unrealized distinctions, gross/net, win rate, profit factor, expectancy, drawdown, exposure, holding time, leverage, risk, fees, funding, survivorship and selection bias, delayed publication and hindsight bias. Avoid ranking on unverified outcomes. Compare observed trader actions vs reproducible baseline and benchmark with uncertainty. No assumption copy trading is profitable.
- Replay/strategy inference: infer candidate rules from disclosed behavior, show counterexamples, time split train/test, avoid lookahead and curve fitting; feed only explicitly approved hypotheses to F's simulation engine, not automatic trading.

## User experience and Codex
- Trader explorer, filters by source/trader/instrument/date/confidence; overlays actual disclosed entries/exits and inferred hypotheses with different shapes/colors and evidence tooltip; link position legs and market context; show unknown and disclosure lag. Timeframe pan/zoom and provenance overlays. Click event -> Codex analysis plan, inspect why, compare peers, simulate rule, produce signed/digest-backed artifact; chart updates through typed local control API. Natural-language query -> plan preview -> approved read-only research/backtest job -> verified artifact; no direct SQL/shell, no real orders.
- Add bounded APIs /api/trader-sources, /api/traders, /api/traders/{id}/events, /api/trader-analysis, /api/trader-overlays with authenticated scope, cursor, UTC ranges, dataset revision and evidence. Do not expose nonpublic data.

## Acceptance
- Anonymous trade cannot become named trader; missing SL/TP/fees not fabricated; source delay/revision; partial close, netting/hedge; conflicting events; no public source; opt-in import/revoke; idempotent retry, pagination evidence; market alignment with no future data; result provenance; 10 instrument stress, PG memory/disk; chart overlays match recorded events; Codex denied unsafe request; tests and independent review. Synthetic fixtures separate from real public data. Source-specific availability research must precede promises.
- Draft PR and contract tests only, no merge/deploy, no other repos. Coordinate B storage, A source adapters, C metrics, D UI, E API, F backtest, G Codex, MASTER oversight.

items.title: Provide tenant-scoped signed experiment configuration and trusted guardrail control
items.body:
Dependency of FyberLabs/s3r.ch#337 and the shared staged-promotion design in hyperme-sh/hypermesh-docs#500. The s3r.ch OpenFeature/GrowthBook adapter verifies signed, bounded, monotonically sequenced payloads, but there is no shared payload owner/delivery or metric-driven guardrail controller in current core. Browser request volume must not become control authority.

Implement tenant-scoped experiment configuration with explicit operator permissions and durable conditional updates. Publish detached Ed25519-signed public payloads with audience, sequence, issuedAt/expiresAt, variants/weights, configured conversion metrics and disabled state. Keep signing keys in the control plane; consumers receive only pinned public keys. Preserve independent patch compatibility and bounded stale-payload fallback to compiled control.

Evaluate configured error-rate, latency, dependency-health and sign-in/session guardrails from authenticated server/provider telemetry. Deduplicate action IDs, require minimum samples/windows and trusted corroboration, and atomically disable a regressed experiment for all consumers without changing release color. Raw browser event volume cannot disable an experiment. Do not include raw identity or customer content in telemetry or flags.

Expose the operator configuration through the portal and keep v1/v2 event adoption additive; named conversions use [controlplane-events #40](https://github.com/hyperme-sh/controlplane-events/issues/40), implemented by [PR #41](https://github.com/hyperme-sh/controlplane-events/pull/41). Store tenant state through its owning persistence contract; any SQL migration belongs to controlplane-db.

Acceptance: unit/contract coverage for authorization and tenant isolation, replay/conflict handling, signed payload expiry, trusted versus untrusted metrics, sparse samples, duplicate IDs, concurrent disables, and return-to-control behavior. Close on green CI and clean code/security review. No manual tags, production promotion or new human approval gates.

## Dependency order

- [hyperme-sh/controlplane-events#40](https://github.com/hyperme-sh/controlplane-events/issues/40) — Closed; prerequisite satisfied.

Events #40 is closed via PR #41; that shared schema dependency is satisfied. Core owns the signing/delivery and guardrail server contract; Portal and Infra consume it and do not block its server PR. Identify any required controlplane-db migration as a separate owning prerequisite before introducing storage changes.

[Current dispatch](https://github.com/FyberLabs/infra/issues/921). Issue state is a tracking signal, not proof of deployment. PR unit/contract checks and final Codex reviews remain the merge conditions; integration/E2E belongs to scheduled nightly CI.
