items.title: [Audit][Roadmap] Ragbot platform architecture audit and prioritized execution plan
items.body:
## Executive summary

Audit baseline: `main` at the September 2026 architecture after durable worker reliability, staged knowledge generations, parser/chunker ports, Golden Dataset and parser/PDF benchmark work.

Ragbot is already beyond a prototype RAG application. Its strongest current properties are:

- PostgreSQL-backed durable ingestion queue with lease/heartbeat/retry/DLQ/reconciliation
- staged source knowledge generations with PostgreSQL activation authority and durable Qdrant cleanup
- dense Qdrant + PostgreSQL CJK-aware lexical hybrid retrieval + RRF + reranking
- Parser/Chunker ports and promotion benchmarks
- multi-tenant ACL/RBAC enforcement
- SaaS/local/object-source ingestion coverage
- Prometheus/OpenTelemetry plus quality benchmark infrastructure
- OpenAI-shaped compatibility API and a preliminary Node client

The next architecture risk is **integration growth without stable platform contracts**. Current factories and ingestion dispatch still branch on implementation/source names; model routing is not wired as the production composition boundary; embeddings are synchronous; vector index schema has no first-class lifecycle; persistence has a legacy inheritance stack/fat repository; and the SDK/identity/object-storage surfaces are not yet at the same maturity as the ingestion core.

The recommendation is therefore **not** to add dozens of providers/connectors/vector databases immediately. First establish stable extension and index contracts, then expand implementations behind them.

---

## Priority 0 — platform correctness and evolvability

### #50 Platform registry / typed runtime profiles
Make connector/model/embedding/vector/upload implementations resolvable behind one stable registry and shared config/capability schemas.

### #51 LLM provider/router plane
Wire capability-aware model routing into production; remove global environment mutation; add OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Azure/Bedrock/Ollama adapters behind one contract.

### #52 Embedding plane
Replace synchronous embedding transport with bounded async batching/retry/rate-limit handling and a complete embedding contract identity.

### #53 Vector index lifecycle
Introduce versioned indexes, shadow validation, Qdrant alias activation and rollback for embedding/vector-schema upgrades.

### P0 exit criteria

- adding a provider/connector no longer requires editing core dispatch switches
- model and embedding clients use pooled bounded transports with explicit capabilities
- every indexed chunk can be associated with an immutable embedding/index contract
- incompatible embedding changes build a new index and support atomic cutover/rollback
- current production paths remain regression-compatible

Do not start broad provider/connector expansion before these boundaries are stable.

---

## Priority 1 — production platform surface

### #54 Connector SDK
Standardize snapshot/incremental/checkpoint/deletion/ACL/rate-limit semantics and then validate with SharePoint/OneDrive, Azure/GCS, Slack/Teams or other new connectors.

### #55 Storage architecture
Split the monolithic `Repo`, retire the `postgres_repo -> pg_repo -> managed_pg_repo` inheritance stack and clarify transaction/capability boundaries.

### #56 PostgreSQL performance gates
Keyset pagination, SQL-side filtering, COPY/staging batch paths, queue claim/reconciliation hot-path cleanup, pool/timeouts and query-plan benchmarks.

### #57 Retrieval engine
Move hybrid retrieval to a reusable async/composable pipeline. Keep current hybrid RRF as control, then benchmark Qdrant dense+sparse, alternate fusion, MMR and multi-vector plans.

### #58 Public API / SDK / MCP
Freeze versioned knowledge/search contracts, add maintained Python+Node SDKs, typed retry/error/pagination/stream semantics and a scoped MCP/tool surface.

### #59 Upload object storage
Keep `UploadStore`, add S3/MinIO first and then Azure Blob/GCS, including direct upload and lifecycle/GC semantics.

### #60 Enterprise identity/security
Add OIDC/JWT, service accounts, hashed/rotatable API keys and unified SecretResolver backends while preserving Ragbot RBAC/ACL as authorization truth.

### #61 Durable quality/observability
Tie production requests and evaluation runs to parser/chunker/embedding/index/retrieval/reranker/model contract IDs; use benchmark evidence as promotion gates.

### P1 exit criteria

- platform can horizontally scale API/workers without shared upload PVC
- source catalog/job APIs remain bounded at large cardinality
- retrieval has deadline/cancellation and measurable stage-level latency
- Python and Node consumers have supported, versioned SDKs
- operators can identify exactly which data/model/index contracts produced a response
- identity/secrets no longer depend on one static plaintext API-key mapping pattern

---

## Priority 2 — controlled capability expansion

### #62 Multimodal RAG
Preserve tables/images/layout and visual citations in the normalized document/index contracts, benchmarked against the text-only baseline.

### #63 Release governance
Remove roadmap drift, lock/constraint CI/runtime dependencies, add SBOM/security/compatibility checks and mechanically validate capability/version documentation.

P2 can be partially parallelized, but multimodal indexing should wait for #52/#53 and object artifacts should build on #59.

---

## Dependency graph / recommended order

1. **Foundation:** #50
2. In parallel after the foundation shape is agreed: **#51, #52, #55**
3. Build **#53** on the embedding/index contract from #52
4. Run database operational work **#56** alongside storage consolidation, but do not delay obvious pagination/hot-path regressions
5. Use the registry in **#54 and #59** rather than adding new branches
6. Refactor retrieval in **#57** after the embedding/index interfaces are stable; preserve the current RRF path as the benchmark control
7. Productize **#58** over stable public contracts rather than exposing internal service objects
8. Implement **#61** across all preceding work so promotion decisions become evidence-based
9. Harden enterprise identity with **#60** before positioning Ragbot as a multi-tenant shared service
10. Add **#62** multimodal representations only after index/artifact lifecycle is explicit
11. **#63** begins immediately and stays cross-cutting

---

## Architectural principles to freeze

1. PostgreSQL is the authoritative control-plane/system-of-record store; Qdrant is a derived vector index.
2. Source publication and vector-index publication are different lifecycles; both require atomic activation/rollback semantics.
3. Product semantics/config schemas live in stable handwritten contracts; vendor adapters sit behind them.
4. Connectors emit normalized source changes; parsers emit normalized document blocks; chunkers emit chunks; embedding/index stages do not reach back into vendor connectors.
5. Tenant/ACL filtering happens before evidence is returned, not as a post-generation cleanup.
6. New retrieval/vector techniques are promoted by Golden Dataset + latency/cost evidence, not by feature novelty.
7. Public API/SDK contracts are smaller and more stable than internal service classes.
8. Production network clients use pooled transports, bounded concurrency, explicit deadlines, retries and structured errors.
9. Secrets and identity are references/claims, not arbitrary plaintext configuration fields.
10. Runtime capabilities and release documentation should be machine-verifiable.

---

## Industry baseline used for the audit

- LangChain: common provider/document-loader/vector-store interfaces and separately packaged integrations
- Haystack: composable pipeline components + distinct Document Store abstractions
- Unstructured: source/destination connector architecture, optional connector packages and configurable ingestion stages
- Qdrant: dense+sparse/named vectors, multi-stage Query API and atomic collection aliases for vector-version cutover
- Weaviate / Azure AI Search: explicit hybrid fusion + reranking stages and multi-tenant/filter-aware retrieval
- Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases: decoupled Retrieve vs RetrieveAndGenerate, metadata filtering, reranking, structured/multimodal knowledge paths and retrieval traces
- Vercel AI SDK: provider registries/capability normalization
- OpenAI / Anthropic SDKs: typed streaming/errors, configurable timeout/retry and provider transport concerns kept out of application logic

This audit intentionally treats these products as architectural references, not dependencies to copy wholesale.

---

## Overall target state

Ragbot should converge from a feature-rich RAG service into a **versioned Knowledge Retrieval Platform** with five explicit planes:

1. **Connector/Ingestion plane** — durable source sync, parsing/chunking, generation publication
2. **Index plane** — embedding contracts, vector/sparse indexes, version/cutover/rollback
3. **Retrieval plane** — filters, candidate retrieval, fusion, rerank, evidence/citations
4. **Model/Agent plane** — provider registry, capability routing, bounded tool/model execution
5. **Control/Developer plane** — PostgreSQL metadata/jobs/evals, identity/RBAC, observability, SDK/MCP/admin

The existing code already contains many of these concepts; the next milestone is to make the boundaries explicit enough that new integrations can grow without destabilizing the core.

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

#8 wires the OpenTelemetry `MeterProvider` into every Go service and defines the initial RED metric surface. What does not exist is the platform that receives those metrics: a time-series store, a recording-rule layer, a cardinality budget, per-tenant and per-country routing, and a query API the consoles and alerting can build on. Without it the metrics are emitted into an OTLP endpoint that has nowhere to put them.

The consequence of that gap is that the platform has no quantitative view of its own behaviour:

- **Per-tenant rate limits and resource quotas cannot be set or enforced empirically.** The brief requires them to prevent noisy-neighbour degradation across a shared-schema, RLS-isolated estate. A quota chosen without a distribution of observed per-tenant request rate and database time is a guess that will either throttle a legitimate hospital during morning OPD peak or fail to contain a runaway integration.
- **EmergencyConnect's mandated capacity headroom is unverifiable.** "Isolated, highest-SLA" is a commitment. Without saturation metrics for its pods, JetStream consumers and connection pools, nobody can say whether the headroom exists on the day an ambulance dispatch surge arrives.
- **Business-critical operational signals have no home.** Bed occupancy, OPD queue depth, pending pathologist approvals in LabConnect, cold-chain excursions in SupplyConnect and open P0 work orders in FacilityConnect are all countable and all currently invisible outside the transactional database — and the architectural rule that analytics must never run on the live clinical DB means they cannot be dashboarded by querying it.
- **Capacity and cost decisions are unevidenced**, which for a platform billed per tenant is a direct commercial exposure.

Affected: SRE on-call, platform engineers sizing services, product owners for each of the eleven products, and the hospital admin who has been promised an availability commitment.

This story delivers the metric storage, cardinality governance, recording rules and query surface. It is a sibling of #605 (centralised logging) and #607 (distributed tracing), and it is a hard dependency for #609, #610, #611 and #612.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** platform SRE and product owner
**I want** a per-country metric store that ingests OTLP metrics from every service with governed cardinality, tenant attribution and derived recording rules
**So that** I can size services, set defensible per-tenant quotas, verify EmergencyConnect headroom and drive dashboards and alerts from a single queryable source.

### Scope

**In scope**

* Metric storage per country deployment, ArgoCD-managed, ingesting OTLP push from the collector established in #8, with long-term retention in downsampled tiers (raw 15 days, 5-minute rollup 13 months).
* A **metric naming and semantic-convention standard** for HMS: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions where they exist, and an `hms.` namespace for domain metrics, enforced by a CI validator that rejects non-conforming names and unbudgeted attributes.
* **Cardinality governance**: a declared per-metric attribute budget, a collector-side limiter that drops and counts series beyond the budget, and a weekly top-cardinality report so growth is caught before it becomes an outage.
* The four golden signals per service and per JetStream subject: traffic, errors, latency and saturation — the last including connection-pool utilisation, JetStream consumer lag, Temporal task-queue backlog and Redis memory.
* **Domain metric registration**: a small Go API (`metrics.RegisterDomainGauge`) so a product module can publish counts such as `hms.beds.occupied`, `hms.opd.queue.depth`, `hms.lab.reports.awaiting_approval`, `hms.facility.workorders.open` with the priority as an attribute, and `hms.supply.coldchain.excursions` — sourced from the module, never from an analytics query against the clinical database.
* Recording rules for the expensive aggregations dashboards and alerts need (per-service availability, per-tenant request rate, p95/p99 latency), so query cost is paid once at write time.
* A query API with OpenFGA-scoped access, so a tenant-facing consumer cannot query another tenant's series.
* Per-country routing and residency enforcement; no cross-country metric replication.

**Out of scope**

* **Log ingestion, retention and search** — owned by #605.
* **Trace storage and sampling** — owned by #607.
* **Alerting rules, thresholds, escalation policy and on-call rotation** — those are consumers of this store and are defined once the golden signals exist; owned by the SRE reliability epic.
* **Dashboard composition, SLO definitions and error budgets** — owned by #610.
* **Per-tenant health scoring and noisy-neighbour attribution surfaces** — owned by #611; this issue provides the series, #611 builds the tenant view.
* **De-identified analytical warehouse and product analytics** — a separate OLAP path owned by #613.

---

## Recommended Solution

### Storage and ingestion

A Prometheus-compatible time-series store per country deployment, receiving OTLP push from the OpenTelemetry Collector DaemonSet rather than scraping pods directly. Push is preferable here because Knative scales services to zero and short-lived pods are missed by scrape intervals; the collector holds the delta and forwards it.

Retention is country-profile configuration on the same pattern as #605:

```yaml
# country-profile: IN
metrics:
  raw_retention_days: 15
  rollup_5m_retention_days: 400
  residency_region: asia-south1
  cardinality_budget_total: 2_000_000
```

### Cardinality governance

This is the single most likely way a metrics platform fails, so it is designed for rather than discovered. Every metric is declared in a checked-in registry:

```go
// pkg/metrics/registry
var BedsOccupied = Declare(Spec{
    Name:        "hms.beds.occupied",
    Kind:        Gauge,
    Unit:        "{bed}",
    Attributes:  []string{"tenant.id", "facility.id", "ward.type"},
    MaxSeries:   50_000,
})
```

The CI validator fails a build that emits a metric absent from the registry or carrying an attribute outside its declared set. At runtime the collector applies a per-metric series limiter that drops beyond `MaxSeries` and increments `otel.metrics.series_dropped`, so overflow is visible rather than silently distorting dashboards. High-cardinality identifiers — `patient.id`, `encounter.id`, `work_order.id`, ABHA numbers — are structurally impossible because they will never pass the validator; that correlation belongs on traces (#607) via exemplars.

### Domain metrics without touching the clinical database

Architectural rule 7 forbids analytics on the live OLTP database. Domain gauges are therefore maintained from the module's own event handling rather than by periodic `SELECT COUNT(*)`: MediCore's bed module increments and decrements `hms.beds.occupied` on `PatientAdmitted`, `PatientTransferred` and `PatientDischarged` consumed from NATS JetStream, with a low-frequency reconciliation sweep (hourly, off-peak, on a read replica) that corrects drift and emits `hms.beds.occupied.drift` so the correction itself is observable.

### Query API and authorisation

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/v1/metrics/query` | instant query, OpenFGA-scoped |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/metrics/query_range` | range query for dashboards |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/metrics/registry` | declared metrics, units, attributes, budgets |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/metrics/cardinality` | current series counts against budget |

```
type metric_scope
  relations
    define tenant_reader: [user, group#member]
    define estate_reader: [user, group#member]
```

The query layer rewrites every submitted expression to inject a mandatory `tenant.id` label matcher derived from the caller's OpenFGA scope. Rewriting server-side, rather than validating a user-supplied matcher, means a crafted expression cannot escape the filter.

### Events consumed

`PatientAdmitted`, `PatientDischarged`, `AppointmentBooked`, `LabResultReady`, `MedicineDispensed`, `StockLow`, `AmbulanceDispatched` — each feeding a declared domain gauge or counter. No module reads another module's tables to produce a metric.

### Sequencing and dependencies

#8 must land first. The collector deployment and country-profile abstraction are prerequisites. This issue must precede #609, #610, #611 and #612. The domain-metric registration API should land early so product modules adopt it as they are built rather than being retrofitted.

### Risks

- **Cardinality explosion** — the dominant risk, mitigated by the checked-in registry, CI validator, per-metric limiter and weekly report.
- **Domain gauge drift** from missed or duplicated events — mitigated by idempotent event handling keyed on event ID and the reconciliation sweep with an explicit drift metric.
- **Metric store outage cascading into request failures** — the export path is asynchronous and bounded; a black-hole test asserts service latency is unchanged when the store is unreachable.
- **Cost growth from 13-month rollup retention** — mitigated by downsampling at ingest and a cost review at the 30-day mark.
- **Metrics becoming a PHI channel via a label** — structurally prevented by the attribute allowlist in the registry; a CI test asserts no declared attribute is a patient-level identifier.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** MediCore is admitting and discharging patients across three facilities of one tenant, and the bed module maintains `hms.beds.occupied` from JetStream events
**When** an SRE issues a range query for `hms.beds.occupied` grouped by `facility.id` over the past 24 hours
**Then** the series are returned for all three facilities with 15-second resolution and p95 query latency under 1 second, the values match the transactional bed state within one reconciliation interval, all series carry `tenant.id` and `country.profile`, and no series carries a patient-level identifier.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a developer adds an attribute `patient.id` to `hms.opd.queue.depth` without updating the metric registry
**When** the change is pushed and CI runs
**Then** the metric validator fails the build with an explicit message naming the undeclared attribute and the registry file to amend, the change cannot merge, and no unbudgeted series is ever created in the store.

### Edge Cases

* A Knative service scales to zero between collector export intervals — the counter's last delta is still forwarded, so a burst on a scaled-to-zero service is not silently lost.
* A tenant on the schema-per-tenant premium tier — metric attribution works identically, and the tenant's schema name never appears as a label.
* A per-metric series budget is exhausted mid-day — new series are dropped with a counter increment and a rate-limited alert, existing series continue unaffected, and dashboards display a staleness indicator rather than an apparent decline to zero.
* A JetStream consumer replays a backlog after an outage — the domain gauge does not double-count, because handlers are idempotent on event ID, and the replay is visible as consumer-lag recovery rather than as a spike in clinical activity.
* A query is submitted by a caller with no resolvable OpenFGA scope — the rewritten expression matches no series and returns empty, never the unfiltered estate.
* Clock skew between a node and the store causes out-of-order samples — samples outside the accepted window are rejected and counted, and the affected node is identified by `k8s.node.name` rather than silently corrupting a series.
## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team’s agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team’s agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** Every service, JetStream consumer, Temporal worker and product module publishes governed, tenant-attributed metrics to a per-country store queryable through an authorisation-scoped API, with cardinality held inside a declared budget.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** Per-tenant quotas and rate limits are set from observed distributions rather than guesswork; EmergencyConnect capacity headroom becomes a measurable claim; dashboards, SLOs and alerting have a single source of truth; infrastructure spend is attributable and defensible.
* **Success metric or validation method:**
  - **100%** of deployed services report all four golden signals within 5 minutes of rollout, verified by a conformance job that cross-checks the deployment inventory against the metric store.
  - Total active series stay **below 80%** of the declared cardinality budget, with zero unplanned series-limit drops over a rolling 30-day window.
  - Dashboard range queries return at **p95 under 1 second** over 24 hours of data and **under 3 seconds** over 30 days, backed by recording rules.
  - Domain gauge accuracy within **0.5%** of the transactional source at each hourly reconciliation, measured by `hms.*.drift` staying inside that band.
  - Metric ingestion adds no more than **2 ms to p95** on instrumented endpoints, measured with export enabled versus disabled.
  - Cross-tenant query attempts return empty in **100%** of adversarial isolation tests.
* **Monitoring period:** 45 days after production rollout, with a cardinality and retention-cost review at day 21.

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

**Guardrail:** Accessibility and User Journey — the primary user journey, WCAG level, keyboard navigation and accessible names.
**Reason:** This story delivers a metric store, ingestion path, cardinality governance, recording rules and a query API. It ships no user interface. The dashboards and tenant views that render these series are owned by #610 and #611, where the accessibility guardrail applies in full.
**Alternative validation:** The query API is exercised by contract tests covering the loading, empty, partial-result and error responses that downstream consoles must render, so #610 and #611 inherit well-defined states rather than inventing them.
**Residual risk:** Low. The risk of an inaccessible surface is deferred, not removed, and is explicitly carried by the consuming issues.
**Approved by:** SRE Team lead (owner of the Observability epic).

**Guardrail:** Automated Testing — critical user journeys covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
**Reason:** Partially applicable. There is no browser journey in this story, but end-to-end metric flow is a genuine integration concern that must not go untested.
**Alternative validation:** An integration suite runs a Go service, the OpenTelemetry Collector and the metric store as test containers, emits declared metrics through the registry API, and asserts that series arrive with the expected names, units and attributes, that undeclared attributes are dropped by the limiter, and that the scoped query API filters by tenant.
**Residual risk:** Low — the failure modes with real consequence are ingestion and scoping, both covered.
**Approved by:** SRE Team lead.

items.title: [CI-04B][P0] Normalize producer and external-source intake adapters with conformance fixtures

labels.name: area:finance
labels.description: Finance domain: usage cost, budgets, ledger, reconciliation, reporting

milestone.title: v1
milestone.description: NeatHack 2026 v1 scope

items.body:
**Stable key:** CI-04B
**Owner role:** Finance and reliability — financial subsystem maintainer. Named implementer and accountable reviewer: unassigned; confirm at kickoff, not an invented GitHub assignee.
**Priority:** P0 — All usage producers must share the same identity, completeness and financial posting semantics.
**Required for v1:** Yes.
**State:** planned; this issue is backlog, not implementation.

## Current evidence

Live inspection 2026-10-10: `main` at `a7b7484d60058708a5c32f8b3637d21f8b94a210` contains only README.md and docs/architecture/{OWNERSHIP,ACCEPTANCE}.md. No AGENTS.md, application package, migrations, tests or CI exist. Issues #1–#3 are planned work packages; PR #4 merged documentation only. No implementation or acceptance verification is claimed.

## Scope and non-goals

Build adapter interfaces and conformance fixtures for agent-harness, event-intelligence, creative-engine, print-production, fulfillment-connectors and supported development-tool provenance. Own intake normalization, not the producers execution, supplier submission or payment authorization. No dashboard rendering, product checkout/purchase authority, provider-side billing, sponsor business-plan modeling or paid provider calls are part of this issue.

## Acceptance IDs and expected outcomes

- [ ] CI-04B.1: Publish an adapter matrix with producer, emitted schema/revision, observation key, operation/transport/provider/billed-attempt mapping, usage categories, source trust, supported fields and explicit unknowns. Each of the six source classes has one valid, one invalid and one duplicate fixture through the real gateway.
- [ ] CI-04B.2: Preserve attributable model expenses, supplier quote versus incurred charge/refund, manual/infrastructure import identifiers and development commit/session evidence. A trace, Entire checkpoint or flat subscription is not itself metered usage; unsupported or unallocatable development cost is visibly unknown/unallocated, never fabricated per-token spend.
- [ ] CI-04B.3: Implement durable producer retry/ack guidance, source signatures/trusted transport at the application or connector boundary, batch item outcomes, bounded import/cursor/checkpoint behavior and replay-safe source IDs. Missing final usage and out-of-order observations are retained for reconciliation.
- [ ] CI-04B.4: Payment and supplier inputs preserve source currency/environment/billing mode/evidence mode and upstream order authorization reference where applicable. Do not call checkout, create supplier orders or mark sandbox observations as actual expenses. External adapters can use sanctioned file imports when no API contract is available.

**Global acceptance mapping:** FIN-01, FIN-02, FIN-03, FIN-04, FIN-10; supporting FUL-01, FUL-04 without assuming fulfillment ownership.

## Approach and migration implications

Normalize into shared UsageEvent/financial-event contracts using small adapters behind CI-04A. Keep raw data restricted and expose only allowlisted financial units and safe evidence refs. Store adapter version/hash on import; migration/reimport preserves original source identities. Existing boundary issues are producer dependencies, not permission for this repo to change their code. Candidate supplier behavior is documented in [Prodigi API](https://www.prodigi.com/print-api/docs/reference/) and [sandbox FAQ](https://www.prodigi.com/faq/print-api/); rates/enabled supplier selection remain external.

## Dependencies and relationships

- Parent / coverage map: [CI-EPIC / WP03 #1](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/cost-intelligence/issues/1).
- Blocked by local artifacts: [CI-04A](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/cost-intelligence/issues/10), [CI-06](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/cost-intelligence/issues/14), [CI-10](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/cost-intelligence/issues/11).
- External interface prerequisites: https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/issues/5, https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/creative-engine/issues/5, https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/event-intelligence/issues/4. These mean accepted contracts, trusted-context adapters or fixture handshakes, not completion of unrelated entire epics.
- Blocks: [CI-12 release gate](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/cost-intelligence/issues/5) Downstream local keys: [CI-11](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/cost-intelligence/issues/18). The parent graph resolves all local keys to issues.
- Related: https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/creative-engine/issues/20, https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/issues/1, https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/1.

## Executable validation

The following is the command contract to be implemented by CI-01 and this issue; these scripts do not exist at the inspected baseline and were not run during triage. Run offline against synthetic fixtures/disposable PostgreSQL, without provider credentials.

```sh
npm run test:adapters
npm run test:metering
npm run test:security
```

Replay each source fixture twice, shuffle delivery and simulate cursor interruption. Assert unchanged effective expense on duplicates, a second cost for a new billed attempt, unknown for absent details, and zero actual revenue/expense from purely simulated/sandbox commerce. Imported live-mode fixture data is synthetic test evidence, never a claim of live provider execution.

## Required evidence for closure

Six-source compatibility matrix, pinned producer fixtures and reviews, sanitized import receipts, duplicate/replay/mode-isolation results; unsupported-source and access gaps explicitly recorded. Include actual command output/exit status, tested component and contract SHAs, runtime versions, fixture/artifact hashes, environment/billing/evidence modes and limitations. Review with an affected producer and consumer where interfaces change. Do not mark global acceptance verified from documentation or issue closure alone; record evidence with the authoritative tracker owner through its normal workflow.

[Ownership](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/cost-intelligence/blob/a7b7484d60058708a5c32f8b3637d21f8b94a210/docs/architecture/OWNERSHIP.md) · [contract catalog](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/blob/main/docs/contract-catalog.md) · [architecture](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/getticketstub.com/blob/main/docs/architecture-kit/v1.0/docs/architecture.md) · [original global verification and evidence requirements](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/integration-evals/blob/main/planning/acceptance-checklist.json). Global IDs, priorities and owner roles remain unchanged; local `CI-*.n` IDs supplement them. All acceptance remains planned.

items.title: Epic: Evidence-grounded memory pipeline and maintained project briefs
items.body:
## Goal

Turn the Hindsight research into a measured, evidence-grounded Continuum roadmap without replacing Continuum's stronger lifecycle/security model or duplicating Engram's code intelligence.

Source: [Hindsight research report](https://github.com/nucleoid/openclaw-workspace/blob/main/second-brain/projects/hindsight-continuum-research-2026-10-16.md), based on `vectorize-io/hindsight@9a499b1759084a86598eff8af30ed59f7354e76c` and Continuum baseline `51fe3a8b9a133fac1969e282fcc08a3aadd96525`.

## Architecture boundary

- **Engram owns code-only architecture intelligence:** implemented symbols, flows, dependencies, contracts, and change impact.
- **Continuum owns memory semantics:** decisions, rationale, constraints, rejected alternatives, supersession, provenance, authorization, and lifecycle.
- Maintained project briefs are thin, source-neutral synthesis over authorized evidence. They distinguish implemented facts, recorded intent, and inference; cite source-memory versions and repository commit/index freshness; surface contradictions; and invalidate/refresh affected sections.
- Engram is optional. Continuum keeps full non-code utility. No Engram API is assumed.
- Continuum scope authorization never grants repository evidence access. Every stage requires the intersection of caller authority, source/assertion authority, connector authority, and residency/provider policy.

## Child work (dependency order)

- [ ] #25 — evaluation corpus and ablation harness
- [ ] #26 — assertion/source authorization and threat model (depends on #25)
- [ ] #27 — versioned evidence DAG, quarantine, and erasure (depends on #26)
- [ ] #28 — serialized context/output/deadline/spend budgets (depends on #25, #26)
- [ ] #29 — pre-final-cut reranking (depends on #25, #26, #28)
- [ ] #30 — optional source-preserving extraction (depends on #25–#28)
- [ ] #31 — event time, ingestion time, TTL, hard filters, and ranking hints (depends on #25, #27)
- [ ] #32 — optional source-neutral Engram connector/query receipts (depends on #26–#28)
- [ ] #33 — scoped maintained briefs (depends on #25–#31; #32 optional)
- [ ] #34 — bounded typed relationship expansion, only if measured (depends on #25–#29 foundations)

## Cross-cutting acceptance criteria

- Evaluation covers retrieval, extraction, synthesis, security, temporal/supersession/deletion behavior, latency, and spend with ablations and frozen fixtures.
- Persistent derivatives use versioned evidence dependencies and are synchronously quarantined after source deletion, revocation, or material change; asynchronous repair never leaves stale prose readable.
- Source-document and extracted-assertion authorization remain separate through extraction, reranking, source expansion, synthesis, cache/history/export, and optional connectors.
- Prompt injection and untrusted-source threats, repeated-source non-independence, failures/fallbacks, provider/local-only controls, resource ceilings, audit, Entra/ACL/offboarding, and erasure are explicit.
- Explicit decision supersession remains authoritative. Deterministic `AGENTS.md` output remains a separate trustworthy reference, not an LLM-maintained brief.

## Non-goals

- Replacing Continuum with Hindsight or adopting Hindsight as a backend.
- Making personality/agent dispositions the default memory model.
- Prompt-based declassification, tags as an ACL substitute, or proof count as truth probability.
- Duplicating Engram's code graph or inventing Engram APIs.
- Building a general relationship graph before measured benefit.
- Deployment, migration, infrastructure changes, or production rollout under this planning epic.

Related existing delivery work: #18, #19, #20, #21. Those issues cover transport, packaging, deployment, and UAT rather than this memory-architecture roadmap.

items.title: Feed saved sources into autopilot

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
**Goal.** Autopilot uses what Genfeed already collects. Each scheduled run of a hired Agent picks eligible unused sources (imported posts, saved competitor ads, own outlier posts, trends, long-form videos), remixes or clips them within the Agent's credit budget, and lands the results in the existing review inbox. Part of #4959.

**Status.** Foundation partly merged: source policy and reservation leaf (#5809), saved-ad reader (#5836), allocation contract (#5878). The earlier precondition #5162 (queue starvation) is closed. The two prerequisite defects (column-only platforms; proactive `create_post` draft path) are owned by #4962 / #4964 and tracked in sub-issue 2.

**Requirements that apply to every sub-issue**
- Typed, indexed lineage on every source-derived post: source kind, internal source id, remix run or clip result id, Agent id, run id. Saved-ad lineage uses the saved-ad record id.
- Zero repeat remixes of the same source by the same Agent unless the operator re-enables it.
- Source content (post text, ad copy, transcripts) is untrusted: it cannot change tools, brand, budget, platforms or publish policy. Every read is tenant-scoped (`organizationId`, `isDeleted: false`).
- Remix and clip spend counts against the Agent's remaining run budget; publishing stays under the #4964 review/graduation policy.

**Sub-issues.** Source policy and consumption records; ranked eligible sources in the brief; remix runs inside the credit budget; clip projects from long-form video; Agent home source list and hardening.

**Non-goals.** New collectors or ad-library APIs (#5092 stays Deferred, #5157), paid ad activation, changing #4964 approval policy, desktop local mode (#4966), browser-extension capture (#4340, #5108).
