labels.name: decision
labels.description: ADR or RFC — a choice to make, not code to write

milestone.title: M6 Beyond one repo
milestone.description: Multi-repo workspaces and the hosted Registry sync. Gated on the taxonomy split and a finished M1.

items.body:
> ADR. Two questions: how state is partitioned locally, and what the hosted
> version runs on. The second was raised as "single-table design on DynamoDB —
> is that a fit?"

## Local: one database per repository, and the Registry is not in it

This is already how it works (`.atlas/atlas.db` at the repo root) but it has
never been stated as a decision, and sosalejandro/atlas#115 depends on it being one.

| Plane | Where it lives | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Index** (declarations, anchors, edges) | `.atlas/atlas.db` — **one per repo** | derived and disposable; rebuilding is a scan, not a migration. Sharing one DB across repos would couple their scan lifecycles and make a partial rescan a cross-repo transaction |
| **Evidence** (coverage runs, per-test rows) | same per-repo DB | tied to a run of that repo's suite |
| **Registry** (capabilities, specs, acceptance criteria, diagrams) | **files in git**, not a database | it is authored, reviewed in pull requests, and must diff. A database would make the one human-edited plane the one thing you cannot review |
| **Views** (matrix, scores, drift) | computed, never stored as truth | reproducibility (#119) requires they be a function of the other three |

That the Registry is git-versioned files is the load-bearing decision here. It
is what lets a spec change be reviewed like code, what makes the cloud sync a
mirror rather than a source of truth, and what keeps atlas from becoming a
system of record that has to be backed up.

## Cloud: per-tenant SQL, not DynamoDB

The instinct — a database per project in the cloud, as locally — is right. The
technology proposed does not fit, for four specific reasons.

### 1. The core screen is an ad-hoc query

The matrix is filtered by state, domain, owner, repo and freshness, and sorted
by score, churn or gap. In a single-table design every one of those is a new
access pattern: a new GSI, or a scan. DynamoDB is excellent when the access
patterns are known and few; this product's main surface is the opposite by
design.

### 2. Trends are aggregations

`atlas trend` (#92) and the regulated change-impact report (#119) roll up
across capabilities and over time. That is `GROUP BY` work. In DynamoDB it
becomes either pre-computed aggregates maintained on every write (correctness
burden, backfill problem) or an export to something else that can aggregate —
at which point the second store is doing the real work.

### 3. Self-hosting is a requirement, not a preference

sosalejandro/atlas-internal#23's buyers need air-gapped or self-hosted operation, and sosalejandro/atlas-internal#24 lists a
self-hostable sync server as a differentiator against Sourcegraph withdrawing
self-hosted. **DynamoDB cannot be self-hosted** (DynamoDB Local is a test
harness, not a deployment target). Choosing it forecloses the segment with the
clearest willingness to pay.

### 4. Two data models, one maintainer

The local store is SQL with migrations and sqlc-generated code. A single-table
design means a second model, a second set of invariants, and a permanent
translation layer between them — for the same domain, maintained by the same
person.

### What to use instead

| Option | Fit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **libSQL / Turso — database per project** | **recommended** | SQLite-compatible, so the *same schema, same migrations and largely the same queries* as local. Multi-tenancy by database-per-tenant is the model it exists for, which is exactly the instinct behind the question. Embedded replicas make the desktop app's offline story simple |
| **Postgres, row-level tenancy** | solid fallback | more operational familiarity, better cross-tenant analytics, and the option every self-hosting customer already runs. Costs a dialect fork in the query layer |
| **DynamoDB single-table** | not now | correct choice for a different problem — see below |

### Where DynamoDB would earn its place

If runtime signal ingestion (#94) becomes a high-volume firehose — millions of
span-derived symbol observations per day, written constantly, read by fixed
key — that is a genuine fit: known access pattern, huge write volume, no ad-hoc
querying. That would be a **separate store for the Evidence firehose**, not the
home of the Registry and Views. Deciding it now would be premature; noting it
as the shape that would justify it is not.

## Consequences

1. `.atlas/atlas.db` per repo is a documented invariant; multi-repo (#115) fans out rather than merging stores.
2. The Registry format is a git-versioned file format with a compatibility promise, and the cloud mirrors it.
3. The hosted service is per-project SQL; the schema is shared with local, and divergence between them is a bug.
4. Self-hostability is a hard constraint on every storage decision from here.

## Revisit if

- The hosted matrix cannot be served in acceptable time from per-tenant SQL at a realistic workspace size (measure before switching).
- Cross-tenant analytics becomes a product requirement, which favours Postgres over per-tenant SQLite.
- Runtime ingestion (#94) reaches a volume where a purpose-built key-value store is the right home for that plane alone.

items.title: Spec: Uroboros engine v1 — seven capability loops over a GitHub Link

labels.name: spec
labels.description: Design/spec document — explored the design space, not the build

items.body:
## Problem Statement

A self-hosting software team runs real projects on Dev Platforms (GitHub today) and wants an autonomous coding agent working its backlog around the clock: reviewing the codebase periodically, reviewing pull requests, digging into reported issues by reproducing them, fixing the confirmed and simple ones, QA-verifying its own fixes on video, and reading feature specs against the actual implementation. Writing bespoke integration code per platform is unacceptable, and a fully autonomous agent that can merge anything is also unacceptable — a human must stay in the loop with a clear, auditable trust boundary.

No existing off-the-shelf service satisfies all of this in a self-hosted appliance form: hosted agents can't run on the team's own infrastructure and keys, and CI-based bots don't reproduce bugs, record QA videos, or expose per-project autonomy and pluggable behavior.

## Solution

**Uroboros engine v1**: a self-hosted agent service (Docker Compose: `api` + `worker` + Postgres, optional Caddy) that connects to GitHub through the official MCP server using a fine-grained PAT link, and executes the seven capability loops per connected **Project**:

1. **Periodic review** — scheduled codebase review producing a **Report**.
2. **PR review** — triggered by webhook and/or polling, delivering Findings per the Project's Autonomy Tier.
3. **Issue → reproduce → fix or propose** — confirming Bugs by reproduction, then acting strictly within the tier: comment (Observe), draft PR (Propose), ready PR + reviewer assignment (Act).
4. **QA the implementation** — `qa-verify` after fixes (Rules-enabled) and on-demand manual QA.
5. **Record video** — every QA run records a webm video, screenshots, and logs as **Artifacts**.
6. **Read features** — `feature-sweep` over in-repo docs and labeled GitHub Issues, emitting typed feature gap Findings.
7. **Pluggability** — versioned **Rules** and **Project Skills** (bases shipped by migrations), tenant **Overrides** pinned to base versions with explicit re-approval and a field-level **Delta**.

All machine judgment is bounded by the three-tier Autonomy model and the hard invariants: the agent never pushes or merges to the default branch, and every applied fix has a named human review before merge. Everything is visible through REST + SSE APIs that the (spec-first, built later) Angular dashboard will consume.

## User Stories

1. As a self-hoster (Admin), I want one-command startup (`docker compose up`) that starts the API, the Worker, and Postgres, so that Uroboros runs entirely on my own infrastructure with no external services.
2. As a self-hoster (Admin), I want an optional Caddy reverse-proxy service in the same Compose file, so that webhooks work without me assembling my own proxy setup.
3. As a self-hoster (Admin), I want first-run initialization that creates the Admin account and provisions the instance encryption key reference, so that the appliance is operable immediately and safely.
4. As a self-hoster (Admin), I want to configure the LLM provider and enter API keys through the Settings API, so that runs bill to my own provider account, never to a hosted middleman.
5. As a self-hoster (Admin), I want credentials and keys stored encrypted at rest and never returned by any read API, so that a database leak does not leak tokens.
6. As a self-hoster (Admin), I want polling ingestion to work with zero public endpoint exposure, so that Uroboros works out of the box behind NAT and firewalls.
7. As a self-hoster (Admin), I want webhook ingestion to additionally cover PR and Issue events when a public HTTPS endpoint exists, so that reactions are near-real-time without waiting for the next scan.
8. As a self-hoster (Admin), I want ongoing configuration to live in the config store rather than in env files, so that later changes never require restarting containers.
9. As a self-hoster (Admin), I want upgrades to ship new Base definitions for Rules and Project Skills via migrations, so that agent behavior improves without manual reconfiguration.
10. As an Admin, I want to create a GitHub Dev Platform Link by submitting a fine-grained PAT, so that connecting happens in minutes without any bespoke integration code.
11. As an Admin, I want Link credential validation at creation (scopes and repo access verified against the platform), so that broken links fail loudly instead of silently.
12. As an Admin, I want to create a Project from a Link's repositories with Observe tier and Base Rules applied by default, so that nothing autonomous happens before I choose to trust it.
13. As an Admin, I want a Link health surface (token validity, rate-limit status), so that failing links surface before Projects silently stop ingesting.
14. As an Admin, I want to rotate a Link's PAT without detaching Projects, so that credential rotation is a thirty-second operation.
15. As an Admin, I want to pause and resume a Project's schedules and ingestion triggers, so that noisy or frozen repos stop consuming compute.
16. As an Admin, I want to delete a Project together with its Runs and Artifacts, so that offboarded repos stop costing storage.
17. As an Admin, I want to authenticate through local credentials, an OAuth provider, or my organization's OIDC SSO, so that access fits my team's existing identity posture.
18. As a Viewer, I want read-only access to Projects, Runs, Reports, Artifacts, and Insights by default, so that I can follow everything without being able to mutate anything.
19. As an Admin, I want OAuth and SSO logins to map to the Viewer role via configuration (default Viewer), so that human-check assignees can log in without me hand-creating accounts.
20. As an Admin, I want to trigger a Run manually (periodic review, manual QA, feature sweep) through the API, so that I can exercise the loops on demand before or without waiting for triggers.
21. As an Admin, I want every Run to carry provenance (webhook, polling scan, schedule, manual), so that I can reason about where churn originates.
22. As an Admin, I want concurrent Runs per Project capped (default one active) with additional same-subject triggers collapsed, so that provider spend and platform rate limits stay sane.
23. As a Viewer, I want to watch a Run's progress live via SSE with its event timeline, so that I see what the agent is doing right now, not just afterwards.
24. As a Viewer, I want every Run's step history retained and queryable, so that I can audit what happened long after it completed.
25. As a repo maintainer, I want periodic review output delivered as a Report summarizing Findings, so that codebase health review arrives without anyone remembering to ask.
26. As a repo maintainer, I want incoming PRs reviewed with Findings delivered per the Project's tier (review comments under Observe, plus change proposals under Propose/Act), so that feedback lands where my team already works.
27. As a repo maintainer, I want reported Issues investigated by reproduction attempt before any fix proposal, so that the agent's claims are evidence-backed rather than patch-and-pray.
28. As a repo maintainer, I want confirmed Bugs fixed within the tier — comments under Observe, draft PRs under Propose, ready PRs under Act gated by "fix if simple" Rules — so that autonomy is explicit and gradual.
29. As a repo maintainer, I want a Request For Human Review (comment plus reviewer request on the platform) raised when the agent's work needs human eyes, with the request mirrored into the Pending Review queue, so that checks surface both where I work and on the dashboard.
30. As a repo maintainer, I want the human-check assignee to default to the issue or PR author with a configurable reviewer override in Rules, so that requests reach someone by default.
31. As an Admin, I want the Autonomy Tier changed only by an explicit audited action, so that nobody can silently widen the agent's permissions.
32. As an Admin, I want the hard invariants enforced structurally — no pushes or merges to the default branch in any tier, human review before every merge — so that the trust boundary does not depend on prompts.
33. As a Viewer, I want QA runs recorded: webm video, screenshots, and logs stored as Artifacts, so that I can watch exactly what the agent saw and did.
34. As a Viewer, I want Artifact downloads through short-lived signed URLs, so that artifact access is auditable and not link-shareable forever.
35. As an Admin, I want `qa-verify` runs automatically following fixes when Rules enable them, so that every proposed fix arrives with verification evidence.
36. As an Admin, I want manual QA Runs triggerable per Project, so that I can verify anything on demand.
37. As an Admin, I want feature sweeps reading in-repo markdown specs plus labeled GitHub Issues, so that documented intent is checked against the implementation.
38. As an Admin, I want feature sweep results as typed Findings (implemented / partial / missing / mismatch) delivered per tier, so that the output is actionable rather than prose.
39. As an Admin, I want to inspect and change a Project's Rules through the API, so that per-Project behavior (schedules, scopes, triggers, tier) is manageable without code.
40. As an Admin, I want to create Project Skill Overrides that route execution to a custom version without replacing the Base, so that my customization is reversible and upgradeable.
41. As an Admin, I want Overrides pinned to the Base version they were created against, so that a shipped Base upgrade never silently changes my customized behavior.
42. As an Admin, I want a field-level structured Delta between a pinned Base and its newer version, plus explicit re-approval to re-route, so that upgrades are conscious decisions, not surprises.
43. As an Admin, I want tool whitelists per Skill enforced at Run assembly, so that Skill changes can never widen the agent's powers invisibly.
44. As a Viewer, I want a Fix Success Rate metric (merged agent fixes that never regress), so that I can quantify whether the agent actually helps.
45. As a Viewer, I want Regressed Bugs detected (previously fixed, then re-detected by file plus failure signature) and visible, so that fragile fixes surface immediately rather than hiding behind green checks
46. As a Viewer, I want Problematic Code Portions ranked by Findings density and QA failures, so that refactoring attention is data-driven.
47. As a Viewer, I want pending Requests For Human Review listed in one queue with resolution status, so that waiting-for-human work never gets lost.
48. As an Admin, I want failed Runs clearly marked with failure evidence and manually re-runnable, so that transient failures don't strand work.
49. As an Admin, I want to cancel a stuck Run, so that a wedged agent never holds a Project's concurrency slot hostage.
50. As a Viewer, I want usage metrics per Project (Run count by type, tokens per Run), so that I can see what the appliance costs in practice.

## Implementation Decisions

All decisions below implement the recorded ADRs; the ADRs remain the "why", this section the "what".

**Architecture (per ADR-0011)** — three apps and six packages, each an architectural seam: `api` (REST + SSE server; also serves the built web statics later), `worker` (run orchestrator; spawns ephemeral run containers), `web` (Angular v22 dashboard — spec-first, not built in this spec), `domain` (shared Zod schemas + DTO contracts), `persistence` (schema, entities, queries on Postgres), `job-queue` (queue + scheduler on Postgres), `agent-core` (AI SDK v5 loop, tool assembly), `platform-mcp` (Link → MCP client factory; GitHub adapter first), `qa-runtime` (Playwright QA driver + video capture).

**Self-hosting & data (ADR-0002)** — Compose ships api, worker, Postgres, and optional Caddy. Postgres is the only datastore: entities, queue, schedules, audit events, and Insights aggregations. No Redis, no message bus. Single-org schema: no tenant identifiers anywhere. Minimal env surface: instance encryption key, webhook base URL, database connection (wired by Compose).

**Ingestion — both modes (ADR-0008)** — Webhook endpoint per Link: HMAC signature verification against the Link secret, delivery-id deduplication, event-type routing (PR opened/updated, PR closed with merge status, review submitted/commented, Issue opened/updated/labeled) — the closed/review events feed RHR resolution mirroring and the Bug proposed→fixed transition that Insights reads. Polling fallback always on: per-Project scan interval (Rules-configurable, default 15 min) sweeping open PRs and Issues since the last scan marker. Trigger collapsing: a new trigger for a subject with a queued/running Run for the same PR head SHA or Issue joins that Run instead of spawning another.

**Run model (new)** — A Run is one agent execution: identity = Project, Run Type (`review`, `pr-review`, `issue-fix`, `qa-verify`, `qa-manual`, `feature-sweep`), Trigger, Subject (PR, Issue, repo path scope, or none), Status, and an append-only event log (step events, Findings raised, Requests For Human Review, platform mutations). Status set: `queued`, `running`, `needs-review` (RHR issued, work stops until resolved), `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`. Concurrency: at most one active Run per Project; a hard execution timeout (env-configurable, default 30 min) applies.

**Execution isolation (ADR-0003)** — The worker executes each Run inside an ephemeral container: repository cloned in, network egress restricted to package registries plus the Dev Platform MCP, filesystem destroyed after the Run. Link credentials are never mounted into run containers; platform access from inside a Run happens through the engine's brokered tool layer. QA (browser driving + video capture) happens inside this same container via the qa-runtime package.

**Agent loop (agent-core)** — Built on AI SDK v5: a provider-abstracted tool-calling loop (`stopWhen`-bounded), tools assembled per Run = Dev Platform MCP tools + read/repo-execution tools, filtered by the Project Skills' tool whitelists. Run behavior is shaped by: Run Type contract text (code), Rules (structured), and matching Skills (instructions). Model selection: instance-level provider + model in Settings; per-Project model overrides are out of scope. Run lifecycle events are written to the Run's event log and pushed live over SSE.

**Dev Platform surface (platform-mcp)** — One normalized command surface (open/find PRs and Issues, read diffs and files, create branch, commit, open draft or ready PR, comment, request review, apply/get labels, read repo file tree) implemented by mapping to the GitHub MCP server's tools. Only the GitHub adapter ships in v1; the normalized surface is the only thing agent-core sees, so wave-2 platforms implement the same seam without touching the loop. The test fake implements this same surface with a mutation journal.

**Trust model (ADR-0004)** — Rules carry the Autonomy Tier; enforcement is structural, not prompt-based: the tier filters which platform commands are callable (comment/report always; draft PR only Propose+; ready PR + reviewer request only Act, additionally gated by the fix-if-simple constraint). The default-branch invariant is enforced in the command layer (writes to the default branch are rejected outright at any tier). Every tier and Rules change is an audited Event.

**Human check (RHR)** — A Run needing human eyes flips to `needs-review`, raises a platform comment + reviewer request via the platform surface, mirrors an entry into the Pending Review set, and stops. Resolution happens on the platform (review verdict / reply) and is mirrored back into the Run record on the next ingestion or webhook receipt. Default assignee: subject (issue/PR) author; Rules may name a fixed reviewer.

**Config store — bases, overrides, deltas (ADR-0009)** — Rules and Project Skills are Postgres rows: definitions carried versioned by migration-seeded **Bases** and optionally a per-Project Override row that stores the Project's custom version plus pinned base version. Overrides are only re-routed onto a newer base by explicit re-approval. The Delta is a structured field-level summary computed by comparing definition versions (field name + change + human-readable value), returned by a dedicated API endpoint — never a code diff, never AI-generated prose. Structure: Rules fields (schedule, scan interval, path scopes, tier, fix-if-simple constraint, QA trigger modes, feature sweep sources as doc globs + label names, max fix attempts, reviewer override); Skills are versioned instruction definitions + tool whitelist + Run Type matcher.

**QA & video (qa-runtime)** — Playwright-driven against a locally served build inside the run container, per Run Type contract — v1 records run only against builds the container serves itself; QA against platform preview URLs waits for a Rules-configured egress allowlist. Records: webm video, screenshots at step boundaries, console/network log capture. Artifacts are written to a shared volume; the Artifacts entity references them; the API serves them through short-lived signed URLs (instance-key HMAC, default TTL 15 min). A storage adapter seam keeps the door open for S3-compatible storage later; v1 ships volume-only.

**Findings → Bugs → Regressed Bugs (Insights foundation)** — Findings are surfaced state: `candidate`, `confirmed` (reproduction or verification succeeded; promoted to a Bug with file list + normalized failure signature), `proposed` (fix PR/branch opened), `fixed` (merged), `rejected`, `duplicate`. A Regressed Bug is a Bug previously marked fixed whose file plus failure signature is matched again by a later Run's evidence; matching is exact file + normalized signature in v1 (fuzzy matching deliberately out of scope). Insights metrics are computed from these entities only: Fix Success Rate = merged fix PRs without a later regression over all fix PRs; Problematic Code Portions = files/paths ranked by Findings density plus QA failure counts; usage = Run counts by type and recorded token usage per Run.

**Auth & roles (ADR-0007)** — Local bootstrap admin (created at Setup), optional OAuth provider logins, optional OIDC SSO discovery. Sessions via HTTP-only cookies. Roles: Admin (all mutations incl. Links, keys, Rules, Overrides, tier changes) and Viewer (read-only + can see Pending Review). OAuth/SSO logins map to Viewer by default with per-user role assignment configurable.

**API shape** — REST + SSE, validated at the seam by shared domain schemas: Link CRUD with credential validation; Project CRUD incl. pause/resume, tier change, Rules + Skills inspection/override/re-approval, Delta endpoint; manual Run trigger; Run list/detail/event-log/retry/cancel; Report and Artifact retrieval (302 to signed URL); Insights endpoints (fix success rate, regressed bugs, problematic portions, usage); Pending Review list; Setup and auth (login, OAuth callback, OIDC). SSE channel per Run exposing the live event log with monotonic sequence numbers.

**Audit events** — Append-only Events for: tier changes, Rules/Skill override creation and re-approval, key/credential rotation, manual Run triggers, RHR issued and resolved, run failures. Actor + timestamp + payload on each.

## Testing Decisions

**What makes a good test here** — Tests assert externally observable behavior only, through the confirmed seams; they never assert internal calls or module structure. A passing test means: a real HTTP request into the api produced the right SSE stream, the right Postgres state, the right mutations on the platform edge, and the right artifact responses.

**Seam 1 — API boundary (primary, the single engine seam)** — Drive `api` over HTTP+REST/SSE with four doubles standing in for the outside world:
- a **deterministic mock LLM** (scripted model responses per scenario) — provider integration is a plugin boundary to fake, not to test;
- a **fake Dev Platform MCP server** — in-process, stateful (repos, branches, PRs, issues, labels, reviews), implementing the exact normalized command surface the real GitHub adapter does, and journaling every mutation for assertion;
- a **stub run executor** — replaces ephemeral containers; pretends to clone/execute and returns fixed outputs, so the orchestration contract is tested without Docker;
- **real Postgres** — the source of truth for queue, runs, findings, and audit; schema reset per test run.

Canonical test shapes: webhook POST → Run appears queued → SSE shows steps → fake platform journal contains the tier-allowed mutation and NOT a forbidden one (e.g. no default-branch write, no merge under Propose); issue loop → confirmed Bug row + RHR raised when the double's scripted reproduction fails after max fix attempts; Rules override → Delta endpoint returns the structured field summary; tier change → audited Event present; Insights reflect the Run history it was fed.

**Seam 2 — qa-runtime fixture (narrow, only where Seam 1 can't see)** — qa-runtime exercised against a small local static fixture page with a real headless browser: asserts the recorded artifact set is a valid webm with frame progression, screenshots exist per scripted step, and captured console/network logs match the fixture's scripted behavior. Everything else about QA (triggering, storage, serving) is asserted through Seam 1.

**Modules under test** — api (with persistence + job-queue + agent-core + platform-mcp assembled behind it) across both seams; the fake platform double is itself contract-tested against the normalized command surface so the real GitHub adapter implements the same interface.

**Prior art** — none yet (fresh repo); this spec establishes the harness. First deliverable of testing is the double set (mock LLM, fake platform MCP, stub executor) since every other test depends on it. bun:test with per-test schema reset is the pattern in CLAUDE.md.

## Out of Scope

- **Angular dashboard implementation** — screens are spec-first per ADR-0006; this spec builds the REST/SSE surface it will consume, nothing in the UI layer.
- **Azure DevOps and Jira Links** — wave two (ADR-0010); the normalized platform surface is built for swappability, no second adapter ships.
- **GitHub App identity** — fine-grained PAT Links only in v1.
- **Hosted SaaS** — multi-tenant schema, billing, public sign-up (ADR-0002).
- **Tenant code plugins** — Rules + Project Skills only (ADR-0005).
- **Email/Slack/web notifications** — RHR surfaces on the platform + API only.
- **Fuzzy bug matching** for Regressed Bugs — exact file + normalized signature only.
- **Per-Project LLM model overrides** — instance-level provider/model only.
- **Non-GitHub webhook sources**; artifact streaming/CDN; K8s/Helm; HA/clustering; i18n.
- **QA against platform preview URLs** — v1 quality gates run against locally served builds only; preview-URL QA arrives with a Rules-configured egress allowlist.

## Further Notes

- **Decision record**: ADR-0001…0011 at the repo root document every architectural decision referenced above; the two glossaries (engine + dashboard) define every capitalized noun used in this spec. Engine vocabulary governs naming in code, APIs, and events.
- **Trigger collapsing** (story 22) is the main defense against trigger storms; polling's scan marker makes the fallback naturally idempotent.
- **`needs-review` is a terminal-until-resolved state**: a Run never proceeds past an RHR without mirrored human action — this is the workflow expression of the Act tier and the hard invariants.
- **The fake Dev Platform double doubles as a product artifact**: wave-2 adapters will build against the same normalized surface the fake implements, so the test harness is also the platform-portability contract.
- Suggested follow-up after implementation lands: break this spec into sub-issues per capability loop if implementation is delegated piecemeal; the dashboard spec is a separate upcoming issue.

items.title: Add in-app GitHub disconnect that stops ingestion cleanly

milestone.title: M5 — Startup MVP
milestone.description: Week 18: production operations and Startup MVP validation gate (roadmap §42).

items.body:
# Add in-app GitHub disconnect that stops ingestion cleanly

## Parent epic

Relates to: #3 (EPIC-003 GitHub App Lifecycle). Also satisfies part of §J under #15 (EPIC-015).

## Roadmap source

- Document: skeleton_v3_mvp.md
- Section: §17 Week 2 ("Add reconnect and disconnect"); Week 12 ("Add repository disconnect", acceptance: "Disconnect stops collection"); §42.2 group J ("disconnect")
- Week: 18 gate (MVP hardening)
- Milestone: M5 — Startup MVP

## User problem

An organization admin who wants to stop observing their GitHub data currently has no in-product way to disconnect — they would have to uninstall the App from GitHub's UI and trust that our side noticed. For a product whose trust posture is anti-surveillance and least-privilege, "you can leave cleanly from inside the product" is table stakes and a §J gate item.

## Desired outcome

An org admin can disconnect GitHub from the workspace settings: ingestion stops immediately, installation state is marked disconnected, the action is audited, and the UI clearly explains — in plain language, before the admin confirms — what stops, what stays, and how to come back. Already-ingested data is retained (workspace deletion remains the way to erase it) and every surface makes clear the picture is no longer updating.

## Scope

- Disconnect action in workspace settings, admin-only, with confirm step and plain-language consequences copy
- Server-side: mark installation disconnected, stop processing future webhooks/backfills for that installation, revoke/forget installation credentials where applicable
- Audit event for the disconnect (§A audit baseline)
- Integration-health surface reflects disconnected state; reconnect path is the existing self-serve connect flow
- Handling of the GitHub-side uninstall webhook remains consistent with in-app disconnect (one converged state)

## Non-goals

- Data deletion (already shipped as workspace deletion; the disconnect copy links to it)
- Per-repository observation control (that is the repository selector, #44)
- Linear/import-source disconnect
- Automatically uninstalling the App on GitHub's side (see open question OQ-42-1; default product behavior is to link out to GitHub's settings)
- Plain-language rendering of audit-trail entries (the existing audit card shows action codes; unchanged here)

---

## Product specification (Stage 1 — completed 2026-07-25)

### Where it lives

Dashboard → Workspace settings (disclosure) → Source · GitHub card. The disconnect control sits at the bottom of that card, visually separated from routine controls (Sync history, delivery health). Note for design: the issue's "settings → integrations → GitHub" phrasing maps to this existing card; whether to break settings out into a dedicated page is design latitude, not a product requirement.

This card is the shared surface with the repository selector (#44). Order within the card: connection status → observed repositories (#44) → delivery health → disconnect.

### Who sees what (permissions)

- Owner and admin: see and can use "Disconnect GitHub". (Connect already allows owner/admin; disconnect is reversible, so admin — not owner-only like workspace deletion.)
- Member: sees connection status only. No disabled button, no destructive control at all.
- Server enforces owner/admin membership on the resolved organization; the org ID from the browser is never trusted alone (ADR-003).

### Confirmation step — behavior and copy

Clicking "Disconnect GitHub" does nothing destructive; it reveals an inline confirm panel (consistent with the existing Danger-zone inline pattern — the app has no modal system). No typed confirmation is required because the action is reversible (unlike workspace deletion). The panel states, in this order, outcome-first:

> **Disconnect GitHub from this workspace?**
>
> - We immediately stop receiving anything new from **github/{account}**.
> - What you already see stays. Your dashboards keep the history collected so far, clearly marked as no longer updating.
> - **Nothing is deleted.** To erase collected data, delete the workspace (link to Danger zone) — that removes everything.
> - You can reconnect any time from this page. Observation resumes from the moment you reconnect.
> - This does not remove the app from GitHub itself. To remove its access there too, uninstall it in your GitHub settings (link to the installation's settings page).
>
> [Yes, disconnect GitHub]  [Cancel]

Cancel (or collapsing the panel) changes nothing. Copy must never use surveillance language ("monitoring", "tracking your team"); it is always about observing repositories and work.

### What happens on confirm

1. Button shows a pending state ("Disconnecting…"); the panel's controls are disabled while pending.
2. On success, the Source card switches to the disconnected state (below), and the audit trail gains an entry recording who disconnected and when.
3. On failure, an inline error: "Couldn't disconnect. Nothing changed — try again." The connection state must be unchanged on failure (no half-disconnected state visible to the user).

### Post-disconnect state (honest, not alarming)

- Source card: "GitHub disconnected on {date}." with a Reconnect control that is the existing connect flow (Install on GitHub link + Connect GitHub button). Sync history control is gone. Delivery-health counters no longer imply live observation — replaced by the disconnected notice.
- Dashboard status line (ticker): shows the source as disconnected (e.g. "source github/{account} · disconnected") instead of the active badge.
- All data surfaces (dashboard tiles, repositories, pulse, brief, risk): keep showing what was collected, with one clear workspace-level notice: "GitHub is disconnected — this picture stopped updating on {date}." The brief and pulse must include this framing so a non-technical reader never mistakes frozen data for current truth.
- No escalating alarms from frozen data: after disconnect the product must not keep producing ever-worse time-based warnings (e.g. a PR "stale for 45 days" climbing daily) as if observation were live. Signals present the state as of the disconnect date. (How to achieve this is design — see OQ-42-2.)

### Webhooks that keep arriving (app still installed on GitHub)

- Acknowledged but not processed into tenant data. No new PRs, events, or signals appear.
- These ignored deliveries must NOT show up as failures or unprocessed counts in the delivery-health UI or dead-letter queue — a disconnected workspace should look calm, not broken.

### Reconnect

- Same self-serve connect flow that exists today (identity-matched installation).
- After reconnect, observation resumes from that moment. The product does not silently paper over the gap: the Source card offers Sync history with copy like "We weren't observing between {d1} and {d2}. Sync history to fill in what we missed."
- If #44 has shipped: reconnect re-runs the repository selection step, pre-filled with the previously remembered selection, and requires the admin to confirm it (see coordination below).
- If the app was uninstalled on GitHub in the meantime, the connect flow's existing error path applies ("No installation found… Install the app on your repositories first").

### Converged states (in-app disconnect vs GitHub-side uninstall)

One disconnected end-state, but the health copy names the cause truthfully:

- Disconnected in-app: "GitHub disconnected on {date}."
- Uninstalled on GitHub (existing installation-deleted webhook): "The app was uninstalled on GitHub on {date}."

Disconnecting twice, or disconnecting after a GitHub-side uninstall (either order), converges to a single coherent disconnected state with no error shown to the user.

### UI states checklist

- Loading/pending: "Disconnecting…" on the confirm button; controls disabled.
- Error: inline, state unchanged, retryable.
- Permission denied: members never see the control; a forged request is rejected server-side with no state change.
- Empty/partial: if the workspace had little or no data before disconnect, the frozen-data notice still shows the disconnect date; surfaces fall back to their existing empty states.

### Analytics and audit events

There is no separate product-analytics stack; the durable record is audit events plus structured logs (this satisfies §42.5 "critical workflows have analytics" — flagging this mapping rather than inventing a new pipeline):

- Audit event on disconnect (suggested name: github.disconnected) with actor and installation account/id — visible in the existing audit-trail card.
- Reconnect is already covered by the existing github.installation_linked audit event.
- Structured log line + counter distinguishing "delivery ignored: disconnected" from real failures.

### Coordination with #44 (repository selector)

- Deselecting all repositories is NOT disconnect: it keeps the connection alive and shows the selector's "observing nothing" state. Disconnect severs the source. The two states have distinct copy and each points at the other's control.
- After disconnect the repository selection is remembered but inert; the selector UI is hidden or read-only in the disconnected state.

---

## User journey

1. Admin opens the dashboard → Workspace settings → Source · GitHub.
2. Clicks Disconnect GitHub; reads the plain-language consequences panel; confirms.
3. Source card shows disconnected with the date; the dashboard shows the frozen-data notice; the audit trail records who and when.
4. New GitHub activity (pushes, PRs) no longer appears anywhere; delivery health shows no failure noise.
5. Later, the admin reconnects via the same card; observation resumes; Sync history is offered to fill the gap.

## Functional requirements

- [ ] Owner/admin-only disconnect with inline confirmation and the consequences copy above (non-admin sees no destructive control)
- [ ] Post-disconnect webhook deliveries for that installation are acknowledged but not processed into tenant data
- [ ] Installation/backfill jobs for the installation halt; Sync history unavailable while disconnected
- [ ] Audit event recorded; Source card, ticker, and data surfaces reflect the disconnected + frozen state; reconnect works via existing flow and offers history sync
- [ ] No new or escalating time-based signals produced from frozen data after disconnect

## Failure and edge cases

- [ ] Disconnect while a backfill job is mid-flight: job halts or completes without writing post-disconnect data — behavior defined and tested
- [ ] Double disconnect / disconnect after GitHub-side uninstall (either order): idempotent, single converged state, no user-facing error
- [ ] Webhook for a disconnected installation must not error-loop, dead-letter-spam, or inflate failure counters in the health UI
- [ ] Disconnect server failure: user sees inline error; connection state unchanged
- [ ] Reconnect when the app was uninstalled on GitHub: existing "install first" error path

## Security and privacy requirements

- [ ] Tenant authorization enforced server-side (owner/admin of the owning org; never trust org ID from browser)
- [ ] Credentials for the installation unusable by this product after disconnect
- [ ] Plain-language privacy copy: what stops, what is retained, how to delete (workspace deletion), and that GitHub-side access removal is a separate step

## Observability requirements

- [ ] Structured log + audit event for disconnect with actor and installation
- [ ] Metric/log distinguishing "delivery ignored: disconnected" from failures

## Technical design

To be completed by Architect Agent.

### Affected components

### Data flow

### Schema changes

### API/interface changes

### Authorization model

### Idempotency and retry

### Migration

### Rollback

## Test plan

### Unit

### Integration

### End-to-end

### Security

### Regression

## Acceptance criteria (user-facing)

- [ ] An owner/admin sees "Disconnect GitHub" in the Source · GitHub card; a member sees no disconnect control at all
- [ ] Clicking shows the plain-language consequences (what stops, what stays, nothing deleted, reconnect anytime, GitHub-side note) BEFORE anything happens; Cancel leaves everything unchanged
- [ ] After confirming: the Source card shows disconnected with the date, and new GitHub activity does not appear anywhere in the workspace
- [ ] Deliveries arriving after disconnect do not appear as failures or unprocessed counts in delivery health
- [ ] The audit trail records who disconnected and when
- [ ] Dashboards keep showing pre-disconnect data with a clear "stopped updating on {date}" notice, and do not keep escalating time-based warnings
- [ ] Reconnect via the existing connect flow works; the observation gap is disclosed and Sync history is offered
- [ ] Disconnecting twice, or after a GitHub-side uninstall, lands in one coherent disconnected state with no error

## Demo script

1. As an admin, open Workspace settings → Source · GitHub, click Disconnect GitHub, show the consequences copy, cancel once (nothing changes), then confirm.
2. Show the disconnected Source card, the frozen-data notice on the dashboard, and the audit event.
3. Open an issue / push a commit on the still-installed repo — show nothing new is ingested and delivery health shows no failure noise.
4. As a member, show the settings card has no disconnect control.
5. Reconnect; show observation resumes and Sync history fills the gap.

## Dependencies

## Risks

- Webhook-path change touches the ingestion hot path — regression risk on live production ingestion; requires careful review (webhooks are on the mandatory distinct-agents list in agents.md §3).

- Program: done (this issue)

items.body:
## Triage record

- **Stable key:** FC-01
- **Owner role:** Creative and fulfillment; reviewer: Agent and research. Named owner/reviewer remain kickoff decisions.
- **Priority:** P0 — Every adapter needs a reproducible, versioned safe boundary.
- **Required for v1:** Yes, mock + selected sandbox release; live excluded.
- **Status:** Planned; backlog only.

## Current evidence

Inspected live GitHub 2026-10-10 at main [4c78849754ed542ca77d3b5e1831f8773f9b54b4](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/commit/4c78849754ed542ca77d3b5e1831f8773f9b54b4). The complete tree contains only README.md, docs/architecture/OWNERSHIP.md and ACCEPTANCE.md; all three were read. No AGENTS.md, runtime, lockfile, tests, workflows, adapters or migrations exist. README explicitly says documentation baseline only. Existing #1 is WP08; merged documentation PR #2 verifies no implementation. Acceptance remains planned.

## Scope / non-goals

Create a worker-consumable package, pinned runtime/lockfile, clean build and offline test command. Inject transport, clock, persistence, authorization verifier, budget client and usage sink. No new standalone service or commercial-order state machine.

## Acceptance IDs and expected outcome

- [ ] FC-01.1: Type capability discovery, quote request/normalization, pre-submit validation, order submit, status retrieval, shipment/tracking observation and cancellation/unsupported results. Declare provider/mode/API version, product limits, operation support, side-effect and idempotency semantics. Unsupported is never silent success.
- [ ] FC-01.2: Errors contain module, operation, typed code, safe message, diagnostic reference, retryability and side_effect_state (not_dispatched/possible/confirmed/unknown). Distinguish invalid input, unsupported, stale quote/auth, rate limit, timeout and ambiguous submission. Retryability grants no spending authority.
- [ ] FC-01.3: Validate shared envelope, trusted tenant scope and schema versions at every boundary; reject unsupported majors and define additive/old-consumer behavior. Offline is default; live endpoints cannot activate implicitly. Publish the stable verification wrapper and machine-readable results; missing suites fail, never skip green.

Mapping: FC-01.1–4; supports CON-01/02/03 and contributes to FUL-01–04. Local cases supplement original global procedures; integrated FUL owners are listed in FC-12 #16.

## Approach and migration implications

Record runtime/package choice compatible with the application worker at kickoff. Own only connector migrations with install/upgrade/recovery instructions coordinated by application assembly. Define ./scripts/verify-fulfillment --suite NAME --mode simulated|sandbox --evidence-dir PATH as the stable runner; exact locked install/build commands must be documented by implementation.

## Blocked-by / blocks / related links

- Parent: [FC-EPIC](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/1).
- Blocked by local prerequisites: None; begin from inspected documentation.
- Upstream accepted contracts/artifacts: [shared-contracts/issues/5](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/5), [shared-contracts/issues/6](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/6), [shared-contracts/issues/7](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/7), [shared-contracts/issues/9](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/9)
- Blocks: [FC-11](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/5), [FC-10](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/6), [FC-02-MOCK](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/7), [FC-03](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/8), [FC-04](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/9), [FC-08](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/10), [FC-06](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/11), [FC-05](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/12), [FC-07](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/13), [FC-12](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/16).
- Fixtures can unblock development; closure needs scoped accepted upstream artifacts, not unrelated epic completion.

## Executable validation

From a clean checkout install locked dependencies, build, then run the suite. Exercise all operations with a fake transport, valid/invalid/additive/old-version fixtures; assert rejected input causes zero outbound calls and unsupported cancellation is typed.

```sh
./scripts/verify-fulfillment --suite contract --mode simulated --evidence-dir evidence/FC-01
```

## Required evidence for closure

Runtime/lockfile/build output; interface and capability spec; producer/consumer review; compatibility fixtures and test report.

Closure requires reviewed implementation links, exact component SHAs and contract/runtime versions, actual commands and exit results, sanitized fixtures/assertions, relevant trace/attempt/artifact references, and explicit environment plus billing_mode (simulated/sandbox/live). Keep full addresses, contact details, secrets, auth tokens, signed asset URLs and raw provider errors out of public evidence. Missing evidence stays pending. The command below is a future implementation requirement: no runner exists or was executed during triage.

Shared schema ownership stays in [shared-contracts](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/blob/main/docs/contract-catalog.md); preserve the [master acceptance IDs, procedures, priorities and evidence](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/integration-evals/blob/main/planning/acceptance-checklist.json). FC-* IDs are local additions. No payment capture, checkout, authorization issuance, creative generation, financial ledger or final profitability belongs here. No provider call or charge is authorized by this triage.

## Shared contract shape ownership addendum

- [ ] FC-01.4: Maintain an explicit ownership table for every cross-repository payload.

| Public shape | Schema owner | Fulfillment-connectors role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Operation request/result envelope, versioned capability and print specification, preflight/validation report | [shared-contracts](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/4), coordinated with [print-production #5](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/issues/5) | Validate and consume the accepted shape; publish provider results only through its versioned contract |
| ProductionBundle | [shared-contracts #24](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/24) | Consume the immutable approved bundle and its pinned schema/fixtures |
| FulfillmentQuote | [shared-contracts #25](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/25) | Produce normalized quotes conforming to the accepted schema |
| OrderAuthorization | [shared-contracts #26](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/26); issuer remains the application | Consume and verify the external authorization; never issue or broaden it |
| Shipment/status observation | [shared-contracts #27](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/27) | Produce normalized observations conforming to the accepted schema |
| Provider SDK classes, private transport payloads and private adapter models | fulfillment-connectors | Own and keep private to this repository |

Coordinate contract intake with print-production #5 and shared-contracts #4; a repository issue or catalog proposal does not itself prove that a schema is accepted. Before closure, record the accepted shared-contracts issue and exact schema/version, fixture revision and digest, producer/consumer review, and compatibility result for each public shape. Any additional public shape without an accepted owner and pin remains a release blocker; do not create a competing local schema.

Run the same pinned contract snapshot and fixture bytes in the owning producer repository and the connector conformance suite. Record both repository revisions and matching expected results. Include both reports and cross-repository schema/fixture pins in FC-01 closure evidence. This addendum clarifies FC-01.1–4 and does not claim implementation.

---

## Triage normalization — 2026-10-10

_Added by org triage. The original content above is kept unchanged. This section maps it to the org issue template._

### Context
Partial runtime foundation merged in PR #17: `npm test` and `./scripts/verify-fulfillment --suite contract --mode simulated` now exist and pass on main (35/35 contract cases at triage). Acceptance stays open pending accepted shared-contracts schema pins and producer/consumer conformance. _(triage: inferred from repository state on 2026-10-10)_

### Scope / Non-goals
See **Scope / non-goals** above.

### Acceptance criteria
See the checkbox list under **Acceptance IDs and expected outcome** above and the shared-contract addendum.

items.body:
## 0. Why this exists — at a glance

Running a multi-layer dead-code sweep on `main` (HEAD `d3b2d4fe`) surfaced a handful of orphan DB tables, API routes with no FE/worker caller, and unused service helpers. None of these are urgent, but each one is **load-bearing complexity without external value**: extra surface for security review, extra confusion for new engineers, extra friction when running schema migrations or RLS hardening.

This issue collects the findings so the team can decide, per cluster, whether to **(a) finish wiring the feature**, **(b) delete the dead surface**, or **(c) keep it parked behind a flag with a follow-up date**.

> Methodology: 4 parallel `Explore` agents on disjoint surfaces (DB schema vs runtime refs · API routes vs FE/worker callers · service exports vs importers · `page.tsx` vs nav/links). Tests, migrations, and `docs/` excluded from "reference" counts. Some FE callers may use dynamic path construction the grep missed — **verify before deleting**.

---

## 1. DB layer — orphan tables (5)

Defined in schema, **zero runtime references** (excluding tests + migrations):

| Table | Definition | Likely status |
|---|---|---|
| `exchange_rates` | `packages/shared/src/schema/index.ts:592` | ADR-032 multi-currency, pre-implementation |
| `receipt_sequences` | `packages/shared/src/schema/index.ts:1051` | **No doc anchor — strongest "abandoned" candidate** |
| `camt_statements` | `packages/shared/src/schema/swiss-qr-bill.ts:291` | ADR-028 / docs/25, ingestion worker not yet wired |
| `camt_credit_entries` | `packages/shared/src/schema/swiss-qr-bill.ts:342` | same |
| `camt_unreconciled_entries` | `packages/shared/src/schema/swiss-qr-bill.ts:395` | same |

**Low-use tables (1–2 refs)** — 20 tables across disputes, postal-export, bulk-import, surveys, pledges. Single-owner domain tables; architecturally normal, **not flagged as dead**.

---

## 2. API layer — routes with no FE/worker caller

Agent flagged ~48 routes. Filtering out external callers leaves the genuine candidates below.

### False positives (called from outside the repo — keep)
- `POST /donations/stripe-webhook` — Stripe
- `POST /session/backchannel-logout` — Keycloak
- `GET /invitations/:token/probe`, `POST /public/signup/dispute`, `POST /public/tenants/lookup` — public / email-link entry points

### Genuine orphan-API candidates

| Route | Suspected reason |
|---|---|
| `GET /constituents/bulk-import/template` | template-download likely served as a static asset |
| `GET /constituents/bulk-import/:id/download` / `:id/results` | UI may use a different shape |
| `GET /constituents/duplicates/search` | merge UI exists; duplicate-search endpoint unwired |
| `GET /campaigns/:id/roi`, `GET /campaigns/:id/stats` | campaign detail page doesn't render ROI/stats yet |
| `GET /campaigns/:id/funds`, `GET/PUT /campaigns/:id/public-page` | linked surfaces exist but GET may be redundant |
| `POST /pledges`, `GET /pledges/:id/installments` | **no `/pledges` page exists — entire pledges surface unreachable** |
| `GET /reports/lybunt`, `GET /reports/sybunt` | **no `/reports` page** |
| `GET /bank-accounts/:id/usage` | bank-accounts settings exists but doesn't render usage |
| `GET /audit` | no `/audit` page |
| `GET /org/style-default`, `PATCH /org/style-default` | branding-defaults UI not present |
| `POST /surveys/:invitationId/respond` | donor-facing survey landing not shipped |
| `POST /superadmin/surveys/:slug/launch` / `schedule` | super-admin reads survey results, no launch UI |
| Superadmin tenants `/lifecycle`, `/confirm-ownership`, `/provision-idp`, IdP `PATCH`/`DELETE` | tenant detail page partial |
| `POST /tenants/:id/admin-dispute`, first-admin-invitations CRUD | admin tenant-lifecycle UI partial |

⚠ **Verify before deletion** — dynamic path construction (`\`\${base}/\${id}/results\``) defeats grep.

---

## 3. Service layer — unused functions

**API (`packages/api`)**
- `cleanupUnverifiedTenants` — `packages/api/src/modules/signup/service.ts:822`. Looks like an intended scheduled job that was never registered with BullMQ.
- `constituentEtag` — `packages/api/src/modules/constituents/service.ts:515`. Helper with no caller.
- Unused constants: `ACTIVE_USER_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, `PER_GROUP_LIMIT`, `MIN_QUERY_LENGTH`.

**Web (`packages/web`)**
- `FilterValidationService` + singleton — `packages/web/src/components/constituents/filters/FilterValidationService.ts`. Entire file orphaned (advanced-filters feature from PR #421 likely moved validation to client-side Zod).

**Shared (`packages/shared`)**
- Unused enum exports: `bulkEmailJobStatusEnum`, `featureFlagScopeEnum`, `paymentAttemptStatusEnum`, `publicPageStyleEnum`, `postalExportModeEnum`, `postalExportStatusEnum`.
- `contracts/branding.ts` — three TypeBox schemas only used via `Static<>` type derivation (`OrgLogoStatusSchema`, `BrandingVariantSchema`, `BrandingVariantSetSchema`).

**Worker processors** ✅ All 22 registered in `packages/worker/src/worker.ts`. **Zero orphans.**

---

## 4. Web layer — unreachable pages

✅ **All 55 `page.tsx` files are reachable** via sidebar, dropdown menu, inter-page links, settings nav, or external entry points (auth flow, email links, `/c/[id]`, `/p/[id]`).

Conditionally-hidden but intentional (correctly gated, no dead-end risk):
- `/settings/feature-flags` — flag `admin.feature_flags_phase2`
- `/admin/finance` — flag `admin.finance_dashboard`

---

## 5. Recommended cleanup clusters (for triage)

Ordered by "lowest risk → highest signal":

- [ ] **Cluster A — safe deletions** (low risk, in one PR)
  - [ ] `FilterValidationService` + singleton
  - [ ] Unused `packages/api` constants (`ACTIVE_USER_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, `PER_GROUP_LIMIT`, `MIN_QUERY_LENGTH`)
  - [ ] `constituentEtag` helper
  - [ ] Unused enum exports in `packages/shared/src/schema/index.ts`
- [ ] **Cluster B — `cleanupUnverifiedTenants`** — decide: register as a scheduled BullMQ job or delete.
- [ ] **Cluster C — half-shipped pledges** — `POST /pledges`, `GET /pledges/:id/installments`, `pledge_installments` table. No UI. Either build the page or remove the API + table.
- [ ] **Cluster D — `/reports` API** — `lybunt`/`sybunt` with no consumer page. Same call.
- [ ] **Cluster E — `receipt_sequences` table** — no doc anchor, no refs. Likely abandoned.
- [ ] **Cluster F — Swiss QR-bill `camt_*` tables + `exchange_rates`** — keep if ADR-028 / ADR-032 are still on the roadmap; otherwise drop and reintroduce when the feature lands. **Defer until product confirms.**
- [ ] **Cluster G — verify before action** (grep may have missed dynamic paths)
  - [ ] Bulk-import GETs (`template`, `:id/download`, `:id/results`)
  - [ ] `GET /constituents/duplicates/search`
  - [ ] `GET /campaigns/:id/roi`, `/stats`, `/funds`, `/public-page`
  - [ ] `GET /bank-accounts/:id/usage`
  - [ ] `GET /audit`
  - [ ] `GET/PATCH /org/style-default`
  - [ ] Survey launch/schedule + respond
  - [ ] Superadmin tenant lifecycle/IdP endpoints

---

## 6. Out of scope

- No changes proposed in this issue — purely an inventory.
- "Low-use" tables (1–2 refs) are explicitly **not** flagged as dead — single-owner domain tables are expected.
- Test files, migrations, and `docs/` were excluded from "reference" counts by design.

items.title: [P1][DATA-10] Add Hindsight bank-scoped memory and temporal evidence adapter
items.body:
### Source and scope
[Hindsight](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight) is a persistent agent memory system with REST/SDK/MCP surfaces and isolated memory banks. Its `retain/recall/reflect` interface is not a bulk-export guarantee. **Only explicitly proven read-only operations are eligible**.

### Implementation
1. Verify pinned Hindsight API version, supported **read-only bank/document/memory** list/get operations or documented export. Start with user-supplied JSON/snapshot of approved bank metadata if safe enumerating APIs are missing.
2. Optional configured bank-specific API/SDK read mode with explicit URL and least-privilege token; preserve bank ID, document/memory IDs, timestamps, source/provenance and temporal validity links where present.
3. Do not call `retain`, `reflect`, reprocess, profile updates or inference-triggering operations. `recall` may consume inference resources; do not invoke it in default import. If a read operation has unverifiable cost/side effects, refuse with clear capability reason.
4. Separate retained document, extracted fact, relationship, synthesized reflection and retrieved hit. `recall` output is a retrieved claim; `reflect` is a generated answer, not independent ground truth. A memory bank shared between users cannot be analyzed across tenants without authorized scope.
5. Preserve `as_of`/validity or explicit temporal metadata when present, with distinct 'record observed' versus 'fact validity' times. Superseded or contradictory memories remain review candidates, not evidence of an agent defect by themselves.
6. Link Codex/Claude sessions only using native source identities when provided by the coding-agent integration; bank names like `codex::project` alone are not sufficient matching.

### Acceptance
- [ ] Import a deterministic synthetic bank snapshot with temporal corrections and distinguish current/historical assertions.
- [ ] A search/recall/relevance score never maps to grader success, skill activation or session completion.
- [ ] Unsupported Hindsight API, missing bank permission or unavailable list/get results return incomplete/blocked without discovery across other banks.
- [ ] No writes/reflect/inference or unapproved external calls on default import.
- [ ] Document bank isolation, source contract version, API/SDK support and limits.

### References
[Hindsight API](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/blob/main/hindsight-api/README.md) · [Bank/retain/recall best practices](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/blob/main/hindsight-docs/src/pages/best-practices.mdx) · [Coding agent integrations](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/blob/main/hindsight-integrations/README.md).
Delivery: API capability audit -> fixture importer -> bank-scoped read-only integration/negative tests.

### Shared acceptance and dependencies
Parent #41; use #42 source schema/guards. All ingestion must be explicitly scoped, bounded, idempotent, read-only, private and version-gated. No default inference, network requests, service start, writes or direct database repair. Claims/retrieval scores never become verified task outcomes. Test mock offline source, duplicate/superseded records, missing IDs, quota errors, malformed output, source isolation, secret canaries and partial resume. Preserve standard-library-only AHL core; optional dependencies/clients are opt-in. Run both README test suites, CLI/help and wheel/archive tests.

milestone.title: Operate
milestone.description: Operate milestone: daily-use governed AI capabilities (search, assistant, scenarios, verticals), SME enablement, editions boundary, and close-out of all open Platform/Enterprise items. Plan: docs/plans/2026-07-11-operate-milestone.md

items.body:
Parent: #285
Related: #340, #360, #376

## Outcome
Add a deterministic decisioning layer that continuously evaluates ontology state, data products and governed event streams to produce explainable scores, watchlist matches and alerts that can enter existing workflows, approvals and actions.

#340 established a governed event-ingestion boundary. This portfolio begins **after ingestion**: it defines how operators express, backtest, version, deploy and monitor detection logic.

## Child slices
- Versioned typed rules engine and rule-set lifecycle.
- Historical backtesting and change-impact comparison before promotion.
- Explainable scoring/cohort framework with reusable features and evidence.
- Watchlists and relationship/graph-pattern detection.
- Real-time correlation of events with ontology state.
- Alert lifecycle: deduplication, grouping, severity, assignment, triage, feedback and routing.

## Invariants
- Rules and scores are deterministic for a fixed input snapshot/version unless they explicitly call a separately governed model.
- Every alert records the rule/score version, input references and explanation needed to reproduce the trigger.
- Rule changes use draft/review/promotion/rollback rather than direct mutation of production logic.
- Alert visibility is no broader than the evidence that generated it.
- Repeated delivery, retries and replay cannot create duplicate logical alerts.
- Automated action remains subject to existing policy, autonomy and approval boundaries; the alert engine is not a new write authority.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Create child issues for rules, backtesting, scoring, watchlists/patterns, streaming correlation and alert lifecycle.
- [ ] Define stable rule inputs over ontology objects, data products, time-series/event windows and graph predicates without coupling to one vertical.
- [ ] Define proposal/review/promotion and rollback semantics for production rules.
- [ ] Reuse #340 event envelopes and checkpoints for streaming input.
- [ ] Route actions through existing workflow/action/approval machinery.
- [ ] Define latency, throughput and per-tenant fairness budgets under #360.
- [ ] Validate at least manufacturing/operations and fraud/risk-style reference rules.

## Non-goals
- No hidden autonomous execution path.
- No claim that rule-based detection alone is predictive AI.
- No vertical-specific fraud/AML schema in shared core.

## Product-learning references
- https://www.palantir.com/platforms/foundry/foundry-rules/
- https://www.palantir.com/platforms/foundry/streaming/
- https://datawalk.com/solutions/anti-fraud-software/
- https://www.quantexa.com/platform/graph-analytics/

## Delivery rule
The first release should favor explainability and deterministic backtesting over feature count. Advanced ML-driven scoring plugs into the same evidence contract later.
