items.title: Spec: PulseIntel v1 collaborative market intelligence dashboard

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an agent

items.body:
## Problem Statement

Small teams that track competitive intelligence, market signals, and internal performance data usually stitch together spreadsheets, news feeds, ad hoc scraping, dashboards, and team chat. That makes it difficult to keep observations trustworthy, collaborate around changes in real time, preserve historical context, and act quickly when something meaningful changes.

These teams need PulseIntel: a shared, real-time market intelligence product where a Tenant can organize Workspaces, attach Sources, monitor Metrics and Observations, create Insights, annotate Dashboard trends, and receive Alerts with clear provenance.

## Solution

Build PulseIntel as a multi-tenant SaaS for collaborative market intelligence. Each Tenant has global Users with Tenant Roles and Workspace Roles, a Tenant Home for navigation, tenant-owned Sources, and one or more Workspaces. Each Workspace owns Dashboards, Custom Metrics, Alert Rules, Insights, Annotations, and subscriptions to tenant Sources.

The v1 product will provide:
- Tenant/workspace collaboration with Invitations, memberships, and role-based access control
- Widget-based Dashboards with a Dashboard Time Range and optional widget-level overrides
- Tenant-owned Sources with Source Kinds for RSS feed ingestion, price tracking, KPI ingest, and Manual Source entry
- Immutable Observation History with Evidence and Evidence Snapshots for trust and auditability
- Base Metrics plus workspace-scoped Custom Metrics with strict Unit Validation, Formula Function Set guardrails, and asynchronous Metric Materialization
- Rule-based Alerts with Alert Severity, per-rule Alert Cooldown, durable Alert Events, per-user Alert Subscriptions, in-app history, and email delivery
- Insights and Annotations with Comment Threads, required Insight Evidence Links, and soft locking for finalized findings
- Revisions, Snapshots, archive/restore, Activity Feed, and Audit Trail behavior that preserves history instead of hiding it

## User Stories

1. As a tenant owner, I want to create and manage a Tenant, so that my company has a dedicated market intelligence boundary.
2. As a tenant admin, I want to invite users by email, so that teammates can join the correct Tenant and Workspaces.
3. As a user, I want a single global identity across multiple Tenants, so that I can work with different customer or internal accounts without separate logins.
4. As a user, I want to land on a Tenant Home after accepting an Invitation, so that I can choose the right Workspace quickly.
5. As a tenant admin, I want to assign Tenant Roles and Workspace Roles, so that administration and day-to-day collaboration stay separate.
6. As a workspace admin, I want to manage membership within a Workspace, so that the right people can view, edit, and administer shared intelligence.
7. As a team member, I want to create a Workspace, through tenant administration, so that different initiatives can collaborate without mixing dashboards and alerts.
8. As a workspace member, I want to open a Dashboard with a shared default time range, so that the team sees the same market picture.
9. As a workspace member, I want certain Widgets to override the Dashboard Time Range, so that a single Dashboard can show both short-term and long-term views.
10. As a workspace editor, I want to arrange Widgets on a fixed grid, so that Dashboards are flexible but still structured and versionable.
11. As a workspace editor, I want to clone a Dashboard as an independent copy, so that I can reuse setup without creating hidden linkage to the original.
12. As a workspace editor, I want to create Insights tied to supporting evidence, so that durable findings stay trustworthy.
13. As a workspace member, I want to annotate Widgets, Observations, and time ranges, so that I can add context exactly where a change appears.
14. As a workspace member, I want Comment Threads on Insights and Annotations, so that collaboration stays attached to the relevant evidence.
15. As a workspace editor, I want to lock an Insight after finalizing it, so that the finding stays stable while discussion can continue.
16. As a workspace editor, I want tenant-owned Sources to be reusable across Workspaces through Source Subscriptions, so that we avoid duplicate setup.
17. As a workspace editor, I want Subscription Filters on a Source Subscription, so that each Workspace can focus on the subset of data it actually needs.
18. As a tenant admin, I want to define Source configuration once per Tenant, so that feed and price tracking logic is consistent.
19. As a workspace editor, I want Manual Sources, so that I can capture intelligence even when automation is not ready.
20. As a workspace editor, I want Manual Source entries to require a Citation Note, so that manually entered values are still explainable.
21. As a system operator, I want RSS feed items normalized into Observations with article evidence, so that news fits the same trust model as other signals.
22. As a workspace member, I want repeated sightings of the same article deduplicated into an Article Identity, so that feeds are readable without losing provenance.
23. As a workspace editor, I want price tracking Sources to capture extracted values plus evidence snapshots, so that pricing changes can be verified later.
24. As a workspace member, I want broken source collection to surface Source Health problems, so that missing data is not mistaken for stable conditions.
25. As a workspace member, I want Collection Runs recorded separately from Observations, so that failed collection is distinguishable from no change.
26. As a tenant admin, I want Base Metrics to be tenant-owned and reused, so that source-backed definitions stay consistent across Workspaces.
27. As a workspace editor, I want to define Custom Metrics inside a Workspace, so that each team can build derived intelligence on top of shared data.
28. As a workspace editor, I want Custom Metrics to reference other Custom Metrics through an acyclic Metric Dependency Graph, so that complex derived analysis remains stable.
29. As a workspace editor, I want strict Unit Validation in formulas, so that derived Metrics do not combine incompatible values incorrectly.
30. As a workspace editor, I want a guarded Formula Function Set with arithmetic, comparisons, conditional logic, and time-window helpers, so that formulas are useful without becoming arbitrary code execution.
31. As a workspace member, I want Custom Metric values materialized asynchronously, so that dashboards and alerts remain fast and predictable.
32. As a workspace editor, I want KPI ingest credentials scoped to a Workspace, so that internal metric ownership matches the collaboration boundary.
33. As an integration system, I want to push KPI Observations with optional Metric Dimensions, so that teams can track segmented business performance.
34. As a workspace editor, I want to create Alert Rules on Observations and Metrics, so that meaningful changes are surfaced automatically.
35. As a workspace editor, I want Alert Severity on Alert Rules, so that high-priority changes stand out from routine monitoring.
36. As a workspace member, I want Alert Events recorded durably, so that I can review alert history in-app and not rely only on transient notifications.
37. As a workspace member, I want to acknowledge an Alert Event, so that the team can see that someone has seen it.
38. As a workspace member, I want Alert Cooldown configured per Alert Rule, so that noisy conditions do not overwhelm the Workspace.
39. As a new workspace member, I want alert subscriptions to start unsubscribed, so that joining a Workspace does not immediately flood my inbox.
40. As a workspace member, I want to subscribe only to the Alert Rules I care about, so that notifications stay relevant.
41. As a workspace member, I want Alerts delivered in-app and by email, so that I can respond quickly whether I am in the product or away from it.
42. As a workspace member, I want realtime updates for Alerts, Annotations, Comment Threads, and dashboard content refreshes, so that collaboration feels live without requiring full concurrent editing.
43. As a workspace member, I want immutable Observation History, so that I can trust what the system actually captured at a given time.
44. As a workspace member, I want long-term historical analysis to transparently use downsampled data when needed, so that old trends remain explorable without keeping infinite raw detail.
45. As a workspace editor, I want every change to a Dashboard, Custom Metric, or Alert Rule to create a Revision, so that restore behavior is simple and auditable.
46. As a workspace editor, I want named Snapshots, so that important milestones can be restored intentionally.
47. As a workspace member, I want restoring a Revision or Snapshot to create a new current Revision, so that history is preserved instead of rewritten.
48. As a tenant admin, I want Workspaces archived before deletion, so that shared intelligence is not lost accidentally.
49. As a tenant admin, I want Workspace Restore to recover the full Workspace state, so that archiving acts as a safety measure rather than a teardown.
50. As a workspace member, I want an Activity Feed for collaboration, alert, and source health changes, so that I can understand what the team and system are doing over time.
51. As an administrator, I want an Audit Trail for security, admin, and restore actions, so that accountability exists without exposing everything as user-facing noise.
52. As a product team, I want PulseIntel to treat evidence and provenance as first-class concepts throughout the product, so that trust remains a core differentiator.

## Implementation Decisions

- Build the product as a modular monolith with separate worker processes for ingestion, metric materialization, alert evaluation, and other asynchronous jobs.
- Use a multi-tenant SaaS model from day one with a single global user identity and shared-schema tenant isolation enforced at the application and query level.
- Implement authentication with Auth0 rather than custom JWT infrastructure.
- Target AWS for v1, running the application and workers on ECS Fargate.
- Use PostgreSQL as the primary store with TimescaleDB for time-series workloads.
- Use Redis and BullMQ for background job orchestration.
- Store Evidence metadata in PostgreSQL and Evidence Snapshots in S3.
- Model the core domain around Tenant, Workspace, Dashboard, Widget, Source, Source Subscription, Observation, Metric, Custom Metric, Alert Rule, Alert Event, Insight, Annotation, Revision, Snapshot, Activity Feed, and Audit Trail.
- Keep Sources tenant-owned, with workspace-level Source Subscriptions and Subscription Filters controlling how each Workspace consumes shared Sources.
- Support first-class Source Kinds for RSS feed, price tracker, KPI ingest API, and Manual Source in v1.
- Represent each collection attempt as a Collection Run, distinct from the Observations it may or may not produce.
- Model Observations with a shared envelope for timestamps, provenance, and analysis, plus kind-specific payloads and evidence details.
- Keep Observation History immutable; corrections and recaptures must create new or superseding records rather than overwriting history.
- Deduplicate repeated news items into a stable Article Identity while preserving collection history.
- Define Base Metrics at the tenant level and allow Workspaces to define Custom Metrics locally.
- Support Custom Metrics over workspace-visible Metrics only, with an acyclic Metric Dependency Graph and strict Unit Validation.
- Materialize Custom Metric values asynchronously when upstream Observations or Metrics change.
- Require explicit Metric Unit metadata and support optional Metric Dimensions on ingested metric values.
- Implement Alert Rules as rule-based conditions only in v1, with per-rule Alert Severity, per-rule Alert Cooldown, durable Alert Events, and user-level Alert Subscriptions.
- Evaluate Alert Rules both on relevant data updates and on scheduled sweeps so missing-data conditions can be detected.
- Default new workspace members to an unsubscribed Default Subscription State for Alert Rules.
- Support in-app and email alert delivery in v1, using user acknowledgement rather than a full incident-resolution workflow.
- Allow Viewers to contribute Annotations and Comment Threads, while structural changes remain limited to Editors and Workspace Admins.
- Require every Insight to carry at least one Insight Evidence Link to an Observation, annotation target, or Evidence reference.
- Support soft-locking for Insights: locked Insights are read-only for normal editors, but discussion can continue and authorized users can reopen them.
- Version Dashboards, Custom Metrics, and Alert Rules with automatic Revisions on every saved change plus named Snapshots.
- Restoring historical state must create a new Revision instead of mutating past history.
- Archive Workspaces before deletion and allow full Workspace Restore, including dashboards, subscriptions, alerts, and historical state.
- Provide a Dashboard Time Range with optional widget-level overrides.
- Keep Dashboards workspace-owned; clones are independent copies and not live-linked templates.
- Expose realtime product behavior through REST APIs plus Socket.io events rather than GraphQL subscriptions.
- Build a user-visible Activity Feed for collaboration, alert, and source-health events, distinct from the admin-oriented Audit Trail.
- Capture source failures as Source Health problems and failed Collection Runs instead of silently skipping data or carrying forward stale values as current truth.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test should verify external behavior and user-visible outcomes rather than internal implementation details.
- The primary seam should be the application boundary: REST API contracts, Socket.io realtime behavior, worker-triggered outcomes, persistence-visible revisions/history, and authorization behavior across tenant and workspace boundaries.
- A narrow secondary seam should exist at the source collector adapter boundary so each Source Kind can be tested against a stable collection contract without depending on live third-party systems.
- Test the tenancy and membership model through public auth, invitation, and authorization behavior rather than direct storage assumptions.
- Test Dashboard behavior through creation, widget layout, cloning, time-range defaults/overrides, versioning, archive/restore, and visibility rules.
- Test source ingestion through Collection Run outcomes, Observation creation, evidence capture, Source Health transitions, and source-subscription filtering behavior.
- Test Custom Metrics through formula validation, Metric Unit enforcement, acyclic dependency handling, asynchronous materialization, and historical query behavior.
- Test Alerts through rule evaluation, Alert Cooldown behavior, Alert Event creation, acknowledgement, subscription defaults, delivery fan-out, and realtime propagation.
- Test Insights and collaboration through evidence-link requirements, annotation anchors, comment threads, locking/reopening rules, and Activity Feed visibility.
- Test historical behavior through immutable Observation History, retention/downsampling query behavior, Revision creation, Snapshot restore, and Workspace Restore.
- Prior art in the current repository is effectively none because the codebase is still greenfield; the initial test suite should establish reusable patterns around high-level contract tests and source-adapter tests rather than low-level unit tests of framework plumbing.

## Out of Scope

- Full Google-Docs-style concurrent dashboard editing with live layout conflict resolution.
- Slack delivery in v1.
- Statistical or ML-based anomaly detection in v1.
- App store tracking in v1.
- Full template libraries with linked dashboard inheritance.
- Generic comments on every object in the system.
- Arbitrary code execution or unrestricted scripting inside Custom Metric formulas.
- Per-tenant schemas or per-tenant databases in v1.
- Separate microservices for each product capability in v1.
- Broad connector catalogs beyond RSS, price tracking, KPI ingest, and Manual Source.

## Further Notes

- This spec should be treated as the v1 product and architecture baseline for PulseIntel.
- The domain glossary in CONTEXT.md and the ADRs in docs/adr are part of the contract for future work and should be read alongside this spec.
- The implementation should favor preserving trust, provenance, and historical explainability over aggressively simplifying away domain history.
- The product differentiator is not just monitoring data, but helping teams collaborate around trustworthy evidence and shared interpretation.

items.title: [ACV1-AH08][P0] Reconcile ambiguous provider effects with bounded attempt and recovery policies

labels.name: area:runtime
labels.description: Runtime: durable workflow execution and recovery

milestone.title: v1
milestone.description: NeatHack 2026 v1 scope

items.body:
<!-- triage-key: ACV1-AH08 -->

# [P0 ACV1-AH08] Reconcile ambiguous provider effects with bounded attempt and recovery policies

**Owner ROLE:** Agent and research. **Named assignee/reviewer:** unassigned; availability and authorization not verified. **Priority:** P0 — Retries must recover safely without hidden paid repeats or duplicate completed effects. **Required-for-v1:** yes, independently of priority. **Release:** Agent & Creative v1. **Type:** implementation. **Workflow state:** planned. **Size/risk:** L / high side-effect and financial risk. **Critical path:** Wave 5; parallel required branch; fixture-based work may begin earlier; no duration estimate.

## Current evidence and gap

Inspected harness revision `eac92175fc5e34b51d3fd6bceaaf8d86d6fe9ca3` ([tree](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/tree/eac92175fc5e34b51d3fd6bceaaf8d86d6fe9ca3)). Observed only README.md and docs/architecture/OWNERSHIP.md / ACCEPTANCE.md. No source symbols, package/build manifests, tests or CI workflows exist. [Issue #1](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/issues/1) retains planned WP04 history and is reused as the runtime epic; [PR #2](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/pull/2) merged documentation only. All implementation paths and commands below are **proposed**. No successful implementation test or provider integration is claimed.

Exact gap: The outcome described below has no implemented and verified harness behavior in the inspected baseline.

Proposed paths:

- src/recovery/*
- src/state/inbox.*
- src/adapters/reconciliation.*
- tests/recovery/*

## Scope, outcome and non-goals

Make provider dispatch, retry and reconciliation state explicit for research, reasoning, classification, image and inspection operations. Reuse completed results or reconcile uncertain outcomes before considering another billable attempt. Do not promise universal exactly-once external execution.

Storefront/UI, production rendering/preflight, printing/shipping adapters, financial ledger/price catalog, dashboard and CFO.ai implementation are outside this leaf. Do not create another JEV transport, approval authority or copied shared schema. No paid triage tests.

## Authority and acceptance ownership

Use the [authoritative checklist](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/integration-evals/blob/ff1f6d2df816ebbff34742f51be728fcb5c28cb5/planning/acceptance-checklist.json) and [maintained contract catalog](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/blob/c4caaccc2ea63b273eeac17ed89af8ac64f6bbde/docs/contract-catalog.md); original IDs, meanings and global owner roles are unchanged. Local AH/JEV IDs extend scoped requirements only.

- Local requirement: **AH-08**; source: user-assigned Agent & Creative v1 operating contract / named outcome area. Implementation scope is the outcome and cases defined in this leaf.

- **AGT-02 — Durable resume**: original P0; global owner **Agent and research**; full runtime outcome ownership. Original verification: Interrupt the worker after a completed step and resume from its saved checkpoint. Required global evidence: Before and after checkpoints and correlated traces.

- **AGT-03 — Bounded recovery**: original P0; global owner **Agent and research**; full runtime outcome ownership. Original verification: Trigger a recoverable failure and show attempts, elapsed time and cost limits terminate or resolve it. Required global evidence: Run showing failure, next action and final outcome.

- **FIN-03 — Distinct billed retries**: original P0; global owner **Finance and reliability**; scoped contribution; does not verify the whole global criterion. Original verification: Execute two distinct billable attempts for one logical operation and retain both costs. Required global evidence: Two attempt identities with attributed usage.

- **FIN-04 — Unknown billing**: original P0; global owner **Finance and reliability**; scoped contribution; does not verify the whole global criterion. Original verification: Remove provider usage or time out after dispatch; retain unknown or estimated cost instead of an invented zero. Required global evidence: Incomplete record, held budget and reconciliation status.

- **BUD-03 — Uncertain in flight cost**: original P0; global owner **Finance and reliability**; scoped contribution; does not verify the whole global criterion. Original verification: Expire a worker lease during an unresolved provider call and retain the conservative financial hold. Required global evidence: Lease state, hold state and reconciliation path.

## Proposed approach and compatibility

Record logical operation, billable attempt, transport attempt and provider-request identities separately. Require per-adapter declaration of idempotency support, dispatch ambiguity, status lookup, billability and safe retry classes. Atomically persist intent and durable observations; deduplicate callbacks/observations using inbox identity. Provider timeout after dispatch and crash-before-checkpoint stay unresolved with financial hold. If lookup/idempotency unavailable, route to review and record unknown, not automatic image regeneration. A new genuinely billed call obtains new attempt identity and authorization. Limit all SDK plus harness attempts by one owner, elapsed deadline and external budget. Cancellation stops future work while late responses reconcile safely.

Boundary changes require affected producer and consumer review; canonical schema ownership remains in shared-contracts. Pin compatible versions, test old consumers/unknown fields and reject unsupported major versions. No silent migration or model-alias change.

## Relationships

### Blocked by

- [ACV1-AH03](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/issues/9); completion. Requires this leaf's specified narrow outcome; fixture-based development may start before final verification.

- [ACV1-AH09](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/issues/14); completion. Requires this leaf's specified narrow outcome; fixture-based development may start before final verification.

- [ACV1-AH05](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/issues/15); completion. Requires this leaf's specified narrow outcome; fixture-based development may start before final verification.

### Blocks

- [ACV1-AH11-OPS](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/issues/20)
- [ACV1-AH12](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/issues/23)

### Related

- https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/issues/1
- https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness/pull/2

Epic checklist membership is separate from these dependency edges. Never use an automatic issue-closing keyword in planning/PR references.

## Testable acceptance cases

1. **Input:** Provider accepts then times out; worker restarts; duplicate observation arrives
   **Expected:** Existing identity reconciled or unresolved review; hold remains; duplicate observation does not charge twice
   **Observable failure:** Blind repeated image generation or fabricated failure/zero cost

2. **Input:** Two genuinely billed retries for one operation
   **Expected:** Separate billable attempts and usage refs, bounded authorized retry count
   **Observable failure:** Costs collapse into transport retry

3. **Input:** Lease expires during unknown provider outcome; cancel races late completion
   **Expected:** Financial hold unaffected by lease; result retained without unauthorized workflow progression
   **Observable failure:** Capacity reused or lost artifact receipt

4. **Input:** Exhausted retries/deadline, unavailable reconciliation endpoint, nonretryable schema/auth failure
   **Expected:** Deterministic stopped/review state with no additional dispatch; resumable only under new authorized command
   **Observable failure:** Retry storm or hidden SDK multiplication

## Verification commands and fixtures

All targets below are proposed and **not run**. For ACV1-CONTRACTS, ACV1-ACCESS and ACV1-JEV-TARGETS, this leaf supplies its own standalone Python verifier and pinned inputs, independent of AH-01. For other leaves, AH-01 establishes the language/build tooling and proposed wrappers. Command names are a delivery contract, not evidence of existing scripts. Default mock checks make no provider calls. Later live checks require separately verified access and external budget authorization. Target output must identify scenario/fixture IDs, pass/fail (nonzero on failure), component revisions and dependency mode; required skipped cases fail readiness.

```sh
make verify CASE=AH-08 MODE=mock FIXTURE=ambiguous-side-effect-matrix
```
Expected: Exit 0; all specified input/expected/failure assertions pass with no required cases skipped. Report fixture IDs, revisions and dependency modes.
Observable failure: Exit nonzero on a listed observable failure, absent required fixture or unexpected dependency access.

```sh
make verify CASE=AH-08 MODE=recorded FIXTURE=provider-attempt-semantics
```
Expected: Exit 0; all specified input/expected/failure assertions pass with no required cases skipped. Report fixture IDs, revisions and dependency modes.
Observable failure: Exit nonzero on a listed observable failure, absent required fixture or unexpected dependency access.

## Required evidence

- Per-provider retry/idempotency capability table with verified limits
- Fault-injection history, durable receipts, unresolved hold/reconciliation records
- Attempt count/deadline/cancellation invariants and sanitized traces
- Tested implementation/contract commit(s), release revision compatibility and successful CI/run artifacts; unperformed checks remain pending.
- Explicit dependency mode per provider: mock, recorded, sandbox or live; sanitized decision/trace/artifact/usage references or explicit not-applicable reason. No credentials/customer data in evidence.

Current evidence status: **pending**. Mock, recorded, sandbox and live are distinct. Contract doubles prove only specified boundary behavior; they cannot impersonate actual JEV/GPT Image/Neatlogs integrations. Missing live access blocks the matching live criterion.

## Closure gate

Implementation and directly related tests merged; all listed acceptance checks executed successfully on the pinned release revisions; documentation updated; exact dependencies satisfied; required evidence accessible and sanitized; no required behavior hidden behind stubs. A PR merge, planning/discovery closure, deferral or label does not verify this outcome. Required scope changes require explicit owner approval and recorded impact, and do not verify the original requirement.

<!-- triage-normalization:v1 -->

---

## Triage normalization (org template)

_Added by org triage on 2026-10-10. All content above is preserved unchanged; this block only maps it onto the org issue template. Nothing here verifies acceptance._

### Context
See **Current evidence and gap** above.

### Scope / Non-goals
See **Scope, outcome and non-goals** above.

### Acceptance criteria
_(triage: restated one-to-one from **Testable acceptance cases** above; the Input / Observable failure text there is authoritative, and the **Closure gate** still applies)_
- [ ] Case 1: Existing identity reconciled or unresolved review; hold remains; duplicate observation does not charge twice
- [ ] Case 2: Separate billable attempts and usage refs, bounded authorized retry count
- [ ] Case 3: Financial hold unaffected by lease; result retained without unauthorized workflow progression
- [ ] Case 4: Deterministic stopped/review state with no additional dispatch; resumable only under new authorized command

### Dependencies
- Blocked by: `ACV1-AH03` Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness#9, `ACV1-AH09` Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness#14, `ACV1-AH05` Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness#15
- Blocks: `ACV1-AH11-OPS` Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness#20, `ACV1-AH12` Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/agent-harness#23

### Evidence required
See **Required evidence** above.

items.title: [ARCH] Read-only audit: Brenvio ↔ SMM AI Helper backend integration strategy
items.body:
## Цель
Read-only архитектурное исследование: как интегрировать действующий FastAPI/Telegram-first backend SMM AI Helper с SaaS frontend Brenvio, **не переписывая AI-ядро, не влияя на Codex и не меняя production**.

## Источники
- Backend: https://github.com/Pickle-Pee/smm_ai_helper (default `master`, изучить актуальные PR, документацию `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `app/main.py`, `app/security.py`, Copilot/Projects/BrandProfile/Chat/Tasks/Workflows, ORM, Alembic, тесты)
- Frontend: https://github.com/Pickle-Pee/smm_ai_helper_web (default `main`; смотреть также PR #3 feat/brand-design-v1 и PR #5 feat/brenvio-brand-and-deployment — оба stacked и ещё open на момент постановки)
- Контекст продукта: backend epic https://github.com/Pickle-Pee/smm_ai_helper/issues/158, задачи #160–#164, #167–#170.
- Домен демо: https://app.24rubridge.ru — **не выполняй никакие операции на сервере**, анализируй repo only.

## Ограничения
1. **Audit only:** не менять backend/frontend код, Alembic, данные, конфиги, CI/CD, DNS, секреты, сервер; не запускать работающие сервисы и не устанавливать зависимости; не выполнять внешние LLM/API вызовы.
2. Не допускать вмешательства в текущие PR Codex.
3. Не предполагать, что существующий `require_actor` является веб-авторизацией: `BOT_BACKEND_TOKEN` + `X-Telegram-User-ID` предназначены доверенному боту, не браузеру.
4. Не переносить маркетинговую бизнес-логику на frontend и не дублировать persistence или graph jobs.
5. Дизайн-решения маркировать как **existing / confirmed / proposed / missing**, со ссылкой на точный файл/метод и по возможности строки.

## Вопросы исследования
### 1. As-Is backend architecture
- Реальный request flow: Telegram → FastAPI → Copilot/Orchestrator → PostgreSQL jobs → worker → saved artifacts; delivery & replay.
- Реестр HTTP endpoints + DTO и owner-scoping: execute, saved executions, runs/status, mentor, projects/history/context/discussion, brand profiles, chat, tasks, image/artifacts.
- Выпиши актуальные модели DB, реальные ключи ownership (`telegram_id`, `tg:<id>`, `chat_id`, `User`, runs/jobs), зависимости и миграционные ограничения.
- Нюансы `202 WORKFLOW_STARTED`, `NEEDS_INPUT`, `409`, receipt retention, stale context/version, unknown provider outcome, retries, idempotency keys. Не выдумывать гарантии exactly-once.

### 2. As-Is frontend
- Маршруты и страницы: dashboard, workspace, projects/project detail, documents, settings.
- Реальные TypeScript contracts, mock-adapter/provider, local state reducers, project and thread identity.
- Карта UI feature → требуемый backend capability → gap (сохранение, auth, tenant, files, billing).

### 3. Target architecture: compare alternatives
- A: browser -> authenticated Web API v2 on FastAPI;
- B: browser -> Next.js BFF/server-side API routes -> FastAPI;
- C: mixed approach;
- explicit recommendation with trust boundaries, secret handling, CORS/CSRF, cookie sessions, OAuth/OIDC / email auth, local deployment, observability and migration.
- Ясно указать, почему нельзя просто передать BOT_BACKEND_TOKEN и Telegram ID из браузера.

### 4. Identity + multi-tenancy (P0 security blocker)
- Предложить `User`, `ExternalIdentity`, `Workspace/Organization`, `Membership`, `Project` и связи c legacy actor.
- Подтверждённое account linking Telegram ↔ SaaS; migration/backfill & rollback of existing owned data; предотвращение cross-tenant leaks.
- Не использовать вымышленные Telegram ID для web-only users.
- Строго разграничить legacy `/projects` history/navigation и SaaS Projects/Brands.
- Отдельный минимально безопасный путь для 1 пользователя и масштабируемый multi-tenant path; что переносить в MVP, что откладывать.

### 5. Feature mapping + typed API contracts
- Первый вертикальный срез: authenticated user → choose/create brand → create request → clarification → async progress → accepted result → reopen/history → mentor → logout/login recovery.
- Метод/путь/DTO (current or proposed), auth, owner, error/retry semantics, backend/frontend changes per step.
- SSE vs polling: current reality and phased plan. No made-up streaming API.
- Documents: отдельно пометить existing image artifacts vs future Document Workspace (XLSX/DOCX/PDF/PPTX), ingestion/storage/export, secure upload; billing later.

### 6. Delivery & deployment
- Раздельные репозитории, independent CI, contract/versioning/OpenAPI TS generation, migrations, feature flags.
- Same-VPS hosting and domain boundary; do not change existing proxy, DNS, Docker, TLS or production.
- Security review: access control, XSS, prompt injection via files, SSRF, rate limits, usage caps, idempotency, server-secret isolation, logging PII, RLS discussion.

## Обязательные артефакты
1. Executive summary + recommendation.
2. As-Is and To-Be architecture diagrams (Mermaid).

items.title: Persist MCP learning state with per-user isolation
items.body:
## Goal
Replace process-memory MCP learning state with a persistent repository layer while preserving deterministic mastery logic.

## Why next
The MCP surface and transport contracts now work, but process-memory state can disappear on cold start and cannot safely support multiple users. This is the main blocker before a real hosted ChatGPT connection.

## Scope
- Introduce repository interfaces for mastery, sessions, attempts, and mistake history
- Implement a Postgres/Neon-backed adapter against the existing schema
- Scope every learning-state read/write by an explicit trusted user identifier
- Keep mastery calculation in domain code; persistence only stores evidence/state
- Preserve the current in-memory adapter for tests/local development
- Add tests proving user A cannot read or mutate user B state

## Acceptance criteria
- MCP service no longer depends directly on module-global mutable state
- restart-safe state through the persistent adapter
- user isolation covered by tests
- existing mastery/prerequisite tests remain deterministic
- no destructive migration and no auth-provider decision in this issue

## Current decision/implementation boundaries
1. **Trusted learner identity source:** the MCP tools must not accept a caller-supplied learner id as authorization. The adapter can be designed without choosing an auth vendor, but the HTTP/ChatGPT host still needs a trusted request context that supplies the learner id before multi-user persistence is safe.
2. **Problem identity mapping:** the current curated problem bank uses text ids such as `sample-factoring-001`, while `db/schema.sql` defines `attempts.problem_id` as a UUID foreign key into `problems`. Before persisting attempts, either curated problems need a deterministic DB mapping/ingestion step or the schema contract needs a deliberate adjustment. Do not silently coerce this in unattended work.

## Non-goals
- choosing a production authentication vendor
- production deployment
- billing or multi-tenant organization features

items.title: [Roadmap 21.17] Celonis skill (process intelligence + Action Flows via first-party MCP)
items.body:
**Celonis skill** — Celonis is the dominant European process-mining /
process-intelligence platform (HQ Munich; large Mittelstand + DACH
enterprise install base). An agent that integrates with Celonis can pull
live process insights, KPIs, and recommendations and trigger Celonis Action
Flows back into source systems (SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow, etc.).

**Manifesto:** Principle I — *the skills are the product*. For DACH
enterprise ops, Celonis is the connective tissue between source systems.

## Why DACH-strategic

- Munich-headquartered; deep Mittelstand + DAX-30 customer base.
- Process-mining is the auditable substrate enterprise ops teams already
  trust to find inefficiencies. An agent that consumes it operates on
  *already-validated facts about the business*, not LLM guesses.
- Action Flows already orchestrate writes into source systems — the agent
  triggers a flow rather than re-implementing every system integration.
- Pairs naturally with R21.8 (SAP Analytics Cloud), R21.9 (DATEV), R25
  (EU deployment).

## API + MCP availability (checked 2026-05-01)

- **First-party MCP server ✅.** Celonis ships an official MCP server: the
  *Agent Tools (MCP) Asset*, GA as of early 2026 (formerly *Model Context
  Protocol (MCP) Server Asset*, private preview Nov 2025). JSON-RPC 2.0,
  rate-limited 500 calls/min per asset (configurable). Tools: search
  insights, get real-time process context, trigger external actions, write
  decisions back to Celonis. Reference:
  https://developer.celonis.com/mcp-server-asset/
- **REST API ✅.** EMS REST API + Data Ingestion API + Action Flow REST
  endpoints + PyCelonis SDK at https://developer.celonis.com/

## Implementation strategy

**Wrap the first-party MCP server, don't re-implement the API.** This skill
should be a thin `SKILL.md` package that registers Celonis as an
MCP-backed tool source, plus eval suite + DACH-specific fixtures. Net-new
code is limited to credential management and operator-facing setup docs.

## Use cases

- *"Show me where AP invoices got stuck last month — group by Lieferant and
  sort by cycle time."*
- *"Find the orders where Liefertermin slipped > 5 days and trigger the
  reschedule Action Flow."*
- *"Pull the top 10 process variants for OTC and tell me which are
  non-compliant."*
- *"Push this approval decision back to Celonis so it shows up in the next
  process refresh."*

## Acceptance criteria

- R21.1-compliant `SKILL.md` package; `metadata.hybridclaw.category: ops`.
- Celonis OAuth credentials in the encrypted runtime secret store; tokens
  never seen by the model (Principle VII).
- MCP server URL + asset ID configurable per tenant.
- Conservative-by-default: Action Flow execution requires explicit operator
  grant or `confirm-each` autonomy; read-only insight queries allowed at
  default autonomy.
- Eval suite: 20+ representative scenarios across query / variant analysis
  / Action Flow trigger paths.
- Cost-per-run measured in `UsageTotals`.
- Operator docs: tenant setup, MCP asset deployment, role/permission
  scoping.

## Depends on

- R21.1 (#579 ✅ skill packaging framework)
- R21.2 (OAuth token-binding pattern)

## Priority

P1 — strategic for DACH enterprise positioning. First-party MCP makes
implementation cost low while strategic moat is high.

items.title: Validate pack-specific event payloads before ledger append
items.body:
## Current agreed context — 2026-10-07

**Scope:** Common-envelope plus owned payload contracts across all ingress. Local optional contracts exist; shared admission enforcement and complete conformance remain open.

**Required proof:** Test invalid domain fields before append, legacy/core compatibility and a supported unfamiliar pack; keep mapping coverage separate from contract presence.

**Shared decisions:** Core is mandatory. Optional memory/user/domain capabilities compose through declared dependencies, without pairwise hardcoded flows. Authenticated tenant identity resolves its authorized Spanner database and pack bundle; processing and retrieval use that same context. Never infer authorization from agent_id, caller-chosen database or artifact IDs.

**Tracking and status:** Parent #34 holds the reconciled six-bucket scope; #35/#42 own composition/capability controls, #43 tenant routing, #39 exact conformance and #41 real-Spanner execution. This is a scope/context reconciliation, not a fresh runtime verification. The issue remains open; historical reproductions below retain their original revision, backend and run scope. Local slice-one work includes optional contracts for all 23 PDLC events, path checks and bounded fixtures; admission, complete oracles, capability routing and cloud acceptance remain unfinished. Historical memory probes are diagnostic evidence, not cloud acceptance. No Redis/Neo4j runners or cross-backend migration are required. Pinned documentation links below are historical published snapshots; newer local reports/run artifacts remain unpublished unless explicitly linked to a published revision.

---

## Problem and evidence

Ingestion validates the shared event envelope and active-pack event namespace, but domain payloads are not validated against an event contract before ledger append. A declared event can therefore be accepted with missing or incorrectly typed projection inputs, leading to omitted nodes/properties or projection failure later.

Verified on `feature/engram-walkthrough` at `6a30dcf`:
- `src/context_graph/domain/ontology.py:300`: At the cited baseline, `EventDef` contained aliases and a note but no payload schema. The current uncommitted prototype adds optional contracts; shared ingress enforcement remains unfinished.
- `src/context_graph/api/ingest.py:87`: `check_events` validates `Event` and envelope invariants; payloads remain dictionaries.
- `src/context_graph/api/routes/events.py:92`: ontology admission checks event type, not domain payload fields.
- `src/context_graph/api/routes/webhooks.py:173`: translated payloads are appended without a shared payload-validation step.

## Intended behavior

Keep one common event envelope. Each ontology pack declares an event-specific payload contract. A shared validator checks normalized events after source translation and before ledger writes. For example, a CRM deal-created event missing a required string deal ID must receive a field-level rejection instead of silently failing to create a Deal.

Use the existing pack model, registry and ingest helpers. This does not require a separate ingestion pipeline or Python adapter for each ontology.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Extend pack event declarations with an explicit, bounded payload contract: required fields, supported types, optional fields and a documented extra-field/coercion policy. Reject invalid schema declarations at pack load.
- [ ] Add one shared validator resolving the contract by active event type. Errors identify event/index, payload field, and expected constraint without exposing the full payload.
- [ ] Enforce it on single ingest, batch ingest, NDJSON import and translated GitHub/Jira webhooks before the rejected event is appended. Single invalid input returns 422; batch/import preserve documented partial-acceptance and per-event outcomes. Specify webhook behavior for a delivery translating to multiple events, avoiding accidental partial writes.
- [ ] Declare contracts for current PDLC and CRM events from their actual producer/rule inputs; do not infer required payload fields from every node property. Decide and document compatibility for schema-less core/agent events, existing clients and historical replay.
- [ ] Preserve namespace ownership, signature/trust checks, deterministic IDs and dedup behavior. Historical replay must not silently rewrite the ledger.
- [ ] Prove valid CRM and PDLC payloads ingest, project and answer queries on the memory backend. Prove missing/wrong-type inputs do not enter the ledger across all ingest paths; keep existing fixtures passing.
- [ ] Update ADR-0018 and pack-authoring/bulk-import documentation with the selected contract and client migration behavior.

## Delivery and review

Priority: first. Estimate: M. Implement in a focused PR linking this issue; include before/after examples, acceptance-test results and compatibility decisions. Close only after review and the end-to-end criteria pass. Do not add a new schema service, queue or adapter framework without a demonstrated need.

## Reproduction added during the focused review

With CRM loaded and all storage ports on memory, post `crm.deal.created` with payload `{"title":"Missing ID"}` and a valid envelope. Observed: **HTTP 201**, **one ledger event**, and **zero planned Deal nodes**. The required identity is missing, but the event is accepted and cannot project its intended artifact.

The focused existing pack/ingest/retrieval suite passes (**95 passed, 2 integration cases deselected**); this missing-key scenario needs a new regression. Review the accompanying trust, completeness, rejected-link, lookup and provenance issues together when drafting the implementation plan.


## Pack integration feature acceptance additions (#34)

- [ ] PE-01/PE-06: contract/load checks must connect to declared mapping paths and explicit missing/null/extra/coercion semantics; optional path use alone does not make a field required.
- [ ] PE-08: cover all23 PDLC event contracts and an unfamiliar pack; use exact fixture oracles and classify declared events without deterministic outputs.
- [ ] Coordinate activation/version, projection and duplicate feature tasks under #34; these tasks own the cross-cutting policies rather than duplicating them here.

Cross-cutting feature tasks: #35, #36, #37, #38, #39. These additions are planned; prior evidence/status remains scoped.


## Published implementation context

- [This issue’s slice, scope and review gates](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pack-integration-context.md#issue-4) — slices **1;2**.
- [Full design and implementation sequence](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/2026-10-06-spanner-compatibility-plan.md).
- [Astra medium review and conformance requirements](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-07-astra-pack-engine-design-review.md).
- [PDLC event contracts inventory](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-event-contract-inventory.csv), [payload experiment matrix](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-payload-experiment-matrix.csv), and [public-source corpus and remaining gaps](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/5e9c883d8087420cb1bd848f27de8eb93cd09233/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/public-payload-corpus/discovery-pass.md).

Links are pinned to documentation commit `5e9c883` on `feature/engram-walkthrough`. This publishes design context, not unfinished runtime code or new compatibility results. Raw execution artifacts remain local; the context index states the evidence limits. All acceptance checklists retain their current open/scoped status.

items.title: Define the CE Persistent Store contract before storage-specific implementations
items.body:
## Goal

Define a small, implementation-independent Persistent Store contract for Claude Ensemble before adding more storage-specific assumptions to Memory, Knowledge, Graph, Learning, or indexing code. SQLite is the initial implementation target, not the contract itself and not a separate network service.

This is CE-only work. Do not turn this into a FlossWare-wide platform or create separate deployable services for SQLite or BM25.

## Contract scope

Specify the minimum shared semantics needed by CE consumers:

- Stable record identity and schema/version metadata.
- Create, read, update, delete, and bounded query operations where appropriate.
- Explicit transaction and atomicity boundaries.
- Idempotency and concurrency behavior.
- Durability, restart/recovery, and migration semantics.
- Structured errors that distinguish missing records, invalid requests, conflicts, unavailable storage, and internal failures.
- Scope/tenant/project boundaries where records are scoped.
- Provenance metadata and safe deletion/reconciliation behavior for derived records.
- Health/readiness behavior and privacy-safe diagnostics.
- Decorator compatibility: wrappers must preserve the same contract and compose without changing semantics.

Keep the contract small. Do not invent a generic SQL abstraction or expose SQLite-specific types, SQL syntax, or FTS5 details as mandatory public API. Add specialized operations only when a CE consumer has a demonstrated requirement.

## Implementation boundary

- SQLite is the initial Persistent Store implementation.
- SQLite FTS5 and its BM25 ranking function belong to the lexical-index/search implementation. BM25 is retrieval-time ranking, not a storage service.
- Embedding generation is separate from vector persistence/search.
- Vector search may use SQLite-backed storage initially, but vector similarity semantics must not be confused with generic CRUD or lexical BM25 semantics.
- No separate SQLite or BM25 daemon/service.
- Keep the implementation standard-library-first where practical and avoid introducing a database server.

## Dependencies and consumers

Review current CE consumers and state which operations they need: Memory, Knowledge, Graph, Learning, lexical/index maintenance, and ingestion/reconciliation. Avoid circular dependencies and avoid forcing unrelated consumers to depend on capabilities they do not use.

## Acceptance criteria

- A concise contract document defines operations, data shapes, transaction guarantees, errors, scope, provenance, and lifecycle semantics.
- A dependency table maps each current CE consumer to the exact contract operations it uses.
- SQLite implementation mapping is documented separately from the contract.
- FTS5/BM25, embedding generation, and vector similarity responsibilities are explicitly separated.
- Contract tests can run against a simple test implementation and the SQLite implementation.
- Decorator behavior and composition are specified and covered by contract tests.
- Existing CE behavior and acceptance gates (#666, #667, #674, #680) are preserved; no duplicate indexing or reindex work is created.
- No implementation expansion begins until the contract is reviewed and approved.

## Related work

- #666: existing SQLite-backed chunk index, FTS5/BM25 retrieval, and local MiniLM embeddings.
- #667: explicit full/incremental reindex and embedding backfill.
- #670-#673: intent detection, entity extraction, retrieval planning, and ranking/regression.
- #680: full-corpus ingestion and reconciliation.
- #674: installed-hook conversational recall acceptance.

## Out of scope

- FlossWare-wide foundation/service contracts.
- A separate SQLite or BM25 network service.
- Replacing SQLite without a demonstrated need.
- Introducing a new vector database or paid/external embedding provider.

items.body:
# PRD: Move embedding backfill off the retrieval hot path and measure retrieval latency

## Executive Summary
Move stored-entry indexing to durable background work so a search embeds only its query. New and explicitly retried Knowledge should become searchable within ten minutes under the documented normal-load envelope, without claiming a measured production SLA. Old missing vectors require an explicit bounded backfill; deployment must not start unexpected historical provider work.

## Problem Statement
Current retrieval rebuilds missing stored-entry vectors before similarity search. Entry creation also waits for an embedding, Knowledge ingestion commits chunk retirement separately from replacement writes, and two promotion paths can mark a version ready before a queued implementation would have completed its chunks. The previous historical preparation references a removed legacy-backfill service and is superseded by the selected current-source plan.

## Goals
- Remove all stored-entry embedding and mutation from retrieval.
- Durably recover admitted indexing after enqueue loss, worker crashes and retries, with one valid committed vector per entry generation.
- Keep Knowledge readiness and refresh promotion truthful until every expected chunk has a valid vector.
- Establish the approved ten-minute engineering freshness target with stage metrics and real disposable database/queue acceptance.
- Repair old missing vectors only through an explicit bounded authorized invocation.

## Non-Goals
- Change the embedding model, dimensions, ranking, audience policy or provider activation.
- Automatically index old historical rows at startup, deployment, retrieval or periodic discovery.
- Claim exactly-once provider billing, production latency, deployment or live acceptance from unit tests.

## User Stories
- As a person searching Knowledge, I want a search to use the index already available so that another entry's indexing does not delay my query.
  **Acceptance:** WHEN a search runs THE SYSTEM SHALL embed only the query and perform no stored-entry mutation.
- As a person saving or refreshing Knowledge, I want a truthful pending state so that incomplete content is not presented as searchable.
  **Acceptance:** WHILE an expected chunk lacks a committed vector THE SYSTEM SHALL keep its staged version pending and preserve any still-eligible refresh predecessor.
- As an authorized maintainer, I want bounded historical repair so that an explicit action controls its provider work.
  **Acceptance:** WHEN I request a bounded backfill THE SYSTEM SHALL admit no more than the requested maximum and return a cursor without automatically continuing.

## System Specification
Stored entries have durable admitted work, generation identity and a conditional processing lease. Work moves through pending, processing, retryable, succeeded, failed or cancelled states. Only the current live lease may commit a vector. Provider execution can occur more than once after an ambiguous failure; successful data commits remain fenced.

Admission records the actual authenticated principal for interactive operations and revalidates current user, key, organization and brand authority at processing and commit. Code-owned workflows retain validated execution authority; genuinely background memory derivatives retain their actual committed source-record authority. A context owner or remembered requester is never substituted for the admitting actor. An approval redemption binds the exact approved operation to the actual server-captured approving principal while preserving requester and memory ownership separately.

A staged Knowledge generation has a sealed immutable ordered chunk manifest, expected count and observed validators. Its readiness remains pending until that exact set has valid committed vectors. Successful completion atomically settles the version and any refresh/capture state. Failed refresh keeps the prior version only while existing visibility, retention, expiry and audience rules still allow it.

The bounded maintenance action requires the existing owner/admin authority, current organization membership, applicable brand access and personal ownership. New and explicitly retried content is admitted transactionally. Historical rows are admitted only by an explicit scoped request; periodic work recovers existing admitted work.

## Functional Requirements
1. WHEN an entry is saved or explicitly retried THE SYSTEM SHALL persist the entry and durable indexing intent atomically before offering work to the queue.
2. IF enqueueing is lost or a worker crashes THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL recover admitted work without requiring a search.
3. WHEN a search runs THE SYSTEM SHALL embed only its query, reuse that query vector across selected-source fanout, and perform no stored-entry provider work or write.
4. WHEN a duplicate job or stale worker returns THE SYSTEM SHALL allow only the current generation and unexpired lease to commit.
5. WHEN provider attempts are exhausted THE SYSTEM SHALL record a safe failure and require an explicit retry instead of silently resetting its attempt budget.
6. WHEN the same ingestion execution is replayed THE SYSTEM SHALL reuse its immutable generation rather than create new chunks or reset exhausted attempts.
7. WHEN a distinct authorized retry follows terminal failure THE SYSTEM SHALL fence the old generation and retain its attempt history.
8. WHEN Knowledge chunks are staged THE SYSTEM SHALL persist the complete bounded ordered manifest, chunks and intents in one transaction.
9. WHILE a staged manifest is incomplete THE SYSTEM SHALL keep its Knowledge version pending and prevent all readiness or refresh-promotion shortcuts.
10. WHEN every exact expected chunk is indexed THE SYSTEM SHALL atomically settle readiness, capture state and any valid refresh promotion.
11. IF source visibility, tenant, audience, retention, expiry or deletion makes content ineligible THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL prevent retrieval even when an old vector exists.
12. WHEN content is deleted or retired THE SYSTEM SHALL fence admitted work so a late worker cannot resurrect it.
13. WHEN a bounded historical repair is explicitly requested THE SYSTEM SHALL admit at most maxEntries from the authorized context base, with maxEntries between 1 and 200 and an optional cursor.
14. WHEN a historical batch completes admission THE SYSTEM SHALL return admitted and skipped counts plus the next cursor without an automatic continuation.
15. THE SYSTEM SHALL preserve existing historical vector bytes, eligibility and provider configuration during migration and admit no historical jobs from deployment.
16. WHEN retrieval stages complete or fail THE SYSTEM SHALL emit privacy-safe stage timings and honest success/error sample counts.
17. THE SYSTEM SHALL document how to calculate per-stage p50/p95 over defined windows and distinguish engineering target proof from measured production performance.
18. WHEN authenticated work is admitted THE SYSTEM SHALL persist the actual canonical principal and revalidate current user, key, organization and brand authority before provider work and before committing its result.
19. WHEN approved memory capture is redeemed THE SYSTEM SHALL bind its exact action, payload, approval state and actual approving principal without accepting a caller-provided authority marker or reconstructing requester key history.
20. WHEN background work is admitted THE SYSTEM SHALL validate its actual code-owned execution or committed memory source and recheck that authority and eligibility before committing.
21. WHEN a bounded historical admission returns THE SYSTEM SHALL preserve its operation counts and cursor separately from serialized context attributes and omit internal actors, jobs, leases and vectors.
22. WHEN the dedicated acceptance tier is invoked THE SYSTEM SHALL fail on missing disposable resources, skipped tests, missing reports or any failed acceptance case.

## Non-Functional Requirements
The freshness target is ten minutes from successful extraction and atomic staging under the stated normal-load envelope. The deterministic envelope is at most 200 eligible admitted chunk jobs and 200 manifests, one healthy two-slot worker, provider requests at most two seconds, database stages at most one second and a maintenance interval at most sixty seconds. This gives a 420-second engineering bound; it neither rejects larger valid work nor asserts production capacity.

Keep 1024 finite dimensions, current tenant and canonical opaque user identity rules, source citations, query ranking and selected-source passage budgets. Use fixed safe failure codes and metrics without source/query text, URLs, credentials or raw provider errors. Preserve public and self-hosted boundaries and existing test floors.

## Feature Phase Breakdown
1. **Durable foundation.** Purpose: establish recoverable indexing identity. In scope: additive schema, atomic intent, bounded queue and leases. Out of scope: model or provider activation. Completion signal: migration and lease/duplicate/race tests pass without changing historical vectors.
2. **Truthful indexing behavior.** Purpose: move stored work off requests while preserving Knowledge correctness. In scope: all current producers, manifest completion, refresh/readiness guards, retrieval-only query embedding and explicit bounded historical admission. Out of scope: automatic old-data processing. Completion signal: consumer, privacy and lifecycle regressions pass through the production modules.
3. **Acceptance and delivery.** Purpose: prove recoverability and measure the right stages. In scope: dedicated real database/queue/fake-HTTP acceptance, metrics, documentation and normal protected delivery. Out of scope: production backfill execution or live provider calls. Completion signal: current-head required CI and named migration/boot/race receipt pass; deployment and live acceptance are reported separately.

## Success Criteria
- Retrieval performs zero stored-entry embedding calls or mutations.
- Atomic writes and actual queue processing make admitted entries retrievable after lost enqueue and worker restart.
- Duplicate, expired, deleted and superseded workers cannot commit.
- No incomplete Knowledge manifest can become ready through ingestion, manual processing or refresh promotion.
- Explicit historical batches obey their requested bound; rollout creates no historical intent.
- The named acceptance tier runs all selected migration and runtime tests with no skips; existing tests and thresholds remain intact.

## Out of Scope
- Automatic historical backfill, provider spending during this implementation, production database/queue operations or infrastructure changes.
- New approval-token systems, hybrid ranking, model rotations, dimensions changes or generic queue frameworks.
- Replaying the obsolete historical 64-path packet or recreating its removed legacy-backfill files.
- Closing this issue solely from a source merge without the required runtime and delivery evidence.

## Dependencies
- Existing Contexts, Knowledge capture/refresh, worker queues, platform schedule registry and Router/OpenRouter embedding integration.
- Existing API E2E disposable pgvector PostgreSQL 17 and Redis 7 service route, with an additive dedicated acceptance tier.
- Current-source ownership and canonical plan header must be refreshed before executor allocation.
- Approved decisions: [ten-minute target](https://github.com/genfeedai/genfeed.ai/issues/5149#issuecomment-6334796655); explicit bounded historical admission confirmed by Vincent on 2026-10-22.

## Verification Plan
Run focused entry/queue/lease/manifest/refresh/retrieval/authorization regressions, the existing API and worker module/consumer guards, source and spec checks, package typechecks and relevant client/UI tests. The exact test manifest and engineering decisions are in the selected implementation plan.

Add the Context Embedding Acceptance tier with real disposable PostgreSQL and Redis plus a loopback fake HTTP provider. Prove actual migrations and legacy upgrade preservation, queue consumption and module boot, enqueue/worker crash recovery, lease contention, deletion/eligibility races, refresh barriers, bounded backfill and real similarity retrieval. Missing resources cannot become a skip. The named real database, Redis, migration, module boot and fake-HTTP acceptance must pass at the exact candidate head before source merge. Required current-head CI stays mandatory; local container unavailability requires the normal hosted acceptance route, never a production fallback. Auto-merge is enabled only after that named runtime proof passes.

## Risks & Open Questions
No unresolved product decision remains: the target is ten minutes and historical work requires an explicit bounded invocation. Provider execution remains at least once after an ambiguous network/process failure; no exactly-once billing claim is made. The target remains an engineering target until observed production counts and windows establish actual performance. Execution must stop for a newly conflicting file claim, a required unowned file or a policy gap rather than weakening a gate.

Current plan: https://github.com/genfeedai/genfeed.ai/issues/5149#issuecomment-6345470209

| Identity model | Entra ID app registrations, not Databricks-managed SPs — decided in comments below |
| Secrets | Azure Key Vault-backed Databricks secret scope — decided in comments below |

`databricks.yml` is wired to this, with `audit_schema_name` and `registry_schema_name` pinned per target (they defaulted to `"bronze"`, which under a single catalog would have silently merged all three environments' audit trails into one table).

## What remains

**Phase B1 — grants and verification**

- [ ] `GRANT USE CATALOG ON CATALOG ingredion_en` to each service principal — **and nothing else at catalog level.** A single `GRANT SELECT ON CATALOG` flattens the entire boundary in one statement
- [ ] `GRANT USE SCHEMA, CREATE TABLE, MODIFY, SELECT ON SCHEMA ingredion_en.ingredion_stg` to the staging SP; same shape for prod. Never `ALL PRIVILEGES`
- [ ] `READ VOLUME` / `WRITE VOLUME` per environment — the package archives files into `processed/` and `quarantine_files/`, so write is required, not optional
- [ ] **Verify isolation rather than assume it**: as the staging principal, `SELECT` against a prod table must be denied. Record the actual output
- [ ] Distribution lists for `notification_email` in staging and prod — both currently resolve to an individual mailbox, which stops alerting if that mailbox goes away

**Phase B2 — first deploys**

- [ ] `bundle deploy -t staging` with the SP client ID, before federation. Isolates "are the grants right" from "does OIDC work"; the grants are the more likely problem
- [ ] Smoke run in staging that actually **ingests a file** — Phase A's first three attempts all exited without reaching a write, which is why the checkbox was ticked and untricked twice
- [ ] Same for prod

**Phase B3 — supporting**

- [ ] Key Vault + Databricks secret scope, backing #115
- [ ] Per-environment Volumes — **split out to #160.** Source-file isolation is currently a naming convention, not a control: `READ VOLUME` is granted at volume granularity, so any principal that can read its own subpath can read `PROD/Raw/`
- [ ] Catalog name decision — `databricks.yml` says `ingredion_en`, the comments below say `ingredion_en_dev`. Reconcile, and decide whether a catalog named `_dev` should hold production tables. Renaming later means re-granting everything

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `databricks bundle validate` passes for all three targets
- [ ] `deploy -t staging` and `deploy -t prod` succeed, each running as its own service principal
- [ ] A staging→prod cross-schema read is **verified denied**, with the output recorded here
- [ ] No human identity is `run_as` for any staging or prod job
- [ ] A real file is ingested in each environment, producing a bronze table plus audit and registry rows
- [ ] `azure_setup.md` Step 12 written from the performed sequence, including problems actually hit — the pattern Steps 7-11 already follow
- [ ] `bronze_layer/README.md` § "What an administrator must provision" corrected — **it still describes the abandoned three-catalog model** (tracked in #161)

## Relevant files

- `azure_setup.md` — Step 12 onward
- `databricks.yml` — targets already wired; grants are not code
- `bronze_layer/README.md` § "What an administrator must provision"

## Blocks / relates

- **Blocks #113** — OIDC federation binds to the service principals
- **Blocks #115** — the secret scope
- **Split out: #160** — per-environment Volumes
- **Doc correction: #161** — README describes the wrong catalog model

## Notes

Two things worth carrying forward from Phase A, because they held every time:

**Nothing was found by validation; everything was found by deploying and running.** Five defects, each only reachable once the previous was fixed. Phase B should assume the same: budget for finding problems in staging that cannot be predicted from here, and do not promote on a green `validate`.

**"It ran successfully" was reported twice before it was true.** The first smoke run exited `FAILED`; the second exited `SUCCESS` while ingesting zero files. Phase B's acceptance criteria are written to require a *write*, not a clean exit, for exactly that reason.

**Trial limits.** If the $200 credit or the 30-day window binds, staging can be deferred — `dev` + `prod` alone still satisfies the separation model, and the third target adds later with no code change.
