items.title: Feature: reusable ontology-pack integration contracts and conformance
items.body:
### 2026-10-14 accepted tenant-isolation checkpoint

Public authenticated dispatch plus two pinned Spanner databases and 10 workers is verified for Core+User+Memory versus Core+PDLC+Memory:184 main + 12 restart assertions, independent audit and Astra acceptance. Final data retained; no database creation/deletion. [Verification and scope](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/4bd47dd/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/tenant-isolation-verification.md).

This checkpoint does not close this issue. Tenant native webhooks/global metrics/import/cursors/prune/replay/reconsolidate, general pending/draining/forced termination and pilot readiness remain outside the accepted proof; hierarchy #49 remains parked. Earlier dated source observations below remain historical context, while the feature requirements remain open.

## Latest checkpoint — User attachment/retry slice, 2026-10-13

- Completed and independently verified the bounded UA01–UA07 slice: 277 accepted Spanner assertions across Core+User, Core+User+Memory and User-off Core+PDLC.
- #20 interest attachment and #59 canonical User personalization are resolved; #59 is a native sub-issue of this umbrella.
- Newly discovered #60 is also a native sub-issue: production consolidation shutdown can leave SDK writes after task completion. It remains open and is a pilot prerequisite. Healthy harness coordination is not a production fix.
- #42, #39, #41 and this umbrella remain open for their broader scope. Enrichment #29, wider combinations, tenant isolation and the pilot have not started in this checkpoint. Stop for stakeholder review before the next stage.
- Code: `782ab1e`; [walkthrough and acceptance evidence](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/61475be/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/user-attachment-verification.md); [Astra final review](https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/61475be/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/user-attachment-review/astra-final-review.md). Final assessment data is retained at epoch29 with matching post-process fingerprints; historical migration remains excluded.

The original buckets below remain the owning feature structure; no additional feature bucket is required for these defects. Dated earlier execution/context statements retain their original evidence boundary.

---

## Latest G04 milestone — verified 2026-10-08

31real-Spanner checks passed for Change→Release→failed/successful deployment, with exact links/properties/evidence and no-write invalid/retry checks. PDLC3.0 scopes deployment identities by repo/service (catalog26events). #47 is the newly confirmed identity bug, fixed and cloud-verified. Evidence update: https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/issues/34#issuecomment-6053441691

This umbrella remains OPEN for remaining acceptance. No new feature bucket; no separate foundation reruns or migration. G05 requires separate approval and has not started. This checkpoint supersedes older milestone/status paragraphs retained below.

---

## Current G03 milestone — 2026-10-08

Goal Three verifies explicit planning → ticket → PR → reviews and verification through ordinary Engram HTTP, five workers, real Spanner and actual retrieval. PDLC2.1 adds bounded reference mappings, reviewer recording, edge-level commit SHA and trace weights; event count remains25. Both changes-requested/approved reviews and failed/successful test runs remain visible. Missing references do not cause invented links; invalid nested keys/verdicts/outcomes reject before ledger append. Detailed final evidence and remaining work are linked in the G03 comment.

This issue remains OPEN for acceptance beyond the bounded journey. G04 and later remain unstarted pending explicit stakeholder approval. Historical migration is excluded from all current disposable-experiment goals; in-run revision/retry/recovery checks remain functional coverage. Public multi-tenant dispatch and native document/source adapter compatibility are not signed off by this single-bound normalized-producer experiment.

---

## Current scope decision — 2026-10-08: disposable experiments

Stakeholder explicitly excludes historical-data migration, old-pack identity conversion and cross-version historical upgrade work from ALL current goals. Do not spend analysis/implementation/review effort on migration or treat it as a completion blocker. Focus on actual Engram ingestion, ontology projection and retrieval on real Spanner using disposable data. In-run revision history and same-pack retry/recovery remain covered. Existing migration-only scenarios/tickets stay deferred, never falsely passed or closed. Goal Three is still unstarted pending approval.

Persisted goal-wide scope and verification standard: https://github.com/arunmenon/Engram/blob/9294db7/docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-08-small-goal-inventory.md . This scope decision overrides historical migration acceptance text below for current goal execution.

---

## Current verified milestone — 2026-10-08

Goal Two verifies the bounded normalized PRD → Requirements ← HLD ← LLD planning journey, revision-specific approval and supersession, duplicates/conflicts/rejections, missing-reference fill and focused retrieval through actual Engram HTTP, five workers and real Spanner. Core remains mandatory; memory/user are disabled for this configuration. PDLC 2.0 extends the catalog from 23 to 25 and changes Requirement/DesignElement revision keys. Historical migration is not proved. #46 is the newly discovered retrieval defect; its final evidence is linked in the milestone comment.

This issue remains OPEN: G02 does not prove all PDLC journeys, whole-pack or multi-tenant compatibility. The original 32 child issues remain tracked; newly discovered #45 and #46 are additional children under #34. The exact executed foundation snapshot is preserved with the evidence; unrelated local foundation work remains preserved. G03 and later require stakeholder authorization. Detailed verification and run links are in the G02 milestone comment below.

---

## Historical context — 2026-10-07 (superseded by current G02 status above)

**Scope:** Feature #34 owns composable packs and agreed journeys, with mandatory core, optional memory/user, tenant-specific database/bundle routing and both retrieval paths.

**Required proof:** All originally reconciled 32 native sub-issues plus newly discovered #45 and linked prerequisites remain tracked. #41 is separate cloud sign-off, not evidence that this feature is complete.

**Shared decisions:** Core is mandatory. Optional memory/user/domain capabilities compose through declared dependencies, without pairwise hardcoded flows. Authenticated tenant identity resolves its authorized Spanner database and pack bundle; processing and retrieval use that same context. Never infer authorization from agent_id, caller-chosen database or artifact IDs.

**Tracking and status:** Parent #34 holds the reconciled six-bucket scope; #35/#42 own composition/capability controls, #43 tenant routing, #39 exact conformance and #41 real-Spanner execution. This is a scope/context reconciliation, not a fresh runtime verification. The issue remains open; historical reproductions below retain their original revision, backend and run scope. Local slice-one work includes optional contracts for all 23 PDLC events, path checks and bounded fixtures; admission, complete oracles, capability routing and cloud acceptance remain unfinished. Historical memory probes are diagnostic evidence, not cloud acceptance. No Redis/Neo4j runners or cross-backend migration are required. Pinned documentation links below are historical published snapshots; newer local reports/run artifacts remain unpublished unless explicitly linked to a published revision.

---

Engram needs a reusable, versioned agreement between ontology packs and the engine so a new compatible pack can produce its declared artifacts, evidence and retrieval behavior without pack-specific engine code. Loading YAML or accepting an event does not currently establish that agreement.

This is an umbrella **feature/enhancement**, not a replacement for existing defect issues. PDLC is the full-pack acceptance case; CRM and an unfamiliar fixture pack establish generality. Astra medium review verdict: **ready with conditions**. Blocking decisions must be resolved before their affected implementation slices; no compatibility sign-off is implied.

### Deliverables
- Explicit pack capability/activation checks, owned event contracts and authorized cross-pack subscribers.
- Reviewed source-to-event mappings and shared validation/trust across single, batch, import and webhook ingress.
- Defined event-to-artifact semantics: missing versus null, bounded list expansion, conditional/no-op behavior, ordering/stale-write policy and property ownership.
- Immutable duplicate policy for same ID/different content, including source-binding revision changes.
- API/worker interpretation compatibility and available historical rules before accepting new metadata; safe replay/upgrade policy.
- Exact relationship/transition evidence and correlated applied/skipped/deferred/failed/unknown processing outcomes, reusing current surfaces where possible.
- Reusable pack conformance fixtures with expected normalized events, exact graph deltas, forbidden effects and retrieval answers/evidence.

### Implementation sequence and review findings
| Slice | Required design/acceptance work | Existing issues |
|---|---|---|
|1: contracts and fixtures|PE-01 missing/null/cardinality; PE-02 ordering/property ownership; PE-04 duplicates; PE-05 revision/obligations; PE-06 capabilities; PE-08 exact fixtures for all23 PDLC events plus third pack|#4 #5 #8 #9 #17 #22 #28 #29|
|2: shared ingress|All-route validation/trust; persisted metadata round trip and compatible/refused N/N-1 worker behavior; valid/invalid unfamiliar pack; uncertain commit and conflicting duplicates|#4 #5 #17 #28; prerequisites #27 and applicable #26|
|3–4: recovery and artifacts|PE-02 A/B/A convergence; PE-03 claim/relationship evidence; PE-07 completion observations; worker ordering, missing endpoints and retention|#8 #9 #10 #14 #18 #19 #20 #29 #30|
|5: retrieval|Exact supporting events and excluded edges; uncertain negative answers; bounded pagination/deadlines|#6 #7 #24 #25 #31 #32|
|6: historical acceptance|Replay/rebuild/cutover, pack visibility and complete bounded Spanner journeys|#11 #12 #13 #21 #22|

PE identifiers refer to the persisted Astra report below. Existing issue associations are not evidence those issues already contain or implement the expanded scope. Track the disposition of each finding here and update affected implementation issues before executing each slice. Do not open eight duplicate bugs automatically.

### Acceptance checklist
- [ ] Resolve blocking contract decisions in slice1 and document the chosen policies; do not assume last-write-wins.
- [ ] Every one of23 PDLC event declarations has a contract and exact supported/no-op/extraction-only/refused classification; the current local classification is 16 deterministic, one extraction-only and six missing mappings.
- [ ] Each event has fixture-linked normalized values, exact artifacts/evidence or deliberate no-op, invalid inputs and retrieval expectations.
- [ ] CRM and an unfamiliar compatible pack exercise the same mechanisms without adding engine type-name switches.
- [ ] Test omitted versus null fields, mismatched lists/write bounds, A/B/A and competing subscriber updates, same-ID changed content, revision mismatch, disabled required worker, duplicate/replay and partial failure.
- [ ] Separate real public records/documents, reconstructed webhook wrappers and synthetic cases; retain source gaps explicitly. Current captures have not been executed.
- [ ] Run applicable end-to-end journeys through actual Engram→Spanner, recording bounds, fingerprints, exact outcomes, defects and cleanup in the existing run ledger. No Redis/Neo4j runners or memory substitution for these cloud journeys.
- [ ] Independent review and targeted acceptance evidence support each completed slice; no blanket compatibility claim from source inspection or counts.

### Scope guardrails
Reuse current registry, adapters, projector, consumers, evaluation and tracking. Add only demonstrated missing checks/metadata. Automatic adapter generation through PRs, general raw-capture infrastructure and a new orchestration service are outside this feature's critical path. No Redis-to-Spanner migration. Future packs must stay within supported DSL/capabilities; arbitrary ontology formats/algorithms are not promised.

### Persisted design and evidence (published documentation snapshot)
- docs/review/2026-10-06-spanner-compatibility-plan.md
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-07-astra-pack-engine-design-review.md
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/2026-10-07-astra-pack-engine-design-review-prompt.md
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-event-contract-inventory.csv
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/pdlc-payload-experiment-matrix.csv
- docs/review/spanner-compatibility/public-payload-corpus/discovery-pass.md

Astra review was code/document/corpus inspection only; no new runtime tests or cloud calls. Existing defect and compatibility statuses remain unchanged.


## Sub-issue implementation map — reconciled after pack/tenant discussions

These are the original six feature buckets, with the newer requirements incorporated. Buckets group scope; implementation follows the dependencies and reviewed slices. Core is mandatory and cannot be disabled. All accepted normalized events use the common Event envelope, enforced in ingestion code; domain payload contracts add checks. Only selected optional capabilities may be assumed available.

| Original feature bucket | Concrete scope, including latest discussion | Owning issues |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Pack contracts and activation | Compose required core with optional memory/user and compatible domains; dependency/version/conflict checks; explicit reusable capabilities; retain specialized workers without pack-combination branches; API/worker agreement; payload contracts and authenticated source trust. | #4 #5 #35 #42 |
| 2. Source mapping and ingestion | Explicit raw-source-to-normalized-event adapters; common envelope plus selected pack payload validation across single/batch/import/webhooks; duplicate conflicts and source/normalization identity; tenant binding before append; clear stored-versus-processed receipt. | #17 #28 #37; shared contract work #4/#5 and tenant context #43 |
| 3. Projection, ordering and evidence | Core Event/history plus selected pack rules; field mapping, omitted/null, bounded fan-out, ordering and ownership; shared Entity writes; transition/relationship provenance; missing endpoints and late causal links. No schema-based guessing of missing mappings. | #8 #9 #18 #20 #29 #30 #36 |
| 4. Worker completion and recovery | Enabled worker responsibilities and subscriptions; extraction/projection handoffs; retries and unprocessed-content retention; applied/skipped/deferred/failed outcomes; keep core summaries/retention independently controlled from optional memory. | #10 #14 #19 #38; composition gates #42 |
| 5. Retrieval and conformance acceptance | Audit both retrieval paths for fixed optional-pack assumptions and fallback behavior; selection-aware intents/seeds/traversal/evidence, historical disabled-data visibility, pagination/deadlines and honest incomplete answers; exact fixture proof across all declared PDLC events, agreed PRD→requirements→HLD/LLD and other journeys, CRM, unfamiliar pack and compatible combinations. | #6 #7 #22 #24 #25 #31 #32 #39 #40; capability gates #42 #45 |
| 6. Versioning, replay and historical acceptance | Interpretation identity and available historical rules; upgrades, disable/re-enable/catch-up, replay, incomplete rebuild failures and same-backend graph cutover preserving ledger; historical evidence and visibility policies. | #11 #12 #13 #21; bundle agreement #35 |

### Cross-cutting requirement: tenant isolation

#43 is a native feature sub-issue spanning every bucket. Confirmed direction: one Spanner database per tenant; a shared Spanner instance is permitted. Resolve tenant from authentication to authorized database plus composed pack/capability bundle. Handshake, ingress, workers/checkpoints, graph/search, retrieval/evidence/caches/cursors, replay/upgrades, admin/maintenance and evaluation must preserve that identity. Do not trust caller-selected database/agent identity, mutate global active routing per request or fall back silently. Different tenant pack selections and colliding IDs require adversarial verification. Separate Engram deployments are not required by this product decision.

### Cross-cutting proof: Spanner compatibility

#41 is a separate linked umbrella, not a duplicate feature or reparenting of defects. Track the 65-row baseline (14 passed, 36 failed, 13 not fully executed, 2 blocked at the recorded checkpoint) separately from new composition/tenant acceptance groups COMP-01–06 and TEN-01–03. These nine groups are planned, not executed; bind exact executable inputs and expected graph/read/forbidden effects before running. All cloud execution goes through Engram on real Spanner with recorded runs, redacted evidence, linked defects and independent review. No Redis/Neo4j runners or cross-backend migration. No compatibility sign-off from schema loading, local probes, 2xx receipts or plausible answers.

### Sequence clarification

Start by defining and enforcing composable pack/capability boundaries (#42/#35) with mandatory core, and tenant/database/pack routing (#43/#35). Define full event contracts and exact fixtures, enforce shared ingress, harden projection and worker handoffs, verify both retrieval paths and full agreed journeys, then complete historical/recovery acceptance. Prove a bounded end-to-end path early on Spanner and expand; it is not full feature completion. Existing partial runtime work stays explicitly partial.

items.title: [Feature] BloodHound attack-path risk scoring — the `attack-path` risk plugin (external data)

labels.name: state:awaiting-design
labels.description: Intent clear; needs an architecture/design/UX decision (architect or designer, not requestor)

items.body:
## Summary

Consume **BloodHound's attack-path analytics** — distance to Tier Zero, node exposure, reachable high-value targets, ADCS ESC findings, choke points — and surface them as **risk findings** on principals/identities. This is the `attack-path` plugin already named as "framework-ready, not built here" in [`docs/architecture/risk-scoring-plugins.md`](https://github.com/Fortigi/IdentityAtlas/blob/main/docs/architecture/risk-scoring-plugins.md) (§ *Future plugins*, flagged `needsExternalData`).

> This is **2 of 3** companion feature requests from a feasibility study ([`docs/architecture/bloodhound-integration-feasibility.md`](``https://github.com/Fortigi/IdentityAtlas/blob/claude/bloodhound-integration-feasibility-2tgoy0/docs/architecture/bloodhound-integration-feasibility.md)).`` The three are **related but independently buildable**.

## Plugs into #672

This belongs to the risk-scoring **plugin tier** being introduced in **#672** ("[Refactor] Re-architect risk scoring into a plugin tier — findings + explainability + override"). It's a concrete `needsExternalData` plugin that fits that framework's finding + reason-context shape. Build order isn't strict, but this plugin lands cleanest **on top of** #672's plugin substrate.

## This was the original motivation

Worth recording: the earlier BloodHound exploration was **specifically about pulling risk metrics** (attack paths) — not data-source ingestion. That instinct was right; this issue is the clean home for it. The two other companion issues (data ingestion #939, reverse feed) grew out of realizing BloodHound could be more than a risk source — but this remains the place where BloodHound is **irreplaceable**.

## Why BloodHound is irreplaceable here (unlike #939)

The feasibility study sorts BloodHound's graph into three buckets:
- **(A) Authorization facts** — memberships, roles, ownership, and control edges (`GenericAll`, `AdminTo`, `WriteDacl`, …). These are *data* → companion issue #939 ingests them.
- **(B) Runtime session telemetry** — dropped.
- **(C) Derived attack computations** — ESC classifications, shortest-path-to-Tier-Zero, choke-point scores. **This is bucket C, and it is BloodHound's unique layer** — analytics computed over the graph, not raw data. **This issue consumes bucket C as findings.**

Bucket C is exactly what a governance product cannot easily compute itself and what makes BloodHound worth talking to.

## How

- **Requires a running BloodHound CE instance** (this is the key difference from #939, which needs no server). BloodHound CE is free/OSS; no Enterprise licence needed for the read API.
- Read via BloodHound CE's `/api/v2` REST API — auth by JWT or HMAC-signed request — and/or the raw Cypher endpoint `POST /api/v2/graphs/cypher`, or the official SDKs (`SpecterOps/bloodhound-python-sdk`, `bloodhound-go-sdk`).
- Pull per-principal attack-path metrics; attach as `RiskFinding`-shaped records (score/severity + rationale + structured evidence), consistent with #672's plugin contract. **Findings, never `ResourceAssignments`.**
- Caveat: the Cypher endpoint has documented rough edges (`SpecterOps/BloodHound#79`) — validate large/whole-graph queries early.

## Relationship to the other two issues

- **Independent of #939**, but **complementary**: #939 (control-edge ingestion) can *tag* the bucket-C-relevant edges at ingest so this plugin has richer local context; not a hard dependency.
- Naturally pairs with the **reverse feed** (companion issue #3): if we feed our correlated superset into BloodHound via OpenGraph, the attack paths this plugin reads back become *cross-system* — paths BloodHound could not compute without our identity correlation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An `attack-path` risk plugin registered in the risk-plugin tier (#672), `needsExternalData`.
- [ ] Configurable BloodHound CE connection (base URL + JWT/HMAC credentials, vaulted).
- [ ] Pulls attack-path metrics via `/api/v2` / Cypher / SDK and emits findings on principals/identities with rationale + evidence.
- [ ] Findings only — nothing written to `ResourceAssignments`.
- [ ] Graceful handling of Cypher endpoint limits / large graphs.
- [ ] Tests per repo conventions (coverage ratchet respected); external dependency mocked.

## References

- Feasibility study §5.4 (Option C), and the three-bucket model in §4.2.
- `docs/architecture/risk-scoring-plugins.md` (§ Future plugins → `attack-path`).
- Risk-plugin tier refactor: #672.

## Related feature requests (BloodHound integration set — independent, not interdependent)

1. Collector **file ingestion** (data *in*, no BloodHound needed) — #939.
2. **This issue** — attack-path **risk scoring** (plugs into #672).
3. **Reverse feed** — export our correlated graph to BloodHound via OpenGraph (data *out*).

Cross-links in a comment below.

items.title: [Feature]: APY-04 — Reconcile Apple Pay transactions with CAL/card-site imports

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database schema, migrations, queries, and Supabase

items.body:
### Problem / proposed capability

Integrate CAL/card-site automated ingestion into the shared APY pipeline. Locate and inspect the actual owner automation integration and payloads; current CAL spreadsheet profiles alone do not establish the running automation's contract. **Do not remove or disable CAL/card automation.**

Apple first: Apple Pay immediately creates the financial transaction; later CAL evidence finds it, attaches/reconciles and enriches without a second financial transaction. CAL-only online/non-contactless purchases without an Apple candidate create normal canonical transactions. CAL-first then Apple-later must use the same policy where supported; explicitly document any unsupported source constraint.

### Matching and enrichment requirements

- Apply APY-01 coarse filters and ranking: resolved payment-source identity, exact comparable minor-unit amount and currency, merchant normalization/aliases, compatible transaction date/window, occurred_at proximity where present, safe provider/reference information and source conflict/confirmation state.
- Apple and CAL identifiers may be entirely different. Same-source replay must stay idempotent, and concurrent Apple/CAL delivery must preserve a single sufficiently identified purchase without collapsing legitimate repeated purchases.
- Both timestamps: use proximity strongly. Only one timestamp: other evidence can still establish a match. Insufficient distinguishing evidence: do not guess; record explicit review outcome without deleting/overwriting candidates or creating repeated financial effects.
- Use independent transaction_date and charge_date semantics; provider processing-date differences require the justified contract window, not arbitrary date changes. Correct comparable charge/original currency basis before considering amounts equal.
- CAL can enrich charge date, provider/card reference, official merchant text, reconciliation state and safe card-side metadata under field precedence. Preserve user category, notes, corrected description, tags and manual overrides; retain official text separately where appropriate.
- Preserve v1 external_id compatibility, spreadsheet/import behavior, dry runs, safe payment-source mapping, cancelled IDs and Loan/Savings invariants. Route applicable adapters through the service; avoid unrelated manual-flow refactors.
- Totals, Budget and reports count a reconciled purchase once before and after confirmation. Attaching evidence does not replay money, installment or domain actions.

### Behavioral acceptance tests

- [ ] Apple first -> CAL later gives one immediately active canonical transaction with two observations.
- [ ] CAL first -> Apple later is covered where supported, with any actual limitation explicit.
- [ ] Different Apple/CAL IDs reconcile and repeated same-source delivery is idempotent.
- [ ] Both sources with occurred_at use compatible time proximity; Apple with time + CAL date-only still supports evidence-based matching.
- [ ] Merchant alias differences reconcile without free-text equality being the sole proof.
- [ ] Provider processing date differences and charge_date distinct from transaction_date follow the reviewed contract.
- [ ] Same merchant/amount twice in one day remains two purchases; time can distinguish a later observation.
- [ ] Same-value/date candidates without enough distinguishing evidence require review, not auto-merge.
- [ ] CAL-only online/non-contactless transactions remain supported and create canonical transactions normally.
- [ ] Same CAL observation twice and same Apple observation twice do not duplicate cash.
- [ ] Concurrent Apple/CAL ingestion, conflicts and retry-after-failure remain safe with real persistence.
- [ ] User category, notes, corrected description and tags edited before CAL arrival survive enrichment.
- [ ] Financial reports/Budget remain single-counted, including corrected/voided/protected transaction cases.
- [ ] Existing CAL automation, external API and Excel/manual flows remain compatible or have an explicit owner-reviewed transition contract.

### Repository context / relationships

Parent: [APY parent #78](https://github.com/OzAvrahami/finance-tracker/issues/78). Follow its verified repository inventory, non-unique candidate/identity rules, immediate-accounting requirement and scope boundaries. Re-inspect current implementations before executing this child. Notifications #52 and Multi-user #63 are contextual only, not blockers; preserve their issues and relationships. Bank-balance #45 and tenant-ingestion #69 retain their separate ownership.

Blocked by: [APY-02 (#80)](https://github.com/OzAvrahami/finance-tracker/issues/80), [APY-03 (#81)](https://github.com/OzAvrahami/finance-tracker/issues/81). These must be native GitHub dependencies as well as readable references.

### Project / triage

Finance Tracker Project: **Backlog / P1 — High**. Labels: `feature`, `backend`, `database`, `testing`. No milestone or assignee. Status and Priority are Project fields, not labels. Keep Backlog → Ready → In Progress → Verify → Done; issue setup authorizes none of the future implementation transitions.

### Release / Version gate — initial planning assessment

- Release impact: **Yes for the grouped APY initiative** — new immediate ingestion, provenance and reconciliation capability.
- SemVer impact: **Minor candidate** for the backward-compatible initiative. A breaking API/schema contract requires reassessment rather than preserving Minor by assumption.
- Candidate release: **v1.4.0 proposed**, relative to verified published v1.3.1. Not reserved. APY-06 must recheck the actual published/prepared line, scope and compatibility before finalization.
- Grouping / included release candidate: **[APY parent #78](https://github.com/OzAvrahami/finance-tracker/issues/78)**, APY-01 through APY-06. One coordinated candidate using the highest applicable impact; no per-child release/version and no milestone at intake.
- CHANGELOG status: **Pending future implementation** — release-relevant work updates [Unreleased] during implementation, not this issue-creation task. Contract-only records need no independent product entry. APY-06 consolidates only finalized candidate entries later.
- Version-bump status: **Deferred** to owner-authorized final coordinated release preparation under APY-06/parent. Inventory and synchronize all seven authoritative fields together; all remain 1.3.1 now. No per-child bump, dependency regeneration or root lockfile.
- Publication status: **Out of scope** — no tag or GitHub Release publication authorized.
- Owner verification / acceptance status: **Pending future implementation and separate owner acceptance**, including real iPhone evidence where required; issue creation is not acceptance of an unimplemented feature.
- Deployment: **Out of scope**. Production migration/configuration/secrets: **Out of scope**.

APY-06 may finalize v1.4.0 only if it remains the appropriate next Minor and no breaking contract requires Major. Version synchronization occurs solely in the deliberate final coordinated preparation step, separately from owner commit/push, deployment, annotated tagging and publication.

### Planning-only authorization boundary

This issue records future work. Current authorization is GitHub issue, native relationship and Project setup only. Do not implement the feature or begin APY-01 under this authorization. Do not modify repository files, CHANGELOG or version fields, stage, commit, push, tag, publish, deploy, run production migrations, change secrets/configuration or touch production data. The owner performs all Git commits. Future implementation and real device/provider/production actions require their appropriate separate authorization.

Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OzAvrahami/finance-tracker/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and the [canonical development standard](https://github.com/OzAvrahami/finance-tracker/blob/main/docs/github-development-standard.md). Keep implementation, automated verification, owner acceptance, coordinated preparation, owner commit/push, deployment, annotated tag and GitHub Release publication distinct. A tag alone is not a published release.

items.title: [Bug] PostgresDb._get_table races on first concurrent write — shared MetaData mutation raises CompileError
items.body:
Copied from https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/issues/8196


## What's wrong

`PostgresDb._get_table(table_type=..., create_table_if_not_found=True)` is not thread-safe on the **first** call from each table type. When two threads share a single `PostgresDb` instance and both attempt a first-write that requires schema materialisation, the shared `self.metadata: MetaData` is mutated under each other's feet, and one thread observes a half-built `Table`. The downstream `insert(table).values(**eval_data)` then raises:

```
sqlalchemy.exc.CompileError: Unconsumed column names: <every column>
```

After the first write materialises the schema, subsequent single-threaded calls work fine — the race is only on the create-or-load-from-scratch path.

## Reproducer

Verified against **agno 2.6.9** (the current latest on PyPI as of 2026-05-31) and confirmed still present on `main` at `libs/agno/agno/db/postgres/postgres.py` SHA `4ce5213b`.

```python
import threading
import uuid

from agno.db.postgres import PostgresDb
from agno.db.schemas.evals import EvalRunRecord, EvalType

# Use any throwaway Postgres URL — Supabase, local docker, RDS, etc.
DB_URL = "postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:5432/db_name"

# ONE instance, shared across threads.
db = PostgresDb(db_url=DB_URL, eval_table="repro_eval_runs")

errors: list[Exception] = []


def write_one(marker: str) -> None:
    try:
        record = EvalRunRecord(
            run_id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
            eval_type=EvalType.ACCURACY,
            eval_input={"q": "hi"},
            eval_data={"score": 9.0},
            name=marker,
            model_id="stub",
        )
        db.create_eval_run(record)
    except Exception as e:
        errors.append(e)


threads = [threading.Thread(target=write_one, args=(f"m-{i}",)) for i in range(2)]
for t in threads:
    t.start()
for t in threads:
    t.join()

assert not errors, errors  # FAILS: CompileError('Unconsumed column names: ...')
```

Workaround (validated in production): **construct one `PostgresDb` per thread** rather than sharing a single instance. Per-thread instances each own their own `MetaData` cache, so there's no shared state to race on. The Postgres-level guarantees (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` checkfirst, per-row UUID PKs) hold up fine across instances.

## Root cause (suggested)

Confirmed on `agno-agi/agno:main` at `libs/agno/agno/db/postgres/postgres.py`:

- `PostgresDb.__init__` creates one shared `MetaData` per instance:
  - L161: `self.metadata: MetaData = MetaData(schema=self.db_schema)`
- `_get_or_create_table` mutates that shared cache on both paths:
  - L306 (in `_create_table`): `table = Table(table_name, self.metadata, *columns, schema=self.db_schema)`
  - L617 (in the load-existing branch): `table = Table(table_name, self.metadata, schema=self.db_schema, autoload_with=self.db_engine)`
- `_get_table` caches the result attribute (`self.session_table = ...`, `self.memory_table = ...`, etc.) so the race is only reachable on the *first* concurrent call per `table_type`. But that's reliably reproducible from any process that batches writes through a single shared `PostgresDb`.

## Suggested fix (two options, in order of simplicity)

**Option 1 — eager materialisation at `__init__`** (smallest patch):

Move all `_get_or_create_table(..., create_table_if_not_found=True)` calls into `PostgresDb.__init__`. Pay the cost once at construction; every subsequent `_get_table` call hits the cached attribute branch and never touches `self.metadata`.

**Option 2 — per-table `threading.Lock` around the cache mutation** (more flexible):

Add a `self._table_locks: dict[str, threading.Lock]` keyed by `table_type` (or one global `self._metadata_lock = threading.Lock()`), and wrap the `_get_or_create_table` body inside `_get_table`:

```python
with self._table_locks[table_type]:
    if getattr(self, f"{table_type}_table", None) is None:
        # materialise + assign
        ...
    return getattr(self, f"{table_type}_table")
```

Option 1 is simpler but eagerly opens 4–5 connections at instance construction (one per known `table_type`); Option 2 keeps the lazy semantics but adds lock contention on cold paths. Either is correct.

## Why we're filing

We hit this in production prep when adopting `PostgresDb` as the eval-persistence backend for an internal product. Our eval runner is single-threaded per process so the race doesn't bite us at runtime, but our acceptance-test fan-out reproduced it deterministically. We've patched our tests to use per-thread `PostgresDb` instances (the workaround above).

Anyone whose code calls write methods on a single shared `PostgresDb` instance from concurrent threads before the schema is materialised will hit this on cold start — e.g. concurrent batch eval/session/memory writers, multi-tenant ingestion pipelines, anything with a thread pool sharing a single db handle.

This pattern echoes other recently-fixed agno concurrency bugs — #7874 (`_safe_hook_call_async` race), #8013/#8015 (`MCPTools.connect()` race), #7790/#7791 (concurrent session-run silent drop). Same shape: shared instance + concurrent first-call → state corruption.

## Environment

- agno: **2.6.9** (also reproduced on 2.6.4)
- Python: 3.13
- SQLAlchemy: 2.0.46
- psycopg: 3.x
- Postgres: Supabase (Postgres 15) + RDS (Postgres 14)

## Acceptance for this issue

- [ ] Repro confirmed by maintainer
- [ ] Decision on Option 1 vs Option 2 (or third path)
- [ ] Fix lands; we'll re-enable the shared-instance variant of our test and bump our agno pin

items.title: SUBTERRANEAN-UTILITY-FABRIC-001: observability-first underground infrastructure intelligence and verification
items.body:
## Purpose

Define the system-level benchmark for a **robot-first, modular subterranean utility fabric** that can reduce theft exposure and lifecycle disruption while improving access to essential services. This is the cross-system integration and economics owner. It does not replace the existing domain-specific workstreams listed below.

The target is not a nationwide tunnel and not blanket undergrounding. It is a risk- and density-selected portfolio of:
- shallow, partitioned multi-duct corridors;
- protected service nodes and accessible chambers;
- robotic inspection / cable and duct maintenance paths;
- small service galleries only where access frequency, criticality and density justify them;
- retained, protected overhead or conventional open-cut alternatives where they are better.

**Sympoietic** means the infrastructure is co-designed and maintained by people, utilities, local operators, robots and accountable institutions—not that autonomous agents acquire authority to alter public infrastructure.

## Existing owners to compose — no duplicate registries or solvers

- Symtropy #3765: evidence-qualified trenchless / open-cut / renewal method eligibility.
- Symtropy #4905: robotic sewer inspection, observation quality, human adjudication and mission evidence.
- Symtropy #1732 and #1834: synthetic road–drainage–utility corridor verifier and robot capability envelopes.
- Symtropy #1843: construction fleet recovery and verified functional output under disturbances.
- Symtropy #3418: grid-forming / islanding / power-resilience qualification.
- Symtropy #3372: asset renewal, maintenance debt and service feedback.
- Symtropy #1951: reuse-first brownfield underground assets versus new excavation / no-build.
- Symthaea #7697 and #7727: civil infrastructure design and decision-value-guided site investigation.
- Symthaea #4795: robotic design, capability and evidence bootstrap.
- Sol-Atlas #450 and #662: renderer-independent spatial evidence / source provenance and South African siting evidence.
- Mycelix #5149: construction procurement, lot, inspection and approval provenance; use existing authority/receipt semantics.

The canonical asset/geometry, work-order, construction authorization, hydraulic/electrical/geotechnical model and evidence ledger remain with their current owners. This benchmark composes references and accepted outputs; it must not mint a parallel source of truth.

## South African motivation (source and year must stay explicit)

- Eskom FY2025 reports 1,585 conductor/cable/network-equipment theft incidents and R77m direct losses (FY2024: 2,380 incidents and R120m). This is the cable/conductor-specific figure currently available in the retrieved report; do not merge it with all non-technical energy losses. Source: https://www.eskom.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Eskom-integrated-report-2025.pdf
- Eskom FY2026 reports broader physical-security crime incidents down 13% and estimated losses down 18% to R191m, with 505 arrests and R34m recoveries. This aggregate includes theft of cable, coal, diesel/fuel, vandalism and other risks; it is **not** a FY2026 cable-theft-only statistic. Source: https://www.eskom.co.za/eskom-reports-second-consecutive-profitable-year-as-turnaround-strategy-execution-strengthens-operational-recovery-energy-security-and-financial-sustainability/
- South Africa's 2025 ITAC export-control guidelines retain a price-preference system for scrap exports; the 2024 Second-Hand Goods Act regulations notice was an invitation for public comments, not proof that every proposed control was enacted. Preserve legal status and effective date in any compliance profile. Sources: https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/202510/53605gen3579.pdf and https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/202407/50929gon5037.pdf

The system should complement lawful enforcement and traceable recycling. It is not a substitute for policing, licensing, prosecutions, community safety or utility governance.

## Paradigm shift

Move from:

`select a cable / pipe / robot / tunnel -> optimize its installation cost`

to:

`service demand + existing assets + site evidence + threat model + lifecycle obligations
-> compare complete corridor architectures
-> select eligible construction methods
-> install with evidence
-> inspect / repair / renew with bounded robotics
-> measure verified service and societal outcomes`

Key design hypotheses to test:
1. **Selective undergrounding, not universal undergrounding.** Compare protected overhead, conventional burial, shared duct banks, shallow service galleries, brownfield reuse and no-build on equal service requirements.
2. **Robot-first maintainability.** Standardize access nodes, duct geometry, pull paths, docking, localization references, isolation points and replaceable service modules where the engineering case supports them.
3. **Replaceable infrastructure, not permanent entombment.** Use pull-through / cassette concepts only after bend radius, cable tension, thermal rating, jointing, fire, water ingress and retrieval tests.
4. **Theft deterrence as a measured system property.** Reduce accessible recoverable material, harden and monitor access points, segment and isolate faults, preserve provenance and lawful end-of-life channels. Material substitution alone is not a security case.
5. **Shared infrastructure as a service.** Evaluate multi-tenant capacity and coordinated 'dig once' installation, while retaining physical and operational segregation for electrical, potable water, wastewater, stormwater, fibre and any other utility.
6. **Verified service contracts.** Measure accepted uptime, repair time, losses avoided and quality—not metres installed, alarms generated, robots dispatched or invoices paid.
7. **Reuse before excavation.** Characterize existing ducts, conduits, tunnels, mine-adjacent routes and brownfield assets before creating new underground space.

## Reference architectures to compare

Use equivalent service floor, route, load, reliability, design life, time horizon, cost year and scenario assumptions for:
- A0: current local practice (observed, not idealized);
- A1: protected overhead / conventional exposed network;
- A2: conventional buried single-utility installation;
- A3: shared partitioned duct bank with conventional maintenance;
- A4: robot-first shared duct bank and modular service nodes;
- A5: accessible mini-gallery / multi-utility tunnel in high-density, high-repeat-work locations;
- A6: reuse / refurbishment of suitable existing assets;
- A7: no-build / targeted hardening / repair-only.

Not every architecture is eligible for every service or site. Water, wastewater, stormwater, potable water and electrical assets must have appropriate independent compartments, interfaces, separation, access and hazard controls. No unpartitioned 'everything tunnel'. Gas / hydrogen and high-voltage services remain out of scope until a separate competent engineering safety case is supplied.

## Benchmark design

### 1. Subsurface information and design quality
Adopt ASCE 38-22 / 75-22 as an interoperability reference, not a substitute for South African statutory and utility-owner requirements. Their quality-level and 3D asset-data concepts are useful for expressing confidence and exchange. Source: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/innovation/everydaycounts/edc_8/subsurface_utility_engineering.cfm and https://www.asce.org/communities/institutes-and-technical-groups/utility-engineering-and-surveying-institute/publications

Measure: location/geometry error against exposed or independently surveyed truth; coverage and unknown extent; CRS/datum/unit correctness; age/currentness; conflict detection; uncertainty calibration; and percentage of critical crossings escalated to high-confidence investigation. A GPR trace or legacy drawing must not silently become a verified as-built.

### 2. Construction and method selection
Compose #3765 and #1732. Compare open-cut, HDD/guided boring, auger/slurry boring, microtunnelling/pipe jacking, impact moling/ramming, pipe bursting/rehabilitation and modular corridor construction only within each method's declared envelope. FHWA explicitly notes that unknown existing utilities and unsuitable soil/rock can rule out trenchless methods. Source: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/utilities/utilitycuts/man04.cfm

Measure accepted route metres/day; total cost per accepted metre; mobilisation, permits, traffic management and restoration; settlement; utility strikes; spoil/material/energy; service interruption; rework; and as-built evidence completeness. Report by geology, diameter, utility density and route class.

### 3. Robotic inspection, localization and maintainability
Compose #4905, #1834 and #1843. Current research has reported 84.8% mAP@50, 10.2 mm mean absolute defect-size error and 11 fps for one RGB-D sewer robot experiment in a 0.8 m pipe. These are paper-specific results, not a general industry score. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.measurement.2025.119694

A 2026 systematic review of 183 papers identifies multi-sensor fusion, signal-denied localization, real-time processing, interoperability and communications reliability as active bottlenecks. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aei.2026.104605

Measure: route and surface coverage; localization median/P95/max error and drift per metre; dimensional metrology error; per-defect precision/recall; critical-defect false-negative rate; confidence calibration / abstention; mission completion and retrieval; energy per metre; human review minutes; time to fault isolation; first-pass repair acceptance; rework; and percentage of eligible interventions completed without surface excavation. Keep sewer-specific baselines separate from cable-duct, water and power use cases. Use NASSCO PACP / WRC MSCC / EN 13508-2 only with a frozen jurisdiction- and version-specific coding profile; human adjudication remains authoritative until class-specific qualification. NASSCO source: https://www.nassco.org/resource/cctv-inspection-quality-in-sewer-cleaning

### 4. Theft deterrence and resilience
Measure outcomes normalized by asset exposure and service delivered:
- theft / attempted tamper events per km-year and per 1,000 asset-years;
- direct replacement cost and consequential service disruption separately;
- loss / outage duration and affected customers or service-hours;
- detection lead time, false alarms per km-month and sensor availability;
- tamper localization error, response time and safe sectional isolation;
- repeat targeting / recurrence after intervention;
- accessible salvage value and lawful recovery / recycling lineage;
- availability and restoration under simultaneous power, communication and sensor failure.

Compare material families by delivered electrical service, ampacity, voltage drop, installation/jointing quality, corrosion, thermal performance, mass, cost, embodied impacts, useful life, repairability and theft attractiveness. Aluminium is not theft-proof and copper substitution does not eliminate theft. No alternative conductor is accepted without applicable electrical design, type tests, utility approval and qualified installation.

### 5. Whole-life economics and public value
Use a discounted, auditable lifecycle model with identical service outputs and declared price year:
- CAPEX, financing, land/wayleave, survey, design and permitting;
- installation, mobilization, traffic, spoil, reinstatement and commissioning;
- energy losses, inspection, maintenance, security, repair, replacement and decommissioning;
- expected theft loss and outage consequences with uncertainty and correlated events;
- avoided future road cuts / multi-utility work and shared capacity revenues;
- contractor concentration, switching costs, local skills, wages, SME participation and distributional outcomes.

Report NPV, equivalent annual cost, cost per service-unit-year, break-even utilisation / repeat-work frequency, payback sensitivity, P50/P90 costs and Pareto frontiers. Do not compare a 2012 UK multi-utility-tunnel model or US trenchless unit prices directly with South African current costs. The multi-utility-tunnel literature finds economic tipping points are sensitive to density and repeat street works; reproduce the model with local quantities and quotations. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tust.2012.02.001

## Initial qualification gates (targets, not achieved results)

- 100% of critical route segments have explicit evidence-quality and uncertainty states; zero unknown-to-clear promotion.
- Zero false acceptance of seeded utility conflicts, unit/frame mismatches, hard geometric constraints or robot capability violations in the frozen synthetic corpus.
- Zero silent observation-coverage gaps: each segment is observed, unobserved, unusable, not reached or unsupported, with reason.
- Zero critical-defect auto-clearance from low-quality, stale, uncalibrated or out-of-envelope evidence.
- 100% of installed pilot assets link to an exact design/material/configuration revision and as-built evidence record.
- 100% of repairs counted as successful have an independent acceptance observation.
- Robot recovery and safe-stop success are measured separately from mission completion; no lost-robot or unsafe-actuation event is hidden in aggregate completion.
- Whole-life cost must beat or justify itself against the best eligible local baseline in the selected site stratum; no universal cost claim.
- theft and outage claims must be based on exposure-normalized, pre-registered before/after or matched-control evidence, not anecdotal incident counts.
- Employment claims count paid hours, local supplier value, wages, training completion and retained capability—not robot units or headline job multipliers.

## First synthetic campaign (offline; no runners or field partner required)

Freeze three abstract site archetypes and all assumptions in versioned fixtures:
1. **High-risk urban feeder corridor:** mixed existing utilities, high service criticality, frequent third-party works, constrained access.
2. **Industrial precinct:** multi-tenant demand, concentrated routes, service-node opportunities and a potential shared-corridor operator.
3. **Developing settlement / expansion edge:** phased demand, uncertain as-built data, affordability and future connection growth.

For each, compare the architecture set above under matched service requirements. Include hostile cases: unknown utility crossing; stale/incorrect as-built; groundwater/rock uncertainty; robot cannot turn / retrieve; cable thermal overload; flooded access node; failed communication; sensor outage; malicious access; material substitution with poor joints; missing authorization; common duct/fire/water event; utility-provider insolvency; and repair accepted without independent verification.

The independent verifier must use an oracle separate from candidate generation and emit Accepted, Rejected, Indeterminate or Unsupported. No composite readiness score. Keep exact inputs, source revisions, units, model limits, scenario seeds and output digests.

## Implementation sequence

P0. Add this cross-system specification and interface map; no production solver.
P1. Add a versioned architecture/scenario manifest and finite synthetic cases to the existing CIV-INFRA corridor verifier (#1732); do not build a parallel corridor model.
P2. Compose method eligibility (#3765), robot capability (#1834), inspection evidence (#4905), resilience/replanning (#1843) and reuse (#1951).
P3. Add a small independent whole-life / theft-risk evaluator with transparent input factors, uncertainty ranges and exact baselines; keep it separate from engineering eligibility.
P4. Bind spatial evidence from Sol-Atlas and authorization/provenance from Mycelix; Symthaea proposes / triages only inside explicit authority limits.
P5. Only after exact-head offline qualification, design an instrumented tabletop duct rig and a supervised field pilot with qualified engineers, utility owners and permits.

## Nonclaims / safety boundary

This issue does not establish that a tunnel, cable, pipe, conductor, robot or route is safe, legal, economically viable or qualified. It does not authorize excavation, energization, isolation, valve operation, dispatch, procurement, land access or work on public infrastructure. Symtropy's generic physics engine is not a geotechnical, hydraulic, cable-rating, protection-coordination or structural design solver. Use competent domain-specific solvers, applicable SANS / NRS / IEC / utility-owner rules and Professional Engineer sign-off for any actual design or construction. A simulation PASS remains only a result for the declared synthetic case.

## 2026-11-12 execution update

- Programme specification and machine-readable eight-suite scenario contract are in draft [PR #4911](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/pull/4911).
- South African deployment / permitting profile and lifecycle economics model are included in that PR.
- Dedicated non-energized cable-duct inspection / draw-tool benchmark opened as child [#4913](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/4913); this keeps cable-duct performance separate from sewer-crawler and walkable cable-tunnel claims.
- Research alignment added for IEC 63439-1-1:2025 terminology, IEC TR 63439-1-2:2026 roadmap, and the in-development IEC 63439-3-31 cable-tunnel inspection robot work item. The latter is not treated as a published standard and is not assumed to cover small microducts.
- Existing CIV-INFRA executable owner #1756 and its bounded synthetic-only claims remain separate. The new work does not claim its arithmetic drainage reserve is hydraulic simulation or that its utility envelopes are an engineering CAD / survey model.

Current delivered files on the PR branch: programme specification, South African deployment baseline, lifecycle economics model, cable-duct robot benchmark, manifest schema and eight-suite manifest. Files were fetched back from the branch and JSON was parsed / structurally checked; this is not a full JSON Schema conformance test, Rust build, CI run or engineering qualification.


## 2026-11-12 localization research extension

- Opened child workstream [#4925 — DUCT-LOCALIZATION-QUAL-001](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/4925) to qualify acoustic–visual localization, chainage uncertainty, route-anchor correctness, active sensing and task-level location claims.
- Added `LOCALIZATION_QUALIFICATION_V0_1.md`, `localization-scenario-manifest-v0.1.schema.json` and `localization-scenario-manifest-v0.1.json` to the existing research branch / draft [PR #4911](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/pull/4911).
- The new research is anchored to Worley et al. (2026), DOI 10.1002/rob.70368. Its sewer-pipe results are a literature reproduction baseline only; the paper explicitly identifies cable-duct generalization as future work. Data reuse is gated on author access and terms.
- The v0.1 manifest contains 12 planned synthetic scenarios across 7 method families. It is a campaign plan, not raw sensor data or executed localization results.


## 2026-11-12 state-of-the-art and spatial-interoperability extension

- Expanded [#4925 localization qualification](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/4925) and added a literature baseline matrix to the SUF research branch:
  - `LOCALIZATION_SOTA_BASELINE_MATRIX_V0_1.md`
  - `localization-sota-baseline-matrix-v0.1.json`
  - `localization-sota-baseline-matrix-v0.1.schema.json`
- The matrix covers Worley et al. 2026 acoustic–visual pipe localization, Sun et al. 2026 dual-resolution acoustic inspection, Chang et al. 2026 UWB/IMU utility-tunnel positioning, Nubert et al. 2026 Holistic Fusion, and the emerging Pipebots acoustic micromachine programme. These are separate populations and claim ceilings; no single pooled leaderboard is valid.
- New Sol-Atlas interoperability workstream [#755 — SUF-SPATIAL-INTEROP-001](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/sol-atlas-leptos/issues/755) and draft [PR #757](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/sol-atlas-leptos/pull/757) define a MUDDI v1.0-aligned underground evidence crosswalk. Sol-Atlas carries provenance-bearing spatial representations; utility owners retain canonical asset identity and operational state. The draft is not a MUDDI conformance claim.
- Standards / interoperability anchors include OGC MUDDI Part 1 v1.0, PAS 128:2022 as a survey-quality reference (not South African law), and IEC TR 63439-1-2:2026 for power-system robot validation.


## 2026-11-12 commercial industry comparator extension

Added an industry matrix to the same SUF research branch:
- `INDUSTRY_COMPARATOR_MATRIX_V0_1.md`
- `industry-comparator-matrix-v0.1.json`
- `industry-comparator-matrix-v0.1.schema.json`

It covers:
- RedZone SOLO (small sewer crawler);
- RedZone multi-sensor pipeline inspection platforms;
- DEEP Robotics X30 / SPock power-tunnel quadruped deployment;
- Coolight CL803D rail-mounted utility-tunnel robot;
- commercial fibre blowing/jetting tooling;
- RedZone Integrity asset-management/reporting software;
- NASSCO PACP/MACP, PAS 128:2022, IEC 63439 and OGC MUDDI.

The matrix separates vendor-reported specifications and case studies from independent measurement, and sets matched-profile evaluation rules. It explicitly forbids cross-comparing sewer robots, cable microduct tools and walkable tunnel robots as if they perform the same task.


## 2026-11-12 continuous-motion acoustic research

- Opened [#4953 ACOUSTIC-MOTION-QUAL-001](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/4953) to compare stop-go direct acoustic sensing against moving acoustic arrays and event-triggered acquisition.
- Added the benchmark protocol and machine-readable 14-case campaign to the SUF branch:
  - `ACOUSTIC_MOTION_BENCHMARK_V0_1.md`
  - `acoustic-motion-scenario-manifest-v0.1.schema.json`
  - `acoustic-motion-scenario-manifest-v0.1.json`
- Each scenario now has an oracle disposition and reference action/rationale. This is a deterministic policy-level corpus, not a physical acoustic propagation simulation.
- Expanded the localization literature matrix to nine studies across seven separate populations/tracks, adding the 2024 linear acoustic beamforming study, 2025 moving circular array / sparse representation study, 2023 guided-wave NDT work and 2025 active-SLAM uncertainty planning. Their metrics are not pooled across task populations.


## 2026-11-13 distributed fibre observability extension

Opened [#4972 FIBRE-OBSERVABILITY-QUAL-001](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/4972), a distinct workstream for:
- DAS fault/event screening on compatible existing communications/SCADA fibre;
- buried-fibre route geolocalization using traffic-induced seismic signals;
- separately labelled exploratory disturbance/tamper classification (not demonstrated by the published papers).

Added to the SUF research branch:
- `FIBRE_OBSERVABILITY_BENCHMARK_V0_1.md`
- `das-observability-manifest-v0.1.schema.json`
- `das-observability-manifest-v0.1.json`

The motivation is two bounded 2026 studies: Kamaruzaman et al. report a field event around 2.8 km on a calibrated 5.4 km MV underground cable corridor using operational SCADA communication fibre (DOI 10.1016/j.rio.2026.101093); Cohen et al. report DAS/traffic-based buried fibre geolocation with sub-metre accuracy, often tens of centimetres, in their studied conditions (DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2026.3729504).

The mandatory research distinction is **DAS fibre chainage != geographic route location**. Coupling and conduit attenuation are first-class profile factors. DAS alerting cannot operate protection, authorize isolation, dispatch, excavation or repair.


## 2026-11-13 DAS commercial benchmark added

Added a product/industry comparator package:
- `DAS_COMMERCIAL_COMPARATOR_MATRIX_V0_1.md`
- `das-commercial-matrix-v0.1.json`
- `das-commercial-matrix-v0.1.schema.json`

It covers AP Sensing DAS, OptaSense ATLAS, ODHF and QuantX, AP Sensing CAMOS as a distinct electrical current-sensing complement, and a 2025 IEEE review. Vendor-stated range, channel pitch and application capabilities are not treated as independent performance measurements. The Luminous research position is vendor-neutral intake, calibrated fibre-to-geography evidence, observability maps, cross-vendor replay and targeted independent verification.

# P0 integration and release gate

## Current checkpoint — 2026-11-10 (supersedes older dated checkpoints)

**Main at this governance checkpoint:** [`a08d881`](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/commit/a08d881a9ba0a1a0e2c99f1c18dee5fb08020816), docs-only README status reconciliation. The prior merged [#16](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/pull/16) code/doc baseline is `7ba650f`; its reported [Go #42367819777](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/actions/runs/42367819777) and [contract #42367819845](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/actions/runs/42367819845) runs succeeded. **Exact-main [Go validation #42654918594](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/actions/runs/42654918594) SUCCESS** for the docs-only `a08d881` commit; this is repository validation, not live Kubernetes/Kueue/DRA or deployed IAM acceptance. No PR is currently open in this repository.

**Merged implementation foundations:** Workload/initial Allocation/Operation + Outbox atomic acceptance (#18), SPIFFE-backed unmounted Workload handlers (#20), FakeProvider UID/generation conformance (#31/#45), Provider registration and Drain acceptance CAS (#34/#42), unmounted management handlers (#52), E1 independently scoped policy/FINAL SQL controls (#41/#44), Provider audit isolation migration 0013 (#55). Design/contract PRs #9/#12/#14/#16 are also **merged**, not Draft. Repository GREEN does not attest deployed IAM, authenticated source evidence, actual device realization, release, metering or billing. The deleted/unavailable #53 issue is **not** an acceptance authority; this #3 and open child gates below remain authoritative.

**Keep OPEN — no production promotion or implicit migration:**
- [#32](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/issues/32): authenticated Provider READY/DEGRADED/Drain, exact-UID cleanup and cost-liability release; migrate 0013 only after independent `ccp_provider_audit_owner` provisioning and restored-role/catalog validation.
- [#33](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/issues/33): real Kueue queue/admission, Kubernetes Job/Pod UID, ResourceClaim/DRA device-claim assignment/deallocation, restart/relist and quota-release evidence. Kubernetes/Kueue/DRA remain scheduling, admission and device authorities.
- [#39](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/issues/39): independently issued and authenticated EvidencePolicy/source provenance, production DB IAM and cost/finance trust; E1 `FINAL` in a repository test is not certified billing evidence.
- This #3: ACP/Runtime/EngageGuard owner/Permit consumer contracts, tenant authorization/RLS, durable transport, release gates and actual process/cluster acceptance.

**Next bounded acceptance order:** (1) disposable PG16 identity/role, migration 0012→0013 and backup/restore checks; (2) authenticated Provider Inspect and process-restart lost-ACK: persisted UNKNOWN → inspect-first → exact resource UID convergence without duplicate create/delete; (3) disposable Kubernetes/Kueue/DRA workload admission/preemption, stale generation, Job UID replacement, ResourceClaim release and missing/quota-stale observation tests (see #33); (4) only after source-proof, run allocated vs busy/effective GPU-hour and cost-liability accounting experiments. No live acceptance environment or cost measurement was obtained in this checkpoint.

Historical sections below are retained as time-stamped evidence; their PR Draft/open states and older main SHAs must not be interpreted as current state.

---

**Authoritative project:** `avaargsh/compute-control-panel`  
**Retirement decision:** `gpu-compute-platform` is retired as an active delivery project. Treat it only as historical reference/migration input; all new implementation, provider adapters, release gates and operational evidence belong here.

Last governance review: **2026-11-04**. Current-state checkpoint appears first; older sections are retained as historical evidence.

## Current checkpoint — 2026-11-04 (supersedes historical snapshots below)

**Current main:** [`e5f294410304f9db23fde030f874274bd3df9b42`](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/commit/e5f294410304f9db23fde030f874274bd3df9b42), including merged [#27 Workload validation](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/pull/27), [#28 JSON null fail-closed](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/pull/28), [#29 terminal Inspect freshness](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/pull/29), and [#30 recovery lease bounds](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/pull/30).

## Non-negotiable invariants

- No custom scheduler. Kueue owns admission and quota; Kubernetes scheduler owns Pod placement; DRA/provider owns device/resource realization.
- A Workload is not admitted/running/released from an API acknowledgement.
- UNKNOWN is inspected/reconciled before retry; never blind-retry an ambiguous side effect.
- Stale generations cannot overwrite current Workload; stale CREATE requires explicit compensation.
- DELETE finality requires absence of the exact provider resource UID and evidence for applicable reservation/quota release.
- FakeProvider is test-only until an authenticated production provider adapter exists.
- Never treat a single-PostgreSQL transaction as distributed exactly-once delivery.

- Read persistence uses a read-only Repeatable Read transaction, filtering by authenticated Tenant. HTTP read path separately checks Project grants and an injected Read authorizer. Cross-Tenant and out-of-Project requests return 404; sensitive lease/fence/provider UID/digest fields are omitted.
- Added a SPIFFE/mTLS Authenticator adapter that requires a verified TLS certificate chain, exact leaf match, one SPIFFE URI SAN in the configured trust domain, and exact resolver Subject binding. It copies resolver Project grants before returning the principal.
- Exact PR #15 HEAD `131869fbb33c25eaad2fca9b87b9f5b751ff675a` passed [Go validation #41802221330](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/actions/runs/41802221330): format, checksum, PostgreSQL migration twice, SQL constraints, vet, Race and 3× SIGKILL all success.
- Rollout remains blocked/staged: the default process still exposes only health/meta; production client CA bundle, workload identity directory, Guard/Project Read/Write policies, Provider selection/Inspect authentication, tenant RLS, broker workers, Kueue/DRA/Pod evidence and production restore remain outstanding.


## SPIFFE identity directory and bounded read projection — 2026-11-04

- PR #15 now includes migration `0004`: trusted SPIFFE service identity → Tenant/Service, time-bounded active/revoked Project grants, and append-only audit snapshots on all identity/grant mutations. The PostgreSQL repository implements `WorkloadIdentityResolver` using a read-only Repeatable Read snapshot.
- PostgreSQL integration tests prove grant resolution/revocation, full identity revocation, audit records written transactionally, audit rollback on parent transaction rollback, and rejection of cross-Tenant grants via composite FK.
- Workload GET history now has a hard bound of 100 Allocations + 100 Operations, returns newest records chronologically and emits `history_truncated` when older history is omitted.
- Exact HEAD `bc0f43f1b67923fd705b6ce0ea95ba3768240000` passed [Go validation #41804347190](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/actions/runs/41804347190), including format/checksum, migration double-apply, schema, vet, Race and 3× SIGKILL.
- Production rollout remains gated: no trust CA bundle or SPIFFE provisioned identities configured in main; no concrete Guard/Project authorizer, provider selector/Inspect, tenant RLS, durable broker workers, or Kueue/DRA/Pod evidence. API remains Draft/unmounted.


## Main branch integration cleanup — 2026-11-04

- Go/PostgreSQL foundation PR #2 was squash-merged to `main` as `1547c18c3a4c4c44f141228e67f3fa75c80dfd85`. The merge scope is the non-production foundation only; default main still does not expose mutation APIs or wire Provider/broker workers.
- Atomic Workload acceptance was integrated via clean main-based [PR #18](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/pull/18), squash merge `0fbb68a503613cdcca22335894be84b8c4a2e60d`, exact-head Go CI [#41805418061](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/actions/runs/41805418061) green. It atomically commits Workload + PENDING Allocation + bound CREATE Operation + accepted/pending Outbox events; low-level primitives emit non-dispatchable recorded events.
- Old stacked PR #11 is closed unmerged; it is superseded by PR #18. This avoids duplicate foundation files in review.
- Economics runtime calculator is being transferred from old PR #10 to clean main-based [PR #19](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/pull/19), four implementation files; exact-head CI pending. Historical PR #10 CI [#41791418652](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/actions/runs/41791418652) passed.
- Authenticated Workload API/GET, SPIFFE resolver and identity directory are being transferred from old stacked PR #15 to clean main-based [PR #20](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/pull/20), 16 files; exact-head CI [#41806276439](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/actions/runs/41806276439) is running. Historical exact-head CI [#41804347190](https://github.com/avaargsh/compute-control-panel/actions/runs/41804347190) passed all Go gates.
- The current accepted scope remains non-production: no concrete production CA/trust configuration, Guard/Project policy engine, authenticated Provider selector/Inspect, tenant RLS/least-privilege runtime DB role, durable broker subscriber, or real Kueue/DRA/Pod evidence. items.title: Epic: bootstrap FDE Agent Platform outcome-delivery control plane
items.body:
## Objective
Build the public, domain-neutral FDE Agent Platform as an **Outcome Delivery OS** that converts enterprise intent, evidence, expert behavior, policies, systems, and baselines into governed Digital Employees; executes only through constrained, durable, observable controls; and binds technical receipts to measurable outcomes without collapsing Human authority or private/public boundaries.

## Shared procedural authority

Every unfinished issue is directed by canonical procedures from:

```text
ed3c/skills-shared@ec5a240fa3cbafda2c6a8bce0ae12143e0992f80
```

Canonical binding and no-vendoring policy: #14.

Skill bodies, shared system prompts, reference procedures, scripts, schemas, and architecture rubrics remain in `skills-shared`. `fde-agent-platform` stores only repository-specific bindings, profiles, task packets, product code/adapters, synthetic fixtures, tests, and exact-subject receipts. No local `SKILL.md` or mirrored canonical `skills/` body is allowed.

## Foundation stack

1. #2 / PR #5 — repository control plane and Shadow Architecture governance.
2. #3 / PR #6 — public contracts and synthetic fixtures.
3. #4 / PR #7 — deterministic Role Pack + Tenant Overlay compiler.
4. #14 / PR #24 — exact external `skills-shared` binding and executable no-vendoring controls.
5. #47 / PR #48 — Agent read order, directory State Machines, full Issue DAG, data flow, and molecular Git Town Stack-PR index.
6. #13 — exact Git Town, local Forgejo, worktree, reconciliation, Actions, and publication receipts.

The executable documentation entrypoints are the root `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture/README.md`, `docs/governance/issue-dag.md`, and `docs/governance/stack-index.md` on PR #48. They index consumer-specific state and requirements; canonical Skill bodies remain external.

## Business, engagement, and organizational plane

- #25 — opportunity triage, baseline, Outcome Charter, and Bounded Value Pilot.
- #42 — full FDE engagement lifecycle and phase-gate orchestration.
- #18 — Human FDE Workbench, process-owner review, approvals, and executive governance.
- #37 — Internal FDE enablement, Domain Champion training, adoption, and handoff.
- #20 — managed operations, SLOs, incident ownership, FDE capacity, and termination.
- #36 — hybrid managed-service pricing, outcome settlement candidates, and SLA credits.

## Evidence, data, and context plane

- #26 — multi-source engagement evidence ingestion, redaction, and entity disambiguation.
- #45 — Data-for-Agent semantic contracts, quality, lineage, and schema/meaning drift.
- #8 — bitemporal Evidence Graph and Current-State Process Twin.
- #27 — provenance-aware retrieval and minimal sufficient ContextPack assembly.
- #29 — PostgreSQL persistence, bitemporal tenancy, migrations, and append-only audit.
- #33 — private Tenant Overlay resolver and exact-digest handoff across dual forge.

## Design, authority, and compilation plane

- #15 — Role Pack, Tenant Overlay reference, Outcome Contract, and compiled-spec registries.
- #28 — WorkflowSpec / ChangeSpec DSL, compiler, and target-state workflow architect.
- #9 — Policy Gateway and Connector Capability Registry.
- #22 — tenant isolation, secrets, MCP/tool authorization, and threat-model evals.
- #44 — enterprise SSO, directory roles, approval signatures, delegation, and access lifecycle.

## Integration, execution, release, and observability plane

- #30 — typed Connector SDK, synthetic capability adapters, and MCP gateway boundary.
- #10 — deterministic durable-runtime simulator, Runtime Receipts, and drift reconciliation.
- #40 — real durable-orchestration adapter, persistent timers, outbox, and crash recovery.
- #17 — simulation, risk-weighted progressive authority, Change Controller, and rollback.
- #32 — trace correlation, audit integrity, redaction, and outcome linkage.
- #34 — SaaS-rich, platform-centric, legacy, private-VPC, and air-gapped deployment profiles.
- #46 — first authorized private read-only/draft System-of-Record connector canary.

## Evaluation, model, learning, and evidence plane

- #31 — multi-layer Eval Pack registry, replay harness, mutation controls, and architecture receipts.
- #12 — model registry, routing policy, version pinning, shadow dual-run, and release train.
- #16 — expert-behavior trace store and governed candidate-Skill mining.
- #19 — failure clustering, reusable asset extraction, and portfolio productization.
- #35 — governed repair routing and post-training dataset lifecycle.
- #23 — independent validation of Varick/Lingyang claims and benchmark artifacts.

## Outcome and economics plane

- #11 — Outcome Ledger, attribution, unit economics, dispute, and settlement-ready records.
- #25 — pre-engagement baseline and counterfactual contract.
- #36 — value-aligned commercial model without automatic invoicing.

## Product and developer surfaces

- #38 — bounded customer-support, sales, marketing, operations, and finance Role Pack catalog.
- #39 — typed API, SDK, CLI, plugin contracts, and synthetic integration examples.
- #21 — first complete synthetic AP invoice/PO exception Digital Employee capstone.

## Assurance and production-readiness plane

- #41 — load, chaos, backup/restore, disaster recovery, capacity, and Human-review budgets.
- #43 — enterprise assurance-control mapping and evidence-pack generation without self-certification.
- #46 — exact private sandbox connector admission before any real deployment claim.

## Hard invariants

- Customer evidence, identities, credentials, private policies, system mappings, private Tenant Overlays, and customer-specific connectors never enter public GitHub.
- Tenant Overlays may restrict a Role Pack but never widen authority.
- Prohibited actions survive composition, release, model changes, retry, recovery, and handoff.
- Generated artifacts bind exact normalized input digests, contract versions, environment, and evidence subjects.
- Parsed documents, retrieval results, model output, expert behavior, external case reports, and business telemetry are candidates/evidence classes, not self-authorizing truth.
- Deterministic policy owns authorization, transition legality, accounting, idempotency, reconciliation, and release-blocking invariants.
- Natural-language requests become typed ChangeSpec candidates; they never execute directly.
- Git Town, Forgejo, local verification, GitHub Actions, publication, merge, release, production, commercial settlement, and business outcomes remain separate evidence lanes.
- Shared procedures direct execution but cannot grant merge, publication, permission, credential, legal, financial, release, or production authority.
- Source-reported external cases never count as this repository's runtime or outcome PASS.
- Planned directories, branches, PR atoms, providers, and state transitions remain explicitly `PLANNED` or `NOT_EXERCISED`; documentation cannot promote them.

## Evidence boundary

Current GitHub connector work can observe/create GitHub issues, branches, commits, and draft PRs. Live local Forgejo, Git Town executable, linked worktrees, private Tenant Overlay resolution, exact-head Actions, real identity/connector/model providers, production runtime, customer acceptance, commercial settlement, and business outcomes remain `ABSENT`, `NOT_EXERCISED`, or `HUMAN_ADMIT_REQUIRED` until their owning runtime/organization emits exact-subject evidence.

## Completion rule

This epic closes only when every linked issue is either:

1. completed at its explicitly declared evidence ceiling with exact-subject receipts; or
2. terminated, superseded, or redirected with a reasoned disposition and affected dependency routes updated.

A mentioned Skill, source-reported case, green leaf branch, successful model response, sandbox canary, documentation diagram, or transport-level success cannot close the epic by itself.
