items.title: Unified metric ingestion contract across agent/sysmon/snmp, native add-ons, and wasm plugins (OCSF-correct)
items.body:
Migrated from Forgejo.

Original Forgejo issue: #3788
Original author: @mfreeman451
Original URL: https://code.carverauto.dev/carverauto/serviceradar/issues/3788
Original created: 2026-06-13T19:41:52Z

---

## TL;DR

A single CPU-utilization metric reaches the anomaly engine through **three structurally disjoint pipelines** (Go agent sysmon, WASM/native plugin via `plugin_result`, native add-on via OTLP relay) that converge **only** on shared gRPC transport (`AgentGatewayService.StreamStatus` with opaque JSON in `GatewayServiceStatus.Message`, disambiguated by an agent-set `Source` string) and shared `IngressId`/`Sr-Ingress-*` attribution headers — **never on schema, subject, point-identity, or storage**. Three series-identity algorithms and three DB sinks (`cpu_metrics`, `timeseries_metrics`, `otel_metric_points`) mean the same physical core produces three uncorrelatable anomaly series, and only the OTLP path is analyzed by default.

The core defects, all verified against code:

1. **Metrics are smuggled inside status/check-result envelopes** because producers have no first-class metric emit path. The agent-gateway then does a **parse-forward-reparse-republish** dance — the same metric JSON is decoded up to **three times** (gateway publisher → core `StatusHandler` after `forward` → core `Metrics` processor off NATS).
2. **Metric-shape fragmentation** is the real disease, *not* OCSF: 4 wire schemas, 3 sinks, 3 non-alignable series-identity recipes, no shared point identity.
3. **No `kind` / `temporality` anywhere in the producer SDKs**, and the anomaly consumer **discards `kind`/`temporality`/`unit` even when the OTLP path supplies them** — a cumulative counter fed raw into z-sigma looks like a ramp.

**OCSF is NOT mis-used.** ServiceRadar correctly keeps metric time-series out of OCSF classes; the separation is deliberate and documented (`elixir/serviceradar_core/lib/serviceradar/event_writer/ocsf.ex:16-20`). The fix is metric-shape unification, which is **orthogonal to OCSF** and must not be solved by routing into it.

**The fix is additive, not a rewrite.** PR #3787 already shipped `serviceradar.metric.v1` as a thin bridge and is the de-facto reference implementation. Evolve it to an OTLP-grade contract (`schema_version 1→2`, add `resource`/`kind`/`temporality`/`points[]`), give all producers a first-class metric emit path, lower the legacy sysmon/snmp/shadow special-cases onto it, and delete the migration-era debt.

---

## Architectural principle

> **Metrics are a first-class signal.** Producers (WASM plugins, native add-ons, and the agent sysmon/snmp/icmp/mtr/sweep/rperf collectors) emit one `serviceradar.metric.v1` shape **directly onto a metric path** — never embedded inside a status / check-result / plugin-result envelope. The gateway stops re-extracting metrics from statuses, and the per-source (`sysmon`/`snmp`/`plugin`) special-cases collapse into one emit + one ingest + one sink.

---

## Current state — four disjoint pipelines (CPU metric traced end-to-end)

| | Go agent sysmon | WASM/native plugin | native add-on OTLP relay |
|---|---|---|---|
| **producer shape** | `MetricSample.cpus[]{core_id,usage_percent}` (`go/pkg/sysmon/metrics.go:25-180`) | `Metric{name,value,unit,warn,crit,min,max}` (`serviceradar-sdk-go/sdk/result.go:52-60`; Rust `src/result.rs:138-184`) | OTLP `NumberDataPoint` in `ExportMetricsServiceRequest` |
| **wrap / source** | JSON in `GatewayServiceStatus.Message`, `Source="sysmon-metrics"` (`push_loop_status.go:200-233`) | embedded in `serviceradar.plugin_result.v1` over `env.submit_result`, `Source="plugin-result"` | opaque OTLP, `Source="otlp-relay"` |
| **gateway publisher** | `SysmonMetricsPublisher` → `serviceradar.sysmon.metrics.v1` → `metrics.sysmon.<family>` | `PluginMetricsPublisher` → `serviceradar.metric.v1` → `metrics.timeseries.<type>.<name>` | `OtlpRelayPublisher` → verbatim → `otel.metrics.raw` |
| **stream** | `metrics` | `metrics` | `events` (separate) |
| **core processor → sink** | `Metrics`→`SysmonMetricsIngestor` → **`cpu_metrics`** per-family hypertable | `Metrics`→`Telemetry` → **`timeseries_metrics`** | `OtelMetrics` (protobuf) → **`otel_metric_points`** |
| **anomaly series id** | `sysmon:cpu:<host>:<core_id>` | `cpu:<TimeseriesSeriesKey md5>` | `otel:<svc>:<name>:<attributes_hash>` |
| **kind/temporality/unit** | none | none (unit stored, then dropped) | **full — then discarded by consumer** |

The gateway is **not a normalizer** — it is four source-keyed pass-through publishers selected by the agent-supplied `Source` string (`status_processor.ex:57-97,328-431`).

### Divergences (why the same core yields three uncorrelatable series)
- **3 series-identity algorithms**, none alignable: sysmon string-built (`sample_extractor.ex` ~`:123`), plugin `TimeseriesSeriesKey` md5 (`timeseries_series_key.ex:6-35`), OTLP `attributes_hash` recipe-v2 (`otel_metric_point.ex:19-198`).
- **3 DB sinks / schemas** with no unifying view or join (repo-wide search found no UNION/view merging `timeseries_metrics` and `otel_metric_points`).
- **3 wire schemas / encodings**: `serviceradar.sysmon.metrics.v1` (whole-sample blob), `serviceradar.metric.v1` (per-scalar JSON), raw OTLP protobuf.
- **Coverage asymmetry**: anomaly `enabled_subjects` defaults to `['otel.metrics.>']` only (`anomaly_detection/config.ex:18`), so **only the native-addon OTLP CPU metric is analyzed out of the box**; sysmon and plugin CPU are subscribed but gated off until `ANOMALY_ANALYSIS_ENABLED_SUBJECTS` is widened.
- **Per-device identity collapse** on the plugin path only: `serviceradar.metric.v1` never sets `device_id`/`target_device_ip`/`if_index` and per-metric labels are not promoted to tags, so many devices under one agent collide into one series (`telemetry.ex:112-137`).
- **Timestamp semantics differ**: OTLP has true per-point `time_unix_nano`; sysmon shares one sample-level timestamp across all cores; plugin shares the `Result` envelope `observed_at` across all metrics.
- **Consumer destroys fidelity uniformly**: `SampleExtractor → ContextOwner → CausalReasoner` reduces every path to `{value, observed_at_unix_nano}` (`sample_extractor.ex`, `context_owner.ex:349-363`). `kind`/`temporality`/`unit`/`is_monotonic` never reach the reasoner even when `otel_metric_points` has them.

---

## The double/triple-decode (the "re-publish" smell)

`status_processor.ex` `forward_then_publish/1` (`:78-97`) does two passes over the same payload: (1) `forward(status)` ships the whole status to core for status/state processing, then (2) re-parses `status.message` and republishes the extracted metrics onto JetStream via three source-specific publishers. Evidence of the same metric JSON decoded three times:

- `sysmon_metrics_publisher.ex:42-51` / `snmp_metrics_publisher.ex:44-53` / `plugin_metrics_publisher.ex:44-53` — each `Jason.decode(status.message)` (decode #2).
- `metrics.ex:46-72` — core re-decodes the republished NATS message (decode #3).

It is **not** a duplicate DB write today: the direct-insert sink is flag-gated off (`plugin_result_ingestor.ex:6-10,:52,:200-206`, `:plugin_result_direct_metrics_enabled` default `false`), and the core gRPC-direct-to-DB metric handlers are already no-op stubs (`results_router.ex:239-245,:611` → `acknowledge_metrics_cutover/1 → :ok`). So half the migration is already done — it just hasn't been cleaned up. The remaining smell is purely the smuggle-and-re-extract architecture, which the first-class metric path eliminates.

---

## OCSF finding — NOT a category error (keep the separation, add guardrails)

This was investigated directly and the "metrics are mis-bucketed into OCSF" claim was **REFUTED** across producers, transport, consumers, and schema:

- Policy is documented in code: `ocsf.ex:16-20` — *"OTel traces/metrics: Keep native format (observability, not security)"* and *"Telemetry metrics: Keep native format (time-series data)"*.
- `ocsf_events` (migration `20260203120000_create_ocsf_events.exs:14-45`) is a pure security-event shape (`class_uid`/`category_uid`/`activity_id`/`severity_id`/observables/actor/device/endpoints) with **zero** metric value/unit/temporality/metric_name columns — it physically cannot hold a series.
- Both WASM SDKs only have `ocsf_event`/`otel_log` payload kinds (`serviceradar-sdk-go/sdk/signal_schema.go:17-18`, `serviceradar-sdk-rust/src/result.rs:356-357`) — there is no metric signal type, so a metric cannot be serialized as an OCSF event.
- The only numbers legitimately inside OCSF are (a) NetFlow byte/packet counters as `traffic{}` in `ocsf_network_activity` class 4001 (event-shaped, OCSF-sanctioned), and (b) anomaly/capacity **Findings** (class 2004) carrying a single anomalous value + thresholds as event context (`verdict_emitter.ex:34-74,:96-118`) — derived *from* metrics, not duplicating the series. Both are correct and stay.

**Recommendations:**
- **Do NOT add a "metric" OCSF class.** OCSF has no metric/time-series primitive; inventing one would be the actual category error.
- **Keep using OCSF for events derived from metrics** (threshold breaches → Findings) — the code already does this correctly.
- **Add mis-bucket guardrails** with the unified contract: the metrics processor rejects any `serviceradar.metric.v1` payload carrying `class_uid`; the OCSF processor rejects payloads carrying `kind`/`temporality`/`points[]`. A misrouted message then errors loudly instead of landing in the wrong hypertable.

---

## Confirmed gaps (verified against code)

1. **No metric `kind`** (gauge/counter/histogram) in any producer SDK or in three of four gateway envelopes — `result.go:52-60`, `result.rs:138-184`. Downstream `metric_type` is a routing label, not an OTel kind.
2. **No `temporality`** (delta/cumulative) in SDKs or the `serviceradar.metric.v1` / `serviceradar.sysmon.metrics.v1` envelopes (`plugin_metrics_publisher.ex:93-111`). SNMP carries only `is_delta`. Result: monotonic counters look like ramps to z-sigma.
3. **No first-class metric emit helper in either WASM SDK** — `telemetry.go` has only `NewOCSFTelemetryRecord`(`:36`) and `NewOTELLogTelemetryRecord`(`:53`); `telemetry.rs` only `ocsf_event`(`:60`)/`otel_log`(`:76`). Metrics can only ride embedded in `submit_result`; there is no metric payload kind.
4. **No per-metric tags / resource identity / point identity** on the `plugin_result` `Metric` shape — labels are envelope-level (`result.go:37`, `result.rs:385`); per-metric dimensions are lost (`plugin_metrics_publisher.ex:113-191`).
5. **Per-device identity collapse on the plugin path** — `serviceradar.metric.v1` never sets `device_id`/`target_device_ip`/`if_index`, so many devices under one agent collapse into one series.
6. **`metrics.timeseries.*` and `otel.metrics.raw` decode into different sinks** (`timeseries_metrics` vs `otel_metric_points`) with no canonical merge.
7. **Anomaly consumer drops `kind`/`temporality`/`unit`** at extraction even when OTLP supplies them (`sample_extractor.ex`, `context_owner.ex:349-363`).
8. **Coverage losses inside the (correct) metric namespace**: OTLP exponential histograms & summaries are counted-then-dropped (`otel_metrics.ex` ~`:258-281`); the SNMP gateway publisher drops every OID except `ifHCInOctets`/`ifHCOutOctets` (`snmp_metrics_publisher.ex`); sysmon `Network[]` interface metrics are collected but dropped at the gateway (only cpu/memory/disk/process families emitted).
9. **No `Nats-Msg-Id` / `duplicate_window` on the `metrics` stream** (`config.ex:206-219`). With `consumer_max_deliver=5` and the planned multi-point fan-out, at-least-once delivery would double-count; idempotency must be enforced at the stream and/or ingestor.
10. **No schema/proto validation of `serviceradar.metric.v1`** — the producer hand-builds the map and the consumer tolerantly defaults missing fields (`metric_type→'gauge'`); malformed envelopes become `gauge`/`unknown` rows instead of being rejected. Non-numeric metrics are silently dropped (`encode_metric` returns `{:ok, nil}` with no counter — invisible data loss).

---

## Producer refactor work-list (every producer smuggling metrics through status)

Swept all 12 native add-ons, both WASM SDKs, and in-tree first-party checkers (22 producers classified).

### `SMUGGLES_METRICS` — first-party in-tree checkers (the real refactor targets)
| producer | metrics | source string | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **sysmon** | cpu/disk/memory/network-iface/process | `sysmon-metrics` | `go/pkg/sysmon/metrics.go:25-180`, `push_loop_status.go:200-233` |
| **snmp** | OID counters/gauges w/ `if_index`,`interface_uid` | `snmp-metrics` | `push_loop_snmp.go:30-42,48-57,63` |
| **icmp** | `response_time_ns`, `packet_loss` | `results` | `push_loop_icmp_results.go:29-68`, `icmp_checker.go:69-77` |
| **mtr** | per-hop RTT/loss/jitter | `results` | `mtr_checker.go:61-70,86-127`, `proto/monitoring.proto:1012-1046` |
| **network sweep** | scanner perf counters (`SweepScannerStats`) | `results` | `proto/monitoring.proto:149-200`, `push_loop_sweep_results.go:28-118` |
| **mapper/discovery** | per-interface metric **descriptors** (`InterfaceMetric`) — catalog, not samples | discovery status | `proto/discovery/discovery.proto:188-214`, `push_loop_mapper_netprobe.go:36-93` |
| **rperf** (Rust checker) | throughput/loss/jitter (`TestSummary`) | `plugin-result` (generic path) | `proto/rperf/rperf.proto:60-72`, `rust/rperf-client/src/server.rs:259-300` |

> Note: mapper/discovery carries metric **definitions** (the catalog the snmp checker samples), not time-series — decide whether the unified contract carries metric-descriptors on a separate channel.

### SDK smuggling helpers (add first-class emit here, then deprecate)
- Go: `Result.Metrics` slot (`serviceradar-sdk-go/sdk/result.go:36`), `Metric` struct (`:52-60`), `AddMetric`/`WithMetric` builders (`:257-273`).
- Rust: `Metric` struct (`serviceradar-sdk-rust/src/result.rs:138-151`), `add_metric_spec`/`with_metric_spec` (`:578-585`), `add_metric`/`with_metric` (`:587-612`).
- 6 SDK examples (`http-check`, `udp-check`, `tcp-check`, `widgets-check` ×Go; `http-check`, `widgets-check` ×Rust) and 2 golden fixtures (`testdata/service_monitoring_result.json` ×2) demonstrate the pattern and must update in lockstep.

### `OTLP_NATIVE` (already first-class)
- **otel-addon** + `rust/otel` library relay customer OTLP metrics via the acked `RelayOtlp` stream (`otlp-relay:v1`): `rust/otel-addon/src/addon.rs:27,556`, `rust/otel/src/lib.rs:529,754`, `addon.proto:159-165` (`OTLP_METRICS=5`, `OTLP_DERIVED_METRIC=6`). Decision needed: normalize OTLP_METRICS frames into `serviceradar.metric.v1` downstream, or keep `otel.metrics.raw` as a high-fidelity express lane.

### `NO_METRICS` (no refactor) — explicitly verified to avoid false positives
bumblebee-scan, endpoint-inventory, scalibr-endpoint-inventory, advisory-producer, sample-addon, powerdns, rdp-adapter, workload-identity, bmp-collector, log-collector, trapd, flowgger, rust-sample-addon, rperf-server. **Correction to parallel sub-agents:** netprobe, flow-collector, and otel-addon's `StreamTelemetry` expose only **operational Prometheus/OCSF-usage self-metrics**, NOT smuggled observability time-series — they are NOT refactor targets.

---

## Tech-debt to delete / collapse (the unification makes the special-cases deletable)

### DELETE (pure migration-era scaffolding)
- `@legacy_sysmon_schema "serviceradar.sysmon.shadow.v1"` acceptance — `metrics.ex:19,:151`.
- `AGENT_GATEWAY_SYSMON/SNMP_METRICS_SHADOW_ENABLED` env defaults (`runtime.exs:314,318`, default `"true"`) + helm `*MetricsShadowEnabled` aliases (`agent-gateway.yaml:30,36`).
- Flag-gated legacy direct insert `maybe_insert_metrics` + `:plugin_result_direct_metrics_enabled` (`plugin_result_ingestor.ex:52,:200-206`; `core/config.exs:131-133`). Keep `build_status_row`/`insert_status` — only the metric insert is debt.
- Vestigial no-op router handlers `handle_sysmon_metrics`/`handle_snmp_metrics`/`acknowledge_metrics_cutover` (`results_router.ex:239-245,:611`) and their dispatch entries (`status_handler.ex:109-111`).

### COLLAPSE (replace source-specific handling with the unified path)
- `SysmonMetricsPublisher` (`sysmon_metrics_publisher.ex` whole module) and `SnmpMetricsPublisher` (`snmp_metrics_publisher.ex` whole module) → fold into a generalization of `PluginMetricsPublisher` (which already emits `serviceradar.metric.v1`). These are the publish boundary (agents are NATS-denied), so they must be **replaced, not merely deleted**.
- Sysmon family-envelope carve-out in `metrics.ex:18,50,59-181` (`parse_sysmon`/`filter_sysmon_sample`/`partition_messages`/`ingest_sysmon_messages`/`metric_kind`) → the generic Telemetry/timeseries path.
- `SysmonMetricsIngestor` (`sysmon_metrics_ingestor.ex`) 5-hypertable fan-out → unified ingest.
- Gateway double-pass `forward_then_publish` + `publish_sysmon/snmp/plugin_metrics` + `*_source?` guards (`status_processor.ex:78-97,313-427`); per-source `max_message_bytes`/`strict_message_size_source?` (`agent_gateway_server.ex:665-680`) — **preserve the large sysmon size budget** on the unified path.
- Anomaly per-source carve-outs: `sample_extractor.ex:67-71,114-189`, `series_config.ex:201-214`, `config.ex:108-109` (`ANALYSIS_METRICS_SYSMON`/`SNMP`).
- Per-source subject prefixes / NATS ACLs (`config.exs:30,35`, `runtime.exs:346,351`, `agent-gateway.yaml:127,131`, `nats.yaml:211`, `values-demo.yaml:488`, `values.yaml:946,948`) — re-bind stream subjects + durable consumer filters **atomically** during cutover.

### MIGRATE (producer code switches to first-class emit)
- Go agent sysmon producer (`push_loop_status.go:118-233`, `sysmon_service.go:604-612`, `go/pkg/sysmon/{metrics,collector}.go`) — flatten cpus/clusters/disks/processes into per-series scalar points.
- Go agent SNMP producer (`push_loop_snmp.go:66,77,101,140`) — keep `if_index`/`target_device_ip` identity.
- (+ icmp/mtr/sweep/rperf per the producer work-list above.)

### KEEP — do NOT delete (sysmon-named but config/UI, not metric debt)
- `sysmon_profiles` table + migrations (`20260519162000_*`, `20260123093000_*`), `sysmon_compiler.ex`, settings UI (`sysmon_profiles_live/index.ex`) — **configuration**.
- Device-detail sysmon charts UI (`device_tab_runtime.ex`) and SRQL catalog — **repoint** to the unified table, do not delete.
- `go/pkg/sysmon/collector.go` + `sysmon_service.go` — the collector itself (migrate the emit shape, not the collector).
- The five sysmon **metric** hypertables (`cpu_metrics`/`cpu_cluster_metrics`/`memory_metrics`/`disk_metrics`/`process_metrics`) + `_hourly` caggs — unification candidates, but they back live UI charts and anomaly baselines: **data-migrate before any DROP**.

### Tests that lock in the per-source schemas/subjects (will need rewriting)
`metrics_test.exs` (legacy shadow + sysmon/snmp fixtures), `sysmon_metrics_publisher_test.exs`, `snmp_metrics_publisher_test.exs`, `status_processor_test.exs:428,456`, `sysmon_metrics_ingestor_test.exs`, `snmp_metrics_ingestor_integration_test.exs`, `results_router_test.exs:431,445`, `sample_extractor_test.exs`, `pipeline_test.exs`, `config_test.exs:40-88`, `series_config_test.exs`/`synthetic_dataset_test.exs`/`verdict_emitter_test.exs`/`baseline_seeder_test.exs`/`stateful_alert_engine_test.exs`, `jetstream_consumer_test.exs`, `pipeline_ack_test.exs`/`pipeline_batch_span_test.exs`.

---

## Proposed unified contract: `serviceradar.metric.v1` (evolve additively from the PR #3787 bridge)

Reuse the existing schema id; bump `schema_version` 1→2 and add the OTLP-grade fields below. Version-1 flat envelopes remain valid (treated as a single gauge point: `value→points[0].value`, `metric_type→kind`, `tags→points[0].attributes`, `observed_at→points[0].time_unix_nano`). Consumers MUST reject envelopes whose `schema` is absent/unknown rather than coercing to `gauge`.

| field | type | purpose | OTLP equiv |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | const `"serviceradar.metric.v1"` | route + version-gate | Schema URL analog |
| `schema_version` | uint32 (default 1) | additive evolution | — |
| `resource` | `{service_name(req), service_instance_id, scope_name, scope_version, attributes:map}` | resource identity carried once per batch/point — the field the SDK `Metric` and PR3787 envelope both lack. sysmon: `service_name='sysmon'`, attrs carry `host_id`/`core_id`/`mount_point`/`pid`; snmp: `target_device_ip`/`if_index`/`interface_uid` | Resource + InstrumentationScope |
| `name` | string (req) | metric stream name (dotted semconv), no longer the sole identity | Metric.name |
| `kind` | enum `{gauge, sum, histogram, exp_histogram, summary}` | the field every producer is missing; lets the engine rate-compute counters | Metric.data oneof |
| `temporality` | enum `{unspecified, delta, cumulative}` (req for sum/histogram) | counter-rate computability; snmp `is_delta→delta` | aggregation_temporality |
| `is_monotonic` | bool (kind=sum) | counter vs UpDownCounter | Sum.is_monotonic |
| `unit` | string (UCUM: `%`,`By`,`1`,`ms`,`Hz`) | stops n_sigma mixing percent/bytes/counts | Metric.unit |
| `points` | array<DataPoint> (req, ≥1) | one OR MANY points per emit so cores/mounts/interfaces/guests dimension **without** splitting envelopes (fixes per-device collapse) | data_points (repeated) |
| `points[].time_unix_nano` | uint64 (req) | per-point measurement time | DataPoint.time_unix_nano |
| `points[].start_time_unix_nano` | uint64 (req for cumulative rate) | counter reset/window anchor | DataPoint.start_time_unix_nano |
| `points[].attributes` | map<string,scalar> | per-point dims (`core_id`,`mount_point`,`if_index`,`guest_id`); volatile keys excluded from identity | DataPoint.attributes |
| `points[].value` | double\|int (gauge/sum) | int vs double preserved | NumberDataPoint.as_double/as_int |
| `points[].histogram` | `{count,sum,bucket_counts[],explicit_bounds[],min,max}` (histogram) | first-class histogram (none today); enables p50/p95 series currently dropped | HistogramDataPoint |
| `points[].exemplars` | `[{time_unix_nano,value,trace_id,span_id,filtered_attributes}]` (opt) | metric→trace pivots the causal engine wants | DataPoint.exemplars |
| `thresholds` | `{warn,crit,min,max}` (opt) | preserves Nagios perfdata semantics **without** conflating with metric data; alerting/display only | — (deliberately outside OTLP) |
| `ingress_id` | UUIDv8 (gateway-stamped) | per-message ordering/idempotency; also set as `Nats-Msg-Id` | — |
| `ingress_timestamp_unix_nano` | uint64 (gateway-stamped) | ingest/transport time, distinct from measurement time | — |
| `ingest_identity` | `{ingest_agent_id, ingest_partition, ingest_identity:'agent:<id>'}` (gateway-attested) | mTLS-bound attested identity, separate from producer-claimed `resource.attributes` (untrusted) | attested overlay |

### Per-SDK emit APIs (new third signal stream: `signal_type:'metric'` / `payload_kind:'otel_metric'`)
- **go-wasm**: `sdk.NewGauge/NewCounter/NewHistogram(name, value, ...MetricOption)` with `WithUnit/WithAttributes/WithTimestamp/WithResource/WithThresholds/WithExemplar`; collected into `sdk.NewMetricBatch(resource)`; add `NewMetricTelemetryRecord(batch)` so metrics ride `env.emit_telemetry`. Keep `Result.AddMetric` as a shim lowering to a gauge point.
- **rust-wasm**: `MetricPoint::gauge/counter/histogram(...)` + `MetricBatch::new(ResourceRef::service(...))` + `TelemetryRecord::otel_metric(batch)`. Keep `Metric`/`add_metric_spec` as a perfdata shim.
- **native add-on** (`rust/addon-sdk`): `MetricBatchBuilder::new(resource).gauge/counter/histogram(...)` + `Addon::emit_metrics(batch)` wrapping a new `TelemetryPayloadKind::SR_METRIC_V1` (alongside `OTLP_METRICS=5`, `OTLP_DERIVED_METRIC=6`). OTLP-native authors keep `relay_otlp()` unchanged.
- **agent sysmon/snmp/icmp/mtr/sweep**: internal `go/pkg/metricpoint` builder mirroring the SDK so the gateway publishers emit `serviceradar.metric.v1` multi-point envelopes (one `Metric{kind,unit,points[]}` per family), replacing the raw-sample blob and the 2-OID hardcode; emit the currently-dropped sysmon `Network[]` and SNMP non-octet OIDs.
- **shared**: `ResourceRef.service(name).instance(id).scope(name,ver).attr(k,v)` so all producers construct the resource tuple once.

### Subject topology
One canonical tree `metrics.v1.<kind>.<domain>.<name-token>` on the existing high-rate `metrics` stream (widen the binding to also own `metrics.v1.>`). Leading token = the real `kind` field (no longer regex-guessed). Legacy subjects (`metrics.sysmon.*`, `metrics.snmp.interface.*`, `metrics.timeseries.<type>.<name>`) stay bound during migration. The addon raw-OTLP path is NOT moved by alias — a decode-and-republish shim lowers `ExportMetricsServiceRequest` into `metrics.v1.*` for a single consumer shape (or keep `otel.metrics.raw` as the express lane — see open questions). **Critical hardening before fan-out:** gateway sets `Nats-Msg-Id`=`ingress_id` on every publish AND the `metrics` stream gains a `duplicate_window`. Add `metrics.v1.>` to `ANOMALY_ANALYSIS_ENABLED_SUBJECTS`.

---

## Relationship to PR #3787

PR #3787 is a correct, deliberately-thin **bridge** that should be **evolved, not replaced**. It ships `serviceradar.metric.v1` as a flat `{schema, metric_name, metric_type, value, unit, tags, metadata}` envelope on `metrics.timeseries.<type>.<name>` → Telemetry → `timeseries_metrics`, wires the anomaly consumer (`ANALYSIS_METRICS_TIMESERIES`), and cleanly gates off the legacy direct-DB insert. It is the de-facto reference implementation of the unified contract. It explicitly does **not** solve the resource-metric SDK contract: no kind/temporality, no resource identity (`device_id`/`if_index`/`target_device_ip` always nil → per-device collapse), no per-metric labels, and `metric_type` is regex-guessed when the producer omits it (note: producer-declared type **is** honored first — `plugin_metrics_publisher.ex:126-131`). Two hardening items it left open and this work must close: the `metrics` stream still has no `Nats-Msg-Id`/`duplicate_window`, and two unrelated changes rode along (`refresh_trace_summaries_worker` chunk-size 3600→300, web-ng raw-traces fallback) that should be separated for clean revertability.

---

## Recommendations (ordered, for the implementing agent)

1. **Land additively, not as a v2 break.** Reuse `serviceradar.metric.v1`, bump `schema_version 1→2`, add `resource`/`kind`/`temporality`/`is_monotonic`/`points[]`/`exemplars` as optional. Version-1 flat envelopes map to a single gauge point; the Telemetry processor keeps consuming both shapes.
2. **Add the first-class metric emit path to both WASM SDKs first** (`signal_type:'metric'` + `payload_kind:'otel_metric'` + `NewMetricTelemetryRecord` / `TelemetryRecord::otel_metric` via the existing `emit_telemetry` import). Keep `AddMetric`/`add_metric_spec` as perfdata shims so existing plugins keep working.
3. **Make producers declare `kind` explicitly** and gate the gateway regex inference to legacy version-1 envelopes only — eliminates the silent series-reshuffle and subject-token instability.
4. **Add `Nats-Msg-Id`=`ingress_id` + a `metrics`-stream `duplicate_window` BEFORE enabling multi-point fan-out**, and enforce idempotency in the TimescaleDB ingestors. At-least-once with `consumer_max_deliver=5` will double-count otherwise.
5. **Pick ONE point-identity recipe** over `(resource tuple + name + point.attributes)` and converge both hypertable PKs (`otel_metric_points` recipe-v2 vs `TimeseriesSeriesKey`). This is a PK migration on both tables — sequence it deliberately.
6. **Upgrade the anomaly consumer to be kind/temporality-aware** (`sample_extractor.ex`/`context_owner.ex`): carry `kind`/`temporality`/`unit` through; rate-compute monotonic counters; ingest histogram count/sum/buckets for p50/p95 instead of rejecting `value=nil`. The contract is only worth its richness if a consumer uses it.
7. **Migrate the gateway sysmon/snmp/icmp/mtr/sweep producers LAST**, after the shared `go/pkg/metricpoint` builder lands: re-emit the legacy schemas as `serviceradar.metric.v1` multi-point envelopes, collapsing the three legacy schemas into one and fixing the gateway drops at the same time.
8. **Keep the addon raw-OTLP relay OTLP-native end to end** (zero re-instrumentation for OTLP authors). Unify via a decode-and-republish shim. Decide two-lane (keep `otel.metrics.raw` as the high-fidelity express lane) vs one-lane.
9. **Do NOT touch OCSF.** Keep the documented separation; add the mis-bucket guardrails; continue emitting anomaly Findings (class 2004) and NetFlow Traffic (class 4001).
10. **Add schema validation** at gateway ingress and core consumer: reject absent/unknown `schema` instead of coercing to `gauge`; reject malformed `serviceradar.metric.v1` rather than silently dropping non-numeric metrics.

---

## Open questions

1. **Wire encoding**: keep `serviceradar.metric.v1` as JSON (matches today, debuggable, loses int/double distinction, heavier) or move the high-rate/addon-volume path to protobuf closer to OTLP `NumberDataPoint`? Hybrid (JSON for plugins, protobuf for collectors) is plausible.
2. **Two-lane vs one-lane** for the addon raw-OTLP path: retire `otel.metrics.raw` in favor of the decode-and-republish shim, or keep it as the permanent high-fidelity express lane (exemplars/exp-histograms)?
3. **Resource-identity trust**: producer-claimed `resource.attributes` vs gateway-attested `ingest_identity` can disagree (a plugin reporting many guest devices under one mTLS agent). Which wins for series identity, and do we need a per-point attested device binding (the DIRE behavioral-identity concern) rather than trusting producer labels?
4. **Single point-identity recipe**: `otel_metric_points` recipe-v2 vs `TimeseriesSeriesKey` differ; which recipe, and what migration sequence for both PKs?
5. **Consumer scope**: does the anomaly/causal engine get upgraded to be kind/temporality-aware (rate counters, ingest histogram p50/p95) as part of this, or does the contract carry the fields while the consumer keeps collapsing to a scalar?
6. **Histogram storage**: `otel_metric_points` stores bucket_counts/explicit_bounds but drops exp-histograms/summaries; `timeseries_metrics` has no histogram columns. Extend `timeseries_metrics` or force all histograms to `otel_metric_points`?
7. **Unit normalization ownership**: producers emit UCUM and the gateway validates, or the gateway normalizes free-form units?
8. **Sysmon per-family hypertables**: retain `cpu_metrics`/`memory_metrics`/`disk_metrics`/`process_metrics` for query-shape reasons after sysmon emits `serviceradar.metric.v1`, or collapse into the unified sink? (Migrating onto the contract does not by itself mandate dropping the per-family tables.)
9. **Metric descriptors**: mapper/discovery emits per-interface metric *definitions* (`InterfaceMetric`), not samples. Does the contract carry metric-descriptors on a separate channel, or is the catalog out of scope?

---

## Verification note

Findings were produced by parallel subsystem readers and an adversarial verification pass; load-bearing claims were re-checked against code. Three initial claims were **REFUTED** and corrected above: (a) metrics are NOT mis-bucketed into OCSF; (b) native add-ons DO have a friendly metric API (same `plugin_result` path as wasm) rather than only raw OTLP; (c) `PluginMetricsPublisher` honors a producer-declared `metric_type` first, regex is only the fallback. The producer sweep also corrected three sub-agent over-classifications (netprobe / flow-collector / otel-addon `StreamTelemetry` are operational self-metrics, not smuggled time-series).

items.title: [SPEC-FR-M11.4] Thread Management
items.body:
# SPEC-FR-M11.4: Thread Management

| Field         | Value                                                         |
|---------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| ID            | SPEC-FR-M11.4                                                 |
| Status        | DRAFT                                                         |
| Milestone     | M11                                                           |
| Component     | conversation-hub                                              |
| Depends On    | SPEC-FR-M3.6, SPEC-FR-M6.0                                    |
| Supersedes    | none                                                          |

## Context

Conversations within communities are organized into threads for multi-turn engagement tracking. To keep the Keeper (control plane) separated from runtime data-plane traffic, thread management and message history persistence are isolated into a new dedicated service: `conversation-hub`.

The `conversation-hub` is responsible for persisting thread/message states in a dedicated PostgreSQL schema/database, exposing CRUD APIs, and subscribing to the NATS event bus to keep historical states in sync with real-time domain events.

---

## Specification

### 1. Domain Entities

The `conversation-hub` service MUST define the following domain entities in its domain layer:

#### 1.1 `Thread` Entity
* **Fields**:
  * `ID`: UUID (Primary Key)
  * `TenantID`: String (tenant isolation)
  * `CommunityID`: UUID (reference to the community)
  * `Status`: Enum/String (`active`, `paused`, `completed`)
  * `Participants`: List/Array of Agent IDs (agents actively assigned or involved)
  * `CreatedAt`: Timestamp (UTC)
  * `UpdatedAt`: Timestamp (UTC)
* **Constraints**:
  * Strict validation on `Status`.
  * Composite index on `(tenant_id, community_id)`.

#### 1.2 `Message` Entity
* **Fields**:
  * `ID`: UUID (Primary Key)
  * `TenantID`: String
  * `ThreadID`: UUID (Foreign Key to `Thread`)
  * `SenderID`: String (e.g., `"user"` or `agent_id`)
  * `Role`: Enum/String (`user`, `assistant`)
  * `Content`: Text (sanitized message content)
  * `OccurredAt`: Timestamp (UTC)
* **Constraints**:
  * Foreign key constraint linking `ThreadID` to `Thread` table.
  * Index on `(tenant_id, thread_id)`.
  * **Scope**: Captured messages are strictly limited to complete conversational messages (user input and final agent replies). Intermediate LLM reasoning traces or tool execution details MUST NOT be persisted in this entity.

---

### 2. REST API Endpoints

The `conversation-hub` service MUST expose the following REST endpoints using the Gin framework (per `SPEC-NFR-HTTP`). These endpoints are designed to be internal-facing and proxied by the BFF (`SPEC-FR-M7.1`), which handles client-facing security, model translations, and OIDC token verification.

#### 2.1 GET `/api/v1/communities/{community_id}/threads`
* **Purpose**: List all threads in a community.
* **Query Params**:
  * `status`: Optional filter (e.g. `active`, `completed`).
  * `limit`, `offset`: Standard pagination parameters.
* **Response**: `200 OK` with JSON array of `Thread` models (empty array if none found).

#### 2.2 POST `/api/v1/communities/{community_id}/threads`
* **Purpose**: Create a new conversation thread.
* **Payload**:
  ```json
  {
    "thread_id": "optional-uuid",
    "participants": ["agent-uuid-1"],
    "initial_message": {
      "sender_id": "user",
      "content": "Hello, world!"
    }
  }
  ```
* **Behavior**:
  * Generates a `Thread` entity.
  * If `initial_message` is provided, sanitizes the message content using the shared sanitization utility (Cc/Cs Unicode characters stripping, 4096-character limit truncation) and creates a `Message` entity.
  * Publishes a `start-thread` domain event (and optionally `add-user-message` event) to NATS subject `ts.community.{community_id}.agent.{target_agent}`.
* **Response**: `201 Created` with the created `Thread` entity and a `Location` header pointing to `/api/v1/communities/{community_id}/threads/{thread_id}`.

#### 2.3 GET `/api/v1/communities/{community_id}/threads/{id}`
* **Purpose**: Get a specific thread along with its message history.
* **Response**: `200 OK` with the `Thread` entity nested with its historical list of `Message` entities. Returns `404 Not Found` if missing or tenant mismatch.

#### 2.5 PUT `/api/v1/communities/{community_id}/threads/{id}`
* **Purpose**: Update thread status (e.g. archiving or pausing).
* **Payload**:
  ```json
  {
    "status": "completed"
  }
  ```
* **Behavior**: Updates the thread status and publishes an `end-thread` event to NATS if the status changes to `completed`.
* **Response**: `200 OK` with the updated `Thread` object.

#### 2.6 DELETE `/api/v1/communities/{community_id}/threads/{id}`
* **Purpose**: Hard/soft delete a thread and its messages.
* **Response**: `204 No Content`.

---

### 3. NATS Integration (Data Ingestion Loop)

The `conversation-hub` MUST act as both an event producer and consumer to remain in sync with the asynchronous agent cluster.

#### 3.1 Wildcard Subscription (Consumer)
* **Subject**: Subscribes to the NATS hierarchical wildcard subject `ts.community.>` (capturing both inbound requests and agent replies).
* **Event Ingestion Handler**:
  * **`start-thread` event**: Creates the thread record in PostgreSQL if it doesn't already exist.
  * **`add-user-message` event**: Appends a `user` role message to the thread record. The content is sanitized before insertion.
  * **`agent-response` event**: Appends an `assistant` role message with the agent response to the thread record.
  * **`end-thread` event**: Marks the thread status as `completed` in PostgreSQL.

#### 3.2 Event Publisher
* When threads or messages are created directly via `conversation-hub` REST endpoints, the service MUST construct and publish standard `DomainEvent` envelopes to NATS (complying with `SPEC-FR-M6.0`).

---

### 4. Non-Functional & Architecture Requirements

* **Code Architecture**: Follow Ports & Adapters (`RULE[code-architecture.md]`).
  ```text
  internal/conversation-hub/
  ├── domain/
  │   └── model/             # Thread, Message aggregates
  ├── application/
  │   ├── ports/
  │   │   ├── inbound/       # ThreadUseCase, EventIngressPort
  │   │   └── outbound/      # ThreadRepository, EventPublisher
  │   └── service/           # Thread service logic
  └── adapters/
      ├── inbound/           # Gin handlers, NATS subscribers
      └── outbound/          # pgx database client, NATS publisher client
  ```
* **Shared Message Sanitizer**: A shared helper utility (`pkg/events/sanitizer.go`) is utilized by both `keeper` (during event ingress) and `conversation-hub` (during REST/NATS message processing) to execute message sanitization uniformly.
* **Multitenancy**: Strict validation and injection of `tenant_id` from claims forwarded by the BFF proxy (governed by `RULE[cloud-first.md]`).
* **Database Isolation**: The `conversation-hub` connects to the same PostgreSQL instance as `keeper` but MUST use a separate logical database or dedicated database schema to ensure isolation, utilizing `goose` for migrations.
* **Observability**: Standard metrics (connections, thread count, latency) exposed via `GET /metrics` and spans instrumented via OpenTelemetry.
* **Liveness & Readiness Probes**: `/healthz` and `/readyz` verifying database and NATS connections in parallel.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Database Schema Separation**: Thread and message tables are managed via independent migrations in `deploy/postgres/migrations/conversation-hub/` and run on startup.
2. **Tenant Separation**: All Thread and Message tables feature a non-nullable `tenant_id` column with corresponding database indexes. All CRUD SQL queries filter strictly by this parameter.
3. **NATS Wildcard Sync**: Emitting a conversational event (`start-thread`, `add-user-message`, or `agent-response`) to NATS results in a corresponding DB insert in the `conversation-hub` PostgreSQL schema.
4. **CRUD REST Endpoints**: The Gin routes for thread list, get, create, status update, and delete are exposed, tested in `gin.TestMode`, and return clean JSON structures.
5. **Location Header**: Creating a thread via `POST` returns `201 Created` with a `Location` header pointing to `/api/v1/communities/{community_id}/threads/{id}`.
6. **OpenAPI Spec**: The service serves a valid OpenAPI 3.x document at `GET /openapi.json`.
7. **Containerization**: The runtime stage uses `gcr.io/distroless/base-nossl-debian13`.

---

## Test Plan

### Automated Tests

1. **Unit Tests**:
   * Model validations (Thread status, Message sender properties).
   * Schema router matching logic.
   * Shared sanitization utility verification.
2. **Integration Tests**:
   * Database repository tests (CRUD, tenant isolation checks, index coverage verification).
   * Event publication and wildcard consumer subscription tests using an in-memory NATS server.
3. **HTTP API tests**:
   * Mocking the `ThreadUseCase` in `gin.TestMode` to verify REST API responses and headers.

### Manual Verification
1. Spin up the `conversation-hub` alongside `keeper`, `agent`, and PostgreSQL.
2. Direct a `POST` request to start a thread; verify record in DB.
3. Stream a user message and ensure NATS wildcard handler appends it.
4. Verify `GET /api/v1/communities/{id}/threads` lists the active thread.


---

items.body:
### Goal

Land only the missing shared Phase 2 contracts in a separate owner-approved PR before dependent implementations (D-47), using the independent new database boundary recorded by #66.

### Decisions

D-4, D-23, D-28, D-29, D-34, D-36, D-47.

### Area

contracts (shared/)

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add validated `backfillFrom` with the existing 365-day/API-start bounds.
- [ ] Reuse the existing Terraform `organization.directory_provider` input; define/align the runtime Graph-default/CSV-fallback contract without introducing a competing setting.
- [ ] Define the CSV directory input shape, required/optional fields, header/encoding validation, and typed errors.
- [ ] Use Zod for runtime schemas: canonical shared contracts in `shared/`; provider-specific wire schemas beside Functions adapters unless another package needs them. Use existing verified AI Credits fields unchanged.
- [ ] State single-writer ownership for affected shared row shapes: one logical `ingestion` component writes `portal.dim_user`/login history, with directory attributes and link/revocation lifecycle owned by directory sync through it. Preserve confirmed immutable principal Entra columns and tenant-FK arrangement.
- [ ] Inventory existing `portal.dim_user`, manager-ID, link/revocation and `DirectorySyncState` contracts before defining only missing directory/CSV deltas. Separate new runtime row requirements from historical `DIRECTORY_CONTRACT_V1`/v2 budget descriptors; do not require v1-compatible shadow tables or old budget-consumer adoption. Any executable descriptor/comment clarification belongs in this contract PR, not a dependent feature PR.
- [ ] Leave `github_license_type` nullable/unsourced wherever retained under D-38; do not reintroduce `consumed-licenses`. Surface any genuinely missing directory field/status contract before dependent implementation instead of inventing old-system compatibility.

### Tests and evidence

Contract tests for settings bounds, CSV valid/invalid cases, and external schemas against synthetic/anonymized fixtures; existing shared tests remain green. Evidence maps required directory fields to existing or explicitly changed contracts and confirms no dependency on the old database.

### Depends on

#66

### Out of scope

Functions implementation, migrations, API consumer DTO changes for #49/#50, AI Credits schema redesign, old database/repository changes, Budget Lookup read-source selection, final data migration.

items.title: Implement approved multi-vendor account hierarchy, scoped RBAC and distinct portals
items.body:
## Decision
Implement the approved Vendor / Reseller / Customer account and portal model as an extension of the existing tenant hierarchy and RBAC implementation.

### Approved product rules
- Start with one default Vendor, while supporting multiple independent Vendors from the first implementation.
- Public Reseller and Customer registration attaches to the default Vendor.
- Public Vendor registration is prohibited. New Vendors and their initial Vendor Owners are created only through an authorized provisioning flow.
- Vendor users with explicit grants can create/manage Resellers and Customers in their Vendor scope.
- Resellers with explicit grants can create/manage only their own direct Customers and customer users.
- Customers may be direct children of a Vendor or children of one Reseller; each Customer has one unambiguous owner path.
- Reseller A has no read or write access to Reseller B or B's Customers.
- Portal identity is distinct from primary account identity. Vendor may access Reseller/Customer portals only with explicit grants; Reseller may access Customer portal only with explicit grants; Reseller can never access Vendor portal; Customer can access only Customer portal.
- Vendor, Reseller and Customer portals have distinct workflows, navigation and visual identity.
- Membership activation is gated by approved payment or an explicitly granted Demo entitlement.

### Scope
1. Audit current tenant hierarchy, user/membership models, signup/login, edition dependencies, RBAC, portal routing and existing commercial license/entitlement work.
2. Produce a compatibility and migration plan; preserve existing users and tenant data.
3. Implement/complete multi-vendor tenant ownership and default-vendor provisioning.
4. Enforce scoped, non-escalating permission delegation and portal access in backend/API.
5. Enforce strict data isolation across APIs, search, reports, files, exports, background jobs and dashboards.
6. Implement public signup to default Vendor with pending/payment/demo lifecycle.
7. Deliver separate Vendor, Reseller and Customer portal experiences and audited portal context switching.
8. Add positive and negative security acceptance tests.

### Security acceptance
- Reseller A cannot read, enumerate, update, export or otherwise infer Reseller B or B's Customer data.
- Customer cannot access Vendor or Reseller portals.
- Reseller cannot access Vendor portal, regardless of assigned grants.
- Vendor A cannot access Vendor B data.
- No actor can grant permissions or portal access beyond their own delegation ceiling.
- Direct API/URL/ID manipulation cannot bypass backend authorization.
- Portal switching never changes primary identity or data ownership.
- Sensitive administration and context-switch events are auditable.

### Execution rules
- First deliver a source-backed Gap Analysis; do not duplicate existing Phase 14 tenant/RBAC functionality.
- Work only in an isolated worktree/branch. Preserve dirty primary checkout and existing local staging artifacts.
- No production data, production deployment, account mutation or payment activation without separate explicit approval.
- Keep issue #19 as the separate external-production evidence gate; this issue tracks engineering/product implementation and local/CI acceptance.
- Update the local and GitHub handoff/state after every meaningful implementation checkpoint, recording exact SHAs and evidence.

### Initial status
Architecture decision approved 2026-11-02. Implementation has not started. Existing docs/current/PHASE_14_RUNTIME_ISOLATION_RBAC_ENGINEERING.md documents a tenant hierarchy and CI verification harness, but does not by itself prove the newly approved multi-vendor provisioning, account creation/delegation, public registration lifecycle, portal context switching or three distinct UIs are complete.
## Source-backed audit checkpoint — 2026-11-02

Initial source audit is documented in [MULTI_VENDOR_PORTAL_GAP_ANALYSIS_2026-11-02.md](https://github.com/ijoolaie/AI-Employee/blob/docs/multi-vendor-portal-architecture-20261102/docs/current/MULTI_VENDOR_PORTAL_GAP_ANALYSIS_2026-11-02.md).

Confirmed gaps against the approved rules:
- Public registration creates a standalone root Customer tenant, immediately activates the user and assigns a broad Admin role; it does not select Reseller/Customer or attach to a default Vendor.
- No authoritative default-Vendor resolver/provisioning path was found in the inspected core code.
- Direct Vendor → Customer provisioning is absent.
- Child creation is edition Admin-role gated, not controlled by per-user delegated action grants.
- Frontend portal access is same-kind-only and backend edition dependencies deny cross-edition APIs; no server-validated portal context/grant flow was found.
- Vendor dashboard is a placeholder; Reseller and Customer UI foundations are more developed.
- Existing Phase 14 isolation tests are reusable, but broader data surfaces and portal-context behavior need additional audit/coverage.

Reusable foundation includes Tenant hierarchy, roles/permissions, edition dependencies, direct-child provisioning, entitlement delegation, billing, separate portal route groups and Phase 14 CI. Do not duplicate these components.

Next: deeper audit of permission-management APIs, resource-query scoping, background jobs and existing-tenant migration. No application code, account, database or production resource was changed during this audit.
RBAC refinement from the deeper source read:
- `backend/app/api/v1/tenant_admin.py` has tenant-scoped user list/status/role-assignment APIs and `_assert_roles_within_authority` prevents assigning roles with permissions beyond the actor's effective set.
- However, the inspected tenant-admin API has no create/invite-user endpoint, and edition child-creation routes are guarded by Admin/Owner role rather than the specific per-user `reseller.customer.create` action permission.
- Therefore the RBAC foundation is partial and reusable; the required per-user operation grants must be wired into child-management endpoints.
Isolation test coverage refinement:
- `backend/scripts/e2e_tenant_rbac_verify.py` registers two standalone root tenants and checks cross-tenant employee/file operations plus knowledge-search isolation; it does not construct sibling Resellers under one Vendor.
- `backend/tests/test_edition_live_api_access.py` checks the Vendor/Reseller/Customer edition API matrix for one hierarchy.
- `backend/tests/test_commercial_license_postgres_api.py` seeds two Vendor roots, each with its own Reseller and Customer, for commercial-license boundary tests; that is not a complete sibling-Reseller cross-read matrix.
- Add explicit Vendor A → Reseller A/B sibling tests and Vendor A/B → Reseller/Customer cross-tenant negative tests across user enumeration, APIs, search, reports, exports, files, notifications and background jobs.
## Documentation baseline merged
- Architecture specification, source-backed gap analysis, documentation index and master handoff were merged to `main` via PR #1351.
- Merge commit: `2819cdc651c0a769b653bf3c92cd74e21a62925a`.
- Latest exact-head Documentation Truth Consistency and CodeQL workflows both completed successfully before merge.
- The isolated Local Staging worktree fetched the documentation branch and completed a successful `git merge --ff-only` to the same branch head before the local MCP session became unavailable. The merge output confirmed fast-forward from `f38faafd` to `57b1505a`. Post-fast-forward `git status` could not be re-read because the local MCP server stopped initializing; do not claim post-sync cleanliness. The primary checkout remains untouched.

## Next audit slice
- Inspect resource ownership enforcement across API/service/repository surfaces: support, files, search/knowledge, analytics/reports/exports, audit, billing, notifications, caches and Celery tasks.
- Build an actor/resource matrix for Vendor A/B, Reseller A/B, direct Vendor Customers, Reseller-owned Customers and sibling Reseller users.
- Identify where current `assert_can_access` is applied and where `tenant_id` scoping is performed independently.
- Produce a migration/reconciliation plan for existing root Customer tenants and local test accounts before any schema or data changes.
- No application code or database records have been changed yet.
## Focused local source/test checkpoint — 2026-11-02
- Created a clean implementation worktree `C:\Users\Ali\AI-Employee\.worktrees\Ai-employee MultiVendor` from merged `main` at `2819cdc651c0a769b653bf3c92cd74e21a62925a`, on local branch `feature/multi-vendor-foundation-20261102`. The previous Local Staging worktree remains separate with its pre-existing runtime artifacts untouched.
- Re-read `edition_service.py`, `edition_control.py`, `tenant_admin.py`, `edition_deps.py`, `deps.py`, and the tenant/user/role models from the clean worktree.
- Existing `TenantContext` binds one authenticated User and one Tenant; JWT `tenant_id` must equal `User.tenant_id`. There is no separate effective portal-context tenant in the request principal today. A future portal context must retain actor identity/tenant separately from the scoped target tenant; it must not rewrite the primary identity.
- `has_permission` already checks tenant-local role permissions, but `require_edition` is still a role-name Admin/Owner gate. Edition API-key scopes are separate from bearer-user grants. This is the clean integration point for action-level permission checks.
- `provision_child_tenant` is transactional around child creation, creates an active child and an initial active Admin user with a fixed permission set, then commits internally. It supports Vendor→Reseller and Reseller→Customer only. It is not a reusable user-invitation flow and cannot create a direct Vendor→Customer.
- `assert_can_access` permits only same-tenant access or one direct child level; it rejects Vendor→grandchild Customer. Existing tests cover direct-child boundaries but not the approved portal delegation matrix.
- `tenant_admin.py` user listing/status/role updates are tenant-scoped; role assignment uses `_assert_roles_within_authority`. There is no create/invite-user route in this router.
- Local focused tests executed in the clean worktree: `tests/test_edition_boundaries.py` + `tests/api/test_tenant_admin_role_boundary.py` — **21 passed**. This is a baseline regression check, not proof of new requirements.
- `git status` on the previous Local Staging worktree after the successful fast-forward confirmed its branch and origin ref both at `57b1505a`; pre-existing modified/untracked runtime artifacts remain. `git diff --check` exit 0 (only line-ending warning for `frontend/tsconfig.json`).

## Refined implementation contract
- Keep `User.tenant_id` as the primary identity home. Add a separately validated portal/effective-resource context rather than moving a user between tenants.
- For every request, retain `actor_user_id` + `actor_tenant_id` and separately resolve `context_tenant_id` + `context_portal_kind`; audit both. Enforce a server-side descendant/owner relationship and explicit portal grant at context activation and on every request.
- Vendor context may target its own Vendor, direct Resellers, or descendant Customers only when the relevant portal grant exists. Reseller context may target itself or its direct Customers only when granted. Customer context is self-only. Reseller-to-sibling and Vendor-to-other-Vendor contexts are impossible.
- Apply action permission checks to the actor in the actor's home tenant, then apply resource ownership checks to the target context. Do not grant a Vendor unrestricted global access through `is_superuser` or `Platform Admin` shortcuts.
- Keep one active owner path for Customer tenants: either direct Vendor child or direct Reseller child; do not support multiple parents or inferred ownership.

## Immediate engineering order
1. Finish route/service/repository audit for tenant ownership, with emphasis on support/files/search/reports/background tasks and global superuser exceptions.
2. Design migration compatibility for existing standalone Customer tenants and account creation; no automatic re-parenting of existing users/tenants.
3. Implement server-side action permissions and a scoped portal-context principal in a small backend-first PR, with negative tests before UI.
4. Then implement default Vendor provisioning, direct Vendor Customer creation, user invitations and public registration lifecycle.
## Resource-boundary audit findings — 2026-11-02
- Most ordinary application API surfaces appear to use the authenticated `ctx.tenant_id` directly in repository predicates (examples: inbox conversations/messages, work items, workflow runs/events/schedules/approvals, workforce proposals, templates, files, knowledge search and run artifacts). These are good tenant-local foundations but would continue to point at the actor's home tenant unless explicitly adapted to a validated portal resource context.
- File service APIs take an explicit tenant_id and scope list/get/delete/quota queries to that tenant. Knowledge API passes `ctx.tenant_id` into the RAG service. Both will need the new effective resource context only for approved lower-portal access; default behavior should remain unchanged.
- Support escalations are scoped by `from_tenant_id` or `to_tenant_id`; attachment download paths also validate the related escalation/message and tenant-owned FileObject. Reuse this participant/tenant check rather than broadening to all descendants.
- Commercial license issuance has a dedicated hierarchy traversal in `license_service.issue_license`, unlike the simpler `assert_can_access` helper. However, the traversal currently requires a Customer's parent to be a Reseller; it will reject a future direct Vendor→Customer path unless deliberately extended and tested.
- Vendor tenant listing (`GET /edition/vendor/tenants`) currently lists direct Resellers and their Customer children only; it omits direct Vendor Customer children. The Vendor license endpoint's target selection and tenant listing must be updated together when direct Customer provisioning is added.
- `assert_can_access` currently permits same-tenant or direct child only and is not a general portal-context implementation. Do not expand it into an unrestricted recursive descendant check; portal-kind and explicit grants must be part of authorization.
- Background Test Center worker loads a run by ID, then binds the test definition to both definition ID and `run.tenant_id`; lifecycle/audit records use that run tenant. This is an example of resource-derived tenant scope. Audit all workers similarly before context support.
- These are targeted source reads/searches, not a complete proof of every repository/query. Continue the route-by-route inventory before enabling cross-portal data access.
## Latest documentation and local/main sync — 2026-11-02
- PR #1352 merged successfully at `06792bf372eaf41dad18b412d2759968563c73d3`; exact-head Documentation Truth Consistency and CodeQL both passed.
- `origin/main` now points to `06792bf372eaf41dad18b412d2759968563c73d3`.
- Clean implementation worktree `C:\Users\Ali\AI-Employee\.worktrees\Ai-employee MultiVendor` was fetched and fast-forwarded to that exact main SHA. Verified branch `feature/multi-vendor-foundation-20261102` tracks `origin/main`, `git status` is clean and `git diff --check` exits 0.
- Previous Local Staging worktree remains on the merged documentation branch at its prior matching SHA, with only its pre-existing staging/runtime artifacts; it has not been repurposed for implementation.
- The primary checkout remains untouched.
- Baseline test evidence remains 21 passing focused tests on the same source baseline; no app behavior or database was modified.
## Implementation slice 1 — direct Vendor-owned Customers

Draft PR [#1353](https://github.com/ijoolaie/AI-Employee/pull/1353) is open from `feature/multi-vendor-foundation-20261102` at `b73e03537801824be6ace88b483fae029aacfbb1`.

Implemented in this slice:
- Vendor direct Customer provision/list/suspend/resume/deprovision endpoints.
- Vendor license target listing includes direct Customers.
- Tenant provisioning, direct-child access and entitlement delegation support Vendor→Customer while preserving Vendor→Reseller→Customer and denying Vendor→Reseller-descendant direct access.
- Commercial license hierarchy supports both direct Vendor Customer and Reseller-owned Customer, with malformed/foreign hierarchy rejection.
- Explicit API-key route scopes and contract docs.

Validation: 36 focused offline tests passed; Ruff passed. Database-backed live API/license tests could not run because dedicated test DB environment variables are absent; no staging DB was substituted. Exact-head CI is pending. PR is Draft and must not merge until PostgreSQL-backed API validation and CI pass.

Not implemented by this slice: per-user action grants, child user invitation/creation, default Vendor provisioning, public signup/payment/Demo lifecycle, server-validated portal context or distinct portal UI. Existing Admin/Owner route gates remain temporarily.

Local branch and GitHub PR head match. Local worktree clean after commit/push. Handoff and Current Status in the implementation branch record this checkpoint.

## Handoff synchronization update
- Latest PR #1353 branch head after the local handoff/status sync commit is `79170a5a2effd2db9cf2380ad9af77af576c9c37`.
- The implementation code commit remains `b73e03537801824be6ace88b483fae029aacfbb1`; the subsequent commit updates only `CURRENT_STATUS.md` and the master handoff.
- The isolated implementation worktree is expected to be clean at the same branch SHA; exact status is rechecked before the next feature slice.
- Exact-head CI on `79170a5a2effd2db9cf2380ad9af77af576c9c37` is in progress; only Documentation Truth Consistency and some independent workflows have completed so far. Do not merge while required checks remain pending.

## Delegated permission implementation update (2026-11-02)

- First enforcement slice committed as `c15e44d1`: `POST /edition/reseller/customers` now requires the explicit tenant-local `reseller.customer.create` permission in addition to the Reseller edition boundary.
- `is_superuser` does not bypass this action check; permissions attached only to another tenant's role do not count. API-key route scope is still independently required.
- Validation: 26 focused tests passed; Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.
- Remaining: Vendor action-permission bootstrap and enforcement, other Reseller operations, role delegation ceiling, secure tenant-local user invitations, server-authorized portal grants and dedicated PostgreSQL-backed API validation. PR #1353 remains Draft.

## Reseller action coverage expansion (2026-11-02)

- Extended action-level enforcement to all Reseller Customer operations: list/read, create, suspend/resume/deprovision, and entitlement delegation. Each route requires its own tenant-local permission; API-key scopes remain an additional gate.
- Validation: 29 focused tests passed; Ruff and `git diff --check` passed. Commit `65e4e2af`.
- Vendor action-permission bootstrap/enforcement, remaining edition operations, tenant-local user invitations, role delegation ceilings, portal grants and dedicated PostgreSQL-backed API validation remain open.

## PostgreSQL fixture follow-up (2026-11-02)

- CI on `48a4c46a` correctly rejected two old PostgreSQL fixtures that expected Reseller Admin to read customers without `reseller.customer.read`.
- Updated the fixtures to seed the explicit tenant-local permission. No production authorization bypass was added. Commit `708d9300`; 29 offline focused tests and Ruff pass. New exact-head CI is pending; shared Staging was not used.

## Vendor action-permission implementation (2026-11-02)

- Added tenant-local Vendor action grants and applied them to Vendor direct Customer and Reseller read/create/manage operations plus Vendor license-target listing. Codes: `vendor.tenant.read`, `vendor.reseller.read/create/manage`, `vendor.customer.read/create/manage`.
- Foreign-tenant role grants and `is_superuser` do not bypass action checks; API-key scopes remain an independent gate. Focused validation: 38 passed; Ruff and diff check passed. Commit `8f93e098`.
- Important prerequisite before deployment: Vendor root provisioning/bootstrap does not yet grant this permission set to the initial Vendor Admin role. A tested bootstrap/upgrade path must be implemented before enabling the enforcement for existing Vendor tenants. Role delegation ceiling and secure invitations remain open. Exact-head CI after this commit is pending.

items.title: [Thiết kế] DeepEval, Ragas và Langfuse trên Knora Evaluation
items.body:
> **Định hướng hiện hành (14/10/2026):** Cloudflare Workers AI là AI platform chính; ưu tiên Cloudflare GPT-OSS 20B judge. Public/synthetic có phép có thể gửi Cloudflare cho inference/evaluation; private chưa có phép gửi xử lý local. Langfuse metadata-only. **Bỏ feasibility A/Ollama judge mặc định**, tích hợp từng thành phần và test trong quá trình làm. Chưa code/calls/cost approval.
>
> [Quyết định mới nhất của tôi](https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/issues/158#issuecomment-6163835716) · [Kế hoạch thay thế A, scope code và dự toán calls](https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/issues/158#issuecomment-6163836290)
## Quyết định

**Tôi đã đồng ý tích hợp DeepEval, Ragas và Langfuse cho KnoraAgent; Guardrails AI được bổ sung vào hướng bảo mật với đề xuất Issue riêng. Chưa triển khai code.** Mục tiêu là đo được chất lượng hệ thống AI/RAG và truy ra nguyên nhân khi câu trả lời sai, đồng thời **tái sử dụng evaluation/traces hiện có**, không xây lại một framework evaluation riêng.

## Phân chia vai trò đã duyệt (11/10; bổ sung Ragas ngày 14/10/2026)

| Thành phần | Trách nhiệm chính | Không nên làm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Knora Evaluation hiện có** | Giữ nguồn chuẩn cho datasets, answers/evidence gold, corpus manifests, versioned runs, deterministic checks, benchmark/release gates và reports | Không thay thế bởi một bộ dữ liệu hay hệ thống chấm điểm độc lập chỉ vì thêm tool |
| **DeepEval** | Bổ sung các phép đánh giá RAG (retrieval/context relevance, answer correctness và faithfulness/grounding), regression tests và model-based metrics khi cần | Không dùng điểm LLM judge để thay thế các kiểm chứng nguồn/citation/ACL bằng quy tắc xác định |
| **Ragas** | Bổ sung đánh giá RAG và tạo câu hỏi kiểm thử, đặc biệt multi-hop, theo phân công metric được duyệt; generated cases được review và nhập vào Knora Evaluation | Không tạo gold/dataset/runner/release authority thứ hai, không tự coi synthetic answer là gold, không nhân đôi DeepEval mặc định |
| **Langfuse** | Quan sát pipeline thực chạy: query rewrite, multi-query/decomposition, retrieval branches, rank/rerank, evidence, generation; trace, model usage, error, latency và phân tích nguyên nhân | Không bắt buộc biến Langfuse thành dataset/test-runner hoặc nguồn chân lý thứ hai; không thu raw private PDF/PII mặc định |

**Tích hợp chung:** Một bộ gold dataset và provenance của Knora là nguồn chuẩn. Liên kết `evaluation case/run ID ↔ Knora trace ID ↔ Langfuse trace` và kết quả DeepEval/Ragas khi khả thi, có kiểm soát dữ liệu. Đây là **phân chia trách nhiệm**, không bắt buộc mọi phép đo phải đồng thời chạy trên các thành phần.

### Bộ đánh giá thăm dò ban đầu

- **Mục tiêu đề xuất đã đồng ý:** 16 PDF có chủ đích + 60 câu hỏi có đáp án/bằng chứng chuẩn, dùng để tìm lỗi và so sánh phương án bước đầu, **không coi là benchmark production đủ lớn hoặc tuyên bố tối ưu**.
- Các PDF trải qua: văn bản sạch; heading/chương mục; nhiều cột; bảng; scan/hybrid; tài liệu học thuật Việt/Anh và mixed language.
- Các câu hỏi trải qua: hỏi đơn giản/đếm chương; so sánh, nhiều ý; theo bảng; tiếp nối; typo nhẹ/nặng, không dấu, chữ+số và exact identifier; multi-hop; no-answer/refusal. Dùng nhãn phụ nếu một câu thuộc nhiều nhóm.
- **Giữ nguyên các bộ hiện có** như M1 20 cases, M3 50 cases, Vietnamese RAG datasets để chạy **regression**, không ghi đè/sửa lịch sử. M3 đang là corpus tài liệu text nhỏ, không thể đại diện thay cho bộ PDF mới.
- Gold label cần có expected facts, source document/version, page/span/region và acceptable evidence; khi thử parser/chunker, **không cố định ground truth chỉ bằng Chunk ID của một derivation**.
- Khi đánh giá release, mở rộng tập dữ liệu và có **held-out set** chưa dùng tuning, đồng thời khóa scoring policy/gates trước lần chạy nghiệm thu.

### Metric và phương pháp kiểm thử

1. **Document understanding:** extraction completeness, reading order, heading/table fidelity, OCR quality khi áp dụng, source anchors/citation mapping.
2. **Retrieval / Query Understanding:** Recall@K, Hit@K, MRR/nDCG@K ở các giai đoạn phù hợp; **multi-intent evidence coverage**, typo recovery + false-correction, exact identifier preservation, query correctness, no-answer.
3. **Answering:** answer correctness, groundedness/faithfulness, citation support và refusal correctness; phân biệt *trả lời đúng* với *bám vào evidence đã truy xuất*. DeepEval là một nguồn đo hỗ trợ, không phải oracle tuyệt đối.
4. **Hiệu năng và tài nguyên:** p50/p95 retrieval + end-to-end latency, number of query branches/model calls, CPU/RAM/GPU, throughput, cost (nếu đo được), index size và ingestion time.
5. **Hard gates không thể đánh đổi:** **0 cross-Workspace/tenant data leakage, 0 unauthorized/stale-version evidence**, không bịa nguồn dẫn chứng, citation locator/anchor phải chính xác. Các kiểm thử này phải là deterministic/integration/security checks của Knora, **không được chấp nhận chỉ vì LLM-as-judge chấm PASS**.

**Điều tra lỗi theo công đoạn:** kết quả eval/trace phải phân biệt được lỗi do PDF parser/chunker, query rewriting/planning, candidate retrieval, fusion/reranking, evidence selection, hay LLM answer generation. Ví dụ “báo cáo có 7 chương” sai có thể do parser đọc sót, retriever không tìm đủ hay generation đếm sai; công cụ phải giúp xác định nguyên nhân thay vì chỉ đưa một điểm số.

**Quy tắc so sánh:** chạy trên cùng dataset/corpus + môi trường và cố định các thành phần không thử nghiệm; đổi **một thành phần tại một thời điểm** (ví dụ `pypdf` vs Docling với embedding/retrieval/LLM giữ cố định, hoặc V3 single-query vs thêm multi-query), báo cáo quality **cùng** cost/latency và regression. Chưa tự đặt ngưỡng phần trăm thắng hoặc p95 cố định khi chưa có baseline và resource budget.

### Tích hợp và dữ liệu — nguyên tắc đã duyệt, chi tiết còn nghiên cứu

- **Tận dụng runner, dataset/manifest, schema/provenance, trace và reporting hiện hành**; thiết kế adapter/instrumentation nhỏ nhất. Không thêm orchestration/plugin framework mới chỉ để sử dụng DeepEval/Ragas/Langfuse.
- **DeepEval:** xác minh khả năng chạy offline/local hoặc cấu hình LLM judge, model/provider, license, runtime dependencies, test reproducibility, chi phí và dữ liệu nào bị gửi ra ngoài trước khi lựa chọn phương án tích hợp. Ưu tiên test tự động trong eval/CI thích hợp, không đưa LLM judge đắt đỏ lên đường phục vụ user nếu không cần.
- **Langfuse:** đã chọn Cloud Hobby metadata-only; không PDF, câu hỏi, câu trả lời hoặc dữ liệu nhạy cảm, không tự nâng cấp. Region, allowlist chi tiết, sampling/quota, masking, retention/deletion, access và failure/replay còn chờ duyệt; không deploy self-host cho pilot.
- **Observability không được quyết định quyền truy cập** hoặc thay thế Knora trace/provenance; nếu Langfuse không khả dụng, ứng dụng cần bảo toàn security/citation và hành vi trả lời đã được kiểm chứng (phương án fail-safe/trace reconciliation sẽ chốt khi triển khai).
- Triển khai từng bước, có versioned configuration và rollback; ghi nhận kết quả thật, không coi “đã cài 2 thư viện” là hoàn tất evaluation.

## Quan hệ với Issue #153

- **#153 — Retrieval V3:** nguồn quyết định về kiến trúc retrieval, Document/Query Understanding, evaluation quality gates, benchmark requirements, citations và authorization.
- **#158 — DeepEval, Ragas & Langfuse:** nguồn quyết định **cách sử dụng/tích hợp công cụ evaluation và observability** với evaluation và traces hiện có; các ràng buộc benchmark/quality/security từ #153 vẫn áp dụng.
- Cross-reference: https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/issues/153. **Không sao chép toàn bộ nội dung #153**; không tự sửa #153 trong lần cập nhật này.

## Trạng thái và phạm vi

**Đã chốt:** dùng **DeepEval + Ragas + Langfuse**, phân vai như trên, kế thừa evaluation hiện có, bộ thăm dò **16 PDF + 60 câu**, tách deterministic hard gates khỏi LLM-as-judge, bảo vệ dữ liệu và tránh duplication/over-engineering.

**Chưa chốt:** compatibility/pins cuối cùng, exact judge config/rubric và input projection (preferred judge Cloudflare GPT-OSS 20B đã chốt), concrete adapters/packet/schema, sampling/replay, numeric calls/tokens/quality gates sau baseline và validator/enforcement sau trials. Đã chốt DeepEval correctness/relevancy/faithfulness; Ragas multi-hop drafts + conditional NoiseSensitivity; pilot Việt/Anh, tôi duyệt gold cuối; Cloud Hobby Tokyo owner-only, metadata-only và mục tiêu tối đa 7 ngày. Guardrails ở Issue #188 review-only. Phiên smoke/code/install/inference/Cloud credentials chưa được phép. Các lựa chọn này sẽ được nghiên cứu và đưa chủ dự án duyệt trước khi triển khai phạm vi cụ thể; benchmark chỉ sau authorization và resource agreement.

**Lịch sử cập nhật thiết kế:** các vòng đầu chỉ sửa Issue #158. Ngày 14/10/2026 tôi cho phép tạo Issue Guardrails #188 để review. Chưa sửa code/config/database/Docker hoặc bắt đầu triển khai.

## Tham khảo

- [DeepEval](https://github.com/confident-ai/deepeval)
- [Ragas](https://github.com/vibrantlabsai/ragas)
- [Langfuse](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse)
- [Knora evaluation hiện có](https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/blob/main/docs/evaluation.md)
- [Knora Retrieval V3 — Issue #153](https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/issues/153)


## Quyết định của tôi — chốt vòng 1 và mở rộng phạm vi (14/10/2026)

Quyết định mới này thay thế các lựa chọn còn mở hoặc khuyến nghị khác trước đó về Q1–Q5. Các comments audit lịch sử được giữ nguyên; khuyến nghị self-host cũ không phải lựa chọn hiện hành.

- **Q1:** Tôi chốt DeepEval scoring và xuất observation từ trace hiện có trước, sau đó mở rộng runtime instrumentation theo #153.
- **Q2:** Tôi chọn **Langfuse Cloud Hobby**, **chỉ gửi metadata an toàn**; không gửi nội dung PDF, câu hỏi, câu trả lời hoặc dữ liệu nhạy cảm. **Không tự nâng cấp gói.** Region, allowlist chi tiết, access, retention/deletion, sampling/quota/replay còn cần chốt. Pilot không deploy self-host server; bản server 4.58.0 từng đề xuất không thành deployment pin.
- **Q3:** Tôi ưu tiên judge local; cần đánh giá tính khả thi và chất lượng trước khi chọn model cụ thể. Chưa cho phép tự chọn model hoặc fallback sang judge bên ngoài.
- **Q4:** Tôi dùng **PDF/Q&A public hoặc synthetic đã kiểm duyệt** cho pilot. Không tự suy quyền phân phối PDF từ URL public; private corpus/PII không tự đưa vào công cụ hoặc Cloud.
- **Q5:** Tôi đồng ý bản ứng viên **DeepEval 4.2.8 / Langfuse Python SDK 4.17.0**, chỉ pin sau compatibility checks. Chưa cài package hoặc nghiệm thu integration.

### Tôi bổ sung Ragas

Tôi quyết định dùng **Ragas** để bổ sung đánh giá RAG và tạo câu hỏi kiểm thử, đặc biệt multi-hop. Ragas tái sử dụng Knora dataset/gold/manifests/case-run IDs/provenance/reports/gates, tránh trùng DeepEval. Metric cụ thể và workflow draft → human/source review → Knora versioned case chưa chốt. Generated questions/answers không mặc nhiên là gold hoặc held-out; không tự tăng/đổi target 16 PDF + 60 câu hoặc ghi đè legacy datasets. Capability tạo/evaluate multi-hop không tự thay đổi quyết định production multi-hop/query planning của #153.

### Tôi bổ sung Guardrails AI vào hướng bảo mật riêng

Tôi quyết định mở rộng bảo vệ trước prompt injection từ PDF, nội dung nguy hiểm và rò rỉ dữ liệu bằng **Guardrails AI**. Tôi yêu cầu đề xuất **Issue bảo mật riêng**, kiểm thử detection cùng false-positive/false-block rates trên tài liệu hợp lệ. Issue riêng ở bước đề xuất, chưa tạo ticket, pin validator/model hoặc thay runtime policy. Không thay deterministic ACL/Workspace/active-version/citation/tool-approval gates; Guardrails không cấp quyền hoặc trở thành oracle an toàn.

### Giới hạn phê duyệt

**Chưa triển khai code.** Tiếp tục nghiên cứu và trình vòng quyết định metrics, validators, judge, chi phí, latency và data policy. Chưa install/import tools, tạo tài khoản/bật Cloud export, gọi model, sửa runtime, tạo worktree implementation, merge/deploy/Done. Sau concrete approval mới implementation/test theo AGENTS.md trong worktree riêng, phối hợp file/runtime với #153.


## Thiết kế vòng 2 — đang chờ quyết định

[Đề xuất DeepEval/Ragas/Langfuse, bản nháp Issue Guardrails và Q6–Q13](https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/issues/158#issuecomment-6162789233). Các metrics, validators, trial/model, region/retention và ngân sách trong đề xuất chưa được duyệt. Không triển khai code.


## Quyết định mới nhất Q6–Q13 và bước thực tế tiếp theo (14/10/2026)

[Quyết định của tôi Q6–Q13](https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/issues/158#issuecomment-6163095296) thay thế các lựa chọn còn mở của vòng 2, gồm smoke nhỏ trước calibration, không bắt hạ tầng Evaluation riêng và tối đa 60 phút mỗi phiên được tôi cho phép.

[Issue Guardrails #188](https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/issues/188) đã tạo để review, chưa code/enforcement. [Phạm vi thử A và hướng adapter B cũ](https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/issues/158#issuecomment-6163140731) đã được thay thế: tôi bỏ A/Ollama feasibility, chuyển sang integration theo kế hoạch Cloudflare mới. Chưa install/import tools, tạo worktree, inference/benchmark hoặc dùng Cloud credentials/export. Routine technical details do agent xử lý; không mở grilling cho chi tiết nhỏ.

Ollama snapshot: không thấy process hoặc listener 11434 khi kiểm tra; không stop/kill/restart process nào.


## Quyết định thay thế và kế hoạch hiện hành

Latest owner decision [Cloudflare Judge/data policy](https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/issues/158#issuecomment-6163835716) supersedes old local-judge/Q10 absolute-local/A proposal. [Kế hoạch integration](https://github.com/NhiBuaa/knora-agent/issues/158#issuecomment-6163836290): DeepEval→Ragas→Langfuse và #188 shadow; không thêm infrastructure. Proposed first DeepEval live integration tối đa24 HTTPattempts/US còn chờ budgetapproval; scope code/install/tests cũng chưa duyệt. Application#153 budget tách riêng. Humanreview/gold/16PDF60cases/securitygates vẫn giữ.
