milestone.title: M10 — Test-Mode Payments & Checkout
milestone.description:
Objective: buyers pay (provider TEST mode) and orders become paid safely and idempotently.
Deliverables: payment schema + append-only ledger; allocation library; order-derived PaymentIntent; verified webhook processing; order consumers; late-payment refund; payment UI; live-mode guard and kill switch; reconciliation v1; test suite; staging E2E.
Exit criteria: a test-card checkout ends with a paid order and ledger entries showing commission; tamper, replay and out-of-order tests pass; live keys are refused at boot.
Depends on: M06, M09. Test mode only; live payments are a separate gated milestone.

items.body:
<!-- planning-id: M10-08 -->

**Milestone:** M10 — Test-Mode Payments & Checkout  
**Planning ID:** `M10-08`  
**Size:** S (planning estimate)  
**Requirements/traceability:** live-payments gate

## Summary
Live money must be impossible to enable by accident.

## Dependencies
Blocked by:
- #51 — Stripe webhook ingestion foundation in payment-service

Do not start until the issues above are merged. If a dependency is missing, comment and stop.

## Current state
The webhook foundation refuses live keys unless the flag is set (M06-06); no kill switch exists.

## Expected behavior
`PAYMENTS_ENABLED` (default true in test mode) — when false `POST /orders` payment step and `POST /payments/intents` return 503 `PAYMENTS_DISABLED` while browsing continues; `PAYMENTS_LIVE_MODE_ENABLED` enforced in payment-service, seller-service and a web build check (`pk_live_` refused when false); `SUPPORTED_SELLER_COUNTRIES` enforced in seller onboarding (already added in M06-02/M06-14) and documented; a startup log line states "payments: TEST MODE" or "LIVE MODE".

## Technical approach and files
Config schema + small middleware; web build script check.

## Implementation steps
1. Kill switch.
2. Boot guards.
3. Web build check.
4. Tests.

## API / data / event / UI changes
New `PAYMENTS_DISABLED` error.

## Security, authorization and tenant isolation
Flags readable only by deployment config.

## Error handling, edge cases and recovery
Toggling without redeploying other services.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a live key and the flag false, then boot fails with a clear message
- [ ] Given `PAYMENTS_ENABLED=false`, then payment creation returns 503 and the catalog still works.

## Testing requirements
Boot and endpoint tests.

## Documentation updates
Payment README; env examples.

_Update in-repository files listed here. Maintainer-held design documents live outside this repository; if you cannot see them, list the required changes in the pull request description._

## Definition of done
Standard DoD. (see "Reference: dod-standard" below for the standard checklist).

## Out of scope
Enabling live mode.

## Embedded references
Essential constraints are inlined below so this issue is self-contained.

<details>
<summary>Reference: repo-context</summary>

**Repository:** pnpm 10 + Turborepo monorepo, Node 22, TypeScript. Apps (`apps/`): NestJS services `gateway` (4000), `auth-service` (4001), `product-service` (4002), `seller-service` (4003), `order-service` (4004), `payment-service` (4005), `notification-service` (4006), `media-service` (4007), `analytics-service` (4008); Next.js 15 apps `web` (3000), `seller-portal` (3001), `admin-portal` (3002). Shared packages (`packages/`): `contracts` (Zod schemas for DTOs/events), `auth-shared` (JWT/JWKS verification, guards), `kafka-client`, `logger` (Pino), `utils`, `ui`, `config` (eslint/tsconfig). Postgres (Drizzle) for auth/seller/order/payment; MongoDB (Mongoose) for product; Redis for rate limits/cache; Kafka-compatible broker for events. All datastores are managed cloud services — **no local Docker is required or may be introduced as a dependency**. Commands: `pnpm install`, `pnpm turbo run lint type-check test build --filter=<pkg>...`, `pnpm --filter <app> <script>`. Each service validates DTOs with Zod from `@betterbasket/contracts` (not class-validator) and exposes `GET /health`. Services compile to CommonJS.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: payments-model</summary>

**Test mode only** until the live-payments gate is explicitly opened by the maintainer. Model: one PaymentIntent per order on the **platform** Stripe account (`transfer_group = order_<orderId>`, card payments only); after success and when the release policy allows, one Transfer per seller sub-order using `source_transaction = <charge id>`. The platform bears Stripe fees, refunds and chargebacks (provisional policy). Refunding a charge does **not** reverse transfers — reversals are explicit. `reverse_transfer`/`refund_application_fee` are destination-charge features and are **not** used. Failed transfers are not retried by Stripe — the platform retries. Amount, currency and destination are always derived server-side from the persisted order; clients send only an order id. Config gates: `PAYMENTS_LIVE_MODE_ENABLED` (default false; live keys `sk_live_`/`pk_live_` refused at boot unless true), `PAYMENTS_ENABLED` kill switch, `TRANSFERS_PAUSED`, `SUPPORTED_SELLER_COUNTRIES` (empty = test mode only). Country, legal and finance policy are **undecided**; every country-dependent behavior must stay configurable and provisional.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: test-mode-gate</summary>

This issue is `gate:test-mode-only`: use Stripe **test** keys and test-mode objects only; the service must refuse to start with a live key unless `PAYMENTS_LIVE_MODE_ENABLED=true` (never set outside production after the maintainer opens the live-payments gate). No real card or customer data in fixtures, logs or tests. Provisional commission, payout, jurisdiction and legal assumptions must stay configurable and must not be presented as final.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: security-baseline</summary>

Validate all input with strict Zod schemas; enforce authorization and tenant scoping on the server for every route; return 404 for foreign objects; never log secrets, tokens, card data, full emails/addresses; parameterized queries only (Drizzle; Mongo filters built from allow-listed fields, never from raw client operators); rate limit abuse-prone endpoints; use constant-time comparison for secrets/signatures; secrets only from validated environment configuration (service fails to start if a required secret is missing; no placeholder defaults); dependencies pinned via lockfile; add negative tests for each authorization rule introduced.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: dod-standard</summary>

Implementation matches *Expected behavior*; every acceptance criterion passes with automated evidence; required tests added and green in CI (no skipped tests without a linked issue); lint, type-check, build, contract and migration checks pass; docs updated; security requirements satisfied including negative/authorization tests; no secrets, credentials or real customer/payment data in code, fixtures, logs or PR text; PR description complete; deployment verification performed when the issue affects a deployed environment.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reference: agent-workflow</summary>

1. Read this whole issue; inspect the files named under *Technical approach*; confirm every item under *Current state* is still true (the codebase may have moved). 2. Verify each dependency issue is merged (see *Dependencies*); if a prerequisite is missing, stop and comment — do not re-implement it. 3. Post a short implementation plan as a comment before large changes. 4. Implement exactly the *Expected behavior*; respect *Out of scope*. 5. Write the tests listed under *Tests* (unit, integration, contract, E2E as applicable); run lint, type-check, tests and build for every touched package. 6. Review your own diff for security issues (authorization, tenant scoping, input validation, secret handling, logging of sensitive data) and regressions. 7. Update documentation named under *Docs* (in-repo files; if the maintainer's private design docs exist locally, update the affected sections too, otherwise list the required changes in the PR). 8. Check every acceptance criterion and quote the evidence (test names/output) in the PR description. 9. Open a reviewable PR: link this issue, list requirements covered, architectural impact, tests added, docs updated, migration/deployment impact. 10. If blocked or if a decision is unresolved, stop, comment with the question and options, and apply the `blocked:decision` label — do not guess or make architectural decisions that are not in this issue.

</details>

items.title: Epic: Platform-wide Jev Decision Intelligence — Superadmin-managed AI classification, scoring, routing, automation & cross-app integration
items.body:
# Objective

Introduce **Jev (TypeSafe AI System One)** as a centrally managed, platform-wide **Decision Intelligence Layer** in Biza Miz, alongside the existing LiteLLM-only generative AI gateway. Support typed **Choice**, **Score**, and **Noul** (yes/no probability) evaluations across the AI assistant, system agents, memory/managed knowledge, automations, Accounting, Growth & Marketing, CRM, Website Management, My Workspace, shared services, and Superadmin operations.

**Principles:** one AI assistant; four tenant apps only; no tenant provider setup; no new generative gateway; no separate tenant agent builder; no duplicate RAG, prompt resolver, wallet, ledger, business logic, or authorization implementation. This is a managed platform capability, not a fifth tenant app. Tenants see understandable intelligent functionality, never Jev/TypeSafe/LiteLLM branding, infrastructure credentials, provider costs, or routing details.

## Background / current repository boundaries

Read before implementation:
- [Current AI subsystem architecture](https://github.com/hamidnoshady/biza-miz/blob/main/docs/ai-subsystem-architecture.md)
- [Platform app boundaries](https://github.com/hamidnoshady/biza-miz/blob/main/docs/app-boundaries.md)
- [CRM relationship OS](https://github.com/hamidnoshady/biza-miz/blob/main/docs/crm-relationship-os.md)
- Existing AI code: src/lib/ai-service.ts, ai-capabilities.ts, ai-prompt-resolver.ts, ai-memory.ts, ai-knowledge-gateway.ts, ai-system-agents.ts, ai-runtime-modes.ts, ai-automations.ts, ai-automations-service.ts, ai-unattended-authority.ts, ai-wallet-billing.ts.

Already implemented, **do not rebuild**:
- LiteLLM is the only **generative model** gateway. Retain model aliases, upstream routing, fallbacks/retries and existing modes: auto / instant / deep_research.
- Superadmin owns prompts, versions, system agents, assignments, AI configuration; tenants cannot create system agents.
- Tenant memory is platform/business/app/project scoped plus temporary conversation context; deleted memory must stop influencing new turns.
- Managed knowledge uses an **external tenant-qualified endpoint**; local pgvector/RAG and application-owned semantic answer cache were retired.
- AI writes go via the existing ACTION_CATALOG, effective permissions, business validation, human confirmation, and recheck-at-execution, including for unattended work.
- Biza Miz has existing Rial wallet/allowance/settlement with usage attribution. Do not introduce a second ledger.
- Only four standalone tenant apps: Accounting (including POS), Growth & Marketing, CRM, Website Management (Eshobe CMS + WordPress/WooCommerce). The AI chat home, My Workspace, and Settings are shared platform utilities.

## 1. Provider capability contract and applicability

Build against the official TypeSafe **System One** API/SDK contract, after verifying the live documentation at implementation time:
- Dedicated endpoint: POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone (not a standard /chat/completions model).
- Official TypeScript SDK: @typesafe-ai/sdk, when suitable for repository Node/runtime; alternatively an equivalent narrowly scoped HTTP adapter.
- Request: model, bounded state (text/structured data), named questions.
- **Choice:** classify or choose among an explicit allowlisted set; preserve option probabilities and no-match/other policy.
- **Score:** evaluate a question using an ordered, versioned rubric; return numerical score/probability details.
- **Noul:** probability for a yes/no judgment; no independent confidence field should be invented.
- Batch **multiple compatible questions over shared state** in one request when useful. Do not assume an entire database fits one state.
- Model IDs/aliases, pricing, rate limits, context bounds, SDK behavior and vendor retention terms must be **reverified**, not hardcoded from a dated snapshot. Pin production model versions; rollout upgrades via canary/evaluations.
- Do not claim Jev is a generative model, image/audio/video model, OCR, embedding engine, full risk predictor, accounting calculator, date calculator, or autonomous actor.

Supported derived capabilities (implemented by application composition, not separate native Jev APIs): classification, intent recognition, routing, triage, qualitative scoring, ranking and re-ranking, candidate matching, label suggestion, sentiment assessment, response/source-support checks, structured-field selection from pre-extracted candidate sets, guardrail signals, agent tool selection, notification priority, workflow branching and human-escalation recommendations.

### Applicability gate
- **Use deterministic code** for exact calculations, dates, amounts, taxes, consent and permissions; keep existing classifiers where they already work.
- **Use Jev** only where qualitative judgment over authorized content plausibly improves accuracy, latency, operational outcomes, or total cost.
- **Use LiteLLM** for generation, complex reasoning, chat answers, explanations, deep research, OCR/vision through approved models, and natural-language drafts.
- Benchmark Jev vs deterministic rules and existing LiteLLM before enabling each use case; support disabling Jev without breaking normal behavior.

## 2. Architecture and interfaces

Proposed request flow:

~~~text
Tenant chat / business event / scheduled job
    -> Biza Miz trusted tenant + actor + branch/app/project scope
    -> entitlement, consent, authorization, business policy, wallet/budget preflight
    -> policy-based decision invocation
       -> (optional) TypeSafe Jev /v1/systemone
       -> typed response validation, confidence/abstention policy
    -> downstream deterministic service / existing LiteLLM generation (as needed)
    -> existing guarded action executor + current-authority recheck + approval
    -> audited result + existing wallet settlement / telemetry
~~~

Deliver a small **internal decision service** without new independent app infrastructure:
- src/lib/ai-decision-service.ts — typed application-facing entry point
- src/lib/ai-decision-types.ts — typed inputs/outputs, decision outcomes, abstain/error shapes
- src/lib/ai-decision-provider.ts — provider adapter, secrets, retry/timeout/rate limits
- src/lib/ai-decision-policy.ts — versioned choice sets, score rubrics, noul thresholds, fallback rules
- src/lib/ai-decision-context.ts — minimal allowlisted inputs and immutable trusted scope
- src/lib/ai-decision-audit.ts and ai-decision-evaluation.ts — trace, feedback and measurement
- src/lib/ai-decision-billing.ts — integrate with existing wallet/usage APIs; **not** a new ledger
- src/app/platform/ai/decisions/** and src/app/api/platform/ai/decisions/** — Superadmin control plane

Names are suggestions; align them with existing repo naming and test conventions. Avoid duplicating ai-prompt-resolver.ts or creating proxy routing policy mirrors.

Example internal API:
~~~ts
evaluateDecision({
  decisionKey,
  trustedActorContext, // server-resolved, never model-controlled
  businessId,
  locationId,
  appKey,
  projectId,
  candidateState, // policy-specific, minimized/validated
  requestId,
});
~~~

Every policy is closed/registered: type, allowed options/rubric, question instructions, policy version, allowed apps/roles/contexts, risk class, input allowlist, maximum size/tokens, thresholds, human review and fallback. Models may choose only among already authorized candidates. Jev output NEVER creates tools, new permissions, executable SQL, endpoint URLs, financial values or arbitrary actions.

## 3. Superadmin-managed Decision Intelligence

Create **/platform/ai/decisions** integrated with existing /platform/ai control plane.

Deliver:
- [ ] Central provider endpoint/credentials in secret store with masked read APIs and test/health checks; no secrets exposed to tenants or logs.
- [ ] Configurable/pinned model version and staged upgrades; explicit model availability/health/status.
- [ ] Decision definition registry: Choice, Score, Noul, typed schemas, criteria, context allowlists, fallback/abstain rules.
- [ ] Draft, simulate, compare, publish and roll back **versioned** decision policy definitions (atomic active policy selection).
- [ ] Global, feature, app, business type, tenant and system-agent assignments, with permission/entitlement intersection.
- [ ] Risk-based approval rules, quality thresholds, review queues, feature flags, shadow/canary modes, kill switches.
- [ ] Quotas, budget caps, fair usage, cost configuration, markup and attribution reporting.
- [ ] Monitoring by tenant, policy, app, system agent and model: calls, outcomes, invalid outputs, latency, 429/5xx, provider spend, customer charges, error/abstain frequency and drift.
- [ ] Quality studio: labeled datasets, Persian test cases, regression evaluation, version-to-version comparison, operator feedback and investigation.
- [ ] Security/audit trail for policy edits, assignments, approvals, key rotation, run results and rollbacks.
- [ ] No tenant-facing provider branding or provider credential / wholesale cost configuration; tenants see only eligible managed features and simplified controls.
- [ ] Superadmin endpoints guarded by **platform** ai.read / ai.config.manage; tenant settings permissions must not grant global configuration rights.

## 4. Central AI assistant & system agents

- [ ] Classify user intent: informational chat, reporting, search, existing tool/action, clarification, research request, task drafting.
- [ ] Rank relevant app contexts and pre-authorized tools; fallback to ordinary tool-selection behavior on uncertainty.
- [ ] Pick among **currently eligible** Superadmin system agents, never create tenant-built agents.
- [ ] Select closed-enum/boolean tool arguments from explicit validated candidates; never accept Jev-generated SQL or arbitrary tool/action IDs.
- [ ] Qualitative complexity estimation and triage while preserving auto/instant/deep_research modes; NEVER silently invoke paid Deep Research, broaden tool access or alter model alias routing policy.
- [ ] Evaluate request/answer safety signals, possible prompt injection, evidence support and human handoff needs. These are advisory classifiers, not a security boundary.
- [ ] Suggest notification priority and relevant AI widgets; check existing permissions on every invocation.
- [ ] Compare outcomes and cost against current LiteLLM-only method, with option to bypass Jev entirely.

## 5. Memory & managed knowledge

- [ ] Relevance-rank only **already authorized** memory candidates within the current tenant/app/project scope.
- [ ] Suggest duplicate/conflicting/outdated/important memories for authorized review; respect deletion and never auto-promote conversations to durable memory.
- [ ] Optional re-ranking of external managed-knowledge retrieval hits, respecting tenant + branch/app/project/source boundaries, reference provenance and source citation integrity.
- [ ] Answerability and claim/source-support classification with clear uncertainty handling; abstain on missing evidence.
- [ ] No second RAG/vector/indexing store, answer cache, ingestion workflow or prompt resolver.
- [ ] Verify no deleted memory, revoked project data, or tenant-private hit appears after policy or permission changes.

## 6. Accounting / POS

All suggestions are advisory and pass existing domain services:
- [ ] Expense/invoice/receipt category suggestions against current chart of accounts.
- [ ] Supplier and transaction-candidate matching, reconciliation exception triage.
- [ ] OCR-produced candidate-field selection; leave OCR/vision to its existing model/service.
- [ ] Accounts receivable follow-up urgency and dispute classification.
- [ ] Accounts payable / cheques / financial exception routing.
- [ ] Inventory catalog duplicate candidate ranking, purchase/return/waste reason classification.
- [ ] Sales/POS feedback classification and service escalation.
- [ ] Financial reporting exception prioritization; fixed-asset document category suggestion.
- [ ] Always keep journal posting, exact monetary computations, tax, date arithmetic, stock costing, payroll, refunds, financial approvals and reconciliation finalization deterministic/authorized.

## 7. CRM

Preserve the existing CRM relationship OS, RFM/health scoring, queues, duplicate checks, consent and source-grounded summaries:
- [ ] Lead intent and inquiry categorization; lead prioritization with reviewable explanations.
- [ ] Qualitative sales-opportunity and follow-up priority recommendations.
- [ ] Sentiment and customer feedback / complaint classification.
- [ ] Support case routing, human-escalation suggestion, urgency triage.
- [ ] Probable duplicate candidate re-ranking after deterministic blocking/matching.
- [ ] Contact/company inquiry and B2B requirement classification.
- [ ] Advisory interpretation of existing, source-backed customer health and relationship events; NEVER silently replace deterministic health scores or account balances.
- [ ] All communications subject to consent, current role, project/branch scope and existing CRM approval paths.

## 8. Growth & Marketing

- [ ] Campaign-type and audience-offer suitability ranking over already eligible customer segments.
- [ ] Qualitative customer-interest classification and retention workflow recommendations.
- [ ] Cashback, loyalty reward and promotional-option recommendations **within** deterministic budgets/eligibility rules.
- [ ] Classify customer replies, marketing vs transactional messages, and follow-up urgency.
- [ ] Assist channel selection across authorized website, messaging and in-person marketer workflows.
- [ ] Classify field/online/B2B marketer visit reports and prospect intent; keep GPS coordinates/facts immutable and permission controlled.
- [ ] Review LiteLLM-generated message content for policy/brand suitability before campaign approval.
- [ ] Support upcoming managed Kavenegar messaging, Torob, Divar and other Growth integrations as they become available (do not reinvent their connectors).
- [ ] Preserve opt-in/consent, cost caps, campaign lifecycle, messaging send limits and required approval; verify real uplift via controlled experiments rather than treating Jev probabilities as customer purchase predictions.

## 9. Website Management (two peers under one app)

- [ ] Eshobe CMS: page/content taxonomy, submission routing, moderation signals, internal-link candidate ranking, content quality review.
- [ ] WP/WooCommerce: category suggestion, product-attribute classification, possible product duplicates, review sentiment, inquiry routing, content quality.
- [ ] Cross-site entity/product matching **with deterministic specifications** and source-site/tenant checks; assist rather than silently merge.
- [ ] Website/Growth marketplace feed-error classification for Torob and Divar where actual integrated data is exposed.
- [ ] Jev only scores/classifies text/structured inputs; retain LiteLLM/vision models for generated articles, descriptions, graphics or image interpretation.
- [ ] Reuse managed website connection boundaries and permission gates.

## 10. My Workspace, shared services & industry packs

- [ ] Project tasks, communications, commitments, procurement inquiries, document type and qualitative project risk triage within membership scope.
- [ ] Architecture/construction/contractor workflows with contract-clause review flags (not authoritative legal determination).
- [ ] Shared Media Library: suggest classifications from OCR/vision *text*, with human review of uncertain tags.
- [ ] Notifications: event priority/duplicate classification, preserving existing urgent alert rules.
- [ ] Data transfer: candidate mapping and duplicate review without autonomously mutating source data.
- [ ] Support/integration errors: incident severity, destination and troubleshooting category suggestions.
- [ ] Tenant backup failures: classify error messages only; backup integrity, restore authorization, retention and pricing stay deterministic.
- [ ] Optional business-type policies for café/restaurant, retail, cars, watches/jewelry, engineering/construction and service businesses; inherit current industry availability and app gates.

## 11. AI-assisted automations

Existing WHEN/IF/THEN automation DSL and five deterministic fact fields continue unchanged for their existing functions.
- [ ] Add an **explicitly opt-in, registered qualitative-decision condition** to appropriate workflows, instead of allowing free-form prompts/SQL in rules.
- [ ] Map typed Jev outcomes to bounded approved branches; configurable threshold, abstain, rate limit, escalation and fallback.
- [ ] Before any actual write, re-resolve actor permissions, active business, location/project access, target object version and current state using the existing authority services.
- [ ] High-risk outcomes require human approval; Jev NEVER bypasses ACTION_CATALOG or approval.
- [ ] Deduplicate event retries and safely prevent repeated campaign sends, record writes or charging.
- [ ] Background jobs use server-derived tenant scope and quotas, not stale serialized privileges.

## 12. Billing, observability & resiliency

- [ ] Reuse Biza Miz business wallet, allowance, idempotent charge-settlement and Rial accounting; capture **every billable Jev request**, including compound assistant turns and late/provider-reported errors.
- [ ] Preserve request IDs, parent assistant-turn IDs, tenant, actor, policy/model version, system agent/app/project (as permissible), input token usage, provider cost, exchange rate snapshot, customer price and markup.
- [ ] Prevent double charge on retries/resumes; handle missing provider usage and partial errors explicitly.
- [ ] Platform configurable feature pricing, inclusion/allowance, metering and spend caps; never publish wholesale cost to tenants.
- [ ] Queue-bound large batches: bounded concurrency, chunking, checkpoint, progress, pause/cancel/resume, safe retries with backoff, idempotent outcomes and tenant fairness.
- [ ] Implement strict input/output validation, timeout, circuit breaker, safe failure modes, quotas, provider health, and explicit 429/error handling.
- [ ] Cloud: managed online calls. Hybrid: optional online decision calls but core local business flows work offline. Local-only/offline: deterministic/local fallback; no implicit remote transfer. If queued for later, re-authorize and verify data/consent on replay.
- [ ] No shared cross-tenant context, unscoped results, or raw secret/personal-data logging.

## 13. Privacy, security, provider governance

- [ ] Data-minimize and field-allowlist every decision context; protect PII, financial details, credentials, project-private content and message histories.
- [ ] Verify TypeSafe service terms, processing regions, actual retention/training policy and any **contractually enabled** enterprise zero-data-retention. Do not assume it by default; provide feature/provider disablement where required.
- [ ] Review data residency, PII minimization, deletion and access requirements before sending tenant data to the external service.
- [ ] Enforce server-side tenant origin/session, RLS and explicit business ID; location/project access; user and system-agent allowlist intersection.
- [ ] Prevent prompt injection, tool catalog widening, forged option IDs and invalid/unbounded output; probabilistic screening is not the authorization system.
- [ ] Use separate platform authorization for Superadmin operations; audit provider key access/rotation and security changes.
- [ ] Never rely on Jev for money calculation, accounting entries, legal judgments, tax, exact date comparisons, customer consent or access decisions.

## 14. Data design & migration

Possible forward-only schema additions (verify against repo conventions and avoid unnecessary tables):
- ai_decision_definitions — registered decision types/ownership
- ai_decision_versions — immutable published policy versions
- ai_decision_assignments — agent/app/business-type/tenant feature availability
- ai_decision_runs — execution metadata and request-level attribution
- ai_decision_feedback — human corrections and outcomes
- ai_decision_evaluations — labeled benchmark/canary results

Every tenant-scoped table requires its RLS policy in the same migration. Global policy rows need platform guard semantics. Prefer existing audit/usage tables where they already fit; **do not create a second customer wallet, duplicate prompt store or semantic cache.**

## 15. Testing and measurements (release gates)

- [ ] Evaluate Persian, English and mixed-language messages, RTL marks, Arabic/Persian yeh/kaf, Persian digits, ZWNJ, Shamsi terminology and actual domain vocabulary.
- [ ] Measure classification accuracy/precision/recall, relevance, ranked-choice outcomes, calibration, abstention/uncertainty, operator correction, false positives/negatives and quality regression by policy version.
- [ ] Compare p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, end-to-end cost per successful task, operator time saved, and real business outcomes vs existing deterministic/LiteLLM baselines.
- [ ] Evaluate financial/inventory/consent/permission boundary invariants, cross-tenant isolation, revoked project membership, wrong-branch data, deleted memory, provider outages and offline startup.
- [ ] Test bounded workload, 429/retry/backoff, model version rollback, response malformed/partial, cancellation, failed settlement, duplicate event, approval race and stale authority.
- [ ] Shadow-mode rollout first; canary by feature/tenant; feature-level rollback/kill switch and monitoring; no universal default enablement until each use case meets acceptance gates.
- [ ] Follow repo CI conventions: unit/integration/tenant-isolation/permission-matrix/billing tests, typecheck and production build.

## 16. Implementation phases

### Phase 0 — Audit & baseline
- [ ] Inventory existing duplicate features and open issues; confirm latest vendor SDK/API, terms, limits and allowed deployment channels.
- [ ] Select first benchmark tasks (intent routing, CRM case triage, tenant-scoped knowledge re-ranking), define labeled Persian datasets and baseline quality/cost.
- [ ] Document security/data processing decisions and vendor-related risk register.

### Phase 1 — Secure shared infrastructure
- [ ] SDK/HTTP adapter, schemas, trusted scope, policy registry, transport, auditing, cost and provider-failure handling.
- [ ] Superadmin connection/model/version controls; kill switches, shadow mode, unit/integration tests.

### Phase 2 — Assistant, memory & knowledge
- [ ] Read-only intent/tool ranking, memory candidate ranking, managed-knowledge re-ranking, answerability/source verification; measure improvement.

### Phase 3 — CRM & Growth
- [ ] Lead/support triage, campaign/offering evaluation, outreach classification and consent-safe recommendations.

### Phase 4 — Accounting, Websites, My Workspace, shared services
- [ ] Extend validated features to document/reconciliation candidates, CMS/Woo product/content decisions, project/operational triage and managed-service error classification.

### Phase 5 — Managed automations & scaled operation
- [ ] Strictly bounded qualitative IF conditions, queue-backed bulk processing, approval workspaces, SLO dashboards, pricing tools, canary promotion and mature offline/hybrid fallbacks.

## 17. Definition of done

- [ ] Jev can be centrally configured, tested, pinned, versioned, assigned, billed, monitored and disabled by Superadmin.
- [ ] All four apps and platform utilities can invoke shared **registered** decision policies without adding a fifth tenant app.
- [ ] Tenant UI remains managed/white-label with no external AI credentials or provider setup.
- [ ] No new authorization, provider routing, prompt resolver, vector store, action executor or billing source of truth.
- [ ] A Jev result cannot grant access, execute unauthorized writes, auto-trigger Deep Research, change accounting truth or bypass approval.
- [ ] Tenant/branch/project/data/consent isolation tests pass; deletion/revocation takes immediate effect on future decisions.
- [ ] Every billable provider call has correct attribution, idempotent settlement and auditable cost; errors/retries cannot double charge.
- [ ] Disabled/offline/provider-error states preserve core business functionality and safe fallback.
- [ ] Each enabled use case demonstrates acceptable Persian-language quality, safety, latency and measured benefit over existing solutions.
- [ ] CI passes the repo's required unit, integration, TypeScript and production build gates.

## References

- [TypeSafe System One API](https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone) (API endpoint, not a browser page)
- [Independent API contract guide](https://typesafe-jev.com/en/guides/api/) — reverify against official docs/SDK before coding
- [Current Biza Miz AI subsystem ownership](https://github.com/hamidnoshady/biza-miz/blob/main/docs/ai-subsystem-architecture.md)
- [Current app ownership](https://github.com/hamidnoshady/biza-miz/blob/main/docs/app-boundaries.md)
- [CRM relationship OS](https://github.com/hamidnoshady/biza-miz/blob/main/docs/crm-relationship-os.md)

**Scope:** Design + implementation epic. Break work into child issues by phase during development; this issue is the platform-level coordination and acceptance contract.

## Unified commercial billing coordination (#1377)

Use #1378's commercial policy for published background agents: setup and enabled-time availability are distinct from actual inference/decision consumption; respect explicit plan inclusion/discount and AI allowances, single LiteLLM billing/wallet path, stable service identities, branch/tenant and permission gates. No charge for suggestion-only chat or duplicate per-event provider settlement. Coordinate #1381 tests.

Implementation source: [GitHub #1377](https://github.com/hamidnoshady/biza-miz/issues/1377); coordinate with ESH-193 in Linear. Preserve this issue's original scope, priority and status; this is an integration requirement, not a duplicate implementation.

items.title: Monthly Dashboard v2 — unified RAW/core/template for W + CPR
items.body:
## Goal

Build **Monthly Dashboard v2** as a shared architecture for W and CPR first, using the same raw data foundation as Daily/Weekly while preserving Monthly-specific business logic and visual structure.

Do **not** work on Orange yet. Do **not** spend time on visual polish or SKU-specific analysis until this task is complete.

## Core principles

1. **One raw data foundation**
   - Daily, Weekly and Monthly must read from the same normalized RAW layer in Supabase.
   - Monthly must not be derived from `sku_daily`.
   - Reports may apply different business logic, but must not maintain separate primary data sources.

2. **One Monthly template**
   - W and CPR must use one shared frontend/core implementation.
   - Cabinet-specific differences live in config/data, not duplicated code.
   - Architecture should be extensible to Orange and future clients after W/CPR are validated.

3. **Monthly lifecycle**
   - LIVE = current month.
   - CLOSING = previous month after cutoff, while validation/enrichment completes.
   - CLOSED = frozen month.
   - Month cutoff is 00:00 on the first day of the next month.
   - Closed month must not drift when order statuses change later.

4. **Compensations are separate**
   - Base Monthly economics must work without compensation/decompensation.
   - Compensation layer is applied independently later.
   - CPR logic: actual SKU compensation.
   - W/Orange logic later: category-level allocation.
   - For now, keep compensation excluded from the core validation of September.

## Existing verified September baseline

### W
- Finance API September 01–30 loaded to Supabase.
- Official Ozon accrual report reconciled exactly: **0.00 RUB difference**.
- Net sales: **6,387,302.00 RUB**
- Result after standard Ozon charges, before compensation: **2,034,525.91 RUB**
- September is now stored in `sku_monthly_w`.

### CPR
- Finance API September 01–30 loaded to Supabase.
- Official Ozon accrual report reconciled exactly: **0.00 RUB difference** at raw Finance level.
- Net sales: **7,159,659.00 RUB**
- Result before compensation/decompensation: **2,536,482.50 RUB**
- Difference to Ozon grand total = **8,533.90 RUB**, intentionally excluded decompensation.
- September is now stored in `sku_monthly_cpr`.

### Shared raw finance table
- `public.ozon_finance_lines_raw_v1`
- tenant_id distinguishes W / CPR.

## Required architecture

Target flow:

```
Ozon API
  -> shared RAW tables in Supabase
  -> normalized/core SQL layer
  -> Daily views
  -> Weekly views
  -> Monthly views
  -> shared Monthly frontend
```

n8n should be used for ingestion/schedules/integrations, not as the business-logic source of truth.

## Data layer tasks

### A. Audit current sources
Document what Daily, Weekly and Monthly currently read from for W and CPR.

Identify:
- duplicated sources;
- report-specific tables that are acting as primary data;
- hardcoded month/account logic;
- duplicated expense classification;
- any dependency on Google Sheets.

### B. Normalize raw entities
At minimum define/confirm shared raw sources for:
- orders/statuses;
- finance accrual lines;
- product/SKU dictionary;
- price history;
- cost history;
- business expenses;
- compensation imports.

Every shared source must include tenant/account identity.

### C. Central expense classification
Create one source of truth for Ozon fee classification:
- type_id;
- Ozon label;
- internal expense_group;
- direct/shared;
- allocation basis.

Daily/Weekly/Monthly must consume the same classification.

Unknown type_id must fail validation or appear in an explicit audit table; never silently go to an unreviewed bucket.

## Monthly core

Create a shared Monthly Core schema/view set parameterized by tenant.

Expected output per SKU/month should include at least:
- tenant_id / account_id;
- month;
- marketplace;
- SKU;
- article;
- product_name;
- master_category;
- sale_operations;
- return_operations;
- sold_units;
- sales;
- returns;
- net_sales;
- commission;
- logistics;
- storage;
- promotion;
- other;
- direct expenses;
- allocated shared expenses;
- total Ozon expenses;
- result without compensation;
- compensation placeholders;
- result with compensation;
- economic units;
- received per unit;
- source;
- month status: LIVE/CLOSING/CLOSED;
- updated_at.

Do not duplicate this logic for W and CPR.

## Month close mechanism

Implement a reusable closing process:

1. At 00:00 first day of next month, previous month leaves LIVE.
2. Freeze order/status snapshot.
3. Backfill full Finance API for all dates of previous month.
4. Validate completeness.
5. Store closed month result.
6. Current month becomes the only LIVE month.
7. Later data changes must not mutate CLOSED month membership.

If exact historical status at cutoff cannot be guaranteed from a current-state table, introduce append-only status history or another reliable capture mechanism.

## Validation / acceptance checks

Build automated checks for every closed month:

- every expected calendar day loaded;
- raw Finance total equals normalized Finance total;
- sum SKU + shared allocations equals account total;
- shared allocation conserves the original shared amount exactly;
- no unknown type_id;
- no duplicate accrual keys;
- no duplicated SKU/month rows;
- closed month is immutable;
- LIVE month remains dynamic;
- W September matches verified control:
  - net sales 6,387,302.00
  - result before compensation 2,034,525.91
- CPR September matches verified control:
  - net sales 7,159,659.00
  - result before compensation 2,536,482.50

Produce a validation report/query that can be run after every monthly close.

## Shared frontend

After the data/core layer is stable:

Create one Monthly frontend/template for W and CPR.

Cabinet differences must be configuration only.

Suggested structure:

```
monthly/
  core/
  config/
  data/
  components/
  tests/
```

No separate W Monthly app and CPR Monthly app.

### Monthly visual structure to preserve

Top KPI block:
1. Net sales
2. Marketplace expenses
3. Ozon result without compensation
4. Compensation
5. Business expenses
6. Final result after all expenses

Below:
- Financial funnel
- Month dynamics: 3 closed + current live
- Expense structure
- Business expenses/capital
- SKU table
- SKU detail card

The frontend must clearly label LIVE vs CLOSED.

## Dashboard data access

Current W/CPR management dashboards are served via n8n webhook and read SQL tables.

For v2:
- prefer a direct prepared API/view layer over using n8n as a read proxy;
- if keeping n8n temporarily, isolate it as transport only;
- frontend schema should be identical for every tenant.

Target API shape conceptually:
- `/monthly?tenant=W`
- `/monthly?tenant=CPR`

## Account config

Create a shared account configuration model/table with fields such as:
- tenant_id;
- marketplace;
- account_id;
- display_name;
- active;
- category/default master category;
- compensation method;
- cost method;
- business expense method;
- dashboard enabled.

Goal: onboarding another cabinet should be configuration-driven, not code duplication.

## Historical cost model

Costs must be time-valid:
- SKU
- valid_from
- valid_to
- unit_cost

Historical months must not change when a new cost is entered.

## Scope order

### Phase 1
Audit + unified RAW/data model.

### Phase 2
Shared Monthly Core for W + CPR.

### Phase 3
LIVE/CLOSING/CLOSED lifecycle + month close automation.

### Phase 4
Automated reconciliation/tests against July/August/September.

### Phase 5
Single Monthly frontend for W + CPR.

### Phase 6
Compensation layer.

### Phase 7
Business expenses + historical costs.

### Phase 8
Only after W/CPR are stable: Orange.

## Non-goals for this task

- No Orange migration yet.
- No SKU-specific pricing analysis.
- No cosmetic UI tweaks unless required for shared-template refactor.
- Do not change Daily business logic.
- Do not break Weekly.
- Do not delete legacy tables/views before parity is proven.

## Definition of done

Monthly v2 is complete when:

- W and CPR use one Monthly template.
- Daily/Weekly/Monthly share one RAW foundation.
- September is CLOSED without manual Excel dependence.
- October is the only LIVE month.
- Next month can transition automatically.
- Finance API reconciliation is automated.
- Expense classification is centralized.
- Unknown fees are surfaced.
- Historical costs are time-valid.
- New cabinets can be added by config.
- Legacy W/CPR monthly paths are archived only after parity tests pass.
- A short migration/readme document explains:
  - final architecture;
  - table/view ownership;
  - close workflow;
  - validation commands;
  - how to onboard a new cabinet.

## Delivery expectations

Work in small verifiable commits/PR(s). For each phase, include:
- what changed;
- impact on dashboard;
- how to verify it;
- any migration/backfill required.

Do not require the user to shuttle implementation details between ChatGPT and Codex. Keep implementation notes in the repository/issue/PR.

items.body:
## What this is

Design-mill starter for the **Atlas v1 program** (Drew directive, 2026-11-12 17:38 CST): build out a full design for a strong v1 of Atlas — search build-out with Workers fan-out, the backup mesh, the Metadata schema + evolution doctrine, the per-embed classification model, always-on corpus ingestion, embed-storage economics, query-as-data, a virtual filesystem over the content-addressed store, and the worker-instructions rollout.

- **Proto design (intake output, merged to main):** `doc/2026-11-12T23-59-00Z_design_atlas_v1_proto/note.md` in developing-today/code — current-state inventory, workstream specs A–I, and the statement map. Read it from the repo.
- **Program home:** epic #8983 (Atlas program). Workstreams are filed as sibling sub-issues of #8983 and linked from the proto design §J.
- **Summit ownership:** the claiming session runs the design-mill pattern (statement inventory → state-of-the-art expansion → versioned designs → granular implementation issues) under the launch packet in `~/workspace/custom-skills/design-mill/SKILL.md`, owning this issue end to end. It elaborates the proto design into the full design set — many smaller designs — and files the granular implementation issues under each workstream issue.

## Binding constraints from the directive

- Atlas is **internal-use only**; the corpus is never exposed directly to a public surface (disclosure contexts are a classification-model concern, workstream D).
- Coordinate, don't duplicate: #9060 design §12 (issue/PR Metadata), slices #9073/#9074; content-plane models in #9084 (reference-vs-copy is UNDECIDED there — this program references its evaluation, never pre-settles it); queue/PM genealogy model from #9060 generally.
- The Metadata schema doctrine (workstream C) is shared between Atlas corpus metadata and issue/PR Metadata: additive-only evolution, version always carried, breaking changes parked and applied as one set with a reclassify-everything pass.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Statement inventory from the proto design §J: zero unmapped statements.
- [ ] Each workstream A–I elaborated into versioned design docs merged under `doc/`, or explicitly folded into an existing design by amendment with a link recorded here.
- [ ] Granular implementation issues filed under each workstream issue with acceptance criteria.
- [ ] Open questions answered in the mill or batched to Drew with options + a recommendation.
- [ ] This issue's checklist updated as workstreams land; the queue task completes only when the above are demonstrably done (not on epic closure alone).

items.body:
## Decision status

This issue is the design authority for independently developed and deployed ingestion extensions.

It must define and validate the boundary **before production APIs or runtime abstractions are added**. The first implementation is a vertical proof of the agreed contract, not an invitation to move the current Knowledge Flow base classes into a public package.

T-KEIR is the first candidate processing provider. Future remote-source connectors are part of the direction, but processors and connectors are deliberately separate contracts.

## Context

FRED has a durable Temporal ingestion workflow and working in-process processor and content-loader abstractions. Those abstractions are currently tied to Knowledge Flow's Python environment and internal models:

- processors are selected through Python `class_path` configuration and internal registries;
- `BaseInputProcessor` depends on Knowledge Flow implementation details and local processing dependencies;
- pull-source loaders and their catalog/scheduler structures also live inside Knowledge Flow.

This is suitable for code shipped in the same repository and image. It is not a stable API for a provider developed in another repository and executed as an independently deployed pod.

We want the ingestion equivalent of an agentic pod in deployment and ownership, while preserving the execution model appropriate for ingestion:

- agentic pods are interactive HTTP runtimes;
- ingestion extensions are asynchronous workers coordinated by Temporal;
- FRED remains the owner of product state, authorization, orchestration and publication.

## Goal

Design a provider-neutral family of contracts and the FRED orchestration required to execute external ingestion work.

The family has two operation-specific contracts:

1. **Document processor:** transforms an authorized input artifact into a normalized or enriched output manifest.
2. **Source connector:** discovers and retrieves changes from a remote source, with stable provenance and a durable cursor owned by FRED.

They may share a small execution/configuration envelope and provider lifecycle rules. They must not be collapsed into one universal plugin interface.

The first implementation slice is one external document processor. Connector implementation follows only after its distinct discovery/fetch contract is designed.

## Architectural convictions

1. Public wire contracts precede public base classes.
2. Cross-repository communication uses versioned serializable data, never Python `class_path`.
3. `fred-sdk` is the proposed owner of stable transport-neutral contract models and generated JSON Schema.
4. Temporal types and Knowledge Flow internals do not leak into those wire models.
5. Knowledge Flow remains the canonical ingestion orchestrator and product/data-plane owner.
6. External pods own computation, not FRED product truth.
7. Processors and source connectors share conventions, not business interfaces.
8. Configuration is strict, versioned and separated from secrets; see #2351.
9. One real external consumer must validate the contract before it is generalized.
10. Migration is complete only when the superseded in-process path for the migrated provider is removed or has a time-bounded removal plan.

## Contract and package boundaries

### `fred-sdk` — stable public surface

Proposed contents:

- versioned shared execution envelope;
- processor request/result models;
- source-connector request/result models;
- artifact references and hashes;
- structured warnings and error codes;
- capability and compatibility metadata;
- configuration manifest/version references;
- provider-facing contract fixtures.

It must not import:

- Knowledge Flow application models;
- Temporal SDK types;
- database/store implementations;
- provider-specific models such as T-KEIR internals.

### Knowledge Flow — canonical owner

Knowledge Flow owns:

- authentication, ReBAC and tenant/team authorization;
- source, document and chunk identity;
- source catalog and durable connector cursor;
- source/preview/output artifact lifecycle;
- ingestion and source-sync tasks;
- durable progress events, SSE replay and cancellation;
- Temporal parent workflows, retry policy and terminal state;
- processing profiles;
- vector indexing and final metadata publication;
- reprocessing, supersession and deletion;
- compatibility admission for provider and contract versions.

### Transport/execution adapter

Temporal is the first transport adapter.

Its package placement is a design decision. Do not put ingestion orchestration into `fred-runtime` merely because that package already exists: `fred-runtime` currently owns agent execution. Reuse it only if the proposed primitive is demonstrably generic and does not turn it into a catch-all runtime. Otherwise keep the adapter with the owning Knowledge Flow worker or propose a small dedicated package after the first consumer proves the boundary.

### External provider pod

The provider owns:

- provider-specific models and dependencies;
- computation and provider-internal checkpoints;
- outputs under the authorized artifact prefix;
- health, metrics, logs and Temporal heartbeats;
- cooperative cancellation;
- validation of provider-specific configuration.

The provider must not introduce another user-facing ingestion API, task service, scheduler, document/source catalog, authentication authority, authorization model, or vector/RAG stack.

## Shared execution envelope

Processor and connector operations should share only fields whose semantics are genuinely identical:

- contract schema/version;
- provider ID and version;
- operation name/version;
- job ID and deterministic idempotency key;
- authorized execution scope;
- provider configuration version and non-secret effective configuration hash;
- input/output artifact scope;
- deadline and cancellation metadata;
- correlation and trace identifiers;
- structured warnings and error envelope.

Raw user JWTs and FRED's full backend configuration must not be passed to provider pods. Artifact access should use least-privilege workload identity, short-lived authorized references, or an internal artifact service.

The exact envelope must be proven by both the processor and connector contract examples before being frozen.

## Document processor contract

### Request

- shared execution envelope;
- FRED document UID;
- normalized input artifact reference and SHA-256;
- requested processing capabilities;
- optional reference-ontology artifact references;
- provider-scoped output artifact prefix;
- stable chunk identity/provenance inputs where required.

### Result

- processor ID and version;
- input and configuration hashes;
- versioned output manifest;
- normalized/enriched artifact references and hashes;
- chunk annotation manifest reference and hash where applicable;
- structured counts and warnings;
- retry classification and non-retryable error codes;
- timing/resource summary where available.

For T-KEIR, output may include entities, relations, subject-predicate-object statements, chunk provenance and document-level JSON-LD/RDF. Those shapes remain provider outputs until FRED explicitly promotes any field into a public canonical contract.

Document contents and generated graphs must not be returned in Temporal payloads. The provider returns only compact manifests.

## Source connector contract

A source connector has different semantics from a processor. It must model remote discovery and acquisition explicitly.

The design must determine whether V1 exposes separate `discover` and `fetch` operations or one bounded synchronization operation. In either case its contract must cover:

### Request

- shared execution envelope;
- FRED-owned source identity;
- connector/provider configuration reference and version;
- FRED-owned opaque cursor or synchronization checkpoint;
- bounded discovery window, filters and page/size limits;
- authorized artifact delivery target.

### Result

- stable provider source-item identity and provenance;
- change kind such as upsert, unchanged or deletion;
- remote revision, ETag/hash and modification metadata where available;
- retrieved artifact reference and hash, or a bounded fetch descriptor;
- next cursor/checkpoint;
- partial-page and continuation semantics;
- structured warnings and retry classification.

FRED persists the authoritative cursor and catalog state only after the corresponding batch is durably accepted. Connector retries must not duplicate documents or lose deletions.

## Proposed V1 processor execution model

```text
Knowledge Flow API
  -> create the canonical FRED ingestion task
  -> start the parent Temporal ingestion workflow
       -> acquire/extract/normalise document     [Knowledge Flow queue]
       -> external processing/enrichment          [provider-specific queue]
       -> validate and atomically accept manifest [Knowledge Flow queue]
       -> vectorise/index                         [Knowledge Flow queue]
       -> publish metadata and terminal success   [Knowledge Flow queue]
```

A future pull-source flow remains FRED-orchestrated:

```text
FRED-owned schedule or explicit sync request
  -> create the canonical source-sync task
  -> start the parent Temporal source-sync workflow
       -> discover a bounded change batch         [connector queue]
       -> persist cursor/catalog decision          [Knowledge Flow queue]
       -> acquire authorized artifacts             [connector/KF per contract]
       -> invoke the canonical ingestion pipeline  [Knowledge Flow workflow]
```

The connector must not become a second scheduler or ingestion coordinator.

## Configuration boundary

#2351 owns the platform-wide configuration architecture. This issue consumes its minimum external-runtime rules without waiting for the complete backend migration:

- strict versioned provider manifest;
- secrets supplied through references or workload identity, not embedded provider YAML;
- observable provider, contract, capability and configuration versions;
- effective non-secret configuration hash included in every job;
- provider-specific configuration validated by an explicitly owned schema;
- no copy of Knowledge Flow's monolithic configuration in an external repository;
- no cross-pod `class_path`.

Static provider registration is sufficient for V1. Service discovery, installation UI and a provider catalogue are out of scope.

## Processing profiles and failure semantics

Define behavior explicitly:

- `standard`: current pipeline; no external semantic provider;
- `semantic`: enrichment is required and failure fails ingestion;
- optionally `semantic_best_effort`: record a durable warning and continue vector-only during a bounded evaluation.

A document must not be marked successfully ingested before all capabilities promised by its selected profile are durably published.

Connector behavior also needs an explicit policy for partial batches, individual-item failures, remote throttling and deletion events. A connector batch must never advance the durable cursor past changes that FRED has not safely recorded.

## Progress, retry and cancellation

Reuse the existing canonical FRED task/event path. Providers never publish frontend events directly.

For the processor slice, the existing ingestion lifecycle remains authoritative, with an explicit external-processing stage mapped into it. For source connectors, define a canonical source-sync lifecycle rather than reusing an inaccurate `uploading` stage or adding a provider-specific frontend state.

Every durable event/state must have one owner and must rehydrate identically after reload or replica change.

Long-running work must heartbeat and react to Temporal cancellation. CPU-bound or native model calls may require stage checkpoints or a killable subprocess so cancellation does not simply wait for the call to finish.

Retry classification must distinguish transient transport/provider failures from contract, authorization, stale-input and deterministic processing failures.

## Idempotency and publication invariants

- Derive processor idempotency from document UID, input hash, provider version, operation version and configuration hash.
- Derive connector idempotency from source identity, remote revision/change identity, connector version and configuration hash.
- Retries must not create duplicate artifacts, catalog entries, documents, graph entries or indexed chunks.
- Write outputs to staging/content-addressed locations and publish manifests atomically.
- Never combine output with a different source/document version.
- Never expose a retrievable successful state before artifacts, metadata and vector publication agree.
- Reprocessing must supersede the old manifest safely.
- Document/source deletion must include provider artifacts according to FRED lifecycle policy.
- Cursor advancement and accepted connector changes must be committed consistently.

## Security and tenancy invariants

- FRED authorizes the source/document operation before dispatch and revalidates any mutable ownership needed at publication.
- Providers receive the minimum provider-scoped execution context; they do not make FRED authorization decisions.
- Artifact grants are short-lived or workload-bound and scoped to exact inputs/output prefixes.
- Logs, metrics, manifests and errors do not expose secrets, raw credentials or unnecessary document contents.
- Provider queues and identities cannot consume another provider's jobs or artifact prefixes.
- Version admission can reject unsupported or revoked provider builds before work starts.

## Design gate — required before production implementation

The assigned design work must produce and receive team confirmation for:

- [ ] Evidence/convergence map of current processor registries, content loaders, schedulers, contracts and dynamic imports.
- [ ] One canonical owner for every durable state, event, cursor and artifact.
- [ ] Package placement decision for public models and Temporal adapters.
- [ ] Processor and connector contract examples proving the shared envelope and their separate semantics.
- [ ] Version compatibility and deprecation policy.
- [ ] Artifact authorization and lifecycle decision.
- [ ] Retry, timeout, heartbeat, cancellation and idempotency matrix.
- [ ] Progress/event mapping with no competing frontend state vocabulary.
- [ ] Minimal #2351-compatible provider configuration boundary.
- [ ] Selection of the first external processor vertical.
- [ ] Migration/removal condition for that processor's current in-process path.
- [ ] Contract and end-to-end test plan.

Do not start broad SDK/runtime implementation before this gate. A disposable contract spike is acceptable only when it answers a named design question and is not merged as an accidental public API.

## First implementation slice

After design confirmation:

1. Implement the minimal versioned contract models and generated schemas.
2. Provide provider-side contract fixtures and validation tests.
3. Extract one processor into an independently buildable repository/container.
4. Execute it through a dedicated Temporal queue using authorized artifact references.
5. Keep task/event publication exclusively in FRED.
6. Prove success, worker loss/retry, cancellation, stale input, duplicate dispatch, contract-version rejection and SSE terminal state.
7. Remove or time-bound the superseded in-process path before declaring the slice complete.
8. Use the evidence from this slice to revise the contract before adding a second processor or implementing connectors.

T-KEIR is the intended first candidate, but the contract must remain usable by a simpler second processor without T-KEIR-specific types.

## Open design questions

- Should Pydantic models in `fred-sdk` generate the normative JSON Schema, or should another schema source own both?
- Does V1 use one remote activity or a provider-owned child workflow for internal stages?
- Should the Temporal adapter remain in Knowledge Flow or justify a dedicated runtime package?
- How do providers obtain artifacts: workload identity, short-lived URLs or an internal artifact service?
- How are stable FRED chunk IDs conveyed when provider chunking differs?
- Which semantic fields belong in canonical vector/document metadata versus provider artifacts only?
- Does a source connector expose separate discover/fetch operations or a bounded sync operation?
- How are connector cursors versioned, migrated and recovered after partial failure?
- What source-sync task/event vocabulary is canonical across backend, SSE and frontend?
- What provider/contract version skew is tolerated during rolling deployments?
- What backpressure, fairness and concurrency limits apply per tenant and provider?
- What observability and SLOs are required per provider, operation and attempt?

## Non-goals for V1

- A universal interface combining processors and source connectors.
- Publishing current Knowledge Flow ABCs or configuration models as the SDK.
- Cross-repository Python imports or `class_path` loading.
- Kubernetes-native provider discovery.
- A general UI for installing/configuring arbitrary providers.
- A provider-owned task service, scheduler, source/document catalog or auth model.
- Corpus-wide entity resolution or graph fusion.
- Replacing FRED vector retrieval.
- Exposing T-KEIR directly to end users.
- Treating ingestion extensions as agent capabilities without evidence that their lifecycle matches.
- Moving FRED document/source/auth/task ownership into the provider.

Corpus/library graph construction remains a separate future Temporal workflow with its own authorization, rebuild and lifecycle semantics.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Confirmed architecture decision for boundary, packages and ownership.
- [ ] Versioned shared envelope plus separate processor and source-connector schemas.
- [ ] Compatibility/deprecation and worker-versioning policy.
- [ ] Artifact authorization and lifecycle design.
- [ ] Progress, retry, timeout, cancellation and idempotency invariants.
- [ ] #2351-compatible provider configuration model.
- [ ] Contract fixtures usable from FRED and an external repository.
- [ ] Minimal external processor proof of concept.
- [ ] End-to-end verification of failure and recovery paths.
- [ ] Migration/deletion plan with before/after production-code and concept metrics.
- [ ] Evaluation plan comparing current ingestion with the first external provider.
- [ ] Follow-up implementation issue for the first source connector after its distinct contract is confirmed.

## Acceptance criteria

- The design gate is confirmed before production API/runtime implementation.
- One canonical owner is identified for every durable state, cursor and event.
- Public models import no Knowledge Flow, Temporal or provider-internal types.
- Processor and source-connector contracts remain distinct while sharing only proven envelope fields.
- An independently released provider can validate and execute the contract without the FRED repository.
- Large documents and graphs never enter Temporal workflow history.
- Retry, cancellation, authorization, deletion, partial failure and version skew have explicit behavior.
- Provider secrets and FRED backend configuration do not cross the runtime boundary.
- The MVP reuses FRED's task service, Temporal scheduler, content storage, metadata and vector pipeline.
- Frontend progress is driven by canonical durable FRED events, not provider-local states.
- The first vertical includes a removal condition for its replaced in-process path.
- Generalization to additional processors or connectors is justified by evidence from the first consumer.
